Frequency-domain dynamic awareness for non-line-of-sight single-pixel imaging: a frequency-aware optical-computational co-design framework
abstract: Non-line-of-sight single-pixel imaging (NLoS-SPI) benefits from the high sensitivity and wide dynamic range of bucket detectors, but its performance is limited by severe signal attenuation and relay-wall-induced low-pass degradation, especially under low sampling ratios. To address these challenges, we propose a Frequency-Domain Dynamic Awareness (FDDA) framework, formulated as a frequency-aware optical-computational co-design framework for intensity-only NLoS-SPI. By jointly optimizing binary modulation patterns and a frequency-aware reconstruction architecture, the proposed framework is designed to better preserve structurally informative details that are weakened during indirect propagation. Numerical simulations and experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework improves hidden-target reconstruction under sub-Nyquist sampling. In the NLoS experiments, the proposed method achieves a peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 25.1 dB and a structural similarity index (SSIM) of 0.81 at a sampling ratio of 6.25%. Even at a sampling ratio of 1.56%, it maintains more recognizable structural cues than the compared SPI methods. These results demonstrate the feasibility of jointly designing optical modulation and frequency-aware reconstruction for improving structure-aware recovery in intensity-only NLoS-SPI under low-sampling conditions.

title: Social relationships, emotion regulation, and emotional wellbeing in adolescence: associations in youth with and without a migratory background
abstract: Emotional wellbeing in adolescence develops within interconnected personal and relational systems, but the relative salience of family, peer, and school contexts may vary across sociocultural experiences. The present study examined associations among perceived functioning in school, family, and peer domains, everyday emotion-regulation difficulties, and affective emotional wellbeing in 79 third-year middle-school students in Rome (M age = 13.80 years, SD = 0.45; 45.6% female), including 42 adolescents without and 37 with a migratory background, defined as having at least one foreign-born parent. Participants completed self-report assessments of relational functioning across the three domains, emotion-regulation difficulties, and positive and negative affect. Two separately estimated observed-variable path models were used for exploratory purposes. Among adolescents with a migratory background, school ( β = 0.44, p = 0.002) and family ( β = 0.53, p < 0.001) indicators were independently associated with greater emotional wellbeing. No direct relational-context path to emotional wellbeing reached significance in the group without a migratory background. Emotion-regulation difficulties were not independently associated with emotional wellbeing in either group, and percentile bootstrap confidence intervals based on 5,000 resamples did not support indirect pathways through emotion…

title: The association between physical activity and internet addiction in college students: a serial mediation analysis of interoceptive awareness and emotion regulation difficulties
abstract: Purpose This study examined the association between physical activity and internet addiction among college students and tested the indirect associations of interoceptive awareness and emotion regulation difficulties using a serial mediation model. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 677 Chinese college students. Standardized instruments were used to assess physical activity, interoceptive awareness, emotion regulation difficulties, and internet addiction. Descriptive statistics, correlation analyses, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), and serial mediation analyses were performed using SPSS 27.0 and Mplus 8.3. Indirect associations and their confidence intervals were estimated using 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Continuous and nonlinear PA specifications, alternative scoring, and measurement checks were added. Results Participants were categorized into low-, moderate-, and high-level physical activity groups. High physical activity, relative to low physical activity, had a negative conditional direct association with internet addiction scores (β = −0.200, p = 0.002). The serial mediation model indicated that high versus low physical activity was positively associated with interoceptive awareness (β = 0.550, p < 0.001) and negatively associated with emotion regulation difficulties (β = −0.287, p < 0.001). Continuous PA was inversely associated with I…

title: Substance Use Frequency and Psychotic-Like Experiences Within a Broader Psychosocial Network
abstract: Abstract Substance use is associated with psychotic-like experiences (PLEs), but it remains unclear how these associations vary with frequency of use and broader psychosocial difficulties. We examined alcohol, cannabis, and stimulant use in relation to PLEs within a broader psychosocial network and compared patterns across substance use frequency groups. Data from 1196 adults were analyzed using regularized network estimation, bridge centrality, shortest path analyses, network comparison tests, and exploratory parallel indirect association models. Networks included alcohol, cannabis, and stimulant use frequency, impulsivity, other psychopathological symptoms, recent stress exposure, adverse childhood experiences, delusion-like experiences, and auditory perceptual abnormalities. Participants were classified as nonusers, lower frequency users, or higher frequency users using an exploratory data-derived frequency boundary. Higher frequency users showed greater psychosocial/PLE network connectivity than nonusers, while the full lower and higher frequency networks differed in both global strength and overall structure. Delusion-like experiences showed more consistent direct network associations with substance use frequency than auditory perceptual abnormalities. In the full network, delusion-like experiences and other psychopathological symptoms showed the highest bridge strength. E…

title: Daily regulation of glucocerebrosidase activity and impact of fixed-time rotarod training in a mouse model of Gba1-associated Parkinson's disease
abstract: Introduction Mutations in the glucocerebrosidase ( GBA1 ) gene are a major genetic risk factor for Parkinson's disease (PD) and result in dysfunctional glucocerebrosidase (GCase), the lysosomal enzyme responsible for cleaving glucosylceramide into glucose and ceramide. The pathogenic L444P variant disrupts the enzyme structure and activity, leading to lysosomal accumulation of glucosylceramide and ultimately impairing the clearance of monomeric α-synuclein (α-syn). Given the functional crosstalk among lysosomal homeostasis, the molecular circadian clock, and physical activity, we investigated whether GCase activity exhibits daily rhythmicity, and can be modulated by daily, fixed-time rotarod activity in healthy and Gba1 -mutant mice. Methods C57BL/6J healthy controls and Gba1 -mutant PD model mice were housed under a 12 h light/dark cycle, and blood samples were collected at four Zeitgeber times (ZT2, ZT8, ZT14, and ZT20), with and without daily, fixed-time rotarod training. A fluorometric assay was performed on plasma samples to investigate the daily pattern of GCase activity. Results Our results showed that rotarod performance was influenced by genotype-dependent vulnerabilities and by daily, fixed-time physical activity, with overall better performance during the dark-phase training. The fluorometric assay revealed that GCase activity shows a ZT-dependent daily pattern in he…

title: Combined effects of Pseudomonas protegens CS11 and lemongrass oil on Sclerotinia sclerotiorum suppression and regulation of defence responses in tomato
The Role of Potassium and Calcium Ion Channels in Membrane Potential Regulation and Diabetes Mellitus
abstract: Potassium (K+) and calcium (Ca2+) ion channels are important regulators of cell electrical activity, membrane potential, intracellular calcium homeostasis, hormone production, vascular tone, neuronal excitability and metabolic function. Their coordinated activity is especially crucial in pancreatic β-cells, where variations in membrane potential act as the electrical coupling between glucose metabolism and insulin release. In healthy β-cells, glucose metabolism increases the intracellular ATP/ADP ratio, closes ATP-sensitive potassium (KATP) channels, depolarises the membrane, activates voltage-dependent calcium channels and increases cytosolic Ca2+, which induces insulin granule exocytosis. Potassium channels of several types, including voltage-dependent potassium channels and calcium-activated potassium channels, then regulate the pattern of electrical activity and membrane repolarisation. Thus, calcium channels not only constitute sources of intracellular Ca2+ but also play an essential part in the stimulus secretion coupling mechanism. In diabetes mellitus altered expression, activity and control of potassium and calcium channels can affect membrane potential, calcium homeostasis and insulin production. Hyperglycaemia, lipotoxicity, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation and advanced glycation can alter ion-channel function and lead to β-cell failure. Simi…

title: Cybersecurity governance in the western Balkans: NIS2 alignment, institutional capacity and critical infrastructure protection
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine cybersecurity governance in the Western Balkans through the combined lens of NIS2 alignment, institutional capacity and critical infrastructure protection. It treats cybersecurity as a regulatory and governance problem rather than as a purely technical domain. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a comparative exploratory regulatory case-study design covering Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia. The empirical basis is a document corpus composed of cybersecurity laws, national strategies, CSIRT/CERT institutional sources, critical infrastructure documents, EU enlargement reports, NIS2-related material and regional policy evidence. Findings The framework identifies a structured basis for comparing formal legal alignment with operational governance capacity. The most relevant differences concern institutional fragmentation, competent-authority design, incident-reporting arrangements, CSIRT/CERT maturity and the integration of cybersecurity into critical infrastructure protection. Practical implications The paper provides a policy-relevant framework for accession-oriented cybersecurity reforms, especially where legal transposition must be connected to enforcement, coordination and cross-border resilience. Originality/value The paper develops a comparative regulatory framework for analysing NIS2-a…

title: Targeted physical therapy for gouty arthritis: a first-principles frequency-screening study
abstract: Introduction Gouty arthritis is caused by the deposition of monosodium urate monohydrate (MSUM) crystals in joints. Current drug therapies are often limited by side effects, and invasive procedures carry associated risks. This study aims to provide a theoretical basis for local physical treatment of gout by identifying specific mid-infrared frequencies for irradiating MSUM crystals via photon-phonon resonant absorption. Methods The vibrational spectra of crystalline MSUM were simulated using first-principles density functional theory. The infrared and Raman peaks were mapped to their corresponding vibrational modes, and relative infrared activities were analyzed. The infrared spectrum of an anhydrous monosodium urate model (anhydrous MSU) was also calculated. Results Analysis of the vibrational spectra revealed infrared characteristic peaks at 1637 and 1696 cm - ¹ for MSUM and at 1627 and 1705 cm - ¹ for anhydrous MSU. This finding provides the theoretical foundation for scanning 1627–1705 cm - ¹ (48.78–51.11 THz) to resonantly excite the crystals. Discussion The irradiation of MSUM crystals with a mid-infrared laser near 50 THz is proposed for initial frequency-scanning experiments. A optical fiber placed near deeper deposits could shorten the distance traveled through tissue. However, experimental validation is required to determine suitable irradiation conditions and assess …

title: Editorial: The role of Light in the Regulation of Growth, Development, and Stress Tolerance in Plants
High-precision group refractive index measurement of static and mechanically perturbed liquids based on femtosecond frequency-comb dispersive interferometry
abstract: Abstract A femtosecond optical-frequency-comb-based dispersive interferometric method is proposed for high-precision bulk-liquid group refractive index measurement. Broadband spectral interferograms are transformed into the delay domain, where the target side peak is selected by window filtering. The single-pass-equivalent optical path difference is then extracted from the unwrapped spectral phase slope and converted into the liquid group refractive index using a calibrated quartz sample cell. The method was experimentally evaluated using a commercial ethanol–water mixture and aqueous NaCl solutions with concentrations from 2.5% to 15%. For the ethanol–water mixture, repeated measurements yielded a mean group refractive index of 1.354 61 with a standard deviation of 1.39 × 10 −4 RIU. For the NaCl solutions, the measured group refractive index increased from 1.374 70 to 1.388 92, with a fitted sensitivity of 1.106 17 × 10 −3 RIU/% and R 2 = 0.9902. The combined standard uncertainty was 4.56 × 10 −5 RIU for the ethanol–water mixture and 1.46 × 10 −5 –5.99 × 10 −5 RIU for the NaCl solutions. A preliminary vibration test from 180 to 260 Hz showed that the target delay-domain side peak remained distinguishable, indicating that OPD extraction remained feasible under low-frequency mechanical perturbation. The proposed method provides a non-scanning route for precise liquid group-index…

title: Open source digital sovereignty: the case for a Canadian national Linux distribution
abstract: Purpose The post-2020 global pivot toward digital sovereignty has been accelerated for Canada by a rupture in trust with the USA: 60% of Canadians report they can no longer trust the USA, while the Clarifying Lawful Overseas Use of Data Act and Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act §702 grant extraterritorial access to data held by the US-headquartered providers regardless of physical location. Despite this exposure, Canada’s federal government remains structurally dependent on a single US vendor for its foundational software stack: Microsoft Windows controls 58% of Canada’s desktop market, federal Microsoft contracts exceeded C$865m over 10 years and Windows-specific licensing alone is C$108m–C$126m/year. Operating systems remain absent from Canadian sovereignty debates dominated by cloud, AI and 5G. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the strategic autonomy and economic impact of a Canadian national Linux distribution. Design/methodology/approach This paper develops a comparative policy analysis of six state-sponsored Linux distributions (China, Russia, India, France, Germany and South Korea) using a dual total cost of ownership (TCO) + strategic autonomy analytical framework, benchmarked against Canada’s procurement landscape, laws and trade obligations. Findings Conservative net 10-year savings of C$350m–C$965m (net present value at 5% discount rate) are achievable, ca…

title: The ASCEND Project (2020-2023): Strengthening clinical trial ethics review and pharmacovigilance capacity in Tanzania mainland and Zanzibar
abstract: Background Clinical trials and related health research in sub-Saharan Africa continue to expand in volume and complexity, increasing the need for strong and responsive research ethics oversight, regulatory reviews, and pharmacovigilance systems. The ASCEND project was implemented in Tanzania Mainland and Zanzibar from November 2020 to December 2023 to support these functions through capacity development and system-strengthening activities. Objective To describe the implementation approach and documented outputs of the ASCEND project as a case study focusing on operational processes that may inform similar initiatives. Approach We compiled and synthesized project documentation produced during implementation, including training materials, activity reports, system development records, and consortium deliverables. We summarized implementation components and verified output counts across records. Outputs The project developed and delivered training packages for clinical trial protocol review and Good Clinical Practice inspection and trained 30 clinical trial protocol reviewers or assessors and 25 inspectors, including on-the-job inspection exposure for Zanzibar Food and Drug Authority staff. Assessors’ mean test scores rose from 61 to 80 out of 100. Nineteen early- and mid-career researchers and 50 trainers from institutional ethics committees were trained on research ethics and cli…

title: Strain Coupled (110)-Oriented Lithium Anodes for High-Rate and High-Capacity Epitaxial Growth
abstract: Abstract Lithium metal is considered as the ultimate anode for high-energy-density batteries, yet its practical realization is thwarted by dendrite proliferation and chemomechanical interfacial instability. While epitaxial growth on crystallographically textured substrates provides a template for ordered deposition, sustaining this ordered growth under high capacities and current densities remains a formidable kinetic challenge. Herein, we overcome this barrier by engineering an elastic (110)-oriented lithium anode (e-Li (110)) comprising a conductive polymer scaffold. The e-Li (110) integrates preferred (110) crystallographic orientation with a mechanically coupled strain corresponding to the optimized 4% tensile-strain condition. Consequently, this strain-engineering strategy enables a capacity of 30 mAh cm–2 and current density of 25 mA cm–2 before lithium epitaxial breakdown. 5.9 Ah Li || LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) pouch cells with a high energy density of 509.8 Wh kg–1 show 90% capacity retention after 140 cycles. In sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), e-Li (110) anode enables stable cycling for over 1600 cycles at a rate of 5 C. By highlighting strain as a critical parameter, our work provides a strategy for mechano-electrochemical coupling in lithium metal anodes for high-rate, high-energy-density batteries.

title: The relationship between disability and intrinsic capacity among older adults with disabilities in nursing institutions: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Introduction Intrinsic capacity was an important indicator of physical and mental function within the WHO healthy aging framework. Previous studies mainly examined IC decline and its relationship with disability and adverse health outcomes. However, whether IC could reflect functional differences among older adults with disabilities in nursing institutions remained unclear, particularly under the GB/T 42195-2022 Chinese National Disability Classification Standard. This study classified disability degree according to GB/T 42195-2022 and examined whether overall IC and its domains varied across disability degrees. From a public health and long-term care perspective, identifying impaired and preserved capacities could inform health management, reduce care dependence, and support quality of life and healthy aging. Methods From August to November 2023, 208 older adults with disabilities were recruited by convenience sampling from five nursing institutions in Jilin Province, China. We collected data through face-to-face interviews, the Integrated Care for Older People tool, the Mini-Mental State Examination, Short Physical Performance Battery, Mini Nutritional Assessment, World Health Organization-recommended visual acuity test, APP-based hearing test, and Patient Health Questionnaire-9. Spearman’s correlation and ordinal logistic regression examined associations. Results Intrinsic c…

title: How public leadership drives innovation: a conceptual model of intellectual capital and absorptive capacity
abstract: Purpose This study develops an integrated conceptual model explaining how distinct public leadership dimensions-transformational, ethical and knowledge-oriented leadership – collectively drive public service innovation (PSI) through the sequential mediating mechanisms of intellectual capital and absorptive capacity. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a conceptual approach, this paper synthesizes insights from the knowledge-based view (KBV), dynamic capabilities theory, and public sector leadership perspectives. A systematic analysis of contemporary literature is used to build a multi-layered framework and develop a comprehensive set of research propositions. Findings The model demonstrates that public leadership styles serve as strategic catalysts to foster intellectual capital. This enhanced knowledge resource subsequently triggers the development of absorptive capacity, which operates as the critical dynamic capability that transforms internal assets into public service innovation outcomes through both direct pathways and a sequential mediation mechanism. Research limitations/implications As a conceptual paper, this framework requires empirical validation. Future quantitative, qualitative, or mixed-method studies are encouraged to test these propositions across diverse public sector configurations and highly turbulent administrative environments. Practical implications The …

title: Higher-level functional capacity and incident long-term care insurance certification: a competing risks analysis
abstract: Background Higher-level functional capacity (HLFC) may capture functional vulnerability beyond basic activities of daily living in older adults. However, the association of baseline HLFC with subsequent incident long-term care insurance (LTCI) certification remains unclear when death is considered a competing event. Methods This prospective cohort study included 688 community-dwelling Japanese adults aged 65 years or older who participated in the 2017 wave of the Community Empowerment and Care for Well-being and Healthy Longevity Study. HLFC was assessed once at baseline using the Tokyo Metropolitan Institute of Gerontology Index of Competence (TMIG-IC), including the total score and the formal subdomain scores for Instrumental Self-Maintenance, Intellectual Activity, and Social Role. Participants were followed for 8 years. Incident LTCI certification at Support Level 1 or higher was analyzed using Fine–Gray competing-risk regression, with death before certification treated as a competing event. The fully adjusted Fine–Gray model included age group, sex, living arrangement, physical activity, smoking status, alcohol consumption, and disease status. Results Among 688 complete-case participants, 145 developed incident LTCI certification and 79 died before certification. In the fully adjusted model, higher HLFC total score was associated with a lower cumulative incidence of incide…

title: Utilization of High-Phosphorus Iron Ore in Steelmaking through Acid Leaching: Phosphorus Dissolution Behavior and Mechanism
abstract: The present study investigates the dephosphorization of high-phosphorus iron ores via chemical leaching methods. The collected iron ore contains 60.3 wt. % and 0.19 wt. % of iron and phosphorus (P), respectively, whereas XRD confirms the presence of hematite and goethite as the iron-bearing mineral phases. A comparative leaching study among the different mineral acids suggests in favour of H₂SO₄ for its lower iron loss and high P-removal capacity. Various leaching parameters were optimised for the highest P-removal, and the corresponding iron loss was noted. Under conditions such as leaching temperature 95°C, stirring speed 600rpm, time 60 min, 100ml 1M H₂SO₄, 20% solid (20g ore in 100ml solution); P-removal to the tune of 56% (0.084 wt.% P in the leached ore) with 0.30% iron loss was noticed. The acid recyclability experiments (20% solid) show the decrease of P-removal capacity from 56% to 51% and then sharply to 34% after the third phase leaching cycle. The FTIR studies reveal the disappearance of many major peaks and the sharp lowering of peak intensities at positions 468cm -1 and 546cm -1 , confirming the structural changes of leached iron ore. Agglomeration of the leached sample due to the formation of active surfaces in the presence of H₂SO₄ was marked by SEM images. The possible mechanism of dephosphorization is discussed using available literature and experimental resul…

title: The dimensions and realization mechanism of brand Jing-Jie(境界) initiated by brand ritual behaviours: a grounded analysis inspired by Chinese Zen Jing-Jie(境界) theory
abstract: Purpose This research seeks to explain the phenomenon of consumers' internal growth initiated by brand ritual behaviours, by establishing a novel construct “brand Jing-Jie(境界)”, inspired by Chinese Zen Jing-Jie(境界)theory. The connotation of “brand Jing-Jie(境界)” is a supplement and expansion of traditional brand loyalty. Design/methodology/approach The data collection is from 32 in-depth interviews. A grounded theory research was adopted for analysis. Findings Through exploring the realization mechanism by which brand ritual behaviours achieve brand Jing-Jie(境界), this paper explores the phenomenon of brand Jing-Jie(境界) and its three dimensions (oneness state, Zen Satori and self-realization). Specifically, brand ritual behaviours (metaphoricity, repeatability and emotionality) facilitate consumers to comprehend brand tacit knowledge (body learning, brand metaphor internalization and brand ritual meaning), thereby facilitating consumer meaning-making (meaning-confirmation, meaning-projection, meaning-expansion and meaning-negotiation), and ultimately achieving brand Jing-Jie(境界). Originality/value The findings propose a novel construct – brand Jing-Jie(境界), which achieves spiritual loyalty, transcends traditional brand loyalty and develops the consumer–brand relationship into a co-cultivation(共修) relationship. Meanwhile, it explores brand tacit knowledge that plays an important a…

title: Hemolytic mechanism and virulence of Antarctic psychrophilic Pseudomonas
abstract: Polar warming is expected to release and redistribute psychrophilic microorganisms, thereby increasing their likelihood of encountering warmer environments and potential hosts. However, it remains uncertain whether psychrophilic polar bacteria maintain pathogenic properties relevant to mammalian hosts during such transitions. Here, we investigated two hemolytic Antarctic Pseudomonas isolates, 3S6 and NS21, assigned to P. antarctica and P. yamanorum , respectively. Both isolates exhibited hemolytic activity, biofilm formation, and siderophore production, although these phenotypes were weaker than those of P. aeruginosa . Functional analyses indicated that their cell-associated hemolytic activity was dependent on the ExlBA two-partner secretion system (TPS), in which the outer-membrane transporter ExlB secretes the pore-forming cytotoxin ExlA: deletion of exlB abolished hemolysis, whereas genetic complementation restored this phenotype, and this activity was temperature-sensitive, consistent with repression of ExlBA expression under elevated temperatures. Temperature elevation from 20 °C to 28 °C reduced hemolytic activity, exlBA transcription, and intracellular cAMP levels, while strongly inducing cpdA , implicating a CpdA-cAMP/Vfr-associated regulatory mechanism. Elevated temperature also triggered a transition from a motile to a biofilm-associated lifestyle in strain 3S6, pote…

title: From leadership and accountability to innovation and learning: culture-climate as a mediating mechanism
abstract: Purpose This study examines how leadership and accountability support innovation and learning in a public organization undergoing restructuring. It argues that formal direction and responsibility become adaptive outcomes only when translated into a supportive culture-climate mechanism. Design/methodology/approach The study used cross-sectional survey data from 2,770 employees in a large Indonesian public organization undergoing restructuring. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings Culture-climate had the strongest direct effect on innovation and learning (β = 0.410, p < 0.001). Accountability strongly shaped culture-climate (β = 0.718, p < 0.001) and directly influenced innovation and learning (β = 0.360, p < 0.001). Leadership also had significant direct and indirect effects, although smaller in magnitude. The model explained 72.6% of the variance in innovation and learning Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional, single-organization and perception-based design limits causal and generalization claims. Practical implications Managers should treat restructuring as a disciplined learning process: clarify roles, create psychological safety, invite bottom-up ideas and monitor whether change moves beyond compliance into embedded new routines. Originality/value The paper advances public-sector organizational le…

title: Screening Mechanism for Tuberculosis among Diabetic Individuals: Health Care Providers’ Perspective: A Qualitative Study
abstract: Introduction: Tuberculosis (TB) and diabetes mellitus (DM) frequently coexist, with diabetes increasing the risk of active TB two- to three-fold and adversely affecting TB treatment outcomes. Bidirectional screening between NTEP & NP-NCD has been introduced to enable early detection, but implementation at the primary health-care level remains inconsistent due to operational, infrastructural, and awareness-related barriers. Methodology: Qualitative data were obtained through in-depth interviews with health care workers at the study Primary Health Centres (PHCs), exploring the tuberculosis screening mechanism followed for diabetic individuals and the barriers encountered during screening. Fifteen health care workers were interviewed to understand the screening mechanism and the difficulties involved. Results: Four themes emerged from the analysis: the screening mechanism, barriers encountered during the screening process, patients’ knowledge, and measures needed to improve screening. Conclusion: Tuberculosis screening among diabetic individuals at the primary care level relies heavily on field workers (ASHAs and ANMs) and PHC staff, and is constrained chiefly by staffing and laboratory gaps, patient non-cooperation, and limited community awareness of the TB–diabetes link. Strengthening laboratory support, appointing dedicated NTEP field staff, and sustained health education are l…

title: Mechanism and parameter optimization method for ordered vibration conveying of maize ears
Insertion into Donor–Acceptor Cyclopropanes with Carbon–Sulfur Moieties Derived from Sulfoxonium Ylides and Elemental Sulfur
abstract: Abstract The (3 + 2) cycloaddition of donor–acceptor cyclopropanes (DACs) with carbon–sulfur 2π components has become an emerging method to rapidly assemble tetrahydrothiophenes. Starting materials donating the carbon–sulfur unit are often isolated from thionation of carbonyls or carboxylic acid derivatives. Herein we report a method for the cycloaddition of DACs with carbon–sulfur moieties presumably formed in situ via β-sulfuration of α-carbonyl sulfoxonium ylides with elemental sulfur. The insertion occurred without the assistance of Lewis acid, perhaps due to the strongly polarized carbon–sulfur-containing intermediate. The hitherto challenging α-monosubstituted tetrahydrothiophenes were obtained with a wide range of tolerated functionalities.

title: Dynamical Drexhage Effect: Amplified Emission in Time-Varying Electromagnetic Environments
abstract: Abstract We investigate the effect of nonrelativistic motion on the emission dynamics of a dipole emitter moving next to a reflective interface. Within the macroscopic quantum electrodynamics formalism, we obtain an equation of motion for the dipole amplitude in terms of a general dyadic Green’s function. We then focus on the dynamical Drexhage effect, where, at short dipole–surface distances, the dipole behaves as a parametric oscillator featuring time-dependent damping and Lamb shifts, both arising from position modulation. Importantly, sinusoidal trajectories with specific modulation amplitudes and frequencies lead to the parametric amplification of the dipole amplitude and radiation. A perturbative Mathieu equation model yields permittivity-dependent amplification thresholds, while Floquet analysis reveals the key role of the dynamical Lamb shift and the absence of amplification for certain epsilon-near-zero materials, regardless of the amplitude of modulation. Our findings open avenues for the dynamic control of the light–matter interaction in nanophotonic environments.

Adsorptive desulfurization of liquid fuels using porous carbon framework
abstract: The increasing demand for clean transportation fuel has gained significant importance because of serious health and environment consequences. As per the government Bharat Stage Emission Standards, the permissible limit of inherited sulfur containing compounds in BS-VI diesel should be 10 ppm. Likewise, several desulfurization techniques used for removing or eliminating sulfur content, among which adsorptive desulfurization emerging as an alternative approach to ultra-deep hydrodesulfurization in terms of environmental and economical cleaning purposes. Accordingly, in the present work, a solid hydrocarbon, named Gilsonite, a naturally occurring, lightweight organic material, originated from the solidification of petroleum, has been explored for developing a porous functionalized carbon framework (FCF) to capture aromatic sulfur compound preferably benzothiophene (BTH). The prepared FCF has been characterized by surface morphology, crystalline phases, and textural characteristics. The desulfurization performance of FCF has been studied in n-heptane model fuel blended with BTH and further in diesel fuel (BS-IV standards). The results have shown the desulfurization efficiency of almost 96% at ambient conditions, highlighting the effect of active functional sites on FCF matrix. The present study has demonstrated the waste to carbon features, supporting the sustainable development in…

title: Metal-Free Carbon with Synergistic Enrichment Catalysis for Rapid Removal of Antibiotics
abstract: Abstract A freeze-drying-assisted pyrolysis strategy was used to prepare nitrogen-doped porous carbon (FNC800) from glucose and dicyandiamide (600–900 °C). FNC800 possessed hierarchical porosity (specific surface area 747.36 m2 g–1) and pyridinic-N sites. After 30 min adsorption–desorption equilibration, FNC800 removed 76.83% of tetracycline hydrochloride (TCH). Subsequent addition of peroxymonosulfate (PMS) produced near-complete attenuation of dissolved TCH within 1 min (apparent rate constant k = 3.49 min–1) with 57.74% total organic carbon (TOC) removal. Radical quenching, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and electrochemical measurements indicated a predominantly nonradical pathway in which singlet oxygen (1O2) was the principal oxidant, with secondary contributions from superoxide (O2•–) and interfacial electron transfer. High TCH removal was maintained at pH 1–11 and declined to ∼30% at pH 14; common inorganic anions caused limited inhibition, whereas humic acid reduced adsorption. Removal decreased from 100 to 90.4% over five cycles. These results show that metal-free porous carbon can couple pollutant enrichment with rapid PMS activation for antibiotic remediation.

title: Electrostatic Attraction of Cationic Carbon Quantum Dots Regulates Palladium Nanocrystal Distribution for Enhanced Ethanol Oxidation
abstract: Abstract Cationic carbon quantum dots (CQD) produced by thermal polymerization of citric acid with an ionic liquid exhibit a unique synergy of electrostatic anchoring, hydrogen-bond enrichment, and electronic modulation. In this study, the electrostatic attraction between cationic CQD and the chloropalladate precursor is exploited to significantly enhance the dispersion and density of palladium nanocrystals (Pd NCs). Meanwhile, the functional groups and defect sites on the CQD establish strong metal-support interactions with the Pd NCs, which modulate the electronic state of Pd, weaken the adsorption of toxic intermediates generated during ethanol oxidation reaction (EOR), thereby enhancing the anti-poisoning ability and durability of the catalyst. Furthermore, the oxygen- and nitrogen-containing functional groups on the CQD can form strong hydrogen bonds with ethanol molecules and the reduced graphene oxide (RGO) support, enriching ethanol molecules on the catalyst surface and creating a unique reaction microenvironment that facilitates the EOR. By synergistically modulating electrostatic attraction and the microenvironment, the obtained catalyst (Pd/CQD-RGO) is strategically designed in this work, which exhibits outstanding anti-poisoning capability and catalytic performance (3234.3 mA mg–1, 8.1 mA cm–2) in the EOR, providing a theoretical basis and practical reference for th…

title: Plant functional type composition drives summer carbon cycling in an ombrotrophic peatland
abstract: Abstract Peatlands are globally important carbon sinks because plant CO 2 uptake outweighs microbial decomposition. These ecosystems are characterised by a distinct microtopography of hummocks and lawns, supporting vegetation communities composed of various plant functional types (PFTs). In this study we assess the direct effects of PFT removal and microhabitats, and the indirect effects mediated through microbial community composition on CO 2 and CH 4 emissions. We utilised a long-term factorial vascular plant removal experiment in a Sphagnum -dominated peatland in southern Sweden. We used structural equation modelling (SEM) to analyse gas flux measurements and microbial community composition, and to assess both direct and mediated effects. Plots with intact vegetation exhibited the lowest CO 2 emissions, which increased progressively with ericoid, graminoid, and both ericoid and graminoid removal. Microhabitat type influenced microbial community structure, and only the removal of all vascular plants affected bacterial composition. However, neither CO 2 nor CH 4 fluxes were shown to be mediated by microbial community composition; instead, CH 4 emissions were directly shaped by microhabitat, with higher fluxes in lawns than hummocks. These results likely reflect the timing of sampling (August), when plant-driven CO 2 uptake dominates carbon cycling dynamics, and the limited sam…

title: Discovery of thermal radio recombination line emission towards the high-mass protostar IRAS18162-2048
abstract: The physical conditions within the innermost few tens of astronomical units of high-mass protostars (M_*>8 M_⊙) remain largely unexplored. At these scales, ionised emission can trace photoionised gas, accretion disks, or the base of protostellar jets. We search for ionised emission in the form of radio recombination lines (RRLs) in high-mass star-forming regions. We used archival data from the Atacama Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) interferometer in band 6 (∼1.3 mm) with a resolution of þeta_ to examine the high-mass protostar IRAS18162-2048, the driving source of the Herbig-Haro (HH) objects HH80-81. beam mas mas We detect, for the first time in this protostar, the thermal emission of the RRL H30α (mathrm rest frequency =231.90093 GHz). The ionised emission is spatially unresolved in our observations, but we estimate an emitting region of łesssim50 au at the source distance of 1.4 kpc. The H30α line profile is broad and spectrally resolved with a local standard of rest velocity of ∼-14 (i.e. ∼-26 blueshifted with respect to the systemic velocity of the cloud) and a full width at half maximum of sim82 . These observations suggest that the H30α line is tracing outflowing blueshifted material in the well-known radio jet from this object. This detection opens the possibility of detailed studies of the kinematics and physical properties of ionised jets. km s^ -1 km s^ -1 km …

title: LED Photoactive Antibacterial Carbon Nanomaterial Surfaces
abstract: Abstract Carbon-based nanomaterials are potentially antimicrobial in water treatment, healthcare, and environmental applications. The antibacterial properties of various carbon nanomaterial surfaces have been investigated; however, studies including direct comparisons between carbon nanomaterials with different morphology, chemistry, and wettability are few. Moreover, photoenhanced surface antibacterial activity is not fully understood. Here, we show that simple light-emitting diodes (LEDs) can enhance the antibacterial surface activity of three carbon nanomaterials with diverse surface morphologies, including laser-induced graphene (LIG), vertically aligned carbon nanotubes (VACNT), and carbon nanofibers (CNF). After 40 min of exposure to low-energy LED light, VACNTs showed the highest bacterial killing activity (93.4%), followed by CNFs (72.5%) and then LIG surfaces (69.0%). Moreover, when hydrophilicity was increased using atmospheric plasma treatment, the LED-activated antibacterial activity of all surfaces was further enhanced, with only 20 min of LED exposure resulted in 99.1%, 92.6%, and 46.1% bacterial killing efficacies for CNF, VACNT, and LIG surfaces, respectively. The LED treatment was the predominant activator of cell toxicity, resulting in reactive oxygen species and bacterial membrane permeability, although morphological factors were also seen, including an incre…

title: Proactive Carbon Management in Asian Manufacturing SMEs: Insights from a Dual-Driver Case Study in Taiwan
abstract: This study examines why resource-constrained Asian manufacturing SMEs initiate proactive carbon management before direct regulatory enforcement and how internal strategic intent interacts with external institutional pressures. A qualitative-dominant mixed-methods case study of an export-oriented Taiwanese powder metallurgy SME combines a 2024 ISO 14064-1:2018 organizational greenhouse gas inventory with three semi-structured executive interviews. Managerial assessment preceded domestic enforcement, while customer ESG requirements, evolving carbon policy, and ISO 14064-1 provided legitimacy and an operational framework. Total 2024 emissions were 3,074.026 tCO₂e, with Scope 2 accounting for 87.40%, making energy efficiency and renewable energy the priorities of a three-phase decarbonization pathway. Interviews identified inconsistent regulatory guidance, limited supplier support, and regulatory knowledge gaps. Integrating the natural resource-based view and institutional theory, the dual-driver model shows that proactive strategic intent initiates carbon action, while institutional frameworks enable systematic and legitimate implementation. The findings qualify portrayals of Asian SMEs as passive compliance seekers, demonstrate the value of triangulating standardized inventory and managerial evidence, and identify potential spillover implications across firm, industry, and societ…

title: Engineering carbon nanotubes-polydimethylsiloxane strain sensors for wearable respiratory monitoring
abstract: Abstract Body movements occur naturally during chest or abdominal motion associated with breathing, providing an accessible physiological signal for non-invasive monitoring of various health conditions. However, developing soft, conformable sensors that can reliably transduce these low-strain deformations into stable electrical signals remains a key challenge. In this work, a flexible and stretchable strain sensor was developed by coating a conductive carbon nanotube (CNT) network onto a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) elastomer, enabling respiration monitoring through strain-induced changes in electrical resistance. Key fabrication parameters, including deposition method, sensing layer thickness, and the ratio of CNTs to a dispersing agent, were systematically optimized to enhance sensitivity and signal stability upon mechanical deformation. The optimized sensor exhibits rapid response and recovery time under cyclic loading conditions, enabling accurate capture of dynamic respiratory signals. The device also demonstrates stable and reproducible electrical output over repeated deformation cycles, indicating good durability for wearable applications. The sensor also shows high sensitivity in the low-strain region, which is particularly advantageous for detecting subtle physiological motions associated with breathing. This work highlights the potential of CNT–PDMS composite sensors a…

title: Digital decoupling: UK aviation productivity and carbon trends vs OECD (2010–2025)
abstract: Purpose This study evaluates the global aviation sector's transition toward sustainability by examining the relationship between Revenue Passenger Kilometers (RPK), carbon dioxide (CO}_2) intensity and Air Traffic Management (ATM) efficiency across all 38 Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) member countries. The research aims to determine the extent of structural decoupling within the industry over the 2010–2025 period. Design/methodology/approach The research utilizes Translog Stochastic Frontier Analysis (SFA), panel regression analysis, dynamic Panel Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) and UK ARDL modeling on a balanced panel of all 38 OECD member countries (N = 38, T = 16, yielding 608 country-year observations) covering 2010–2025. The methodology focuses on isolating the drivers of emissions versus the impact of technological and operational interventions. Findings The results identify a significant structural decoupling. While traffic volume remains the primary driver of fuel burn (0.029), carbon intensity has plummeted, showing a −0.98 correlation over time. Fleet modernization is the strongest decarbonization engine (0.98 correlation), while ATM improvements act as a significant countervailing force (−0.125) against emissions. However, 41% of annual fuel burn remains tied to previous operational baselines, reflecting substantial infrastructure …
venue: Management of Environmental Quality: An International Journal

title: Current State of Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage Technologies
abstract: Addressing climate change requires significant efforts toward decarbonization. This review provides a comprehensive technical, economic, and policy assessment of 239 carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) technologies. Categorizing pathways by application and physicochemical processes, we evaluate technological maturity using Technology Readiness Levels and economic viability via capture costs and the impact of capture on product price. Findings indicate that CCUS technologies are heterogeneous; most currently remain immature and face prohibitive costs, trapping private capital in a wait-and-see dynamic driven by severe risk premiums and externalities. To overcome these market failures, we advocate for a hybrid public-private framework: utilizing early-stage public funding to derisk development and catalyze learning-by-doing, subsequently transitioning to robust carbon pricing mechanisms. Furthermore, we highlight the critical role of international coordination in resolving systemic challenges associated with global externalities, spatial heterogeneity, and the fragmentation of markets, supply chains, and regulatory regimes.

Soil organic carbon storage across Mediterranean mountain forests: a comparative assessment of forest ecosystem diversity and geological substrate in Ifrane and Talassemtane National Parks, Morocco
abstract: Soil organic carbon (SOC) stored in forest ecosystems represents one of the largest terrestrial carbon reservoirs and plays a crucial role in climate change mitigation and ecosystem functioning. In Mediterranean mountain regions, SOC storage is characterized by pronounced spatial variability resulting from the combined influence of vegetation, climate, topography, parent material and soil-forming processes. Although numerous studies have examined the influence of dominant tree species on SOC accumulation, comparatively few have investigated how the diversity of forest ecosystems interacts with geological substrate to regulate soil carbon storage across heterogeneous protected landscapes. This study evaluates the combined effects of forest ecosystem diversity and geological substrate on SOC storage by comparing two major Moroccan Mediterranean protected areas: Ifrane National Park, located in the Middle Atlas Mountains, and Talassemtane National Park, located in the Rif Mountains. A harmonized dataset comprising 67 observations was assembled from independent field inventories. In Ifrane, the sampled ecosystems were distributed over basaltic and dolomitic substrates, whereas all Talassemtane sites developed on calcareous formations. SOC stocks differed markedly between the two national parks. Mean SOC stock reached 173.99 t C ha - ¹ in Ifrane compared with 69.44 t C ha - ¹ in Tal…

title: Ventriculo-arterial coupling in acute heart failure: prognostic and therapeutic insights - a systematic review and meta-analysis of multivariable-adjusted data
abstract: Abstract In acute heart failure (AHF), non-invasive ventricular-arterial coupling (VAC) surrogates, including right ventricular-pulmonary arterial (RV-PA) and left ventricular-arterial (LV-Ao) coupling, have emerged as practical bedside indices, but their prognostic significance remains largely unknown systematically. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the prognostic significance of non-invasive VAC assessment, in patients hospitalized with AHF. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, HF hospitalization, length of hospital stay, use of therapies, the composite of all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization, and in-hospital adverse cardiovascular events. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and odds ratios (aORs) were pooled using random-effects. Subgroup-analyses were performed according to follow-up duration and left ventricular ejection fraction. Thirty-six studies comprising 36,989 patients were analysed. Twenty-eight studies evaluated RV-PA coupling, predominantly the TAPSE/PASP ratio, and eight evaluated LV-Ao coupling, mainly using non-invasive Ea/Ees estimates. RV-PA uncoupling was independently associated with increased all-cause mortality (aHR 1.90; 95% CI 1.42–2.56; I²=49%), with consistent associations at 12 months (aHR 2.03; 95% CI 1.44–2.85) and long-term follow-up (aHR 1.67; 95% CI 1.06–2.64). Associations with HF hospitalization, hospital stay,…

title: Tunable graphene-integrated metasurface biosensor with hybrid plasmonic-2D material coupling for dual cancer detection in terahertz regime
abstract: Abstract This study presents a vertically integrated terahertz metasurface biosensor that combines graphene with transition metal dichalcogenides for breast and colorectal cancer detection based on refractive index sensing. The resonant region uses a clustered cross geometry composed of four hollow circular rings and four solid circular resonators linked by orthogonal MoS2-coated rectangular strips on a graphene layer. Selected regions are coated with silver, gold, and copper, along with WS 2 , WSe 2 , and MoSe 2 , to control the electromagnetic response over 0.19 to 0.72 THz. Simulated absorption exceeds 98%. Resonance frequency tuning is accomplished by varying the graphene chemical potential between 0.1 and 0.9 eV and modifying the structure’s geometric parameters. For breast cancer detection, the sensor exhibits a sensitivity of 1000 GHz per RIU over refractive indices ranging from 1.385 to 1.401 RIU. Comparable sensitivity is observed for colorectal cancer detection within the 1.329 to 1.348 RIU range. The reported quality factors span from 1.5 to 1.63, yielding figures of merit up to 6.45 RIU⁻¹ and a minimum detection limit of 0.365. A Random Forest regression model predicts the sensor’s response under variations in incident angle and resonator geometry, achieving $$\:{R}^{2}>0.9996$$ and a root mean squared error below 0.003 across the evaluated dataset. Electric field s…

title: Molecular Connectivity Controls Electronic Coupling and Charge-Transfer Dynamics at Anthracene–MoS2 Interfaces
abstract: Abstract Controlling interfacial charge-transfer (CT) interactions is a central challenge in two-dimensional (2D) organic–inorganic hybrid materials. Here, we show that molecular connectivity strongly governs excited-state evolution at a 2D heterointerface using anthracene (An) donors covalently attached to few-layer MoS2 nanosheets through an N-benzylsuccinimide linker at either the 2- or 9-position, generating two constitutional isomers, MoS2-2-An and MoS2-9-An. Ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy reveals markedly different photodynamics that depend strongly on the donor attachment position. Photoexcitation of MoS2-2-An produces a long-lived interfacial CT excited state, whereas MoS2-9-An undergoes rapid formation of a full charge-separated state. The contrasting behavior is consistent with connectivity-controlled differences in donor orientation at the interface, which modulate orbital overlap and electronic coupling and may influence structural reorganization. Theoretical calculations further support that the more coplanar geometry of 2-An, exhibiting a calculated tilt angle (θ) of 29.5° relative to the MoS2 basal plane, enhances electronic coupling and stabilizes an intermediately coupled CT state, whereas the more upright 9-An orientation (θ = 42.1°) weakens orbital mixing and favors direct charge separation. These findings demonstrate that constitutional connecti…

title: From statutory mandate to institutional integration: lessons from the national survey of Israel’s healthcare ethics committees
abstract: Abstract Background Israel’s Patients’ Rights Act (IPRA, 1996) established a unique statutory model for ethics committees (ECs), with legally binding authority, differing from the advisory nature of ECs in most countries. Following the 2015 State Comptroller’s report highlighting widespread under-implementation, the Ministry of Health (MOH) issued a directive in 2018 aimed at standardizing EC structure, procedures, and training. However, the extent of subsequent implementation and operational activity has remained unclear. Methods This secondary analysis of the 2022‑2023 MOH national survey examined EC structure, governance, training, and activity in 52 institutions (response rate: 71%), including general, geriatric/rehabilitation, and psychiatric hospitals, MOH district bureaus, health maintenance organizations (HMOs), and the Israel Defense Forces (IDF). Institutional characteristics were merged from MOH administrative databases and compared with available 2015 baseline data. Logistic regression and Generalized Estimating Equation (GEE) models were used to identify factors associated with low EC activity. Low EC activity was defined as a committee that reported both one or fewer (≤ 1) meetings AND one or fewer (≤ 1) applications per year. Conversely, committees reporting more than one meeting or more than one application annually were classified as having high activity for th…

title: Modified ITO/PANI Electrodes as Energy Storage Materials: Influence of Electrodeposition Time on Morphological, Optical and Electrochemical Properties for Aniline Optimum Concentration
abstract: In this work, we improved the non-faradic properties of ITO electrodes modified by polyaniline films (PANI) deposited electrochemically by chronoamperometry for electrical energy storage. Cyclic voltamperometry, galvanostatic charge-discharge and impedancemetry measurements were performed on the obtained PANI/ITO electrode. Morphological analysis was curried on SEM images. A strong correlation was established between the quantified surface morphology and the electrochemical properties. Non-faradaic phenomena have been studied through CV scanning rate. The capacitive character of the modified electrode is extracted from the modeling of the EIS data of the interface by an equivalent electrical circuit, whose CPE elements were used to track the evolution of such character for an appropriate concentration of aniline in an electrolytic solution of H2SO4 and for different electrodeposition times. The highest capacitive performance was obtained for 0.5 M aniline concentration and 900 seconds deposition time.

Integrating macro- and meso-level perspectives on school nutrition programs in Dubai: a joint display mixed methods integration study
abstract: Background School Nutrition Programs (SNPs) are increasingly recognized as essential public health interventions that influence children's health, educational attainment, wellbeing, and future non-communicable disease risk. While previous studies in Dubai explored stakeholders' macro-level perceptions regarding the upscaling of SNPs and quantitatively characterized SNPs implementation across schools, the integrated understanding of how policy-level aspirations align with school-level realities remains limited. Generating such an integrated understanding is essential for informing implementation strategies that are effective, efficient, equitable, and contextually responsive. Objective This study aimed to integrate the primary inferences generated from two complementary studies investigating SNPs in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Methods This study represents the third integrative phase of a multi-staged mixed methods research program. The first study qualitatively explored perceptions of key opinion leaders involved in planning, implementation, and evaluation of SNPs in Dubai. The second study quantitatively examined the status quo and characteristics of SNPs across public and private schools in Dubai. In the current study, findings from both studies were merged through a structured joint display analysis process informed by mixed methods integration approaches. Primary inference…

title: Parasitism induces negative effects of clonal integration in the invasive plant Sphagneticola trilobata regardless of nutrient heterogeneity
abstract: Introduction Clonal integration typically enhances the fitness of clonal plants in heterogeneous resource environments, whereas it reduces fitness under parasitic stress. However, it remains unclear whether parasitic stress interacts with nutrient heterogeneity to affect the ecological effects of clonal integration. Methods We conducted a greenhouse pot experiment using the invasive clonal plant Sphagneticola trilobata , with or without one ramet parasitized by Cuscuta chinensis , and with or without severing the connection (allowing or preventing integration), under heterogeneous or homogeneous nutrient supply, combined with 15 N tracing. Results and discussion Our results showed that (1) compared with the severed treatment, the connection treatment significantly increased C. chinensis biomass and markedly decreased the biomass of connected but unparasitized ramets, but did not affect the biomass of directly parasitized ramets, ultimately leading to a significant decrease in the total biomass of clonal fragments of S. trilobata ; (2) heterogeneous nutrient supply significantly intensified the detrimental effect of C. chinensis on parasitized ramets, but did not significantly affect connected unparasitized ramets; and (3) neither nutrient heterogeneity nor parasitism by C. chinensis affected the amount of 15 N translocated among ramets. Collectively, these findings indicate tha…

title: Fabrication and Lithium Storage Performance of Trigonal W2N Thin-Film Anode
abstract: Abstract The preparation, characterization of materials, and electrochemical performance of trigonal W2N thin film as the anode material for lithium-ion batteries have been reported. The trigonal W2N thin film with the space group of P3̅ was synthesized by the sputtering deposition followed by a nitridation treatment. The first-principles calculations reveal that the adsorption energy of Li+ on the (001) crystal plane of trigonal W2N is −1.55 eV and the Li+ diffusion energy barrier is only 0.23 eV, indicating a significant kinetic superiority for rapid Li+ transport. The results of electrochemical tests demonstrate that the trigonal W2N thin-film electrode maintains a stable specific capacity of 700 mA h g–1 at the current density of 0.1 A g–1 after 100 cycles. Even at the current density of 1 A g–1, the specific capacity is initially decreased but subsequently rebounded, finally retaining that at 680 mA h g–1 after 300 cycles. The results of cyclic voltammetry and ex situ XPS analyses confirm that the lithium storage mechanism involves Li+ intercalation/deintercalation and a reversible conversion reaction. Owing to its high specific capacity, good cycling stability, and superior rate performance, the trigonal W2N thin-film electrode offers a promising research direction for high-performance anode materials of thin-film lithium-ion batteries in the future.

title: Centrifuge and numerical modelling of the thermomechanical behaviour of energy cantilever walls in sand
abstract: Energy diaphragm walls are a form of energy geostructure that have been demonstrated to have high heat exchange efficiency. The thermomechanical behaviour of energy walls subjected to thermal cycles has been studied mainly through numerical modelling over the past decade, yet quality data are severely lacking to validate the models to further understand the soil–wall interaction. In this study, centrifuge model tests were conducted to investigate the thermally induced structural responses of an energy cantilever wall embedded in a uniform sand bed of different densities, accompanied by numerical back-analysis. A transient peak in wall moment was identified during each heating–cooling cycle. This phenomenon occurred prior to reaching a steady-state thermal equilibrium due to the delayed responses of soil at a distance before the heating and cooling front arrived. This transient moment can be 7–16% higher than the steady-state value in each cycle, highlighting the importance of capturing the transient responses for safe wall design against the ultimate limit state. Significant ground surface total and differential settlement were induced by the thermal cycles, mainly within 2 times the excavation depth away from the wall. The cumulative settlement could exceed the serviceability limit state threshold for any foundation being built right behind the wall.

title: Dehydrogenation of 1-Methyldecalin as a Liquid Organic Hydrogen Carrier: Effect of Isomer Composition on Catalyst Performance and Stability
abstract: Abstract Liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHCs) represent a safe and cost-effective resource for hydrogen storage due to reversible hydrogenation/dehydrogenation cycles. Although scarcely studied, the 1-methylnaphthalene/1-methyldecalin (1-MN/1-MD) pair could be an attractive LOHC due to its physical properties and because it can be obtained from waste streams of the carbochemical industry. However, 1-MD dehydrogenation is strongly affected by its stereoisomeric composition, as cis- and trans-isomers exhibit different reactivities and can undergo concurrent isomerization. In this work, the influence of individual 1-MD stereoisomers on dehydrogenation performance was systematically investigated using two feeds enriched in either cis- or trans-isomers. Pd- and Pt-based catalysts supported on alumina and activated carbon were evaluated, and the effect of temperature (250–400 °C) was studied over the most active catalyst, Pt/Al2O3. Based on the experimental data, we hypothesized that trans-isomers promoted catalyst deactivation and coke formation, whereas cis-isomers enhanced dehydrogenation activity. This effect is also believed to influence the formation of intermediate products. Specifically, 1-methyltetralin, which is generated mainly from cis-isomers, readily dehydrogenates to 1-methylnaphthalene (1-MN), whereas 5-methyltetralin, formed preferentially from trans-isomers, app…

title: Energy Justice Amid the Transition: The Role of the Humanities in Fostering Environmental Awareness and Equitable Benefits
abstract: Indonesia’s energy transition involves social, cultural, and ethical challenges alongside technical change. Despite relatively high public awareness of environmental issues and climate change, a gap persists between awareness and action supporting the transition. This study examined the role of the humanities, encompassing narrative, cultural representation, ethical awareness, and public participation, in fostering environmental concern and promoting equitable benefit distribution. A descriptive qualitative approach combined literature review and content analysis of scholarly journal articles, books, government policy documents, and interview data from relevant informants. Four principal themes emerged: the disparity between societal values and actions; the role of local narratives and cultural values in cultivating environmental concern; limited inclusivity in community participation in renewable energy projects; and the need for more equitable energy policies. These findings frame the energy transition as a social process in which humanities perspectives can help connect technical policies with communities’ social realities. The study highlights the importance of culturally grounded environmental engagement, inclusive participation, and attention to equity in transition governance. It contributes to the development of a conceptual framework integrating the humanities into ene…

Exploring the impact of solar community projects for remote communities in Indonesia
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the impact of the solar community projects (SCP) on households in remote areas in Indonesia. Design/methodology/approach This study used a mixed-methods approach, combining a household survey with in-depth interviews. A total of 219 households were selected through purposive sampling across three remote communities in East Kalimantan, Indonesia. In addition, 19 key informants, including community members, local business owners, community leaders, government officials and energy experts, were interviewed. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and a paired-samples t-test to compare conditions before and after SCP implementation, while qualitative data were analyzed thematically to contextualize and enrich the quantitative findings. Findings SCP implementation is associated with perceived improvements in household income, lower electricity expenditures and increased electricity use, particularly during nighttime hours. Beneficiary communities have also experienced broader benefits, including the vital role of electricity in supporting socio-economic activities, improved access to electricity, greater adoption of electronic devices and increased productivity. Research limitations/implications This study was conducted in several remote areas where the findings may not represent other remote areas across Indonesia. The involve…

title: Cultural integration through the worship of the Hùng Kings: the case of the Tày at Pịt Temple in Vietnam
abstract: Purpose Based on a field survey and interviews with several Tày people in Bảo Yên, Lào Cai in 2020, together with relevant literature, this article aims to examine how the Tày community at Pịt Temple has adopted and reinterpreted the worship of the Hùng Kings. By doing so, it seeks to elucidate the dynamics of acculturation between ethnic minorities and the majority Việt, as well as to assess the cultural implications of the Vietnamese government's policies on cultural management and development in ethnic minority areas. Design/methodology/approach This study employs a qualitative research design grounded in ethnographic fieldwork. Data were collected through field surveys and semi-structured interviews with members of the Tày community at Pịt Temple in Bảo Yên, Lào Cai, conducted in 2020. In addition, relevant academic literature and policy documents were analyzed to contextualize local religious practices. The study adopts an interpretive approach to examine processes of cultural acculturation between ethnic minorities and the majority Việt within the framework of state cultural management and development policies. Findings The study finds that the worship of the Hùng Kings at Pịt Temple reflects a synchronization of cultural beliefs between the Tày and the majority Việt. This convergence results from both the Tày community's adaptive practices and the Vietnamese government's…

How Policy Design Affects Perceptions of Beneficiaries and Support for Welfare
abstract: Abstract Most of the public supports welfare policies in the abstract, but many hold deep misgivings about the deservingness of welfare recipients, driving down support for specific policies. Welfare policies are often designed to mitigate these concerns by restricting access to benefits, but it is unclear to what effect. According to an influential strain of research drawing on social construction theory, these restrictions may backfire, instead increasing concerns about a free-riding public. In contrast -- drawing on psychological research on the deservingness heuristic -- I argue that policy features, such as work requirements, signal effort on behalf of recipients and thus deservingness. Using an experiment, I find that several policy features increase perceptions of deservingness and, in turn, increase policy support and generosity. However, some policy features are also perceived as overly burdensome, reducing the effects on policy support. Treatment effects on perceptions of beneficiary deservingness are largest among ambivalent respondents, but largely generalize across partisanship, ideology, and racial resentment. Overall, these findings help clarify the implications of the deservingness heuristic while challenging predictions from social construction theory and informing ongoing debates over public opinion and policy feedback.

title: Fermented Sargassum-Based Seafood Rice Seasoning: Prototype Development and Mix Design Optimization
abstract: Direct incorporation of brown-seaweed biomass into foods is limited by its fibrous texture and by the challenge of retaining desirable marine and umami notes without an excessive fishy odor. This study evaluated whether fermented commercial Sargassum spp . biomass could be incorporated into a dry seafood seasoning for rice and whether a constrained mix design could identify a formulation with high preliminary hedonic acceptability.Commercial dried Sargassum spp . biomass was rehydrated for 6 h, washed, pretreated with 1.5% sodium bicarbonate at 90–100°C for 2 h, reduced to 1–2-mm fragments, and fermented with a mixed lactic starter containing Companilactobacillus farciminis and Lactiplantibacillus pentosus . The fermentation involving 2.15% starter culture and 5.0% sugar lasted for 86 h at 30°C. The methods of hot-air, low-temperature, and freeze drying were compared using moisture content and handl- ing attributes. Seven variable ingredients were optimized within predefined ranges in an 18-run constrained mix design comprising 15 unique formulations. The response was the mean overall hedonic score for each run, based on evaluations by 30 assessors on a nine-point scale.The fermented biomass had a pH of 4.56 ± 0.05. The freeze-drying processing at −50 ± 2°C for 40 h yielded material with 4.51 ± 0.20% moisture and a crisp, loose, non-clumped structure. It was selected on the bas…

title: Comparative Study of Garuda (Khrut) Mythical Creature Visual Representation in Indonesian and Thai Architecture
abstract: Indonesia and Thailand share a common mythical heritage, Garuda (Khrut), which serves both as a spiritual figure and a symbol of national identity. However, significant differences exist in the stylistic approaches, symbolic narratives, and functional placements of Garuda imagery, shaped by each nation's unique historical, religious, and socio-cultural contexts. This study explores how the visual language of Garuda in architecture contributes to contemporary expressions of national identity and environmental design in public spaces. The objectives of this research are: (1) to identify how mythological symbolism is applied in prominent public architecture in Indonesia and Thailand; (2) to examine the socio-cultural and historical influences that shape the stylistic variations of Garuda representations; and (3) to analyze the visual interpretation of Garuda imagery within architectural contexts in present-day Indonesia and Thailand. This study employs a comparative visual analysis method, investigating how Garuda is interpreted and integrated into architectural elements in both countries. Implementing comparative analysis, this study integrates a semiotic perspective using Charles Sanders Peirce’s triadic model (signifier, signified, and referent) to deepen the interpretation of Garuda’s imagery within architectural contexts. Findings reveal a shared Southeast Asian architectural…

title: Pedagogical GenAI use and self-reported creative cognition in art education: a three-wave time-lagged correlational study among design students
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used in design education, yet the psychological pathways associated with students' self-reported creative cognition remain unclear. In this three-wave time-lagged correlational study, 389 design students at a South Korean university reported pedagogical GenAI use at Wave 1, creative self-efficacy and AI-related learning anxiety at Wave 2, and creative engagement and self-reported creative cognition at Wave 3. Pedagogical GenAI use referred to coursework-related use for ideation, style exploration, revision, comparison of alternatives, and feedback seeking. Covariance-based structural equation modeling showed good fit [comparative fit index (CFI) = 0.983, root mean square error of approximation (RMSEA) = 0.026]. Higher GenAI use was associated with higher self-efficacy (β = 0.489) and lower anxiety (β = −0.191). The total modeled association with self-reported creative cognition was β = 0.456 [95% CI [0.314, 0.604]]; its indirect components constituted approximately 59%. The GenAI-origin serial indirect association through self-efficacy and engagement was β = 0.122, whereas the corresponding anxiety-engagement association was β = 0.015. Separately, self-efficacy was indirectly associated with creative cognition through engagement (β = 0.249); this quantity does not include the preceding GenAI-use path. Because the study …

Design of metamaterial-inspired multiport diamond-shaped MIMO antenna with dual interlocked rings for 5G NR n258 band applications
abstract: Abstract The proposed work demonstrates the design, simulation, analysis and validation of a low-profile, miniaturized four-element Multi–Input–Multi–Output MIMO antenna system optimized for 5G NR FR2 n258 band (24.25–27.5 GHz) Communication applications. The designed quad-element MIMO antenna structure comprises dual interlocked rings diamond-shaped radiator etched on a low-loss Rogers 5880 substrate having a thickness of 0.254 mm with a compact size of 12 × 24 mm 2 . Further, the gain and isolation of the proposed antenna is enhanced by incorporating an optimized metamaterial-based rectangular Split Ring Resonator (SRR) array structure between the adjacent element region. The proposed SRR unit cell structure is first optimized using unit-cell boundary conditions to exhibit high reflection and low transmission to reduce intercoupling between elements. Further, the S-Parameters, permittivity, permeability, and refractive index plots are analyzed to validate the behavior of SRR at the resonant frequency. Further, the radiation performance of MIMO antenna exhibiting peak realized gain (5.79 dB), radiation efficiency > 80%, with better isolation > 35 dB is demonstrated. Also, the diversity performance is validated achieving low Envelope Correlation Coefficients (ECC) < 0.001, Channel Capacity Loss (CCL) < 0.0025, Diversity Gain (DG) > 9.995 and Total Active Reflection Coefficient …

title: Designing a Research Methodology for Secure IIoT Implementation in Indonesia: A Research Onion–Based Methodological Design
abstract: Selecting an appropriate methodological configuration is a persistent difficulty in applied cybersecurity research, where technical, regulatory, and organizational evidence must be reconciled within a single design. This paper presents a methodological design study: it derives, justifies, and operationalizes a complete research methodology for developing a secure Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) framework in the Indonesian industrial context, using Saunders’ research onion as the organizing structure. Each of the six layers (philosophy, approach to theory development, methodological choice, strategy, time horizon, and techniques and procedures) is examined and a specific option selected, with justification grounded in the multi-source, multi-stakeholder character of IIoT security in Indonesia. The paper contributes three artifacts: a justified six-layer configuration (pragmatism, inductive, grounded theory, mixed-method, cross-sectional, interviews, focus group discussions, and systematic literature review); an operational protocol translating that configuration into research phases, informant categories, instruments, and analytical treatments; and an assessment of the methodological risks the configuration carries. The study reports a research design rather than empirical findings; data collection and framework validation are the subject of subsequent work, for which the p…
