title: Elicitation and scale-up of Bacopa saponin production by plant cell suspension culture in stirred tank bioreactor
Valorization of agri-food wastes: impacts of vinasse, olive pomace, and tomato peel biochars on plant physiology, soil health and sustainability
abstract: Introduction Utilizing agri-food by-products and residues to create soil improvers reduces waste and promotes environmentally friendly agriculture within a sustainability framework. This study evaluates the agronomic, biological, and economic impacts of biochars produced from three agri-food residues: vinasses, olive pomace, and tomato peels. Methods Biochars were applied to tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum cv Heinz 1301) and wheat ( Triticum durum cv Svevo) in a greenhouse experiment at concentrations of 0.1-0.25-0.5% w/w, to assess their effects on plant biomass, physiology and gene expression, total countable microorganisms, enzymes involved in nitrogen mineralization (arylamidase), cellulose degradation (β-glucosidase) and phosphorus release (phosphatases). Economic and environmental assessments were also carried out. Results and discussion Vinasse biochar contained the highest levels of nitrogen (12000 mg/kg), potassium (11700 mg/kg), and phosphorus (4200 mg/kg), performing comparably to vinasse-based compost. A concentration of 0.5% biochar derived from vinasses increased canopy cover in tomato (+125%), and stem length (+13%), fresh and dry root weight (+97% and 57%, respectively), and stem weight (+41% and 44%, respectively) in wheat. The same biochar modulated genes involved in plant growth and development, cell wall biogenesis, nutrient transport, hormone signaling, and s…

title: Plant versus animal protein intake and muscle mass, strength, and physical function in middle-aged and older adults: A systematic review
abstract: Background: Aging is associated with progressive decline in skeletal muscle mass and function, contributing to frailty and reduced healthspan. Adequate dietary protein is central to muscle preservation, but whether animal or plant protein is optimal remains controversial. This review evaluated plant versus animal protein intake in relation to muscle mass, strength, physical function, sarcopenia, frailty, and bone mineral density in middle-aged and older adults, following PRISMA 2020 guidance with design-matched risk-of-bias appraisal. Objective: To systematically review and synthesize evidence on plant versus animal protein intake in relation to muscle mass, strength, physical function, sarcopenia, frailty, and bone mineral density in middle-aged and older adults. Methods: We searched PubMed and ScienceDirect from inception to June 2026, supplemented by a targeted Google Scholar search and forward/backward citation tracking to identify additional literature likely indexed in Scopus and Embase. Eligible studies reported original data on plant/animal protein intake and the outcomes above in middle-aged/older adults. We appraised risk of bias using RoB2 (trials) and Newcastle-Ottawa Scale adaptations (observational designs). Given heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively. Results: Of 113 primary-search and 21 supplementary-search records, 31 studies (13 cross-sectional…

Evaluating genotype-specific responses in bread wheat (Triticum aestivum) to late-spring frost conditions
abstract: This study investigated the effect of late-spring frost (LSF) stress on wheat (Triticum aestivum) through critical reproductive stages. A factorial experiment was conducted with three wheat genotypes (Roshan, Falat, and Superhead), at three growth stages (pollen development, spike emergence, and anthesis), and with three frost stress durations (control, 1 day of stress, and 4 days of stress) in a completely randomised design with nine replications. Analysis of variance and mean comparison using the l.s.d. method showed that wheat varieties responded differently to growth stages and stress durations, with genotype Roshan being more sensitive and genotype Superhead being more adaptable. Proline accumulation and increased photosynthetic pigment levels were identified as potential mechanisms of stress tolerance, although these responses did not fully prevent yield losses. Principal component analysis explained 75.42% of the total variation, revealing negative correlations between yield-related traits, including grain number, and grain weight. In contrast, chlorophyll, carotenoid, and proline contents were positively correlated with the first principal component. These results highlighted the importance of understanding genotype differences in the LSF tolerance. The genotype- and stage-dependent physiological adjustments drive contrasting yield responses, thereby supporting targeted…

title: Leaf economic strategy and stand structural complexity are associated with net woody productivity in a subtropical mixed forest
abstract: The associations of net woody productivity with biodiversity, functional composition, and stand structure remain poorly resolved in subtropical mixed evergreen–deciduous broad-leaved forests. We used the 2016 and 2021 censuses of 150 contiguous 20 × 20 m subplots in a 6-ha permanent plot at Jinzi Mountain, central China. Net woody productivity was calculated as the annualized net change in live woody biomass. Univariate and multiple linear regressions, random forests, and piecewise structural equation modeling were used to examine relationships with community attributes measured in 2016. Live woody biomass increased from 144.78 to 167.86 t·ha -1 , corresponding to a mean net woody productivity of 4.62 t·ha -1 ·yr -1 . Net gains were concentrated in the tree stratum and larger diameter and height classes; classes with a diameter at breast height ≥29 cm accounted for 78.53% of community net woody productivity. In univariate regressions, productivity was positively associated with community-weighted mean (CWM) leaf thickness and negatively associated with CWM specific leaf area and leaf area. Multiple regression also identified species relative-abundance structure and stand structural heterogeneity as significant correlates. In the piecewise structural equation model, species diversity and structural diversity had significant positive direct associations with productivity. A princ…

title: Integrated multivariate analysis reveals genetic diversity for yield, grain quality, and stress tolerance in rice (Oryza sativa L.) genotypes
abstract: Rice (Oryza sativa L.) is a major staple crop, and simultaneous improvement of yield, grain quality, and stress resistance is essential under changing climatic conditions. However, comprehensive diversity analyses that integrate agronomic, quality, and stress related traits remain limited in rice improvement programs. Therefore, the present study was conducted to evaluate 36 rice varieties during the Kharif season of 2025 at Nuthankal Farm, Hyderabad, using a Randomized Complete Block Design (RCBD) with two replications. Data on 22 traits, including six agronomic, 12 grain quality, and four biotic and abiotic stress-related parameters, were analyzed using analysis of variance (ANOVA), cluster analysis, and principal component analysis (PCA). The results revealed significant differences among the genotypes for all the measured parameters, indicating the presence of high genetic variability. The cluster analysis grouped the genotypes into four distinct clusters, with the highest number of genotypes in Cluster II and only one genotype in Cluster IV, which was highly divergent. The genotypes in Clusters II and III were found to be superior for yield, milling quality, and moderate stress resistance, whereas Cluster IV genotypes had unique characteristics such as early flowering and herbicide resistance. PCA revealed that the first six components explained 81.58 % of the total variat…

title: Plant discourse and ecomultimodality
abstract: Abstract This article discusses the relevance of multimodal communication for representing embodied interaction as an intrinsic part of ecosystems within a more-than-human and multispecies perspective. The research question focuses on how multimodal affordances can contribute to orienting addressees toward the recognition of plants’ actions and interactions, and raising awareness of plants in texts. Plants are life-sustaining participants for the planet, and yet, especially in industrialised and urbanised societies, they tend to be represented as inert beings, or commodified resources for human needs. The present qualitative study brings together plant discourse studies, multimodal discourse studies, and ecolinguistics. The term “ecomultimodality” is adopted here to highlight the interrelation between ecological discourse and multimodal studies when investigating the influence of human communication on ecosystems. The analysis and discussion of two multimodal texts (a scientific article and an art installation) demonstrate how co-deployed modal affordances can enhance the addressees’ engagement in discourse about plants. Multimodal and multisensory aspects facilitate the perception of plants’ actions and interactions, which generally remain unnoticed by humans. Offering a more equal perspective on diversity, and acknowledging common grounds within the more-than-human context, a…

title: Editorial: Plant responses to environmental change
Fine-scale grassland land-cover classification using UAV RGB and multispectral imagery with staged feature selection
abstract: Introduction Accurate mapping of grassland vegetation and bare land is important for grassland degradation assessment and ecological management. This study investigated the effectiveness of integrating visible and multispectral imagery with staged feature selection for fine-scale grassland land-cover classification. Methods Four representative grassland land-cover classes, including Caragana microphylla, Artemisia scoparia, Agropyron cristatum, and bare land, were selected as classification categories. Spectral bands, vegetation indices, and texture metrics were combined to construct a multi-source feature pool, and different feature optimization strategies and classification models were systematically compared. Results Multi-source feature fusion improved the discrimination of spectrally similar land-cover classes, while staged feature selection provided a workflow for reducing cross-source feature redundancy while retaining complementary information. The model with the highest observed validation accuracy selected only ten features from the original feature pool and achieved an overall accuracy of 91.54% with a Kappa coefficient of 88.72%. Compared with direct feature fusion, the optimized feature subset substantially reduced feature dimensionality while maintaining comparable classification accuracy. The resulting classification maps showed broadly consistent spatial pattern…

title: Field or virtual? Perceived impact of academic excursions through the eyes of (future) hydrologists
abstract: Field training such as excursions has always been an integral part of the education of geoscientists. The value of these excursions is frequently debated, related to the efforts and costs involved with their organization. Professionally prepared virtual excursions are sometimes presented as a possible alternative for field activities. This debate has been accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic: the lockdown forced teachers to come up with virtual and online educational material, also for fieldwork and excursions. One of the courses at Wageningen University (the Netherlands) that was heavily affected by COVID-19 restrictions was the Master course Catchment and Climate Hydrology. An important and integral component of that course is an 8 d excursion to Iceland where relatively undisturbed catchments are studied in a country heavily affected by climate change. All students from the 2020 and 2021 cohort took the alternative professionally prepared virtual excursion. After the pandemic, in 2022, these students were offered to join an extra added excursion. About 50 % of that population was able to join. This configuration, involving student cohorts that participated only in the field excursion, only in the virtual excursion, or in both, provided an unique opportunity to assess student evaluations of field-based education and the potential of virtual alternatives. A questionnaire was s…

title: Genetic diversity among economically important bamboo species of India as revealed by ISSR markers
abstract: Bamboo taxonomy rests largely on vegetative and culm-sheath characters, which are diagnostic on mature culms but show marked phenotypic plasticity across sites and culm ages, while reproductive characters are seldom available because flowering is gregarious, unpredictable and separated by cycles of 3–120 years. Molecular markers therefore provide a complementary rather than a substitute route to characterisation. In the present study, an inter-simple sequence repeat (ISSR) marker system employing 21 primers was used to study the genetic relationships among 15 bamboo accessions representing 13 species in four genera, collected from different regions of India. The 21 primers amplified 316 scoreable bands, of which six primers yielded 15 or more bands each; the maximum was recorded for UBC826 (20 bands), followed by UBC827 (19). Polymorphism reached 99.7 %, and polymorphism information content averaged 0.312 per primer against a theoretical maximum of 0.5 for a dominant marker. Similarity coefficients based on simple matching varied between 0.52 and 0.96. The phylogenetic tree based on the genetic similarity matrix, constructed using the unweighted pair group method with arithmetic average (UPGMA) algorithm, resolved the 15 accessions into seven clusters. The highest similarity (0.96) was recorded between Arundinaria falcata and the unidentified hill bamboo accession, supporting i…

Calcium application coordinates seedling heat tolerance and yield-quality formation in ginger under summer high-temperature conditions
abstract: Summer heat stress constrains ginger production. Although calcium (Ca) enhances stress tolerance in various crops, its effects on heat tolerance, yield, and quality in ginger remain unclear. A pot experiment was conducted using Zingiber officinale cv. ‘Laiwu Big Ginger’ to evaluate Ca effects on plant growth and quality under natural summer high-temperature conditions. Six Ca rates (0, 15.2, 30.5, 45.7, 60.9, and 76.2 mmol Ca 2+ plant -1 ) were established using calcium nitrate tetrahydrate [Ca(NO 3 ) 2 ·4H 2 O]. Seedling-stage physiological and biochemical parameters were analyzed with linear mixed-effects models; harvest-stage growth, biomass, and quality parameters were analyzed with ANOVA or non-parametric tests. PCA, correlation analysis, and membership function analysis were used for multivariate evaluation. At Day 16, the 60.9 mmol Ca 2+ plant -1 treatment significantly improved photosynthetic capacity (chlorophyll +23.3%, Pn +13.0%), antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, POD, CAT), and proline content, while reducing oxidative damage (MDA, REC) and ROS (O 2 ·- , H 2 O 2 ). These adjustments promoted biomass and rhizome quality, with the highest rhizome fresh weight (727.7 vs. 447.3 g plant -1 ), dry matter (+3.6%), soluble sugars (+28.1%), soluble protein (+36.5%), free amino acids (+19.1%), and vitamin C (+17.5%). Multivariate analyses confirmed positive correlations amo…

title: PENGARUH PEER MENTORING DALAM MENCEGAH CYBERBULLYING DI SMA
abstract: Cyberbullying is one of the problems frequently experienced by adolescents due to the increasing use of social media and digital technology. One of the efforts that can be made to prevent Cyberbullying is through Peer Mentoring This study aims to analyze the effect of Peer Mentoring on Cyberbullying prevention among grade XI Creative 1 students at SMA Negeri 2 Tanjung. A quantitative associative research approach was used, involving a research sample of 34 students who had participated in the Peer Mentoring program. Data were collected using a Peer Mentoring questionaire base don Albert Bandura’s Social Learning Theory and a Cyberbullying questionnaire based on Bronfenbrenner’s Ecological theory, both of which had been tested for validity and reliability. Data were analyzed using simple linear regression aided by IBM SPSS Statictic versión 27. The result showed that Peer Mentoring and Cyberbullying prevention were in the moderate category. The simple linear regression analisis revealed a significance value of <.001 (< 0.05) and R2 = 0.624. These findings indicate that Peer Mentoring has a positive and significant effect on Cyberbullying prevention, contributing 62.4%. This Finding emphasizes the importance of strengthening Peer Mentoring as a structured preventive service program in school Guidance and Counseling. Future research is recommended to expand the sample coverage and…

title: Targeting food addiction through an intensive energy-reduced Mediterranean diet lifestyle intervention: evidence from the 3-year PREDIMED-plus trial
Synergistic Tuning of Electrochemical Performance in Ni-Modified CuCo-MOFs for Flexible Energy Storage Devices
abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of flexible, portable, and wearable electronic technologies has heightened the need for energy-storage systems that provide mechanical durability and operational safety. MOFs (Metal Organic Frameworks) have attracted considerable attention due to their highly tunable porous architectures, large accessible surface areas, and abundant redox-active metal centers. In this work, a Ni intercalated bimetallic CuCo-BDC MOF was synthesized, aiming to exploit multimetal synergistic effects, enhance redox activity, and improve ion-transport dynamics. Structural and morphological analyses confirm that Ni incorporation preserves the crystalline integrity and mesoporous, sheet-like architecture of the parent framework. Electrochemical investigations demonstrate that the Ni-CuCo-BDC MOF significantly enhanced charge storage behavior, achieving a high areal capacity of 82.917 μAh cm–2 at a current density of 1 mA cm–2 in a three-electrode configuration. The assembled solid-state FES device exhibits a capacity of 13.389 μAh cm–2, an energy density of 5.356 μWh cm–2, and a power density of 400 μW cm–2, along with excellent mechanical flexibility and ∼90.2% capacity retention after 5000 cycles. These outcomes highlight the potential of the Ni-CuCo-BDC MOF as a promising energy storage candidate for wearable and portable electronics.

title: Joint planning–control optimization of EV charging stations, battery energy storage, and DSTATCOMs in distribution networks
abstract: Abstract The increasing penetration of electric vehicles (EVs) is placing growing planning and operational demands on distribution networks due to the spatially concentrated and time-varying nature of charging loads. Although previous studies have investigated the coordinated planning of electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs), battery energy storage systems (BESSs), and distributed static compensators (DSTATCOMs), infrastructure planning and operational control are commonly treated as separate stages, with planning decisions typically evaluated using predefined operating strategies or static operating conditions. This paper proposes an integrated planning–control optimization framework that simultaneously determines the optimal siting, sizing, and operational control of EVCSs, BESSs, and DSTATCOMs in radial distribution networks. Unlike conventional approaches, the proposed formulation embeds 24-hour BESS charging/discharging schedules and droop-controlled DSTATCOM operation directly within the planning optimization, enabling candidate solutions to be assessed under realistic time-varying operating conditions. The resulting mixed-integer nonlinear optimization problem is solved using the Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO) algorithm. Simulation studies on the IEEE 69-bus distribution system show that the proposed framework reduces the mean absolute voltage deviation by approxim…

title: Spectral Degradation Markers in Lipid Profile of Whole Milk Powder during Storage
abstract: Whole milk powder is one of the most sought-after dairy ingredients due to its high nutritional value, long shelf life, and wide range of functional and technological properties. However, milk powder is rich in lipids, which makes it sensitive to oxidative and hydrolytic spoilage, resulting in the accumulation of milk fat degradation products and quality deterioration. New rapid, non-destructive testing methods can identify the early stages of spoilage in whole milk powder. This research evaluated the use of Raman spectroscopy for the early detection of spoilage in whole milk powder during storage.The study featured samples of whole milk powder stored at 45 ± 2°C for 15 weeks, with analysis performed in 3-week increments. Raman spectra were recorded using a portable EnSpectr R785 Raman spectrometer (Russia). Changes in the fatty acid composition were analyzed using a Crystallux 4000M gas chromatograph (Russia).The most informative spectral ranges included the regions at 325–370, 375–425, 800–900, and 2840–2970 cm–1. The highest statistical significance belonged to the range of 800–900 cm–1 (F = 7.36; p < 0.001), which reflected the structural transformations of the lipid-protein component of the milk matrix. Principal component analysis (PCA) showed the non linear nature of spectral changes during storage. Gas chromatography analysis revealed a relatively stable fatty acid comp…

title: Fungi and mycotoxins during conventional and improved postharvest processing and storage of local rice in Nigeria
abstract: Abstract This study applied a polyphasic characterization approach and LC-MS/MS analysis to elucidate fungal and mycotoxin contamination dynamics during conventional (CPRP) and improved (IPRP) postharvest processing and a 90-day storage of rice in Nigeria. Three hundred and twenty-five fungal isolates belonging to 21 genera (10 moulds, one crust fungus, 10 yeasts) and 54 species were recovered from rice across both processing chains. The CPRP chain had greater diversity of fungal genera compared to the IPRP chain. Aspergillus predominated both processing chains while yeasts occurred only in the CPRP chain. Species belonging to Aspergillus sections Aspergillus , Candidi , Flavi and Nidulantes , and Penicillium section Citrina predominated in stored rice in the two processing chains. A total of 106 extrolites including several uncommon extrolites and potential species markers were identified in agar cultures of 38 strains from 19 mould species. Fifteen mycotoxins were detected in rice along the processing and storage chains. Processing of rice in the IPRP chain and hermetic storage for 90 days reduced total aflatoxins by 9% compared to non-reduction in CPRP chain. Conventionally processed and stored rice in jute bags after 90 days recorded at least twice higher percentage reductions of total fumonisin, nivalenol and tenuazonic acid compared to hermetically stored rice from the IP…

title: Drivers of continuance participation intention in online retail sales events
abstract: Purpose This study aims at identifying the major drivers influencing the consumers' continuance participation intention (CPI) in online retail sales events (ORSE). It focuses on the associations of ritualistic consumption and deal proneness with shopping engagement (SE), the association between SE and CPI, and test the moderation effect of fear of missing out (FOMO). Design/methodology/approach Data were collected using an online self-administered questionnaire from 500 respondents with past online retail sales events (ORSE) experience. Consistent partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was applied to the gathered data as the method for analysing the proposed research model. Further, the moderating role of FOMO was validated with a multigroup analysis based on permutations. Findings The findings show that ritualistic consumption and deal proneness are positively related to SE. SE is positively associated with CPI. In addition, FOMO strengthens the relationship between SE and CPI. The multigroup analysis further supports this moderating effect. Originality/value The present study contributes to the literature in three distinct ways. First, it shifts attention from initial participation to continuance participation in ORSE, a context that remains underexplored. Second, it extends engagement research by identifying ritualistic consumption and deal proneness as…

title: Grain Industry Waste in Lithium-Ion Battery Production
abstract: The Kaliningrad Region generates over 200,000 tons of straw annually, and its disposal often causes environmental degradation. However, straw-derived biochar can be utilized in the production of lithium-ion batteries. This article describes the most effective processing methods and structural parameters for this application. The study utilized winter wheat straw collected from farms in the Kaliningrad Region. The raw material was subjected to hydrothermal carbonization with varying temperatures (200–260°C), residence times (1–3 h), and water-to-biomass ratios (1:6, 1:12, 1:18). The optimal hydrothermal carbonization conditions proved to be 260°C for 60 min with a water ratio of 1:12. The resulting biochar was then subjected to multi-stage pyrolysis at temperatures up to 800°C. The products were characterized using elemental analysis, gravimetry, laser diffraction, and electrochemical testing in laboratory coin-cell lithium-ion batteries, which were compared against commercial AGP-2 graphite.The elemental composition of the precursor straw revealed a high carbon content (44.2%), confirming its suitability for thermochemical conversion. The hydrothermal carbonization under optimal conditions raised the carbon mass fraction to 61.3%, while the subsequent pyrolysis increased it to 80–95%. The average particle size of the resulting biochar (D50 = 26.2 μm) complied with industrial st…

title: Downscaling GRACE storage change to analyze groundwater dynamics and drought evaluation in the Ganga Basin
Electric-Field-Oriented Interfacial Solvent Engineering Enables High-Voltage Ether Electrolytes for Ni-Rich Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract High-voltage operation of nickel-rich cathodes (>4.5 V) significantly boosts the energy density of lithium-ion batteries but triggers catastrophic oxidative decomposition of conventional ether electrolytes. Under high-potential electric fields, ether molecules in the electric double layer orient their oxygen atoms toward the cathode surface. This intimate contact accelerates α-hydrogen dehydrogenation and subsequent degradation. Herein, we report an electric-field-oriented interfacial solvent engineering strategy that decouples the vulnerable ether linkage from the charging interface. By introducing a rigid, asymmetric solvent molecule, 4-cyano-tetrahydropyran (THP-CN), we exploit the preferential adsorption of the highly polar cyano group under the intense interfacial electric field, driving the formation of a self-assembled “cathode-cyano-ether-bulk” configuration that effectively shields the ether oxygen and adjacent α-hydrogen atoms from the reactive cathode surface, thereby suppressing oxidative decomposition. Meanwhile, cooperative FSI– and NO3– decomposition constructs a robust, inorganic-rich cathode electrolyte interphase, further stabilizing the cathode structure. Consequently, the low-concentration THP-CN-based ether electrolyte exhibits exceptional oxidative stability up to 4.8 V. Demonstrating practical viability, the assembled 1.5 Ah graphite||NCM811 p…

title: Structural topology optimization of railway vehicle wheel damping plates considering acoustic-vibration interaction
From crash evidence to injury prevention: factors associated with injury severity in heavy vehicle crashes involving vulnerable road users in Pakistan
abstract: Crashes involving heavy vehicles and vulnerable road users (VRUs) represent a serious public health challenge in low- and middle-income countries, where road traffic injuries contribute substantially to injury-related morbidity and mortality. However, the existing literature remains limited, as most studies focus on single VRU groups and are concentrated in high-income settings. As a result, little is known about injury severity in mixed-traffic environments such as Pakistan, where pedestrians, motorcyclists, and motorized rickshaw users interact with heavy vehicles under substantially different roadway and traffic conditions. To address this gap, this study investigates the factors associated with injury severity in crashes involving heavy vehicles and VRUs in Pakistan using 1,007 anonymized emergency-service crash records collected by Rescue 1122. A random parameters binary probit model with heterogeneity in means and variances was estimated to account for unobserved heterogeneity and variation in the effects of explanatory variables across crashes. The analysis indicates that male VRUs are less likely to sustain severe injuries, whereas VRUs aged 25 years or younger face a significantly higher probability of severe injury. Crashes occurring during weekends, at night, and under rainy conditions are associated with a higher probability of severe injury. Pedestrian and motorcyc…

title: Balancing Aesthetics and Performance: An RGB-Based Coloring Strategy for Building-Integrated Photovoltaics
abstract: Abstract Building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV) represents a promising approach for energy generation in urban environments, although balancing aesthetics and photovoltaic performance remains challenging. This work presents and validates a novel tunable coloring strategy for flexible Cu(In,Ga)Se2 (CIGS) solar cells that allows to balance optical induced losses with gains while reducing color angle dependence. Inspired by the light-emitting diode display technology, the strategy combines micropatterned Red, Green, and Blue Bragg reflector (BR) coatings in adjustable proportions to achieve tailored colors. Two line-based microarchitectures were fabricated on soda lime glass and flexible CIGS solar cells. White coloration was selected due to its compatibility with common building facades, with patterns designed to appear visually uniform at distances higher than a 1 m viewing distance. The developed process demonstrated reproducible defect-free microfabrication and successful color perception. Compared to conventional uniform BRs, the RGB pixel coloration strategy significantly reduced color angle dependence and improved optical performance, limiting short-circuit current density losses to below 1.5 mA·cm–2. Moreover, individual color BR led to a short-circuit current loss of 1% to 4% or an enhancement of nearly 10% depending on the final color. The proposed strategy demonstrate…

title: Integrated farming as an adaptation strategy to climate change and variability in frequently drought prone regions of Southern India
abstract: Though integrated farming is believed as an adaptation strategy to climate change and variability, information about the extent of adaptation benefits due to drought remains limited. In rainfed production systems, small and marginal farmers are vulnerable due to frequent droughts leading to crop failures, low farm productivity aggravating hunger and poverty. Identification and effective integration of multiple adaptation strategies at the farm play an important role in improving resilience, particularly in agroecosystems exposed to a high frequency and intensity of climatic shocks such as droughts. In this study, we propose a framework to strengthen the existing rainfed farming systems by characterizing them, prioritizing the constraints and resilient strategies and assessed their impact. Data was collected from 240 farm households (HHs) and characterized, 24 farmers (12 small and 12 marginal farmers) were selected for on-farm assessment under rainfed and partially irrigated (PI) situations. Prioritized interventions were implemented in four predominant farming systems and assessed their contribution to resilience. Diversified farming systems with drought-tolerant and high yielding varieties, intercropping systems, conservation furrows, improved fodder varieties and livestock feed additives, enhanced the system productivity by 77 and 29% of small farmers under rainfed and parti…

title: AI-induced corporate social responsibility (AICSR) and e-retailing: a game-changing strategy or a gimmick to attain customer loyalty
abstract: Purpose This study examines the direct and mediated effects of AI-induced corporate social responsibility (AICSR) initiatives on customer loyalty in e-retailing, grounded in an integrated theoretical framework of stakeholder theory and signaling theory. It clarifies whether AICSR fosters customer loyalty directly or indirectly via a series of intervening pathways. Design/methodology/approach We tested the framework using cross-sectional survey data collected from 234 active Chinese online retail consumers, and analyzed the dataset via partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) using SmartPLS 4. Findings Results reveal that AICSR exerts a significant positive direct effect on customer loyalty. Meanwhile, its influence is transmitted through six constructs – retailer service quality, customer satisfaction, electronic word-of-mouth (e-WOM), retailer image, retailer reputation and customer trust – through both individual mediation pathways and a sequential pathway involving all six mediators. These mediators exhibit significant positive relationships, highlighting their interconnected roles in explaining customer loyalty. Originality/value This study extends extant literature by unpacking the paradox of legitimate distinctiveness amid AICSR in the e-commerce industry. It demonstrates that the effectiveness of AICSR initiatives extends beyond their direct contribut…

title: The Principal's Strategy to Improve Deep Learning-Based Learning Quality
abstract: This study aims to analyze the principal’s strategy for improving the quality of Deep Learning-based instruction at SMA Negeri 13 Surabaya, Strategic planning, Deep Learning deployment, Academic oversight, evaluation and assessment, and professional development for teachers, enabling and impeding conditions, and follow-up measures for ongoing improvement are the main topics of the study. A case study methodology combined with a descriptive qualitative design was used. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, passive-participation observations, and documentation involving the principal, vice principal for curriculum, teachers, and students. Observations were conducted from 22 June to 5 September 2026. The Plan, Do, Check, Act (PDCA) framework was used as the substantive analytical framework. Data condensation, data display, cross-source comparison, and conclusion verification were used to examine the data. The findings show that the principal’s strategy operates as an integrated instructional leadership cycle. The Plan stage includes collaborative curriculum planning, analysis, teacher competency development, resource preparation, and quality targets. The Do stage translates the strategy into mindful, meaningful, joyful, collaborative, contextual, and student-centered learning supported by mentoring, learning communities, technology, and innovation. The Check stag…

title: The hidden risk of regulatory arbitrage: strategic exposure in global markets
abstract: Purpose This article examines the strategic and ethical implications of regulatory arbitrage in global markets. While firms expand into less regulated environments to increase flexibility and growth, these strategies raise questions about long-term sustainability and corporate responsibility. The purpose is to show that regulatory arbitrage is not only a source of competitive advantage but also a potential source of strategic exposure, as actions taken in one market increasingly shape stakeholder perceptions across others. Design/methodology/approach The article adopts a conceptual approach supported by a case-based illustration of the 2008 spin-off of Philip Morris International. Drawing on institutional and stakeholder perspectives, it develops a three-dimensional framework to analyze how regulatory distance, stakeholder visibility, and legitimacy spillover interact to shape the risks associated with global expansion strategies. Findings The analysis shows that regulatory arbitrage can simultaneously generate economic value and increase legitimacy risk. While firms benefit from reduced constraints and expanded market access, these gains may be offset by heightened scrutiny and cross-market reputational effects. The findings suggest that strategic decisions cannot be evaluated solely within local regulatory contexts, as stakeholder expectations increasingly operate across glob…

Rearticulating Authority: Hybridity, Power, and the U-Thong Nai Assembly Hall in Thai Statecraft
abstract: This paper investigates the ideological function of hybridity in modern Thai architecture through a postcolonial lens, focusing on the U-Thong Nai Assembly Hall, completed in 1974 and serving as Thailand’s National Assembly for forty-four years, as a case study. As one of the country’s most significant political buildings during the Cold War, the Assembly Hall embodied the military government’s effort to project a modern national identity while consolidating state authority. While Thailand was never formally colonized, its cultural and architectural development was deeply shaped by indirect Western imperial influences, a condition scholars have described as crypto-colonialism. Drawing on Homi Bhabha’s theory of hybridity and Néstor García Canclini’s concept of mestizaje, this study argues that Thai architectural modernity emerged not through passive imitation but through a calculated process of cultural appropriation, ambivalence, and elite political self-fashioning. Using parliamentary records, committee minutes, and government documents, as well as architectural analysis of the building’s spatial organization, form, and symbolic composition, the paper demonstrates how modernist forms were selectively combined with Thai architectural and iconographic elements to articulate both national identity and political legitimacy. Rather than merely reflecting foreign influence, the U-T…

title: Robotic automation of maintenance work in nuclear power plants a cross-sector survey and recommendations
abstract: Background Nuclear power plants face increasing cost pressures, workforce constraints (aging workforce and skilled labor shortages), and safety requirements that are accelerating interest in robotic systems for inspection and maintenance. Methods We conducted semi-structured interviews with personnel from seven U.S. nuclear utilities and compared deployment models, operational use cases, and integration practices with those reported by participants in the oil, gas, and petrochemical sector. Results In nuclear plants, robotic use remains concentrated in inspection—particularly indoor unmanned aerial vehicles and submersible remotely operated vehicles—with limited application to physical maintenance tasks. Reported near-term value includes reduced radiological and industrial risk, reduced outage labor, and improved data for planning and condition assessment. Key barriers include integration and data-interoperability constraints, operator qualification requirements, cybersecurity review burden, and difficulty demonstrating reliability in plant-representative environments. Conclusions Cross-sector benchmarking highlights organizational and deployment practices that may help nuclear plants scale from pilots to routine use. We propose recommendations emphasizing modular payload strategies, representative qualification pathways and testing environments, and improved data governance to…

title: Measuring digital payment transformation in small retail businesses: mixed-method evidence from blockchain adoption in Colombia
abstract: Abstract This study aims to evaluate how blockchain-based payment systems affect operational performance, customer-related outcomes, and organizational coordination in small retail businesses operating under institutional fragmentation and uneven digital infrastructure. Using transaction-level data from 76 small retailers in Colombia’s Caribbean region, the analysis combines pre/post comparisons, non-parametric tests, repeated-measures models, regression controls, endogeneity checks, and thematic content analysis of open-ended pre- and post-implementation questionnaire responses from participating business owners or managers. The findings show improvements in transaction speed, payment reliability, operating costs, customer retention, and perceived service quality, but they also reveal that these effects are conditioned by infrastructure quality, staff readiness, seasonality, and local market composition. Rather than treating blockchain as an isolated technological intervention, the study interprets payment adoption as a socio-technical governance mechanism that reorganizes coordination, trust, and operational routines. The article contributes to digital transformation research by offering a mixed-method framework for evaluating technology adoption in small firms where causal inference is constrained by non-random adoption, heterogeneous contexts, and imperfect administrative r…

title: Food retail drivers of sustainable packaging and labelling: a review
abstract: Purpose Sustainable packaging and labelling play an increasingly important role in food retail as communication tools that influence consumer perceptions and behaviours. Understanding how retailers can effectively leverage these tools to encourage consumer adoption and foster sustainable consumption is therefore crucial. Accordingly, this paper systematically reviews the literature on sustainable packaging and labelling in food retailing to identify key research gaps and outline directions for future research. Design/methodology/approach Following the SPAR-4-SLR protocol, 271 articles from Web of Science and Scopus were systematically reviewed, examining publication trends, methodologies, theoretical frameworks, and key constructs in food retail. Findings The review identifies the main theories and constructs, methodologies, and dependent variables investigated in existing literature. It also reveals five thematic clusters concerning labels, psychological drivers, awareness, social influences, and packaging/branding, and proposes a future research agenda covering theoretical and methodological developments. Originality/value This study provides an integrative synthesis of the fragmented literature on sustainable packaging and labelling in food retail. Identifying five thematic clusters and synthesising prior findings, it supports cumulative theory building and offers actionable…

title: Crisis-induced hybrid learning, cognitive offloading, and generative AI reliance among Pakistani CS undergraduates
abstract: Purpose In spring 2026, geopolitical tensions prompted the Pakistani government to mandate full online instruction (10 March–3 April 2026), followed by a hybrid schedule for the rest of the semester. This shift is treated here as an externally imposed crisis context for AI adoption, not as a natural experiment. No pre-crisis baseline or control group was available. The study characterises generative AI (GenAI) adoption patterns and the psychological antecedents of AI dependency among undergraduate computer-science (CS) students during this window. Three hypotheses, grounded in the reviewed literature, structured the analysis. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey was administered across Pakistani higher education institutions (HEIs) in April–May 2026. Of 360 responses collected, two incomplete records were removed, and a thirteen-criterion data-quality screen was ap-plied, yielding N = 299. Fourteen constructs were operationalised from UTAUT, Cognitive Load Theory (CLT), Self-Determination Theory (SDT), and the AI Anxiety Scale (AIAS). Block-entry OLS regression and bootstrapped mediation (5,000 resamples) tested the hypotheses; ANOVA and Spearman correlations supported descriptive analysis of adoption patterns. Findings Adoption was near-universal (>99%), with 45.2% of respondents reporting ≥ 31% of submitted work directly AI-generated. A three-block OLS regr…

title: Ultrasound learning experiences in a Japanese student-led circle: A descriptive study
abstract: Introduction: Peer-assisted learning (PAL) is widely used to support collaborative clinical skill development. In Japan, PAL is often organised through student-led extracurricular groups known as circles or “bukatsudō”. This descriptive study examined the educational characteristics of a student-led ultrasound circle, the Hamamatsu Emergency Room Ultrasound (HERUS), and explored students’ learning experiences. Methods: We conducted a retrospective survey of sixth-year medical students who completed their clinical clerkships. The duration and extent of HERUS members’ (n = 14) and non-members’ ultrasound learning were compared. Additionally, HERUS members were surveyed to examine factors associated with learning frequency and faculty recognition. Qualitative open-ended responses about perceived educational benefits were analysed using content analysis. Results: HERUS members gained earlier ultrasound experience in the cardiac, abdominal, and neck regions, and were more likely to have performed cardiac ultrasound on patients during clerkship, than non-members. HERUS members with ≥30 months of participation reported more departments where HERUS was discussed with faculty. Half of the HERUS members practiced ultrasound with peers at least weekly. Content analysis indicated that wearing scrubs helped faculty identify HERUS members and provide them with opportunities for ultrasound pr…

Integrated multi-omics and machine learning identify core mechanobiology-associated immune genes in pulmonary arterial hypertension
abstract: Background Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) involves vascular remodeling and altered mechanical signaling. The immune-associated transcriptomic changes accompanying this environment remain incompletely characterized. Methods We integrated bulk lung (GSE15197), PBMC (GSE33463), and single-cell RNA-seq (GSE169471) data using a curated set of 2, 537 mechanical-related genes. WGCNA, LASSO, random forest, and single-cell localization supported candidate prioritization. The four-gene panel was examined in a monocrotaline-induced PH rat model and PBMCs from 10 IPAH patients and 10 controls. Results PAH transcriptomes showed enrichment of stress-fiber, actomyosin, ECM, and immune-related programs. CD83, CD86, IL6, and TLR7 were prioritized, with compartment-dependent expression patterns. Single-cell data localized CD83/CD86 to myeloid/APC compartments and IL6 to endothelial/fibroblast populations; TLR7 was sparsely detected. In MCT-treated rat lungs, CD86 and TLR7 proteins increased, whereas CD83 and IL-6 decreased. Clinical PBMCs showed corresponding expression directions, and each gene had an AUC >0.7. The exploratory four-gene disease-state score achieved an internal cross-validated AUC of 0.765. Conclusions The four candidates provide a cellular and molecular context for investigating immune-stromal interactions in PAH, including responses to noninfectious vascular injury. …

title: Pengasuhan Otoritatif dan Dukungan Teman Sebaya sebagai Prediktor Motivasi Akademik Siswa SMP
abstract: Academic motivation is an important factor in students’ engagement and learning success and develops within social contexts. This study examined authoritative parenting and peer support as predictors of academic motivation among junior high school students. A quantitative cross-sectional explanatory survey design was employed. Participants were 320 students in Grades 7–9 from several junior high schools in Bekasi City and Bekasi Regency, Indonesia, recruited through voluntary response sampling. Data were collected using measures of academic motivation, authoritative parenting, and peer support, and analyzed using multiple linear regression. The results showed that authoritative parenting and peer support jointly predicted academic motivation significantly (R² = .418, F = 113.90, p < .001). Authoritative parenting showed a stronger standardized predictive contribution (β = .460, p < .001) than peer support (β = .307, p < .001). These findings suggest that both family and peer contexts are significantly associated with students’ academic motivation during early adolescence. The results also indicate that authoritative parenting has a stronger predictive contribution within the model, while peer support remains an important social factor. These findings highlight the importance of involving families and schools in creating social environments that support adolescents’ academic mot…

HSV-Net: hybrid state-space and self-supervised vision fusion with progressive contour learning for CT pulmonary nodule segmentation
abstract: Accurate voxel-level segmentation of pulmonary nodules on chest CT is needed for diameter and volume measurement, growth tracking, and quantitative assessment in lung cancer screening. The task remains difficult: nodules vary in attenuation, size, and contact with vessels or pleura, and clinically relevant morphology often lies in a thin, ambiguous margin. Existing systems commonly trade contour fidelity for speed—large prompt-driven foundation models can be accurate but slow, whereas compact CNN or SSM decoders are efficient yet tend to smooth spiculated and ground-glass borders. We propose HSV-Net (Hybrid State-space–Vision Network), a dual-stream 3D network that is prompt-free after nodule localization: an SSM3D stream provides whole-patch context with linear-complexity state-space blocks, and an OrthoLoRA stream adapts frozen DINOv2 features on axial, coronal, and sagittal slices. A Hybrid Gated Mixer (HGM) fuses the two streams before FPN decoding, and Progressive Contour Learning (PCL) supervises overlap, signed-distance-field geometry, and uncertainty-weighted contour refinement. On a 10-patient QIN Lung CT/QIN-LungCT-Seg development subset ( n = 12 tumors; nested patient-level 5-fold CV), HSV-Net obtained the highest mean Dice (90.1% ± 1.0%; 95% CI [88.9, 91.3]) and Boundary F1 (86.3% ± 1.3%) among the compared methods on 128 × 128 × 64 patches, with a latency of 58 ms.…

title: Strengthening learning in Rwanda’s local NGOs
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to review the latest management developments across the globe and pinpoint practical implications from cutting-edge research and case studies. Design/methodology/approach This briefing is prepared by an independent writer who adds their own impartial comments and places the articles in context. Findings Firms become better placed to increase their organizational learning ability (OLA) when they prioritize organizational development (OD). Optimal outcomes can be attained by introducing key learning activities and ensuring they are appropriately aligned and implemented. Other crucial measures include strengthening communication, building a supportive culture and integrating learning into strategic decision-making. Originality/value The briefing saves busy executives and researchers hours of reading time by selecting only the very best, most pertinent information and presenting it in a condensed and easy-to-digest format.

We hypothesised that (a) GMR is comparable to Guided Physical Practice (GPP) for learning Pupillary Examination (PE), and (b) Mental Imagery (MI) ability improves GMR practice. On day 1, baseline MI ability was assessed, followed by PE instruction. Subjects were practiced at week 1 and 3. PE performance and MI ability were reassessed using a checklist score sheet (month-1) and the Movement Imagery Questionnaire-3 (month-2). Results: Data is presented as median with interquartile range. The Mann-Whitney U test showed no significant differences in PE performance between GMR and GPP at month-1 (35.00 [14.00] vs. 33.25 [12.00], p=0.91) and 2 (40.00 [10.50] vs. 36.42 [12.00], p=0.50). Innovative teaching-learning methods of pandemic module: A qualitative needs assessment in India
abstract: Introduction: COVID-19 pandemic has underscored critical deficits in global health preparedness. Traditional lecture-based teaching is frequently criticised for its limited effectiveness in practical skills required for real-world crisis response, creating significant "readiness gap". Hence, this study was done to evaluate perceived necessity and importance of innovative teaching-learning methods for the pandemic module amongst medical undergraduates. Methods: Qualitative needs assessment was conducted using an interpretive description approach to explore stakeholder perspectives regarding the existing pandemic management teaching module and public health preparedness training within the undergraduate Community Medicine curriculum. Three focus group discussions were held with 28 purposively sampled participants at tertiary care teaching hospital, comprising faculty from Community Medicine (n=10), medical students who had completed pandemic training (n=10), and students awaiting training (n=8). Data were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed using manual thematic analysis. Results: Analysis identified four central themes. First, profound theory-practice gap in existing teaching, inadequately preparing students for real-world scenarios. Second, simulation and gamification were widely endorsed as promising, engaging solutions for teaching complex skills like outbreak …

title: A Framework for Real-Time Phishing Resource Locator Detection Using Structural and Lexical Feature Analysis Based on Machine Learning
abstract: Phishing attacks remains a leading, rapidly evolving threat in cybersecurity domain, where cyber-criminals deploy fraudulent websites that are deceptive in nature acts exactly same as legitimate platforms to transfer sensitive user credentials, financial data and corporate data to an external location. Traditional counter measures including blacklist-based systems and rule-based filters demonstrates limited efficiency against newly created malicious URLs and real-time generated phishing URLs. This paper presents PhishGuard+, a random forest-based phishing detection framework that performs real-time suspicious URL classification through complete structural and lexical feature analysis of the URL. The proposed system utilizes a dataset of 10,000 labeled URLs, from which 48 distinct features are extracted that includes URL patterns, domain characteristics, and heuristic indicators. A Random Forest classifier is trained on preprocessed data comprises min-max normalization and the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) to address skewed data distribution. The trained model is deployed with a Flask-based RESTful API, that real-time inference through an interactive web interface. Experimental evaluation demonstrates an overall classification accuracy of 98.4%, with precision and recall exceeding 98% across both phishing and legitimate URL categories. The proposed framework …

title: Deep learning-based segmentation of choroid plexus calcification on quantitative susceptibility mapping: a feasibility study
abstract: Abstract Choroid plexus calcification (CPC) is a common age-related imaging finding associated with neuroinflammation and cognitive decline. Its accurate quantification remains challenging on computed tomography (CT), the current clinical gold standard, due to concerns regarding ionizing radiation exposure. Quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) offers a non-invasive, radiation-free alternative for accurate assessment, but manual segmentation is impractical for large cohorts. We developed a deep learning-based framework for automated CPC segmentation using QSM. Using data from 106 subjects, we trained nnU-Net v2 models to evaluate input combinations comprising QSM, 3D T1-weighted images, and choroid plexus (CP) masks. The automated pipeline achieved its highest segmentation accuracy using QSM with CP and CPC masks and the strongest volumetric correlation with manual ground-truth annotations ( r = 0.964) using both QSM and T1-weighted images. QSM-derived CPC volumes were strongly correlated with CT-derived volumes in a validation subset of 22 subjects ( r = 0.728). In an additional cohort of 91 subjects, the framework revealed age-related changes in CPC, with volume increasing and susceptibility values becoming more diamagnetic with age. This framework provides a tool for direct CPC quantification on QSM that shows strong correspondence with CT-derived volumes, enabling large…

abstract: Conceptual understanding is the most important aspect in informatics learning. However, learning that is still dominated by conventional material delivery causes conceptual understanding to not develop optimally. This study aims to develop interactive gamification multimedia based on discovery learning that is valid, practical, and effective in improving students' conceptual understanding in Informatics subjects in grade VII of junior high school. This study uses the Research and Development (R&D) method with the ADDIE model which includes the stages of analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation. The research subjects consisted of content experts, media experts, design experts, Informatics subject teachers, and grade VII students at SMP N 1 Kuta Selatan. Data were collected through validation sheets, teacher and student response questionnaires, and pretest-posttest tests to measure conceptual understanding. Data analysis was carried out descriptively and inferentially using paired sample t-tests, N-gain calculations, and effect size. The results showed that the developed multimedia was categorized as very valid based on the assessment of content, media, and design experts, and very practical based on teacher and student responses. The results of the effectiveness test using a paired sample t-test showed a significant difference between the pretest and posttes…

title: Transcriptomics-guided serum podoplanin and interpretable machine learning for early risk stratification of necrotizing enterocolitis in preterm infants
abstract: Background To evaluate podoplanin (PDPN) as a circulating biomarker for early necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) risk stratification and to determine whether an interpretable machine-learning framework integrating PDPN with prediagnostic clinical and inflammatory variables could improve individualized risk estimation. Methods PDPN expression was examined in two public NEC intestinal transcriptomic datasets. Serum PDPN was then measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay in a nested case-control cohort of 132 preterm infants (66 with NEC and 66 gestational-age- and birth-weight-matched controls). All candidate predictors were obtained before NEC onset in cases and before the matched reference time in controls. Restricted cubic spline, receiver operating characteristic, precision-recall, LASSO, multivariable logistic regression, 11 machine-learning algorithms, SHAP, and nomogram analyses were performed. Results PDPN was upregulated in NEC intestinal tissue. Serum concentrations were higher in infants who developed NEC than in controls (48.36 ± 22.89 vs 19.75 ± 6.26 ng/mL, P < 0.001) and in Bell stage III than in Bell stage II NEC [69.43 (58.91–77.95) vs 30.59 (24.06–42.79) ng/mL, P < 0.001]. title: Differentiated Instruction as Proactive Classroom Management in Early Childhood Science Learning: A Multi-Site Qualitative Case Study
abstract: Early childhood classrooms are developmentally heterogeneous, making instruction and classroom management inseparable challenges. This study examined how differentiated instruction was enacted within science-based learning and how teachers perceived and managed the resulting classroom dynamics. A qualitative multi-site case study was conducted across four early childhood education institutions in Brebes Regency, Central Java, Indonesia. Participating teachers were purposively selected because they implemented differentiated instruction, used inquiry-oriented science activities, and had at least two years of early childhood teaching experience. Data were generated through non-participant classroom observations, semi-structured interviews, and analysis of daily lesson plans and instructional materials, then examined thematically. Three interconnected findings emerged. First, differentiation was enacted through adjusted task complexity, flexible grouping, varied hands-on activities, and responsive scaffolding. Second, these practices were associated with more sustained engagement, clearer routines and transitions, and less need for reactive behavior correction, suggesting that instructional design functioned as a form of proactive classroom management. Third, teacher competence and instructional flexibility supported implementation, whereas planning time and high teacher–child rat…

Robert S. Pindyck: Real Options, Optimal Control, and the Pedagogical Legacy of Uncertainty
abstract: Robert S. Pindyck, who is the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Professor in Finance and Economics as well as a professor of applied economics at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), has shaped how economists and policymakers analyze investment, energy markets, and climate policy under uncertainty. Beginning with early work in dynamic optimization, he helped migrate option-pricing logic from finance into the economics of “real” decisions (such as entry, exit, and capacity choice) via the real options program developed with Saman Majd and Avinash Dixit. In energy and natural resources, Pindyck's models and empirics clarified interfuel substitution, storage and inventory dynamics, and cartel behavior. In climate economics, he became a prominent critic of the overprecision of integrated assessment models (IAMs), proposing decision frameworks that emphasize deep uncertainty and tail risk while arguing for robust carbon pricing. Equally important is his pedagogical legacy: with Daniel Rubinfeld, Pindyck coauthored two widely used textbooks ( Microeconomics and Econometric Models and Economic Forecasts ) that trained generations in rigorous modeling, identification, forecasting, and market analysis. This article synthesizes his career and research arc, contrasts the Dixit–Pindyck real options approach with the Fisher–Arrow–Henry tradition of quasi-option value, reviews his energy …

title: Modeling Uncertainty in Integrated Assessment Models
abstract: Integrated assessment models (IAMs) are pivotal tools that synthesize knowledge from climate science, economics, and policy to evaluate the interactions between human activities and the climate system. They serve as essential instruments for policymakers, providing insights into the potential outcomes of various climate policies and strategies. Given the complexity and inherent uncertainties in both the climate system and socioeconomic processes, understanding and effectively managing uncertainty within IAMs are crucial for robust climate policy development. This review provides a comprehensive overview of how IAMs handle uncertainty, highlighting recent methodological advancements and their implications for climate policy. We examine the types of uncertainties present in IAMs; discuss various modeling approaches to address these uncertainties; and explore recent developments in the field, including the incorporation of advanced computational methods.

Real-time optimization of urban traffic using predictive algorithms
abstract: Abstract Urban traffic congestion remains a critical challenge in modern cities, contributing to increased travel times, environmental pollution, and economic inefficiencies. This research paper explores the application of predictive algorithms for real-time optimization of urban traffic flow, aiming to enhance mobility and reduce congestion. Leveraging machine learning models—including recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and reinforcement learning, the study develops a dynamic traffic management system that processes real-time data from sensors, GPS, and historical traffic patterns to predict congestion and optimize signal timings. Key findings demonstrate a 20–30% reduction in average travel delays across simulated urban networks, alongside improved adaptive responsiveness to unexpected disruptions. The implications of this research extend to smart city infrastructure, offering scalable and data-driven solutions for sustainable urban mobility. Unlike existing studies that primarily combine traffic forecasting and signal optimization as independent processes, the proposed framework tightly integrates LSTM-based congestion prediction with Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based spatial dependency modeling and embeds predictive traffic states directly into a Reinforcement Learning (RL) controller. This proactive architecture enables traffic signal decisions to anticipate congestion before…

title: Ecological drivers of the colon cancer microbiome: evidence for niche-based selection over stochastic colonization
abstract: Colon cancer is a leading global malignancy influenced by genetic, environmental, and microbial factors. This study integrates ecological theories, including Hubbell’s neutral theory, augmented by Ning et al.’s (2019, PNAS) stochasticity analysis framework, and classic niche theory, to assess the contributions of stochastic colonization and deterministic niche selection in shaping microbiome assembly and dynamics in colon cancer tissues. Specialist species were identified using Levins’ niche breadth analysis. By reanalyzing the datasets from Nejman et al., including 22 normal adjacent tissue (NT) and 22 primary tumor (PT) samples, we find: (i) deterministic niche selection appears to dominate community assembly and diversity maintenance in both NT and PT microbiomes, as demonstrated by the normalized stochasticity ratio (NSR: 0.267 for NT, 0.287 for PT; both below 0.5; Wilcoxon PT>NT, p=0.027). Only 18.2% NT and 27.3% PT samples fit the neutral model, confirming stochastic drift plays a limited role and niche selection predominates in structuring tissue microbiomes. (ii) Through niche breadth analysis, we identified 106 specialist species, of which 14 are known CRC-associated taxa, including Fusobacterium nucleatum , Escherichia coli , Enterococcus faecalis , and Peptostreptococcus anaerobius . These species have established roles in inflammation, genotoxicity, immune modula…

title: Optimization of Pregnancy Testing in the Emergency Department: A Quality Improvement Initiative
abstract: Background: At our institution, a review of emergency department pregnancy testing identified excess use of serum quantitative (quant) human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) when only a binary result was clinically indicated. Additionally, we observed delays in point-of-care (POCT) urine hCG turnaround time. In response, provider education and electronic health record default modifications were implemented to promote serum qualitative (qual) hCG. Methods: Following a pre/post intervention design, we reviewed emergency department pregnancy tests over 2 periods: July 1, 2024–June 30, 2025, and September 1, 2025–February 28, 2026. Outcomes included utilization patterns, order-to-result time, per-test cost, appropriateness of serum quant hCG, and test completion. Results: Inappropriate serum quant hCG orders decreased from 42.2% to 36.2%. Serum qual hCG use increased from 8.4% to 55.4%, while POCT and serum quant hCG use decreased from 71.8% to 33.0% and 19.8% to 11.6%, respectively. POCT order-to-result time decreased from 92.2 to 77.6 minutes, with no significant change in serum turnaround time. Mean cost per test decreased from $211.08 to $147.79, a $63.29 (30%) reduction. Pregnancy test completion increased from 78.8% to 89.8%. Conclusions: Pairing electronic health record default order modification with targeted provider education reduced low-yield quant hCG ordering and increased…

Determinants of agri-entrepreneurship success in Jordan: an integrated model of family, government and personal factors
abstract: Purpose This article aims to examine the key drivers of agri-entrepreneurship success in Jordan by investigating six critical factors and their impact on the success of agricultural ventures. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative methodology was employed, with data collected from 131 agricultural-sector entrepreneurs in Jordan via an electronic survey. Structural equation modeling was used to analyze the data and test the hypotheses. Findings Family support, family background, government support and internal locus of control had a significant impact on entrepreneurial success. In contrast, managerial skills and social network ties were found to have no significant effect. Research limitations/implications First, using a convenience sampling approach may limit the extent to which the findings can be generalized. Second, the use of self-reported measures can affect response accuracy and potentially inflate observed relationships among variables. Third, the present study is cross-sectional, meaning it captures only a “statistical” time point. Fourth, control variables were not examined in the current study. Finally, the present study considered only the entrepreneur's internal locus of control as a personal attribute that influences agribusiness success. Originality/value This study enriches the literature by introducing a multidimensional model based on various theories that…

Developing a Mehri–Arabic Neural Machine Translation System Using a Multilingual Transformer Model (mT5)
abstract: Machine translation for low-resource and endangered languages remains a challenging task due to the scarcity of parallel corpora and limited computational resources. Despite its linguistic and cultural significance, the Mehri language has received little attention in natural language processing research. This paper presents a Mehri–Arabic machine translation system based on a multilingual neural model. A custom Mehri–Arabic parallel corpus was constructed and preprocessed using rule-based techniques. The multilingual mT5 model was fine-tuned via transfer learning and evaluated using both automatic metrics and human assessment. Experimental results indicate that satisfactory Arabic translations can be achieved despite limited data availability. This work represents an early computational effort in Mehri– Arabic machine translation and highlights the potential of multilingual pretrained models for supporting under-resourced languages.
venue: International Journal of Computers and Informatics

title: Expanding capitation accountability and healthcare utilization in an integrated care network: evidence from China
Supersonic sustainability transitions: an integrated life cycle and triple bottom line assessment with socio-technical transition lenses for next-generation passenger aircraft
abstract: Purpose This study aims to evaluate the environmental, economic and social sustainability of next-generation commercial supersonic transport and develops the Supersonic Sustainability Transition Assessment Model (SSTAM) to distinguish near-term actionable pathways from options dependent on wider socio-technical readiness. Design/methodology/approach SSTAM integrates ISO 14040/44-aligned life-cycle assessment, triple bottom line indicators, multi-criteria decision analysis, scenario and Monte Carlo uncertainty testing and socio-technical systems/multi-level perspective interpretation. Reference, best-case and worst-case scenarios were modelled using regulatory, NASA/OEM, life-cycle inventory and peer-reviewed evidence. Findings Supersonic aircraft show CO2 emissions about 2.3–2.6 times higher than subsonic benchmarks, with additional high-altitude non-CO2 effects. Passenger-normalized unit operating cost ranges from US$0.118 to 0.190/RPK against unit revenue of US$0.150–0.170/RPK, producing positive margins only in the reference and best-case scenarios. Energy intensity reduction, verified low-carbon SAF uptake and noise/contrail-aware operations emerge as no-regrets pathways; liquid hydrogen propulsion and overland low-boom permissions remain conditional on infrastructure, policy, certification, market and community safeguards. Originality/value SSTAM moves beyond parallel sust…

Multi-Scenario Comparative Analysis of Objective Weighting Techniques in MOORA-Based Decision Support Systems
abstract: This study presents a multi-scenario comparative analysis of objective weighting techniques integrated with the MOORA method in decision support systems to evaluate their consistency, robustness, and reliability in alternative ranking. Various objective weighting methods, including WENSLO, LOGSTA, RECA, LODECI, ITARA, CRISUS, MPSI, and SITDE, were applied to a decision matrix representing candidate store locations with multiple criteria such as rental cost, building area, accessibility, consumer traffic, parking availability, and infrastructure. The analysis was conducted under different data scenarios to examine the sensitivity of each method to variations in data characteristics. The results show that although there are differences in the weight distributions generated by each method, the final rankings produced by the MOORA approach remain highly consistent, with NSL 5 consistently ranked as the best alternative. Furthermore, the Spearman correlation analysis reveals very strong agreement among the methods, with correlation values of 0.9762 for WENSLO, LOGSTA, LODECI, ITARA, CRISUS, and MPSI, and perfect correlation values of 1.000 for RECA and SITDE. These findings indicate that the proposed approach is stable and not sensitive to the choice of weighting method, thereby enhancing confidence in the decision-making process. Overall, this study demonstrates that integrating mu…

Precarious conditions of partnership sustainability: examining the factors that enabled a multi-school–university partnership to persist
abstract: Purpose This article illustrates how participants' continuous productive learning interactions within a multi-school–university partnership strengthened the organizations' enabling conditions, thereby sustaining the work amid threats to partnership funding. The partnership was designed to support school leaders in implementing evidence-based practices in reading. By combining elements from several established research-practice partnership (RPP) frameworks, we examine the interactions among the RPP's structural components, affording us a more nuanced understanding of factors that contribute to learning among partners and to the partnership's long-term outcomes and sustainability. Design/methodology/approach This study draws on data from a larger instrumental case study (Merriam, 1998; Stake, 1995; Yin, 2018). Researchers collected data from 2023 to 2025 across multiple sources, including interviews, meeting observations and documents. The participants included members of the RPP leadership team from the participating university and school district, as well as participating principals and instructional leaders at 15 elementary schools. Findings This study provides insights into how organizational enabling conditions, despite threats to funding, were central to long-term sustainability through interactions among partnership participants as they navigated boundaries around the timi…

title: A Locally Adaptive Multi-Resolution Encoding Framework for Spiking Neural Network based ECG Beat Classification
abstract: Objectives This study highlights the importance of an appropriate encoding technique in Spiking Neural Networks, and proposes the use of multiresolution encoding, which combines multiple encodings based on input features. Methods This research experiments on The MITBIH dataset was split into train-test data using AAMI standards. It uses the Pan-Tompkins method to extract features from ECG signals and feed these features to the SNN model post-encoding. Multiple encoding schemes were implemented, including rate, temporal, population-based, and multiresolution encoding. All these encodings were compared with respect to macro-recall, accuracy, and local spike characteristics, such as Spike Efficiency (SE) and Temporal Dispersion (TD). Findings These results confirm that encoding quality in SNNs should not be judged only by accuracy or recall independently, but by the joint relationship between spike efficiency, temporal dispersion, and classification performance. The proposed clinically guided Multi-Resolution encoding offers a practical and novel solution for ECG beat classification by integrating physiological knowledge directly into spike generation with the highest accuracy of 89%. Novelty This work recommends a locally adaptive multiresolution spike encoding framework based on the local morphological characteristics of the beat features for ECG beat classification using SNNs. …

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of multi-organ pathology and antigen localization in BALB/c mice following intragastric infection with Brucella melitensis
abstract: Brucellosis is a globally distributed zoonosis that invades hosts mainly through the gastrointestinal route, yet the spatiotemporal patterns of organ colonization and tissue injury following intragastric Brucella infection remain poorly defined. Objective To investigate the dynamic colonization patterns, histopathological progression, and spatiotemporal antigen localization characteristics of Brucella melitensis 16M in multiple murine organs following intragastric infection. Methods The mice were randomly divided into an uninfected control group and infection groups euthanized at 1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 42, and 56 days post-infection (dpi). Mice received intragastric inoculation of 10 10 CFU standard B. melitensis 16M strain. Body weight and organ indices were dynamically monitored throughout the experiment. Bacterial loads in the liver, spleen, lung, and mesenteric lymph nodes (MLNs) were quantified by plate spreading assay. Tissue lesions and antigen localization were assessed via hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining with semi-quantitative scoring and immunohistochemistry (IHC). Flow cytometry was performed to dynamically quantify total dendritic cells (total DC) alterations in hepatic and splenic tissues at 1, 2, 4, 6, and 8 weeks post-infection. Results After intragastric infection, mice developed prominent splenomegaly and transient hepatic weight gain, both peaking at 14 dpi…
