title: Epidemiology of voluntarily reported dog and cat bite incidents in a large-scale, multi-site veterinary network in the UK and Ireland
abstract: Introduction Dog and cat bites are an occupational risk within veterinary practise. Despite this, there is minimal research exploring the occurrence and details surrounding such incidents. Methods The aim of this study was to use a large veterinary group’s existing incident and near miss reporting system in the UK to explore the incidence of dog and cat bite reporting and surrounding details of such incidents. Results Dog and cat bite incidents were identified from January 2024 to October 2025 covering all clinics in the UK and Ireland (>1,000). A total of 2,327 dog (1,239; 53.24%) and cat (1,088; 46.76%) bites were reported. The most common anatomical bite location was reported to be the hands and fingers for both dog (63.0%) and cat (80.6%) bites. The majority of bites for cats (77.96%) and dogs (80.60%) occurred between 9 a.m. and 6 p.m. Location of in-clinic bites differed between staff, with the veterinarians most commonly bitten in the consult room and non-veterinarians most often bitten in the preparation area. Regarding perceived behaviour, the term ‘aggression’ was most frequently used in reports. Conclusion In conclusion, this report highlights the common occurrence of dog and cat bite related injuries, providing insights into surrounding factors. Factors need to be considered to reduce bites such as low stress handling, environment adaption and encouraging advance…

title: Associations between behavioral trait expression, anxiety, and depression in a multi-site recovery sample
abstract: Background Anxiety and depressive symptoms are commonly evaluated as indicators of psychological distress, yet less is known about how broader patterns of behavioral trait expression relate to these symptoms at the individual level. This study examined associations between overall trait expression and anxiety and depression among adults participating in recovery-oriented behavioral health programming. Methods A retrospective observational analysis was conducted using routine assessment data collected between August 2023 and May 2026 across multiple U. S. behavioral healthcare settings. Records from the Trait and Hero Discovery Assessment, Generalized Anxiety Disorder scale (GAD-7), and Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) were matched to the same participant and assessment occasion. The primary analytic sample included 278 matched assessment occasions representing 252 participants. Associations were evaluated using Pearson correlations, with Spearman correlations, participant-clustered regression, mixed-effects models, and alternative assessment-matching windows used as sensitivity analyses. Internal consistency was also evaluated for the study measures. Results Higher Trait Index scores were moderately associated with lower anxiety ( r = −0.471, 95% CI [−0.557, −0.372], p < 0.001) and lower depressive symptom severity ( r = −0.508, 95% CI [−0.595, −0.408], p < 0.001). Dehumanized platform workers dehumanize customers: how algorithmic management reduces customer-oriented behavior
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how algorithmic management affects platform workers' customer-oriented behavior and to explore the potential mediating and moderating mechanisms underlying this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on social cognitive theory, this study proposes that algorithmic management serves as a contextual force that shapes workers' moral cognition and increases their tendency to dehumanize customers, which in turn reduces customer-oriented behavior. In addition, customer gratitude expressions may alleviate the relationship between algorithmic management and workers' dehumanization of customers. We collected data from a three-wave survey of 312 food delivery riders. Structural equation modeling was employed to test the proposed model. Findings Our findings suggest that algorithmic management is positively associated with workers' dehumanization of customers, whereas their dehumanization of customers is negatively associated with customer-oriented behavior. The dehumanization of customers plays a mediating role in this relationship. In addition, customer gratitude expressions weaken the positive association between algorithmic management and customer dehumanization. The moderated mediation results further indicate that this indirect effect is weaker when customer gratitude expressions are high. Originality/value This study clarifies the r…

title: Inclusive leadership in Finnish early childhood education centres – leading pedagogy, professional development and the community
abstract: Purpose Inclusive education is a core principle of Finnish early childhood education (ECE), requiring leadership that supports inclusive pedagogy, professional learning, and collaboration with the wider community. Despite strong policy emphasis, little empirical research has examined how ECE centre leaders perceive inclusive leadership. This study explores leaders’ perceptions and develops a refined measurement tool suited to the Finnish ECE context. Design/methodology/approach A translated and adapted inclusive leadership scale was administered to 116 leaders from public and private ECE centres across Finland. Exploratory factor analysis was conducted to examine the structure of ECE leaders’ perceptions of inclusive leadership and to enhance the scale’s parsimony. Findings Three dimensions of inclusive leadership were identified: (1) leading pedagogical processes, (2) constructing an inclusive community and (3) leading the professional development of staff. Leaders reported engaging most strongly in supporting inclusive pedagogical practices and staff competence development, while community-level collaboration was less frequent. Group comparisons revealed small but significant differences: leaders in public and smaller centres reported more community-oriented practices, whereas leaders in private centres reported more active support for staff professional development. title: Climate risk and firm-level cost structures: empirical analysis of Saudi listed companies
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how climate variability affects operating efficiency, cost of capital and total costs among firms in climate-sensitive Saudi sectors. Design/methodology/approach Using a balanced panel of 80 Saudi listed firms in seven sectors during 2010–2024, the study estimates two-step system Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) models for soil moisture, precipitation, specific and relative humidity, wet-bulb temperature and wind speed. Principal component analysis (PCA)-based estimates test robustness to multicollinearity. Findings Soil moisture, specific humidity, wet-bulb temperature and wind speed increase firm costs, whereas precipitation reduces them; relative humidity is insignificant. Leverage increases costs in the baseline model, while larger and faster-growing firms show lower costs. PCA results confirm the climate–cost relationship. Research limitations/implications Results are limited to listed firms in seven Saudi climate-sensitive sectors, the 2010–2024 period and six climate metrics; generalization to private firms, other settings and extreme events should be cautious. The evidence nevertheless frames climate variability as a material financial-risk channel. Practical implications Managers should incorporate climate indicators into budgeting, maintenance, water and cooling investment, liquidity buffers and financing decisions. Regulators and…

title: Minimally invasive versus open emergency right-sided colectomy for malignant obstruction: a nationwide propensity score–matched cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background Minimally invasive surgery (MIS) improves short-term outcomes in elective colectomy, however, the choice of surgical approach in hemodynamically stable patients with obstructing right-sided colon cancer remains unclear in emergency settings. MIS could be considered and the present study aims to evaluate short-term outcomes of MIS in bowel obstructed patients compared with open surgery (OPEN). Methods A retrospective nationwide study including patients from the nationwide Swedish Colorectal Cancer Registry (SCRCR) undergoing emergency right-sided colectomy in Sweden (2017–2023) was conducted. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed based on sex, age, ASA class, hospital size, and operative timing (on-call vs. daytime). Outcomes included length of stay (LOS), postoperative complications, and surgical quality indicators. Analysis was performed according to intention-to-treat. Results A total of 1147 patients were identified. Of the 1,147 included patients, 99 (8.6%) underwent an initially minimally invasive approach. After matching, 99 patients remained in each group. The conversion rate was 34%. Median LOS was 9 days (IQR 6;14) after OPEN and 6 days (IQR 5;10) after MIS. In quantile regression with bootstrap standard errors, MIS was associated with a 3-day shorter median LOS (median difference − 3.0 days, 95% CI − 4 to − 2, p = 0.002). Postoperative comp…

title: Ancestors, Transmission, and Belonging: Reconsidering Chinese Ancestor Rites from the Perspective of Biblical Genealogy
abstract: Abstract This article argues that Chinese ancestor rites should be understood through a structure of transmission. Transmission refers to a relational continuity through which identity, belonging, responsibility, inheritance, and legitimacy are received from a chain of relations that precedes the individual self. The article redeploys transmission as a theological and comparative category for interpreting Chinese ancestor rites in relation to biblical genealogy and covenantal continuity. Its central claim is that ancestor rites express a prior order of belonging: ritual does not create belonging; belonging authorizes ritual.1 , 2

title: Determinants of Foreign Direct Investment in Saudi Arabia: An Empirical Analysis Using the QARDL Model for the period (1985-2024)
abstract: This study aims to examine the impact of macroeconomic determinants on foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows in Saudi Arabia over the period 1985–2024, employing the Quantile Autoregressive Distributed Lag (QARDL) methodology developed by Cho et al. (2015) to capture nonlinear and asymmetric relationships across different quantiles of the FDI distribution. The study relies on annual data for five independent variables: trade openness, per capita income, human capital index, oil revenues, and inflation rate. The results reveal the existence of quantile cointegration among the variables and reject the symmetry hypothesis, confirming that the impact of macroeconomic determinants varies across different levels of FDI inflows (low, medium, and high). Furthermore, the findings indicate significant positive effects of trade openness, per capita income, and human capital in both the short and long run across all quantiles, with human capital recording the largest positive impact. Oil revenues, by contrast, exhibit a significant negative effect consistent with the resource curse hypothesis. Inflation displays a negative relationship at higher investment levels, with a limited positive shift observed at lower investment levels. Asymmetric quantile causality tests further reveal significant causal relationships that vary according to the magnitude of the shock and the quantile level. Th…

title: Cluster investigation report: a probable urine-associated transmission event of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome—a case report
abstract: Introduction Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne viral disease with a high case fatality rate. Human-to-human transmission has been increasingly documented, primarily through direct contact with blood or bloody secretions. On June 21, 2025, a case of SFTS was reported in Zhumadian City, Henan Province. On July 3, a second case—epidemiologically linked to the first—was reported to the local Centers for Disease Control (CDC) through the notifiable disease reporting system, following laboratory confirmation on July 1. Case presentation A 77-year-old female farmer with underlying comorbidities was hospitalized with fever, leukopenia, and thrombocytopenia, and subsequently died of SFTS. Her 31-year-old granddaughter, who had an open wound on her hand, cared for the patient and cleaned her urine. Eleven days later, she developed fever, nausea, vomiting, headache, fatigue, and myalgia. Laboratory tests confirmed SFTS virus infection by RT-PCR, with an initial cycle threshold (Ct) value of 38.85, which subsequently decreased to 31.48 over the following 2 days, indicating active viral replication. She recovered after antiviral therapy and was discharged on July 7. Comprehensive epidemiological investigation ruled out other potential transmission routes, including blood contact, tick bites, and environmental exposure. However, direct virological e…

title: Agricultural Investment and its Role in Economic Diversification in the Al-Jawf Region under Saudi Vision 2030
abstract: This report analyzes the state of economic development in the Al-Jouf region during the 2020–2030 period, focusing on the agricultural sector's role in driving economic growth, improving key economic indicators, and the resulting impact on the region. The study reveals that Al-Jouf possesses significant economic and agricultural assets, establishing it as one of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia’s leading agricultural regions—particularly in the production of dates, olives, and other crops. The report concludes that agricultural investment has directly contributed to enhancing local economic performance. It helped lower regional unemployment rates by creating both direct and indirect job opportunities within agricultural activities and related industries. Furthermore, it boosted income levels and purchasing power—driven by increased agricultural productivity and the profitability of agricultural enterprises—while also stimulating commercial activities and services linked to the sector. The findings also indicate that the expansion of agricultural production bolstered economic stability and mitigated inflationary pressures by increasing the local supply of food commodities and reducing import dependency, thereby supporting regional food security. Additionally, Al-Jouf witnessed significant growth in investment volumes and development projects—supported by government funding and agricu…

title: Ensuring Right to Life for the Slum Dwellers: Obligations of the States under International Human Rights Law
abstract: In urban governance, the rapid expansion of informal settlements has become the most pressing human rights challenge. Although the right to life is universally recognised as the supreme and non-derogable human right, millions of slum dwellers continue to experience systemic deprivation arising from inadequate housing, insecure land tenure, limited access to healthcare, unsafe drinking water, unhygienic sanitation, environmental degradation and recurrent forced evictions. All these issues raise a pressing question about the enforcement and protection mechanisms of international human rights law, which requires States parties to give proper effect to the right to life, to refrain from arbitrary deprivation, and to take positive measures securing the minimum conditions for a life lived with dignity. This article focuses on protecting slum dwellers’ right to life and examines the scope of State obligations as it relates to international human rights law. Using a qualitative doctrinal and comparative methodology, it analyses the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the ICCPR, the ICESCR, and the interpretative jurisprudence of United Nations treaty-monitoring bodies, alongside the doctrines of positive obligations, progressive realisation, minimum core obligations, and procedural safeguards against forced eviction. It further evaluates comparative constitutional jurisprudence from…

title: Developing Digital Green Financial Literacy Based on Sharia Economic Principles to Enhance Youth Financial Capability
abstract: Research integrating Islamic and green financial literacy into digital education for young adults remains limited, particularly in translating Islamic economic values into environmentally oriented financial learning. This study developed and evaluated “SyarGreen Finance,” a digital educational platform incorporating justice, public welfare, and the prohibition of riba, gharar, and israf, to support young adults’ financial literacy. A research and development approach using the ADDIE model was combined with a one-group pretest–posttest design involving 96 college students aged 18–25 selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through expert validation questionnaires, financial literacy tests, and semi-structured interviews. Evaluation employed the content validity ratio, a paired-samples t-test, and N-gain analysis. Content and media experts rated the platform as highly valid, with validation scores of 90.4% and 88.7%, respectively. Participants’ financial literacy scores increased significantly from pretest to posttest (p < .001), with a mean N-gain of 0.56. These findings support the platform’s expert-assessed validity and provide preliminary evidence of its educational potential, although the single-group design limits causal attribution of the observed improvement. The study contributes to Islamic financial literacy and green finance scholarship by operationaliz…

title: Defence Spending in the Multiannual Financial Framework 2028–2034: More Own Resources but No EU Tax Sovereignty
abstract: Abstract This article examines the European Commission’s proposal for the Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) 2028–2034 and argues that the European Union (EU) should complement temporary debt- and flexibility-based defence financing with a permanent tax-based source of revenue. While recent initiatives, including the activation of the Stability and Growth Pact’s national escape clause and the Security Action for Europe (SAFE) instrument, have expanded member states’ fiscal space, they remain temporary and primarily finance national rather than European defence. The new MFF foresees new own resources which, however, do not provide the EU with significantly more money for defence. Drawing on a comparative analysis of fiscally decentralised multilevel governance systems, the article examines value-added tax (VAT) arrangements in the United States, Switzerland, and Germany to identify institutional lessons for the EU. Neither the Swiss model of exclusive federal VAT nor the German model of shared federal VAT can be directly transplanted to the EU. Instead, the article proposes a distinct European model in which a small, treaty-based share of national VAT would constitute a genuine EU tax while preserving member states’ tax sovereignty. Such a reform would provide the EU with a stable source of own revenues to finance common European public goods, particularly defence.

title: Happiness, religiosity and economic hardship: cross-national evidence on household financial position
abstract: Purpose This study examines how happiness, religiosity and recent economic hardship are jointly associated with household financial position across countries. It addresses limited cross-national evidence on how subjective well-being and religiosity relate to household financial position under conditions of material hardship. Design/methodology/approach Individual-level data are drawn from Wave 7 of the World Values Survey (2017–2022) across 64 countries. Household financial position is measured on a four-category ordinal scale ranging from spending savings and borrowing to saving money. Mixed-effects ordered logit models with country-level random intercepts and random income slopes are estimated using a baseline sample of 84,765 respondents. Robustness analyses employ alternative measures of religiosity, economic hardship and household financial position, together with alternative country treatments, model specifications and sample-composition checks. Findings Higher happiness is consistently associated with a more favourable household financial position, including lower predicted probabilities of spending savings and borrowing and higher probabilities of saving money. Religiosity has no statistically significant direct association in the baseline model, while the negative happiness × religiosity interaction indicates that the positive happiness association becomes weaker as re…

title: Design Modification and Initial Performance Evaluation of a Multivariant Briquette Press for Multiple Biomass Feedstocks
abstract: Biomass residues can be converted into solid fuel, but small-scale briquetting is often constrained by fixed molds and limited pressure adjustment. This study developed an initial multivariant briquette press concept using a modular mold and adjustable pneumatic compression, then evaluated briquettes produced from coconut-shell charcoal, corn-cob charcoal, and sawdust charcoal. Each formulation used 1,000 g of biomass charcoal and 100 g of tapioca binder (10% of charcoal mass). Three replicate samples per biomass were tested for moisture content, texture/hardness, and ash content. Mean moisture contents were 4.7142 +/- 0.0141% for coconut shell, 4.3147 +/- 0.5643% for sawdust, and 6.3146 +/- 1.1283% for corn cob. Coconut shell produced the highest relative texture/hardness value (3808.67 +/- 203.38) and the lowest ash content (3.1150 +/- 0.0433%). Sawdust had the lowest mean moisture content, whereas corn cob showed the lowest hardness and the greatest moisture variation. The results confirm that one press can form briquettes from different biomass feedstocks while also showing that biomass-specific control of pressure, particle size, moisture, and binder conditions is necessary for consistent product quality

title: Digital-Twin-Oriented Surrogate Modelling of Architectural Identity and Thermal Performance in Benghazi A Semi-Physical, Evidence-Informed Framework for Multi-Objective Design-Space Exploration
abstract: This study develops a Digital-Twin-oriented computational framework for exploring relationships between selected architectural-envelope characteristics, thermal performance, and a limited evidence-informed proxy of architectural identity in Benghazi. The framework integrates documented historical geometric evidence with a semi-physical thermal formulation, tree-based machine-learning surrogates, permutation importance and SHAP analysis, and a 50,000-point Monte Carlo design-space exploration followed by Pareto analysis. HistGradientBoosting achieved an independent-test R² of 0.98940, RMSE of 0.29227 °C, and MAE of 0.23646 °C, while five-fold cross-validation produced a mean R² of 0.98815 ± 0.00116. Wall thickness and external temperature were the dominant thermal predictors within the current formulation. The documented geometric evidence from the Sidi Khrebish/Berenice context showed substantial variability, with a weighted empirical mean ratio of 1.37453 (SD = 0.24723); the Golden Ratio (φ ≈ 1.618) was therefore retained as an independent comparative geometric reference rather than embedded in the base AIPI. The multi-objective exploration produced a computational Pareto set of 16 non-dominated solutions under standardized conditions of 35 °C outdoor temperature and 800 W/m² solar irradiance. Short-lived halogen sources and chemistry in the Community Earth System Model v2 (CESM2-SLH)
abstract: The implementation of short-lived halogen (SLH) sources and atmospheric chemistry in the Community Earth System Model v1 (CESM1) allowed to study the influence of SLH chemistry on the oxidative capacity of the atmosphere and, consequently, the Earth's climate. In this manuscript, we summarize 15 years of research on SLH chemistry and present a complete revision of the porting of the original developments into the latest version of CESM (v2), hereafter CESM2-SLH. This includes a detailed description of all offline and online sources of organic and inorganic SLH, as well as the gas-phase and heterogeneous recycling of chlorine, bromine and iodine in the troposphere and stratosphere, including their species-independent atmospheric sinks. In doing so, we provide a comprehensive evaluation of how changes in model parameters and coupled dynamics within the Community Atmosphere Model v6 (CAM6) affect SLH abundances and their implications. The new CESM2-SLH implementation offers various model configurations and resolutions, all of which result in equivalent global budgets and zonal distributions of organic and inorganic chlorine, bromine and iodine, which in turn, lead to SLH impacts on atmospheric composition that are consistent with previous CESM1 results. Capital Structure Decisions and Financial Performance of Firms Listed in the Alternative Investment Market Segment of the Nairobi Securities Exchange.
abstract: Financial performance, reflected in profitability, liquidity and market valuation, is a critical measure of the sustainability and growth of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) listed on the Alternative Investment Market Segment (AIMS) of the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE). Despite relaxed listing requirements and tax incentives intended to widen SME access to public capital, AIMS-listed firms continue to face thin market liquidity, high perceived investment risk, limited access to affordable long-term debt and governance gaps, with the segment accounting for less than 5% of total NSE market capitalization and more than 60% of its firms reporting volatile or declining profits between 2019 and 2024. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to examine the relationship between capital structure decisions and financial performance among firms listed on AIMS. It specifically examined the influence of debt-based financing, equity-based financing, hybrid financing and retained earnings-based financing on financial performance. The study was anchored on the Static Trade-Off Theory, Agency Cost Theory, Market Timing Theory and Pecking Order Theory. A descriptive and explanatory cross-sectional research design was adopted, targeting all nine AIMS-listed firms through a census, from which five finance and strategic decision-makers per firm were purposively selected, giving a samp…

title: Market Inquiries and the Enforcement of Competition Law in South Africa: A Case Study of the Banking Market Inquiry in Light of the Foreign Currency Cartel
abstract: This paper examines the role of market inquiries in the enforcement of competition law in South Africa, focusing on the Banking Market Inquiry (BMI) and its intersection with the foreign currency cartel case. It explores how market inquiries, as formal investigations into market structure and conduct, enable competition authorities to identify and address market failures, enhance regulatory knowledge, and promote consumer welfare. The analysis highlights the unique regulatory landscape of South Africa’s banking sector, characterised by high concentration, significant barriers to entry, and concurrent jurisdiction between competition authorities and sector regulators. The BMI’s findings revealed persistent challenges, including opaque pricing, exploitative penalty fees, and limited access to payment systems, while also noting progress in transparency, consumer choice, and digital transformation. The paper discusses the impact of cartel behaviour and merger control on market dynamics, emphasising the importance of robust coordination and adaptive regulatory strategies. Ultimately, the study demonstrates that market inquiries are invaluable tools for diagnosing structural issues, informing policy, and guiding enforcement actions. Ongoing reforms and vigilant oversight are essential to foster a competitive, transparent, and inclusive financial system that serves the diverse needs o…

title: Empirical performance of rough volatility models in the KOSPI 200 options market using deep surrogates
abstract: Purpose This study provides a systematic comparison of the pricing performance of the rough volatility models—rBergomi and rHeston—with that of classical one-factor stochastic volatility (SV) and stochastic volatility jump-diffusion (SVJ) models in the KOSPI 200 index options market. Design/methodology/approach Using an extensive daily option dataset spanning the 22 years from 2003 to 2025, we conduct daily calibration and out-of-sample forecasting experiments. To overcome the computational bottleneck of rough volatility models and to place all models in a uniform comparison environment, we adopt the deep surrogate methodology, which replaces the pricing function with a deep neural network and delivers calibration at effectively real-time speed. Findings In terms of in-sample pricing fit, the SVJ models with eight to nine parameters perform best, but the rBergomi model, which has only three core parameters, is not far behind. Out-of-sample, by contrast, the forecasting accuracy of the SVJ models deteriorates sharply because of parameter overfitting, whereas rBergomi dominates at every forecast horizon. The estimated Hurst exponents lie mostly between 0 and 0.5, confirming that the roughness of volatility is present in the KOSPI 200 options market under the risk-neutral measure as well. Arts and the market: an ethnography of their complex contemporary relationships
abstract: Purpose An in-depth understanding of how art is valued in the market using photography as context. Changes in how photography is produced and consumed warrant a contemporary understanding of the contributions of artistry and commercialism. Design/methodology/approach A seven-year ethnography explored the current state of the relationship between arts and the market through four phases – education and training; initial fieldwork; in-depth interviews; confirming and clarifying findings through additional fieldwork. Findings Analysis of ethnographic data reveals eight inter-related categories of findings – artistry; commercialism; contrariety of artistry and commercialism; credibility of photographer (producer); shared vision; value co-creation; control of access; collaboration and coordination. As these categories progress, there is a shift in control over identifying and creating value from artistry to commercialism. Research limitations/implications The relationship between artistry and commercialism has a history of contrariety, culminating in a contemporary situation that favors the contributions of commercialism. Recommendations are made for how the definition of value can begin to shift back in the direction of artistry. title: Drug shortages in Italy: strategic insights and empirical evidence from the Italian pharmaceutical market
abstract: Abstract Drug shortages disrupt healthcare delivery and pose a critical challenge to the resilience of pharmaceutical supply chains. This study investigates the drivers of drug shortages in Italy – Europe’s leading pharmaceutical producer – to identify the factors associated with supply disruptions and inform evidence-based health policy. Using national data from 2018 to 2023, we analysed 17,619 drugs across 3,013 groups of substitutes, covering community , dual-dispensed , and hospital distribution channels. Generalised linear mixed models were employed to assess how drug characteristics, market dynamics, and regulatory features influence shortage risk. Shortages were most prevalent among community drugs, where high market fragmentation and low-profit margins contributed to supply instability. Patent protection was associated with lower shortage risk for non-sterile drugs, while sterile drugs remained vulnerable regardless of patent status, likely due to manufacturing complexity. Notably, price effects were age-dependent: higher prices mitigated shortage risk, particularly for older drugs. This study offers a comprehensive evaluation of shortage patterns in a key pharmaceutical market, identifying structural risk factors and market vulnerabilities. The findings provide actionable insights for policymakers aiming to design targeted interventions, strengthen supply chain resilie…

Investor attention and GCC stock market connectedness during the first wave of COVID-19: evidence using Google trends and VIX
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the behavioral determinants of financial market connectedness in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) during the first wave of COVID-19. It examines whether the Chicago Board Options Exchange Volatility Index (VIX), regional investor attention measured via Google Trends, and their interaction are associated with changes in connectedness. Design/methodology/approach Time-varying parameter vector autoregression (TVP-VAR) is used to estimate the Total Connectedness Index (TCI) across GCC stock markets from (2018–2022). Moreover, behavioral regressions over the first wave (January–August 2020) assess the role of VIX, Google Trends-based regional attention (GTR), and their interaction. Findings TCI nearly doubled from 31.94% during the pre-COVID period to 64.25% throughout the crisis. After controlling for oil volatility, neither VIX nor GTR was significant. Notwithstanding, their interaction is positive and statistically significant, nearly doubling the model's explanatory power. Given fundamental controls, Granger causality tests show unidirectional precedence from GTR to TCI in bivariate specifications. Results hold despite the exclusion of March 2020 and the addition of COVID-19 case growth. Originality/value This study integrates TVP-VAR connectedness with behavioral finance theory in GCC markets. Organisational Resilience and Distributor Satisfaction: The Moderating Role of Market Competitive Intensity in Beverage Manufacturing Firms
abstract: Purpose: This study examines the effects of four organisational resilience dimensions on distributor satisfaction among beverage manufacturers in North-Central Nigeria and tests the moderating role of competitive intensity. Design/Methodology/Approach: A cross-sectional survey design was adopted. Data were collected from the census population of 206 distributors of a leading beverage manufacturer operating in the Abuja cluster of North-Central Nigeria, yielding 183 valid responses (88.8% response rate). Data were analysed using covariance-based confirmatory factor analysis and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). Research Limitation: The study draws on distributors of a single beverage manufacturer within one geographic cluster, which may limit the generalisability of findings to other manufacturers, product categories or regions. Findings: The measurement model demonstrated adequate reliability (Cronbach's alpha 0.735–0.874; composite reliability 0.735–0.875), convergent validity (AVE 0.502–0.694) and discriminant validity (HTMT < 0.90), and the estimated model showed a satisfactory fit to the data (χ²/df = 1.785, RMSEA = 0.056, SRMR = 0.052, CFI = 0.955). title: When Do Organizational Capabilities Matter Most? Environmental Dynamism as a Boundary Condition in an Emerging-Market Telecommunications Sector
abstract: Organizational capabilities are widely recognized as key drivers of firm performance; however, their value depends on the environmental conditions in which they are deployed. This study considers environmental dynamism as a boundary condition that influences the relationship between organizational capabilities and organizational performance in an emerging-market telecommunications sector. This research is grounded mainly in Contingency Theory, with further insights from Dynamic Capabilities Theory. It views organizational capabilities as encompassing marketing, learning, innovation, and integrative dimensions. In examining organizational performance, the study distinguishes explicitly between financial and non-financial outcomes. To gather data, the study conducted a cross-sectional survey targeting managers from four leading telecommunications operators in Nigeria. Of the 364 questionnaires distributed, 289 were returned and deemed usable, yielding a robust response rate of 79.4%. The hypotheses were tested using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), incorporating 5,000 bootstrap resamples to ensure statistical rigor. Results indicate that organizational capabilities are positively associated with financial performance (β = .40, p < .001) and non-financial performance (β = .47, p < .001). Environmental dynamism is also positively associated with both fi…

Emergency preparedness knowledge and training needs among community volunteers in Shanghai, China, during the 2022 COVID-19 response: a cross-sectional questionnaire study
abstract: Background Community volunteers support community-level emergency response, but in China they are typically mobilized on an ad hoc basis, without standardized entry requirements or systematic training. Their task-specific knowledge during actual public health emergencies has rarely been measured directly. Objective This study assessed emergency preparedness knowledge and its demographic and training-related correlates among community volunteers during the 2022 COVID-19 response in Shanghai, China. Methods A cross-sectional survey of community volunteers in Songjiang District, Shanghai, was conducted in May 2022 using convenience sampling. Knowledge was measured with an 18-item scale across five domains: COVID-19 transmission, hand hygiene, personal protective equipment (PPE) use, disinfection, and medical waste disposal; the maximum score was 18 points. Groups were compared using t -tests and one-way ANOVA with Bonferroni correction; multivariable linear regression identified independent correlates of the knowledge score. Results Of 600 questionnaires distributed, 514 (85.67%) were analyzed after excluding 33 that were not returned and 53 that were incomplete. The mean knowledge score was 14.11 (SD 2.19) out of 18 points; item accuracy ranged from 30.54 to 99.81%, with eight of 18 items below the 75% mastery threshold. Accuracy was highest for medical waste disposal (94.70%) an…

title: Effect of immunosuppressive drugs on glucose-stimulated insulin secretion: concentration-response studies in dynamic perifusion assays
abstract: Immunosuppressive drugs, which are required to maintain graft function in transplant recipients, are associated with many unavoidable side effects including posttransplant diabetes mellitus (PTDM) that involves both peripheral insulin resistance and impairment of insulin secretion. To characterize in detail the concentration-dependency of the effect of well-known immunosuppressive drugs on glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS), we performed dynamic perifusion studies with human pancreatic islets. The effect on the time-profile of GSIS has been assessed over a wide concentration range for several clinically relevant immunomodulatory therapies, including small-molecule drugs (cyclosporine, sirolimus, tacrolimus, prednisolone acetate, and loteprednol etabonate) and biologics (abatacept and anti-CD40L), plus a prospective β-cell proliferation-inducing agent (harmine). While biologics showed no significant detrimental effects after one-day treatment even at relatively high concentrations (5 µM), all small-molecule drugs inhibited insulin secretion in a concentration-dependent manner, although glucocorticoids showed a distinct response pattern. Calcineurin and mTOR inhibitors preserved GSIS within their therapeutic ranges but progressively distorted its time-profile at higher concentrations and completely suppressed secretion at the highest levels, where they were also cytotoxi…

CEDAW, Digital Violence and State Due Diligence: Assessing India’s Response within a Global Framework
abstract: Abstract Online gender-based violence (OGBV) is escalating worldwide. This article argues that the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW), read together with its General Recommendations, provides an operationalizable due diligence framework for evaluating state responsibility for OGBV across prevention, protection, prosecution, punishment and reparation. It develops this argument through India, where a rapidly expanding digital-regulatory landscape offers an important site for assessing how due diligence obligations are translated into domestic law, enforcement, intermediary regulation and civil-society interventions. The article assesses the state’s alignment with CEDAW and identifies structural challenges hindering compliance, including regulatory fragmentation, weak enforcement, limited cross-sectoral coordination, inadequate remedies, competing rights concerns and entrenched misogyny. It provides a structured method for assessing state accountability and shows that digital due diligence must be operationalised through coordinated, survivor-centred, rights-sensitive digital governance. It advances debates on digital governance, gender justice and state responsibility under international law.

title: Perspectives on Credit Ratings: A Response to Reviews on “Rating Politics”
abstract: Abstract I would like to thank Matthias Thiemann and Yuri Biondi for organizing this symposium on Rating Politics and Jacqueline Best, Quentin Bruneau and Alexandra Ouroussoff for their generous reading and inspiring comments. In my response to them, I elaborate on the strengths and weaknesses of the “financial infrastructures” approach to credit ratings. I argue that this approach allows for better understanding the dependence of both states and markets on credit ratings and the counter-intuitive incentive structure that shapes rating agencies’ behavior. At the same time, this approach yields a structuralist argument that has limitations when exploring the role of ideational factors in credit rating decisions.

title: Durable complete response to tislelizumab in advanced pMMR cervical cancer and successful rechallenge after immune-related NSTEMI: a case report
abstract: Background Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have substantially improved long-term oncologic outcomes in patients with advanced malignancies; however, ICI-related cardiovascular adverse events have emerged as a growing clinical challenge. Accumulating clinical evidence confirms that ICI treatment markedly increases the risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Although cardiovascular toxicities secondary to ICIs are relatively infrequent, these complications carry severe and potentially fatal clinical consequences. Herein, we describe a rare case of acute non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) complicated by accelerated atherosclerosis potentially associated with ICI therapy in a middle-aged woman with advanced cervical squamous cell carcinoma harboring proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) status. Following successful coronary revascularization, the patient safely reinitiated immunotherapy and achieved long-term sustained tumor-free survival. Case presentation A 39-year-old woman was diagnosed with International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage IVB cervical squamous cell carcinoma, with comorbid type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension. abstract: Abstract Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains an aggressive disease with limited treatment options. Oncolytic adenoviruses represent a promising platform, but their efficacy as single agents is often insufficient. This study examined whether an oncolytic adenovirus co-delivering decorin (DCN) and CD40 ligand (CD40L), designated rAd.DCN.CD40L, could enhance antitumor activity and immune activation against TNBC. Recombinant adenoviruses expressing DCN (rAd.DCN), CD40L (rAd.CD40L), or both proteins were constructed and evaluated in breast cancer cells using cell viability, apoptosis, migration, invasion, and damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) release assays. Compared with rAd.DCN or rAd.CD40L alone, rAd.DCN.CD40L triggered greater apoptosis and tumor cell death and elicited more pronounced DAMP release. Co-culture experiments also revealed enhanced dendritic cell function following rAd.DCN.CD40L treatment. For in vivo evaluation, syngeneic 4T1 and EMT-6 subcutaneous tumor models and a 4T1 lung metastasis model were employed. rAd.DCN.CD40L substantially delayed tumor growth and improved survival in tumor-bearing mice. Flow cytometric and histological analyses further confirmed enhanced local and systemic T-cell responses, elevated CD8⁺ T-cell activity, and modulated inflammatory macrophage phenotypes. title: Supernatants from stored platelet concentrates modulate the inflammatory response in platelet-depleted blood ex vivo
abstract: Introduction Platelets contain a wide range of bioactive mediators, many of which accumulate during storage of platelet concentrates and have immunomodulatory properties. Our objective was to investigate how mediators derived from stored platelet concentrates modulate the acute inflammatory response using an ex vivo model. Methods Platelet-depleted whole blood from healthy donors (n=8) was supplemented with pooled platelet concentrate supernatants generated from six platelet concentrates sampled on storage days 1, 3, 5, and 7, and incubated with or without heat-inactivated Escherichia coli for four hours at 37 °C. Inflammatory responses were assessed by measuring complement activation, platelet-derived mediators, and cytokines. Results In the absence of E. coli , addition of platelet concentrate supernatants increased the levels of 24 of 32 measured inflammatory mediators. In contrast, under E. coli -stimulated conditions, the supernatants increased 10 markers and attenuated 14 markers, including the key pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF. The attenuation of these cytokines ranged from 25-43%, whereas several other mediators were unchanged or increased. The majority of biomarkers showed limited differences across the investigated storage time points. Conclusions Our findings demonstrate that soluble factors released from platelet concentrates can modulate inflammat…

abstract: This study aims to develop and standardize a test to measure motor response speed using auditory stimuli colors among fourth-year students at College of Physical Education and Sports Sciences, Kirkuk University. title: MSMEs financing and bank profitability: evidence from Saudi Arabia’s dual banking system
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine the impact of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) financing on the profitability of Saudi Arabia’s dual banking system. Design/methodology/approach This study applies the random effect model on the manually collected MSMEs financing data set from the annual reports of the Saudi Arabia 3 full-fledged Islamic banks (FIBs) and 6 hybrid conventional banks (HCBs)- conventional banks with Islamic windows over the 2018–2023 period. Findings The findings of this study show that MSME financing has statistically significant positive impacts on overall bank profitability. However, when we estimate FIBs and HCBs separately, the findings show that the impact of MSME financing on the profitability of FIBs is also positive and statistically significant. Notably, the findings are economically significant and are robust even when we apply alternative dependent variables and econometric models. While the overall MSMEs total financing increases the mean value of the profitability [return on assets (ROA)] of the overall banks by 12%, it boosts the mean value of the profitability (ROA) of the FIBs by 23%. title: Weaving History: A New Historicist Dialogue on Power, Anxiety, and Spider Imagery in Whitman and Yuan Mei
abstract: This study aims to examine the spider imagery in Walt Whitman’s and Yuan Mei’s poetry through a New Historicist lens. It reveals the role this imagery plays in a cross-cultural dialogue on power and anxiety. By integrating Foucault’s “power discourse”, Greenblatt’s “cultural negotiation” and Althusser’s “symptomatic reading”, the analysis proceeds from imagistic essence to strategic deployment and finally to structural metaphor. At the level of imagistic essence, Whitman’s spider condenses the spiritual symbol of an expansive, foundational self in early America, while Yuan Mei’s spider, through its operation of a “selective web”, reveals the pragmatic, calculating nature of power within the peak of Qing Dynasty. At the level of textual dialogue, Whitman’s constructive poetics actively participates in shaping an emerging national mythology, whereas Yuan Mei’s deconstructive irony deftly punctures the latent rules and unspoken compromises of the proclaimed prosperous age. At the level of power structure, the “radially expansive” power metaphor embodied by Whitman’s spider reflects a distinct modern “anxiety of blankness”, while the “centripetally selective” power mapped by Yuan Mei’s spider corresponds to the late imperial “anxiety of density”. Together, they demonstrate how poetic imagery, by engaging in the negotiation and articulation of contemporary power discourses, vividly …

abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore the relationship between artificial intelligence (AI) disclosure and bank profitability, and to assess whether family ownership plays a moderating role in this relationship. It takes into account the trade-off between increased disclosure and near-term profitability pressure, as well as how family ownership reduces that effect. Design/methodology/approach The study utilizes a balanced panel data of 14 banks included in the Amman Stock Exchange (ASE) for the period 2015–2024, which provides a total of 140 bank-year observations. Ordinary least squares regressions are employed to explore the association between AI-related disclosure and bank profitability, measured by return on assets (ROA) and return on equity (ROE), and the moderating effect of family ownership. In order to mitigate the potential endogeneity concerns and evaluate the robustness of the results, two-stage least squares (2SLS) estimations are conducted. Findings AI-related disclosure is negatively and significantly associated with bank profitability (ROE and ROA), showing that greater disclosure does not necessarily imply positive financial outcomes. title: Family firm finance research in the MENA region: a bibliometric analysis
abstract: Purpose This study maps the development and structure of family firm finance research in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, focusing on its financial themes, theoretical foundations, methodological approaches, and geographical patterns. Design/methodology/approach A bibliometric analysis of 116 Scopus-indexed articles published between 2008 and 2025 was conducted. Bibliometrix and VOSviewer were used to analyze scientific production, contributors, keywords, co-occurrence networks, thematic clusters, and research trends. Findings Research has expanded considerably in recent years but remains geographically concentrated. Financial governance and financial performance dominate the literature, whereas investment, cash-holding, and particularly dividend policies remain underexplored. Quantitative methods prevail, while Socioemotional Wealth, Agency, and Institutional theories constitute the main theoretical foundations. The Journal of Family Business Management emerges as the most relevant journal in the field. The analysis also reveals geographical differences in research themes and methodological approaches across the MENA region. title: A Smart Mental Health Monitoring System using Computer Vision and Physiological Signal Analysis
abstract: Mental health disorders such as stress, anxiety, and mental fatigue have become increasingly prevalent in modern society due to rapid technological advancements, increased workload, and prolonged screen exposure. Continuous stress without proper monitoring can lead to severe physical and psychological health problems. Traditional stress detection methods rely on manual observation, questionnaires, or clinical diagnosis, which are often timeconsuming and unsuitable for real-time monitoring. This paper proposes a real-time mental health monitoring system that utilizes multimodal artificial intelligence techniques combined with webcam-based facial analysis and Internet of Things (IoT) physiological sensing. The system collects facial expressions through a webcam and physiological parameters such as heart rate and body temperature through IoT sensors. Machine learning and deep learning algorithms process the collected data to identify stress patterns and classify stress levels accurately. The system generates alerts when abnormal stress levels are detected and stores data for further analysis. The proposed system improves detection accuracy by integrating multiple data sources and enables continuous monitoring of mental health conditions. The system can be implemented in workplaces, educational institutions, healthcare facilities, and remote monitoring environments to support early…

title: Baree (Homestead Garden) as a Socio-Ecological System in Rural Assam-A Review
abstract: The traditional Baree, or homestead-based production system, is an important component of rural landscapes in Assam. Often perceived simply as a household garden, Baree is in fact a multifunctional socio-ecological system where biodiversity, food production, livelihoods, traditional knowledge and human well-being are closely interconnected. A typical Baree may contain many plant species including fruit trees, vegetables, spices, medicinal plants, bamboo and other multipurpose species, together with birds, insects, soil organisms and other associated biodiversity. These components collectively provide food, income, ecosystem services and cultural benefits. This review examines the Baree from a socio-ecological perspective with a focus on its contributions to biodiversity conservation, food and nutritional security, livelihood diversification and human well-being. It also discusses emerging pressures such as commercialisation, land-use change, biodiversity loss, changing lifestyles, erosion of traditional knowledge and climate change. The review argues that the value of Baree should not be assessed only through its direct economic output. Its ecological, nutritional, social and cultural functions must be considered together. Recognizing Baree as a multifunctional socio-ecological system can support more sustainable, biodiversity-friendly and climate-resilient approaches to rural …

PTSs not only decrease the specimen turnaround time but also reduce the burden of manual transportation. However, different types of automatic transmission systems or different design schemes may have various impacts on the samples. Therefore, laboratories should conduct an evaluation prior to using PTSs to understand their effects on laboratory tests. We aimed to explore the impact of PTSs on urine, haematology, coagulation, and biochemical and immunological test parameters. Methods We compared the effects of PTS and manual transport on test results. title: Management of headwater catchments: cultural background, science and policy
abstract: Headwater catchments serve as water towers and initial regulatory buffers against hydrometeorological hazards, yet they face several forms of degradation from unsustainable land use and accelerating climate change. We argue that effective headwater control requires an integrated approach combining watershed governance, science, policy, and cultural background. Old societies showed considerable capacity to solve hydraulic problems but did not fully understand watershed runoff formation and downstream impacts. Effective ecological engineering in headwaters still requires a better understanding of detailed processes in the soil-vegetation complex and wider land use concerns. Religion and environmental ethics intersect as global faith traditions support ecological conservation as a moral imperative influencing how communities perceive, value, and protect natural resources. However, cultural and ethical values alone may be constrained by short-term human interests, human-centered worldviews, and social instability. Their contribution to headwater protection therefore depends on how such values are translated into community participation, land-use decisions, and locally adapted governance. Compared to blanket legislative regulation of ‘Protected Headwater Areas’, our case studies suggest a more effective strategy concentrated on a particular catchment outlet and combining technical, …

title: Working towards a triadic collaboration among teachers, academics, and community: a review of curriculum co-design
abstract: Purpose This review synthesises empirical studies on collaborative curriculum co-design involving schools, universities, and community stakeholders. It examines how different partnership configurations: teachers-community, academics-community, teachers-academics, and triadic collaborations are conceptualised, enacted, and studied in practice. The purpose is to identify common collaborative approaches, methodological trends, and reported strengths and challenges, with particular attention to the underexplored role of three-way partnerships. By mapping existing evidence, the review aims to inform more culturally responsive, equitable, and sustainable curriculum development and co-design practices across educational contexts. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a systematic review approach guided by PRISMA principles. Peer-reviewed empirical studies published since 2015 were identified through searches of five databases (ProQuest, Web of Science, Scopus, EBSCO, and PsycINFO) using a PCC framework. Records were independently screened by multiple reviewers, with disagreements resolved through consensus. Twenty-nine studies were included and categorised by collaboration type (teachers-community, academics-community, teachers-academics, and triadic). title: Transformational leadership and lecturer performance in Indonesian higher education: the mediating role of work motivation
abstract: Purpose This study examines whether work motivation mediates the relationship between transformational leadership and lecturer performance in Indonesian higher education, focusing on a private Islamic university context. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative ex post facto survey was conducted with 289 lecturers selected proportionally from a population of 754. Expert-validated questionnaires measured transformational leadership, work motivation and lecturer performance. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and structural equation modelling. Findings Transformational leadership, work motivation and lecturer performance were rated high. The final SEM model showed good fit (RMSEA = 0.029; GFI = 0.958; TLI = 0.991; CFI = 0.988). Transformational leadership significantly predicted work motivation, and work motivation significantly predicted lecturer performance. The direct influence of transformational leadership on lecturer performance was positive but insignificant, whereas the indirect influence through work motivation was significant. Research limitations/implications This study is subject to several limitations. abstract: Machine learning-based network intrusion detection systems often perform extremely well on standard test datasets. However, high accuracy on clean data does not necessarily mean that these models can withstand carefully designed input manipulation. In this study, we examine the robustness of three widely used classifiers, namely Random Forest, XGBoost, and a multilayer perceptron (MLP), using the InSDN dataset. The problem is treated as a binary classification task in which network traffic is categorized as either Normal or Attack. Before training the models, duplicate records were removed, while identifier and timestamp fields were excluded from the dataset. The remaining data was processed using training-only preprocessing, and the 40 features with the highest mutual information scores were selected for the experiments. The three classifiers were initially tested using an untouched test set to establish their performance under normal conditions. They were then evaluated against a controlled feature-space adversarial evasion procedure, where bounded directional perturbations were applied using normalized budgets of ε ∈ {0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.10}. The models achieved almost perfect results on the clean test set, with F1 scores of 99.9927% for Random Forest, 99.9952% for XGBoost, and 99.9855% for MLP. However, their performance changed considerably when adversarial perturbations …

title: A Development Model for Madura Batik Smes:
abstract: Purpose: This study examines the effects of brand image and product quality on customer satisfaction and purchase decisions among Madura Batik consumers, while also investigating the mediating role of customer satisfaction in these relationships. Research Method: A quantitative research design was employed involving 150 Madura Batik consumers in Pamekasan Regency, Indonesia. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to assess both direct and indirect relationships among brand image, product quality, customer satisfaction, and purchase decisions. Results and Discussion: The findings indicate that brand image and product quality positively and significantly influence customer satisfaction. Brand image, product quality, and customer satisfaction also positively affect purchase decisions. Furthermore, customer satisfaction significantly mediates the relationship between brand image and purchase decisions, highlighting its important role in translating positive brand perceptions into purchasing behavior. Implications: Madura Batik businesses should strengthen brand positioning and maintain consistent product quality to enhance customer satisfaction and encourage purchase decisions. Future studies may examine additional behavioral and cultural factors across broader consumer segments. Origina…

title: Pengaruh Kualitas Pelayanan dan Kedisiplinan Pegawai terhadap Kepuasan Masyarakat di Kantor Desa Kepudibener Lamongan
abstract: This study aims to determine the influence of service quality and employee discipline on public satisfaction at the Kepudibener Village Office, Turi District, Lamongan Regency, both partially and simultaneously. The study employs a quantitative approach with a causal design. The population consists of 881 households, with a sample of 90 respondents determined using the Slovin formula (10% margin of error). Random sampling was used as the sampling technique. Data were collected through interviews, questionnaires using a 1–5 Likert scale, and observation. The instruments comprised five service quality indicators (Parasuraman's SERVQUAL), five employee discipline indicators, and three public satisfaction indicators. Data analysis involved validity testing, Cronbach's Alpha reliability testing, multiple linear regression, t-tests (partial), and F-tests (simultaneous) using SPSS version 26.0. The results indicate that: (1) service quality has a positive and significant effect on public satisfaction (t-count 4.530 > t-table 1.66235; significance 0.000); (2) employee discipline has a positive and significant effect on public satisfaction (t-count 3.342 > t-table 1.66235; significance 0.001); and (3) simultaneously, both variables have a significant effect (F-count 13.229 > F-table 2.36; significance 0.000). The regression equation is Y = 3.590 + 0.231X₁ + 0.189X₂. Service quality and …

title: Driving organizational performance through OHS culture and management in manufacturing SMEs within construction supply chains
abstract: Introduction This study examines the relationships among Organizational Culture, Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Management, and Organizational Performance in manufacturing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) operating within construction supply chains in Norte de Santander, Colombia. Methods We collected survey data from 204 employees across 16 manufacturing SMEs and analyzed them using structural equation modeling (SEM). The model evaluated the direct relationships among the three constructs and the indirect effect of Organizational Culture on Organizational Performance through OHS Management. Results The results indicate that Organizational Culture is positively associated with OHS Management and Organizational Performance, while OHS Management is positively associated with Organizational Performance. The bootstrapped indirect effect supports OHS Management's partial mediating role. Discussion These findings suggest that Organizational Culture is associated with performance through two complementary pathways: a direct pathway involving shared values, managerial commitment, communication, and organizational practices, and an indirect pathway involving the institutionalization of OHS management practices. The study contributes to the literature by positioning OHS Management as an organizational mechanism that helps explain how cultural conditions relate to performan…

An optimized spectral flow cytometry pipeline for longitudinal blood leukocyte immunophenotyping reveals stable, individually distinct immune signatures
abstract: Introduction Peripheral blood leukocyte immunophenotyping offers a minimally invasive insight into an individual’s immune system and is an attractive biomarker for detecting and monitoring disease. Advances in high-parameter spectral flow cytometry now resolve leukocyte subsets in unprecedented detail, but this depth adds complexity to sample preparation, acquisition and analysis, introducing technical variability that can obscure the biological signatures required for longitudinal monitoring. Methods We built and validated an optimized, high-parameter spectral flow cytometry pipeline for repeated blood leukocyte profiling and asked whether the resulting signatures are stable and distinct enough to identify individuals over time. Results Using rainbow beads and monoclonal-antibody spectra, we confirmed that instrument performance and spectral unmixing remained stable across more than two years, and that this dual measure localized faults to either the instrument or a reagent. Against a stabilized biological-invariant control, gating built on the dimensionality-reduction method PaCMAP was substantially more reproducible between operators than traditional two-dimensional gating and produced cleaner populations. Chemical fixation and one-week antibody pre-storage preserved leukocyte composition, whereas delayed processing and, more severely, cryopreservation altered it, the latter…

title: Systematic evaluation of ETAS forecasting skill across 69 $$M_L \ge 6$$ earthquakes in Taiwan (1999–2024)
abstract: Abstract Operational earthquake forecasting (OEF) increasingly relies on the Epidemic-Type Aftershock Sequence (ETAS) model to provide short-term, time-dependent seismicity rates, yet whether the model performs consistently across Taiwan’s complex tectonic settings has not been systematically evaluated. This study retrospectively assesses the forecasting skill of a 2-D ETAS model across 69 $$M_L \ge 6$$ earthquakes in Taiwan between 1999 and 2024, computing forecasts at three model times (immediately before the mainshock, immediately after, and one hour later) and evaluating them against observed earthquakes with $$M_L \ge 2$$ , $$M_L \ge 3$$ , and $$M_L \ge 4$$ using the Molchan diagram. Forecasting skill improves as the target-aftershock magnitude threshold is raised, because larger-magnitude events concentrate more strongly within the high-seismicity-rate region. Pre-event forecasting skill remains limited unless preceding activity has already concentrated the seismicity rate around the impending epicenter, as exemplified by the 2022 Taitung sequence, in which the $$M_L$$ 6.6 event on 17 September produced a concentrated hotspot that encompassed the $$M_L$$ 6.8 event on 18 September. Once a mainshock has occurred, forecasting skill improves within the first hour as each newly recorded aftershock refines the high-seismicity-rate region, although the $$M_L \ge 2$$ comparison r…

title: Random analog prediction provides a benchmark for seasonal Arctic sea ice extent forecasting
abstract: Abstract We develop a random analog predictor (RAP) algorithm for the forecasting of Arctic sea ice extent (SIE) on seasonal timescales. This is a stochastic variant for scalar time series of the method of the analogues that only uses the historical SIE record to produce ensemble forecasts. When comparing the observations with the most representative forecast of the ensemble (as identified through the band–depth, a centrality measure for functional data) the algorithm shows negligible bias and RMSE no larger than $$0.6\cdot 10^6$$ km $$^2$$ . Hindcasts of the September average SIE show a level of skill comparable to that of the models of the Sea Ice Prediction Network. We argue that simplicity, interpretability, independence on physical hypotheses, and the ability to attach an uncertainty estimate to its own forecasts, should make RAP a necessary baseline for physics–based and AI–based models alike: failure to outperform RAP should be considered as a serious shortcoming for models aiming at realistically describing sea ice dynamics.

title: Deep learning-based prediction of HER2 status from breast diffusion-weighted MRI
abstract: Background and objective The accurate classification of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) status is very important for the diagnosis and treatment of breast cancer. However, the biopsy, the current gold standard for differentiating HER2 status, is invasive and time-consuming. To overcome these drawbacks, a novel deep learning model was developed to differentiate HER2-negative and HER2-positive status in breast cancer solely based on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI). Materials and methods This retrospective study included 239 women patients confirmed with breast cancer from two local medical centers. A hybrid CNN-Transformer DL model was proposed, which took DWI images (the ADC maps, DWI images with b = 0 s/mm² and b = 800 s/mm²) as inputs and output the classification of HER2-negative and HER2-positive status. Classification by the proposed DL model was quantitatively compared to the classification by the other benchmark DL models and two clinical experts. Results Data of the 239 patients (mean age, 49.4 ± 10.0 years) were separated into a training set (n = 156), an internal test set (n = 39), and an external test set (n = 44). On the internal test set, the proposed DL model performed numerically better than the best benchmark DL model (area under the curve [AUC]: 0.93 vs. 0.89; accuracy: 0.90 vs. 0.85). On the external test set, the proposed model also performed …
