Biological interaction fingerprints improve prediction of drug-induced steatosis
abstract: Abstract Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) is a major safety concern in drug development, with steatosis constituting a relevant toxicological phenotype within DILI. Current in vitro assays typically rely on lipid accumulation measurements in hepatocyte models, capturing only selected aspects of the underlying biology. Computational approaches complement these assays by leveraging machine learning to detect multivariate and nonlinear patterns relevant to steatosis. In this study, we developed binary classification models using steatosis-positive drugs curated from the Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) and steatosis-negative compounds from the DILIst dataset. Separate models were trained on chemical (PubChem fingerprint) and biological features (target and pathway fingerprints). Biological fingerprints significantly outperformed the chemical fingerprint, highlighting the added predictive value of target- and pathway-level information for steatosis prediction. The outputs of all three models were combined into a consensus classifier using majority voting, which achieved a balanced accuracy of 0.72 and a sensitivity of 0.69 in 5×2 repeated cross-validation, comparable to the individual biological fingerprint models. To challenge model generalizability, the 10% most dissimilar compounds based on maximum Tanimoto similarity were withheld as an extern…

title: AIPFusion-Net: an interaction-fusion framework for anti-inflammatory peptide prediction using protein language model embeddings, local sequence patterns, and handcrafted descriptors
abstract: Introduction Anti-inflammatory peptides (AIPs) are promising candidates for treating inflammatory diseases. However, experimental identification is time-consuming and costly, creating a need for accurate computational prediction methods. Methods We developed AIPFusion-Net, an interaction-fusion framework that integrates three complementary sources of peptide information: global contextual embeddings generated by the ESM2 protein language model, local sequence patterns extracted from biologically relevant subsequences, and handcrafted physicochemical and sequence descriptors. These representations were integrated through an interaction-fusion module and evaluated on two independent test datasets, Ind-1049 and Ind-426. Results On the Ind-1049 dataset, AIPFusion-Net achieved an accuracy of 84.6%, sensitivity of 71.7%, specificity of 89.3%, MCC of 0.654, and AUC of 0.884. On the Ind-426 dataset, it achieved an accuracy of 82.3%, sensitivity of 84.4%, specificity of 76.9%, MCC of 0.673, and AUC of 0.882. The model outperformed the comparative predictors in overall classification performance and discriminative ability. Discussion The results indicate that combining global contextual information, local sequence patterns, and handcrafted descriptors through interaction fusion improves the representation and identification of AIPs. AIPFusion-Net provides a useful computational framework…

title: Early prediction of gestational diabetes mellitus using deep learning applied to routinely collected clinical data
abstract: Background Prediction of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) in early pregnancy enables timely, targeted interventions to reduce risks for both the mother and fetus. We aimed to improve early GDM prediction and clinical risk stratification using a novel deep learning (DL) approach that transforms tabular clinical data into images using a genetic algorithm. Methods A dataset of 1,611 pregnancies was used. The dataset contained routinely collected early-pregnancy data, including clinical measurements, blood tests, and medical history. A novel method to transform tabular data into images was applied to enable the use of deep learning models for GDM prediction. A genetic algorithm optimized the spatial arrangement of variables during image generation by determining their spatial positions. Interpretability was assessed using gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) to identify variables the model preferentially attended to for positive and negative predictions. Results Multiple model configurations were evaluated by varying the spatial arrangement of variables within the transformation. Prioritizing high sensitivity, one model achieved an accuracy of 0.86, sensitivity of 0.82, specificity of 0.87, and an AUC-ROC of 0.83. Another model achieved an accuracy of 0.79, sensitivity of 0.92, specificity of 0.77, and an AUC-ROC of 0.85. Compared with previously published machi…

title: An interpretable feature-augmented stacked ensemble framework for student dropout prediction
abstract: Abstract Student dropout prediction is regarded as one of the significant research fields in educational data mining. It aids the sustainability of institutions and early interventions in schools. This study proposes an Enhanced Stacked Dropout Predictor (eSDP), which is a feature-enhanced hybrid stacking framework. The proposed framework combines heterogeneous base learner predictions with important original student-level features during meta-learning. As level-0 learners, Gradient Boosting, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, and Logistic Regression were adopted, whereas the meta-learner was Gradient Boosting. To compare the proposed feature-augmented stacking with the stacking strategy, another feedforward neural network (FNN)-based stacking ensemble was implemented as a comparative baseline. A synthetic educational dataset was used for the experimental assessment with 7,000 student records. The proposed eSDP framework achieved the highest overall predictive accuracy of all the models tested, with an F1-score of 0.928 and ROC-AUC of 0.987. The framework showed competitive results and Friedman and Nemenyi analyses were used for comparative ranking of the models evaluated. The framework’s predictive ability was also evaluated at the cross-dataset level by replicating the framework on an independent education dataset that showed a decrease in predictive ability compared to t…

title: A primary care-oriented framework for osteoporosis prediction: integrating multi-algorithm feature selection and machine learning model benchmarking
abstract: Summary Large-scale screening and primary care diagnosis of osteoporosis are challenging due to the limited availability of dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Therefore, predictive models for osteoporosis that do not rely on bone mineral density measurements are essential. Using routine health examination data and applying a consensus feature selection strategy, we constructed machine learning (ML)-based models and compared their performance across multiple dimensions. Purpose To develop a robust, low-cost, and interpretable framework for osteoporosis prediction based on readily available information, which can be easily integrated into electronic health systems to inform DXA referral in resource-limited settings. Methods Variables covered by the basic health examination package were obtained from participants who underwent health examinations between January 2024 and January 2025. We implemented a strategy in which only features selected by at least four out of the seven feature selection methods were retained. Six ML algorithms were employed to develop models, and their prediction performances were compared across discrimination, goodness-of-fit, and clinical utility. Results A total of 2,260 participants were included, with an osteoporosis prevalence of 7.1%. Eight features: age, sex, body mass index, alkaline phosphatase, hematocrit, high-density lipoprotein, urea, and…

title: Artificial intelligence for craniofacial and mandibular growth prediction: A systematic review
abstract: Abstract Objectives The primary objective was to evaluate the predictive performance of artificial intelligence (AI) models for craniofacial and mandibular growth prediction. Secondary objectives were to assess methodological quality and identify research gaps. Materials and methods Nine databases were searched through August 12, 2026, supplemented by manual searches. Human studies assessing AI-based models for craniofacial or mandibular growth prediction were included. Study characteristics, prediction intervals, AI approaches, performance metrics, and validation strategies were extracted. Risk of bias and applicability were assessed using PROBAST. Results Twelve studies were included. Six assessed overall craniofacial growth, whereas six mandibular development. Prediction horizons ranged from ≤ 1.5 to approximately 10 years, with sample sizes of 33–639 participants. Predictive accuracy varied by anatomical region and methodological approach. Sex and malocclusion type were frequently used to define study populations but were not consistently incorporated as predictors, whereas ethnicity and skeletal maturation were rarely considered. Seven studies had overall high risk of bias and five unclear risk, mainly due to analytical limitations and inadequate validation. Conclusion AI-based models show promising predictive performance; however, current evidence is insufficient to estab…

Load, Work Discipline, Performance Assessment and Financial Rewards on Account Representative Performance at The Sukoharjo Pratama Tax Service Office
abstract: This study aims to examine and analyze the influence of workload, work discipline, performance appraisal, and financial reward on the performance of Account Representatives at the Sukoharjo Primary Tax Service Office, both partially and simultaneously. This study employs a quantitative research design. The population consists of all Account Representatives at the Sukoharjo Primary Tax Service Office, totaling 43 individuals. The research sample consists of the entire population of 43 individuals (all Account Representatives at the office). Data collection was conducted using questionnaires. Statistical analysis techniques used include multiple linear regression, the F-test, the t-test, and the coefficient of determination. The research results indicate that: (1) Workload does not have a significant effect on the performance of Account Representatives at KPP Pratama Sukoharjo; (2) Work discipline does not have a significant effect on the performance of Account Representatives at KPP Pratama Sukoharjo; (3) Performance appraisal does not have a significant effect on the performance of Account Representatives at KPP Pratama Sukoharjo; and (4) Financial reward does not have a significant effect on the performance of Account Representatives at KPP Pratama Sukoharjo. title: ​Digital Literacy, Local Tax Service Digitalization, and Tax Compliance: Evidence from Malang, Indonesia
abstract: Digital tax services are often treated as an uncomplicated route to compliance, although their effects depend on users' capabilities. This study examines whether digital literacy changes the relationship between perceived local tax service digitalization and taxpayer compliance in Malang, Indonesia. A cross-sectional questionnaire survey yielded 201 usable responses from individual and business taxpayers who used electronic local tax administration. Ten items measured each construct, and moderated regression analysis tested the proposed relationships. Digitalization (B=1.226, p<0.001) and digital literacy (B=1.650, p<0.001) were positively associated with compliance. Contrary to the hypothesized strengthening effect, their interaction was negative (B=-0.030, p<0.001). The model explained 73.0% of the variance in compliance. This pattern suggests diminishing dependence, digitally capable taxpayers may comply more independently, whereas less-capable users rely more heavily on service simplicity, stability, security, and support. This result does not make literacy undesirable. It shows that uniformly improving digital interfaces may produce unequal marginal gains. Local tax authorities should combine accessible system design with targeted assistance and capability building. Exploring Culturally Responsive Teaching Awareness in the Age of GenAI: Voices from Indonesian EFL Pre-Service Teachers
abstract: This study explores pre-service EFL teachers’ awareness of integrating GenAI into CRT in West Kalimantan, Indonesia. Using a qualitative descriptive design, data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 35 final-semester pre-service EFL teachers and analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s thematic analysis. Interview analysis reveals four interconnected dimensions of awareness: cognitive, pedagogical, critical/evaluative, and developmental. Participants recognized GenAI's limitations in representing local cultural knowledge, struggled to design culturally responsive prompts, and demonstrated the ability to identify cultural biases and inaccuracies in AI outputs. They also emphasized the need for practical training and institutional support to effectively integrate GenAI into culturally responsive learning. Based on these findings, this study proposes Culturally Responsive AI Literacy as a conceptual extension of AI literacy, positioning technical competence, critical evaluation, cultural knowledge, and pedagogical decision-making as integrated competencies. Keywords: culturally responsive teaching, generative AI, AI literacy, pre-service EFL teachers, teacher education.

title: Occupational burnout among medical staff in a designated infectious disease hospital in Lanzhou: differences by length of service
abstract: Objective To investigate the current status of occupational burnout among medical staff with different lengths of service in a designated infectious disease hospital in Lanzhou, and to analyze inter-group differences so as to provide a basis for stratified interventions. Methods In May 2025, a questionnaire survey was conducted among 290 on-duty medical staff of the hospital, and 278 valid questionnaires were returned (valid response rate: 95.86%). Occupational burnout was assessed with the Chinese revised version of the Maslach Burnout Inventory–Human Services Survey (MBI-HSS), and burnout level was classified according to the criteria proposed by Li Yongxin et al. The Kruskal-Wallis H test was used to compare groups based on measurement data; the Fisher-Freeman-Halton test was used to compare groups based on burnout levels; and Spearman's rank correlation analysis was used to examine the relationship between burnout levels and years of service. Results The overall detection rate of occupational burnout was 66.91% (186/278). Total burnout scores did not differ significantly across groups (H = 8.956, P = 0.111). Scores on the diminished personal accomplishment dimension differed significantly among groups ( H = 13.409, P = 0.020), with the 21–25-year group scoring higher than the 0–5-year group (adjusted P = 0.045). title: Meritocracy Versus Patronage: The Impact of Political Connections on Administrative Efficiency in Nigeria's Public Service
abstract: The debate between meritocracy and political patronage remains a central concern in public administration, particularly in developing democracies where political considerations often shape bureaucratic processes. This study examines the impact of political connections on administrative efficiency in Nigeria's public service through a qualitative desk review approach. Anchored on Weberian Bureaucratic Theory, the study investigates how merit-based administrative principles and patronage-driven practices influence bureaucratic performance, service delivery, and institutional effectiveness. Adopting a qualitative desk review approach, the study synthesizes evidence from peer-reviewed journal articles, policy reports, and governance studies focusing on meritocracy, political patronage, recruitment practices, and public sector performance in Nigeria and comparable developing-country contexts. The findings reveal a consistent positive relationship between meritocratic recruitment and administrative efficiency. Merit-based systems enhance professionalism, employee commitment, organizational productivity, and policy implementation by ensuring that public positions are occupied by competent and qualified personnel. Conversely, the review identifies political patronage, manifested through clientelism, godfatherism, nepotism, and politically motivated appointments, as a major impediment t…

title: Service Quality, Facilities and Infrastructure, Interpersonal Communication, and Accommodation Image on Customer Satisfaction in Nakula Sadewa BBGTK Hospitality
abstract: The purpose of this study is to test and analyze the influence of service quality, facilities and infrastructure, interpersonal communication and lodging image on customer satisfaction in using Wisma Nakula Sadewa in BBGTK Central Java Province. This type of research is quantitative research. This research took place in The research was conducted at the office of the Center for Teachers and Education Personnel (BBGTK) Central Java Province. Data collection techniques through questionnaires. The research sample was 100 respondents. Data analysis techniques used multiple regression tests, F tests, t tests, and determination tests (R2). Based on the results of research that has been done on the influence of Service Quality, Facilities and Infrastructure, Interpersonal Communication and Lodging Image on Customer Satisfaction in using Wisma Nakula Sadewa in BBGTK Central Java Province, it can be concluded that service quality influences customer satisfaction in using Wisma Nakula Sadewa. Facilities and infrastructure influence customer satisfaction. Interpersonal communication influences customer satisfaction. Image of the accommodationinfluences customer satisfaction. A positive image created through good service, adequate facilities, and a comfortable environment can increase customer trust and satisfaction in using Wisma Nakula Sadewa.

title: Preferred service model and other factors associated with pre-exposure prophylaxis willingness among Indonesian men who have sex with men: analysis of PrEP APPEAL survey
abstract: Background Men who have sex with men (MSM) are disproportionately affected by HIV in Indonesia. To prevent transmission, there is a need to scale-up HIV prevention, especially pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP). This analysis aims to identify the preferred service model and factors associated with PrEP willingness among MSM. Methods PrEP APPEAL was an online cross-sectional survey conducted among MSM in 15 Asian countries/territories, including Indonesia, about preferences for PrEP service delivery. Participants included MSM aged >18 years who believed themselves to be HIV-negative. This analysis is limited to Indonesian participants. Participants were asked about their preferences for the PrEP regimen, willingness to pay and whether they would prefer healthcare workers who are MSM. A discrete choice experiment was also conducted to identify preferences for PrEP service models across six attributes (regimen, location, cost, visit frequency, side-effects and extra services), each with three to five levels. Logistic regression was conducted to identify factors associated with willingness to use PrEP, and latent class analysis was conducted to identify classes with similar service model preferences. Results The analysis included 1139 participants with a mean age of 30.6 years (s.d. 7.5). Service model preferences associated with PrEP willingness included accepting (but not preferr…

title: Are Islamic features enough to fulfil ethical service expectations? Insights from customer emotions in mobile banking
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the influence of core Islamic mobile banking services and customer emotions on satisfaction using a text mining approach. Design/methodology/approach The paper applies a lexicon-based dictionary method to identify service quality dimensions of Islamic mobile banking in Indonesia and develops explanatory models using panel data regression. Findings The results reveal that ease of use, convenience, perceived usefulness and adherence to Islamic attributes significantly contribute to customer satisfaction. This reflects the fulfilment of customers’ right to service parity with mobile banking in general, which forms the basis of their ethical service expectations. Moreover, positive emotions positively influence customer satisfaction, whereas negative emotions have the opposite effect. These findings demonstrate that core services in Islamic banking encompass beyond merely following Islamic principles; they also require reliable and user-centered operational performance. Therefore, Islamic banks should prioritize improvements in system updates, verification processes, financial and banking functionalities, and overall system stability. Deficiencies in these fundamental service attributes generate negative emotional responses, signaling unmet ethical service expectations and ultimately undermining customer satisfaction. Research limitations/implicat…

title: Service Quality, Waiting Time, Therapeutic Communication and Infrastructure on Patient Satisfaction
abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of service quality, waiting time, therapeutic communication, and infrastructure on the satisfaction of outpatients participating in BPJS at Gantiwarno Community Health Center, Klaten Regency. The study used a quantitative approach with a survey method. The study population was outpatients participating in BPJS with an average of 2,000 visits over the past three months. The study sample consisted of 100 respondents selected using probability sampling techniques with a random sampling method. Data collection was carried out through distributing questionnaires, while data analysis used multiple linear regression. The results of the study show Based on the results of data analysis and hypothesis testing, it can be concluded that work discipline and transfers have a positive and significant effect on job satisfaction and employee performance at the Surakarta Class IA Religious Court. In addition, job satisfaction is also proven to have a positive and significant effect on employee performance. The results of the study indicate that job satisfaction acts as a mediating variable that is able to positively and significantly mediate the effect of work discipline on employee performance, as well as positively and significantly mediate the effect of transfers on employee performance.

title: Graphite-induced interface regulation in hard carbon for high-performance sodium-ion storage
abstract: In this work, we propose a graphite-induced interface strategy, in which pre-carbonized coconut shell carbon is wrapped with graphite paper and then carbonized. This process induces ordered rearrangement of carbon atoms on the hard carbon surface, forming ion transport channels composed of graphitic domains. These channels lower the kinetic barrier for Na+ entry into the internal closed pores, thereby converting inaccessible closed pores into accessible ones. The designed hard carbon achieves a high specific capacity of 359.64 mAh g−1 at 30 mA g−1, with a plateau contribution of 215.08 mAh g−1 and an excellent initial Coulombic efficiency of 91.21%.

title: PolyAnalysis: a deep learning–based framework for nanopore-based poly(A) tail estimation and 3′-end regulation profiling
abstract: Abstract Background Polyadenylation at the 3′ end of mRNA regulates transcript stability, export, and translation, but poly(A) tail length and polyadenylation-site usage remain difficult to resolve from nanopore sequencing data because of homopolymer-associated errors and complex 3′ end architectures. We developed PolyAnalysis, a signal-level computational framework for estimating poly(A) tail length from raw Oxford Nanopore Technologies signals and linking per-read estimates to confidence-aware analyses of polyadenylation sites, alternative polyadenylation, and repetitive-element-associated 3′ ends. Results PolyAnalysis combines CNN–BiLSTM-based region classification with multi-task connectionist temporal classification decoding and adenine-aware training and decoding to infer poly(A)-proximal boundaries, tail length, and model-derived sequence features. Benchmarking against Nanopolish, tailfindr, and Dorado on controlled RNA002 and RNA004 datasets showed competitive tail-length accuracy and high callability. Component-wise ablation and bias-control analyses indicated that region classification, multi-task optimization, adenine-weighted loss, and A-rich decoding jointly contributed to performance. Application to human cell-line and vertebrate transcriptome datasets identified dataset-level variation in tail-length distributions, gene-level heterogeneity, and weak associations …

title: Health belief model constructs and sociodemographic factors associated with minimum meal frequency among children aged 6 to 23 months in Harar City, Eastern Ethiopia
abstract: Abstract Background Optimal nutrition in the first 24 months of life is vital for child development. While socioeconomic factors associated with feeding practices are well-documented, evidence regarding the psychosocial correlates of minimum meal frequency (MMF) in Eastern Ethiopia remains scarce. Objective To assess the magnitude of minimum meal frequency and identify Health Belief Model (HBM) constructs and sociodemographic factors associated with minimum meal frequency among children aged 6–23 months in Harar City, Eastern Ethiopia. Methods A facility-based analytical cross-sectional study was conducted from December 2023 to January 2024 among 514 mothers/caregivers of children aged 6–23 months attending three randomly selected public health centers in Harar City. Participants were selected using systematic random sampling. Minimum meal frequency was defined according to WHO guidelines: ≥2 meals (breastfed, 6–8 months); ≥3 meals (breastfed, 9–23 months); ≥4 feeds (non-breastfed, 6–23 months). The Health Belief Model (HBM) was applied to assess psychosocial factors, including perceived susceptibility, severity, benefits, barriers, and self-efficacy. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire administered via KoboToolbox. Bivariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed, and adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were …

title: A continuous spiral-spring triboelectric nanogenerator for energy harvesting and self-sensing under ultra-low-frequency rotation
abstract: Self-powered monitoring of slowly rotating components is hindered by the small relative speed and limited installation space available to conventional rotary triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs). Here, a continuously driven unidirectional rotary TENG (CDUR-TENG) is developed by integrating a multilayer spiral-spring electrode with a ratchet-triggered energy-storage/release mechanism. During winding, the spring stores elastic energy while its adjacent triboelectric interfaces progressively separate; ratchet disengagement then initiates rapid elastic recoil and concentrated charge transfer. The device therefore decouples the electrical pulse from the slow external rotation. At 0.2 Hz, the CDUR-TENG provides a peak-to-peak open-circuit voltage of approximately 130 V and a maximum short-circuit current of 55 μA; it transfers 0.165 μC per cycle and reaches a maximum instantaneous power of 2.182 mW at 1 Hz and 1.1 MΩ. The resulting normalized power density reaches 191.4 W m−3Hz−1, at least 8.57 times that of the compared rotary harvesters. Voltage signatures further distinguish operating angle, angular overshoot, and reverse rotation, demonstrating a compact route toward self-powered condition monitoring under ultra-low-frequency rotation.

Spatial surveillance of Plasmodium falciparum Kelch 13 mutations reveals High-Frequency A675V and the First Molecular Evidence of Suspected Partial Artemisinin Resistance in Baringo in Kenya
abstract: Abstract Background This surveillance study evaluated the polymorphisms of Pfk13 gene in samples from symptomatic individuals from eight geographically distinct locations in Kenya to determine the prevalence of mutations associated with partial artemisinin resistance. Methods Between 2018 and 2024, blood samples from individuals with symptoms of uncomplicated malaria at eight hospitals in four of the five distinct malaria transmission zones of Kenya were sequenced for single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in Pfk13 and Pfmdr1 . Subsequent positive samples were tested to monitor treatment outcomes. Results A total of 44/679 (6.5%) samples harbored 49 Pfk13 mutations. These include 14 nonsynonymous mutations at Pfk13: A675V ( n = 20, 2.9%), A578S ( n = 4, 0.6%), C469Y ( n = 3, 0.44%), V386A ( n = 1, 0.15%), P553L ( n = 1, 0.15%), R561H/P ( n = 1, 0.15%), S522C (n = 1, 0.15%), K455E ( n = 1, 0.15%), S600F ( n = 1, 0.15%), E612D ( n = 1, 0.15%), N489K (n = 1, 0.15%), F491L ( n = 1, 0.15%) plus A504V ( n = 1, 0.15%). Four WHO-validated markers of partial artemisinin resistance were detected in 25/679 (3.7%) samples. Most Pfk13 A675V mutations (n = 12, 1.8%) were detected in Baringo County, where the mutation frequency reached 16.9%, exceeding the WHO 5% threshold for classification of areas with suspected partial artemisinin resistance. This represents the first molecular evidence c…

title: Fe-mediated phase evolution and defect regulation in flexible Cu2Se films for enhanced thermoelectric transport
abstract: The monoclinic copper selenide (α-Cu2Se) is a promising thermoelectric (TE) material due to its ordered Cu sublattice and intrinsically low thermal conductivity for near-room-temperature applications. However, excessive Cu vacancies in α-Cu2Se lead to carrier overconcentration and limit TE performance, whereas the disordered Cu sublattice of β-Cu2Se provides a potential route for carrier transport regulation. In this work, flexible Fe-incorporated Cu2Se films were fabricated by combining low-temperature hydrothermal synthesis with screen printing and subsequent thermal annealing. Moderate Fe incorporation enables the controllable α/β phase evolution and defect landscape modulation, promoting structural reconstruction and optimizing Cu-related defect chemistry. Structural analysis is consistent with partial Fe occupation at Cu sites in β-Cu2Se, together with the formation of a crystalline Fe2O3 secondary phase. Such regulation exploits the complementary characteristics of ordered α-Cu2Se and defect-mediated β-Cu2Se, leading to a balanced carrier concentration and mobility relationship for enhanced thermoelectric transport. As a result, the optimized Fe-doped Cu2Se film exhibits a maximum power factor of 657 μW m−1 K−2 at room temperature. Furthermore, a flexible six-leg thermoelectric generator fabricated from the optimized film delivers an open-circuit voltage of ∼12 mV at ΔT =…

title: A fault-aware, explainable proximal policy optimization based intelligent control framework with neuromorphic-inspired encoding for voltage and frequency stability
abstract: Abstract High penetration of inverter-interfaced generation, faults, and sudden load changes in power systems makes them more vulnerable to voltage and frequency deviations. Traditional controllers often struggle to adapt to varying disturbance types and severities in real time. Adaptive, data-driven control methods are required for responding dynamically to such disturbances. The proposed research work addresses this need by combining Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based Reinforcement Learning (RL) with neuromorphic-inspired spike encoding, enabling temporally meaningful representation of system disturbances for interpretable and effective stability analysis in a simulation-based surrogate framework across different fault types. The controller adjusts its actions based on observed deviations in voltage and frequency. Instead of fixed control, the proposed framework enables dynamic fault-aware responses. For systematic fault investigation, a synthetic fault dataset is developed for the IEEE New England 39-bus system. It provides a controlled and flexible environment for reproducible experimentation and focused evaluation of the proposed strategy. The fault types covered are Single Line-to- Ground fault (SLG), Line-to-Line fault (LL), Line-to-Line-to Ground fault (LLG), and Three-Phase faults (3PH). Voltage deviations and frequency deviations capture the disturbances in the …

title: Creating Consistency in the Courtroom?: Chambers Practice Manuals and the Turn to Formal Regulation at the International Criminal Court
abstract: Abstract The establishment of the International Criminal Court (ICC) was intended to provide a stable framework for international criminal justice. Yet the Court’s hybrid legal structure has generated significant procedural challenges, including divergent working methods across chambers that reflect competing civil and common law traditions. In response, ICC judges have since 2015 adopted successive Chambers Practice Manuals to promote coherence through institutionalised best practices. This article argues, however, that these manuals offer only a limited contribution to consistency: they are non-binding, several solutions remain insufficiently tested, and the Court’s rotating judicial composition repeatedly disrupts continuity. Against this backdrop, recent years have witnessed a gradual but notable shift towards formalisation, with judges increasingly seeking to codify procedural practices through amendments to the Court’s regulatory framework. This article examines whether this turn to binding, formal mechanisms offers a more sustainable path to procedural coherence at the ICC, and what implications it holds for the Court’s evolving institutional identity.

title: Lipid metabolism: a potential checkpoint for cGAS-STING regulation in colorectal cancer
abstract: Immunotherapy for colorectal cancer (CRC) continues to face significant challenges, particularly in patients with microsatellite stable (MSS) tumors. The cyclic GMP–AMP synthase–stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS–STING) pathway is a key regulator of innate immunity and has emerged as a promising target for enhancing anti-tumor immune responses. Meanwhile, lipid metabolic reprogramming is a defining hallmark of CRC and contributes to tumor progression, evasion, and therapeutic resistance. Although direct evidence linking lipid metabolism to cGAS–STING signaling in CRC remains limited, accumulating studies from diverse disease models suggest extensive interactions between these two processes. This review summarizes the major features of lipid metabolic reprogramming in CRC and discusses current understanding of cGAS–STING signaling in tumor immunity. We further examine potential mechanisms by which lipid metabolism may influence cGAS–STING activity, including the regulation of mitochondrial DNA release, intracellular trafficking of signaling components and lipid-associated post-translational modifications. Emerging evidence also indicates that cGAS–STING signaling can affect lipid metabolic pathways by regulating lipid metabolic homeostasis and inducing lipid peroxidation-driven ferroptosis. Importantly, microbiota-derived lipid metabolites exert context-dependent effects on cG…

title: Integrating Identity and Emotion Information in Faces: Capacity Limits of Information Processing in Autism
abstract: Abstract The ability to combine identity and emotional information when viewing faces allows typically developing individuals to process facial information efficiently. The aim of this study was to examine whether autistic adults share this ability and test if it reflects a broader pattern of integrative information processing. Nineteen autistic adults and nineteen typically developing adults completed a divided-attention task where they had to indicate when a target was present. Each participant completed two separate experiments: (i) the face experiment, which required detecting targets based on identity and emotional expression; and (ii) the object experiment, which required detecting targets based on colour and shape. Analyses assessed whether, and how, participants responded more efficiently in the presence of both targets, compared to either single target. By employing mathematical modelling tools developed in the System Factorial Technology (SFT) framework, results showed that autistic individuals process faces at the rate of typically developing individuals, but failed to exhibit integrative properties (supercapacity) seen in typically developing adults in either domain. In autistic adults, this pattern ranged from limited capacity for faces to capacity consistent with independent parallel processing for objects. Implications of these findings generalise to personalisat…

title: Optimalisasi Investasi Wakaf Uang melalui Diversifikasi Aset dan Peningkatan Kapasitas Nazhir: Studi Kasus Badan Wakaf Uang Muhammadiyah Sumatera Barat
abstract: Aims: This study aims to analyze the optimization of waqf investment at Badan Wakaf Uang Muhammadiyah (BWUM) West Sumatra by focusing on waqf asset diversification, investment management, risk control, and the utilization of investment returns for community welfare. Method: This research employs a qualitative approach using an ex-post facto method. Data were collected through interviews and documentation related to waqf investment management at BWUM West Sumatra. The data were analyzed descriptively to examine the practices of investment development, supervision, reporting, risk management, and distribution of waqf benefits. Results: The findings indicate that BWUM West Sumatra has developed waqf funds through Islamic financial institutions and productive business activities, including UD Berkah. However, several investments have been discontinued due to considerations of efficiency and sustainability. Waqf investment management is supported by supervision, financial reporting, reserve fund establishment, and the distribution of investment benefits to social, educational, and healthcare sectors. These findings demonstrate that waqf investment optimization requires a balance between asset development, risk control, professional nazhir management, transparency, and the orientation toward public welfare. Conclusion/Novelty/Implications: The novelty of this study lies in its integr…

A socio-technical mechanism of the agricultural digital divide: Ecuador within a heterogeneous Latin American context
abstract: Digital agriculture can improve farm management, resource-use efficiency, and decision-making; however, access to technology alone does not guarantee equivalent economic benefits. This perspective article conceptualizes the agricultural digital divide as a socio-technical and economic inequality that can arise along a sequence linking structural conditions, resource accessibility, capability formation, technological appropriation, productive integration, economic value realization, and value capture and benefit distribution. This definition extends the analysis beyond connectivity and adoption by considering whether agricultural actors can integrate technologies into viable productive activities and retain a significant share of the value generated. Institutions, extension services, cooperatives, financing mechanisms, technology providers, business models, and data governance can shape the transitions between these stages. Ecuador is examined as a focal analytical case within a heterogeneous Latin America, without assuming regional representativeness. The framework redirects the evaluation of digitalization away from the number of technologies deployed and toward their productive appropriation, economic viability, and the distribution of their benefits, thereby reinforcing the relationship between digital transformation and agricultural economics.

Overcoming the Resistance Penalty in Large-Bandgap Carbon Nanotube Electronics via Synergistic Interfacial Engineering
abstract: Abstract High-pressure carbon monoxide (HiPCO) carbon nanotubes (CNTs) offer superior ION/IOFF ratios due to their larger bandgap (EG), yet they suffer from high series resistance limiting drive currents. Here, we demonstrate a synergistic dual-engineering strategy to simultaneously minimize channel and contact resistance in top-gate HiPCO CNT field-effect transistors (FETs). A 200 °C forming gas annealing (FGA) process effectively scavenges organic residues, reducing the intrinsic channel resistance to 318 Ω·μm for specific 50 nm gate-length devices. Furthermore, localized p-type contact doping using contact-defined self-aligned MoOx nanoparticles deposited selectively within the source/drain windows reduces the effective Schottky barrier height from 233 meV to 66 meV. Optimized HiPCO CNTFETs exhibit a record-high on-current density of 2.5 mA/μm at VDS = –0.5 V while maintaining excellent off-state suppression. Our devices outperform existing benchmarks and exceed the IRDS 2039 conductance projections by 4×. This synergistic approach provides a robust pathway for high-performance, low-power carbon-based nanoelectronics.

title: Low-coercivity and high-resistivity medium-entropy alloy via binder jetting-enabled in-situ carbon doping
Global value chains and carbon emission nexus in India: Do scale, composition and technique effects matter?
abstract: Purpose This study examines how participation in the global value chain (GVC) influences carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions in India from 1995 to 2020. It distinguishes between forward and backward GVC participation and reconceptualises scale, composition and technique effects as moderating mechanisms shaping the environmental consequences of GVC integration. Design/methodology/approach The study employs an autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) cointegration framework using annual time-series data for India. Interaction terms capture the conditional effects of scale, composition and technique channels on the relationship between GVC participation and CO2 emissions. Robustness is assessed using fully modified ordinary least squares (FMOLS), dynamic ordinary least squares (DOLS) and standard diagnostic and stability tests. Findings The results reveal asymmetric environmental impacts of GVC integration. Forward participation is significantly associated with higher CO2 emissions, whereas backward participation is associated with lower emissions in the long run. Technique effects are associated with a weaker emission-increasing impact of forward participation and a stronger emission-reducing effect of backward participation. In contrast, composition effects are associated with higher emissions and partially offset the environmental gains from backward integration. Originality/value This…

Behaviour of carbon fibre-reinforced polymer-reinforced macro-synthetic fibre-reinforced concrete columns under axial compression
abstract: This study experimentally and theoretically analyses the axial compression behaviour of concrete columns reinforced with longitudinal carbon fibre-reinforced polymer (CFRP) bars and steel spirals, incorporating macro-synthetic fibres. Sixteen specimens in four groups (CRPC, CRMSP, SRPC, SRMSP) varied concrete type (plain/macro-synthetic fibre-reinforced concrete (MSFRC)), longitudinal bar material (CFRP/steel) and spiral pitch. Failure modes were consistent across all groups. The axial strength of CFRP-reinforced columns averaged 90.7% of that of equivalent steel-reinforced columns. However, CFRP-reinforced columns exhibited 8.5–12.1% higher ductility. MSFRC columns showed 11–19% greater axial strain at peak load than plain concrete counterparts. Although current codes lack design rules for polymeric compression reinforcement, the proposed theoretical model – accounting for CFRP bar contribution after cover spalling, spiral confinement and concrete type – accurately predicted column performance. The research demonstrates the viable structural performance of CFRP-reinforced MSFRC columns under compression.

title: Green knowledge trading and corporate energy efficiency: asymmetric effects of patent inflows and outflows
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine how the exchange of green knowledge affects corporate energy efficiency. This study focuses on determining whether green knowledge flows in different directions produce asymmetric effects on energy efficiency and how green knowledge flows are transformed into energy-saving performance through internal knowledge management processes within firms. Design/methodology/approach This paper uses the acquisition and sale of green patents by firms to measure the inflow and outflow of green knowledge, respectively. An empirical analysis is conducted using panel data from Chinese A-share listed companies between 2012 and 2023. Findings Green patent acquisition significantly improves energy efficiency, whereas sale has no independent effect once acquisition is controlled for. The asymmetry arises because acquisition triggers organizational knowledge absorption processes that sale does not. Patent acquisition can improve corporate energy efficiency through two mechanisms: knowledge diversification and digital knowledge management capabilities. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the energy efficiency effects of purchasing green patents vary across different companies and regions. Originality/value This paper distinguishes between two types of knowledge flows – green patent sales and purchases – and verifies their asymmetric effects on energy efficiency. …

title: Beating and coupling in pulsating stars: A unified Fourier description and observational diagnostics
abstract: Long-term amplitude and phase variations in pulsating stars produce side peaks or multiplets in the Fourier spectrum of the light curves around the pulsation frequency and its harmonics. Such structures are often attributed to modulation, although linear beating and the non-linear coupling of close oscillations can also produce similar patterns. We developed a unified analytical Fourier description of these alternatives and identify observational relations that retain discriminatory power when their frequency patterns overlap. We represented the signal as a dominant, non-sinusoidal oscillation plus one or more secondary oscillations close to it, and analytically derived the frequencies, complex amplitudes, and phases resulting from linear superposition, quadratic coupling, and general non-linear coupling. Synthetic light curves illustrate these results. We implemented , which compares modulation with primary--secondary quadratic coupling models anchored to either the higher- or lower-frequency side peak, using the same normalised complex amplitudes, and supplements the fit with hierarchical tests of side-peak amplitude progression. A sinusoidal secondary signal produces only one additional peak in the linear-beating case, whereas a non-sinusoidal secondary signal produces a harmonic sequence whose separation from the primary harmonics increases with order. Quadratic coupling pr…

title: Coordinated Interfacial Electron Transfer and Metabolic Coupling Drive Acetate Electrosynthesis in a Synthetic Microbial Consortium
abstract: Abstract Microbial consortia in microbial electrosynthesis (MES) can couple cathodic electron utilization with CO2 fixation through interspecies electron transfer and metabolite cross-feeding. However, how defined functional members coordinate interfacial electron input with downstream acetogenic metabolism remains insufficiently understood. Here, we constructed a defined three-member consortium comprising the Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 and the acetogens Clostridium aceticum and Acetobacterium woodii to investigate how functional complementarity supports acetate electrosynthesis. The three-member consortium reached a maximum acetate concentration of 2.33 ± 0.17 g L–1, 2.62-fold that of the A. woodii and C. aceticum binary consortium, accompanied by a higher current density, stronger redox activity, and more pronounced riboflavin-related signals. Phase-resolved fhs abundances, metabolomic profiles, and flavin perturbation experiments further supported spatially differentiated roles within the consortium: S. oneidensis enhanced cathode-associated electron input, while phase-resolved fhs abundances and H2/formate dynamics indicated that acetogenic functions were maintained across both biofilm and planktonic phases and coupled to soluble-intermediate turnover. Despite varying initial inoculation ratios, the consortium consistently converged on similar acetate production and communi…

Social identity coupling model in university students in high-level sports teams: based on grounded theory and fsQCA
abstract: Background University students from high-level sports teams in China assume dual roles as formal students and elite athletes. This study develops a localized social identity coupling model to address the theoretical and empirical gaps in the existing literature. Method Based on social identity theory, this study employs a mixed-method research paradigm integrating grounded theory and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA). The sample comprises 36 university students from high-level sports teams in China recruited from six universities. Semi-structured interviews and three-stage coding procedures were performed to extract core conceptual dimensions, thereby constructing a specialized social identity coupling model that accommodates the dual-role characteristics of student-athletes. The fsQCA technique was implemented to systematically evaluate configurational mechanisms, structural robustness, empirical reliability, and hierarchical bottleneck characteristics of the proposed model. Results This study establishes a five-dimensional coupling model of social identity for university students from high-level sports teams in China, encompassing: (1) a dual-dimensional perceived physical literacy kernel; (2) a dual-dimensional sense of belonging construction logic; (3) a single-dimensional inclusive leadership openness attribute; (4) a dual identity categorization conductio…

title: Reimagining Hadith Studies: Embodied Islamic Knowledge and the Integration of Religion and Science in Southeast Asia Islamic University
abstract: The transformation of Islamic higher education institutions into universities has intensified demands to integrate religious sciences and modern disciplines, while also raising concerns about marginalizing hadith studies as a core normative field. This article reimagines hadith studies in the university era by examining how an embodied Islamic knowledge approach sustains their relevance within religion–science integration frameworks. Employing a qualitative comparative case study design, this research draws on fieldwork conducted at State Islamic University Syekh Wasil Kediri, State Islamic Institute Madura, State Islamic Institute Ponorogo in Indonesia, and Fatoni University in Southern Thailand. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, participant observation, and document analysis, and analyzed thematically. The findings show that although institutional transformation creates structural opportunities for interdisciplinary integration, formal policies and curricular reforms alone are insufficient to sustain hadith studies. Instead, hadith demonstrates resilience through embodied practices, including pesantren-based academic traditions, ethical pedagogical exemplification, community engagement, and applied ethical initiatives. Through these practices, hadith functions not merely as a textual reference but as a lived moral and epistemological foundation that mediates re…

title: Fuel properties of biodiesel blended with glycerol-derived acetyl glycerol esters as antifreeze additives
abstract: Converting glycerol into higher-value chemical feedstocks or additives can help address the global surplus of crude glycerol and increase the value of this biodiesel byproduct. In this study, a sulfated titania (SO 4 2- /TiO 2 ) solid superacid catalyst was prepared to catalyze the esterification of glycerol with acetic acid, producing a mixed acetyl glycerol ester product for use as a cold-flow additive. The glycerol-derived ester product was mixed with ethanol or isopropanol as a cosolvent and added to biodiesel at a total additive concentration of 1 vol%. The effects of cosolvent-to-ester ratio on cold filter plugging point (CFPP) and other fuel properties were systematically evaluated. An ethanol-to-acetyl-glycerol-ester ratio of 5:95 provided the lowest CFPP, decreasing it from 2 °C for neat biodiesel to −4 °C, whereas an isopropanol-to-ester ratio of 10:90 decreased the CFPP to −3 °C. Increasing cosolvent content also lowered kinematic viscosity and the non-standard carbon-residue index but reduced flash point and increased water content and acid value. The results therefore demonstrate a practical cold-flow benefit while also defining formulation trade-offs to consider when selecting the cosolvent level.

AI-DRIVEN EARLY WARNING SYSTEMS FOR SEPSIS DETECTION IN ICU SETTINGS: A STRUCTURED REVIEW OF PREDICTIVE PERFORMANCE, CLINICAL INTEGRATION AND EQUITY OUTCOMES
abstract: Background: Sepsis remains a primary cause of mortality and organ dysfunction in Intensive Care Units (ICUs) globally. Although AI models show considerable promise for the early identification of sepsis, moving these tools from retrospective performance to bedside utility is hindered by socio-technical barriers, workflow friction, and algorithmic equity issues. Objective: This structured review evaluates the state of AI-driven sepsis Early Warning Systems (EWS), identifying systemic barriers to clinical integration and assessing algorithmic fairness across demographic cohorts. Methodology: A structured review of peer-reviewed literature published in PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar between January 2018 and June 2026 was conducted, focusing on predictive performance, clinical implementation, and algorithmic equity. Results: Retrospective assessments of deep sequential architectures demonstrate high diagnostic accuracy (AUROC>0.95) (Boussina et al., 2024; Siddiqui, 2026). Prospective trials of landmark systems such as TREWS (Adams et al., 2022), COMPOSER (Shashikumar et al., 2025), and CONCERN EWS (Rossetti et al., 2025), confirm clinical utility, yielding mortality reductions of 17% to 35.6%. However, real-world effectiveness is frequently hindered by severe alert fatigue (Wong et al., 2021). Furthermore, because models rely on historical health data, they often inherit systemi…

title: Advancing cardiac xenotransplantation: overcoming challenges and ethical considerations for clinical integration
abstract: Advanced heart failure affects over 6 million adults in the United States alone. Orthotopic heart transplantation remains the definitive treatment, with over 90% one-year survival and meaningful gains in functional status and quality of life. The therapy is, however, constrained by an intractable supply problem. For decades, xenotransplantation (XTx), the transplantation of organs across species, has been proposed as a means of closing this gap, though for most of that time it remained a theoretical aspiration. With the discovery of CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, improved immunosuppressive strategies, and refined preclinical models, the field has accelerated at an unprecedented pace. Multi-gene-edited porcine donors have survived for more than 200 days in orthotopic non-human primate models, and two compassionate-use pig-to-human cardiac transplants at the University of Maryland (2022 and 2023) demonstrated some feasibility for clinical cardiac XTx for the first time. In May 2026, the FDA granted clearance under an investigational new drug application to allow the EXPRESS study, the first prospective clinical trial of a gene-edited porcine heart, to proceed. In this perspective, we discuss the ethical, regulatory, and equity considerations that remain as decisive barriers to clinical integration and may shape how this therapy is introduced along the remaining immunologic and virolog…

title: Integration of Islamic Educational Values and Environmental Educational Values: Perspectives of Hasan Langgulung and David Orr
abstract: Environmental crises show that technical knowledge is insufficient when education does not also cultivate spiritual, moral, and ecological responsibility. This study analyzes Islamic educational value contents reconstructed from Hasan Langgulung’s thought, environmental educational value contents reconstructed from David W. Orr’s thought, and formulates their conceptual integration. Using qualitative library research with a philosophical-integrative approach, the analysis involved construct identification, value reconstruction, substantive correspondence, cross-relational analysis, and philosophical-integrative synthesis. Langgulung’s thought was reconstructed through tawhid, fitrah, akhlaq, integration of knowledge, and stewardship responsibility, while Orr’s thought was reconstructed through ecological awareness, environmental responsibility, sustainable living, ecological justice, and participation and environmental action. Integration operates across reconstructed value contents through dynamic, multidirectional, reciprocal, and continuous relations rather than one-to-one pairing, with human-nature interconnectedness as an ontological principle. The synthesis produces the Integrative Spin conceptual model comprising Spiritual-Ecological Awareness, Sustainable and Just Living, Ecological Ethics of Responsibility, Integrative Ecological Literacy, and Participatory Ecological …

Optimal decision-making method for power grid maintenance scheduling during multiple power outage events based on large language models
abstract: Introduction When several outage maintenance events take place at the same time, the topology and operating mode of the power system change considerably, and experience-based maintenance plans designed for single outage events can no longer capture the combined risk of these events. Methods This paper proposes an optimal decision-making method for maintenance scheduling during multiple outage events based on a large language model. First, an adaptive load forecasting model is built, in which frequency-domain features extracted by the Fourier transform and convolutional networks are fed into a pre-trained large language model; the forecasts then support a weak-link evaluation based on electrical betweenness. Second, a risk overlapping degree model quantifies the cumulative risk of simultaneous outages. On this basis, a joint optimization model coordinates the monthly maintenance schedule and the day-ahead risk-prevention measures. Results Case studies on a 35-node test system show that the method identifies weak links in each maintenance window and achieves a risk overlapping degree of 2.6. Compared with the baseline models, it reduces the level of risk. Tests on IEEE standard systems up to 118 buses confirm the applicability of the method to larger grids. Discussion The proposed method provides a practical decision-making tool for maintenance scheduling under multiple power out…

Energy-Based and Ablative Destructive Therapies Versus Surgical Excision for Primary Basal Cell Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: Background: Surgical excision is the reference treatment for basal cell carcinoma (BCC), but energy-based and ablative therapies, including photodynamic therapy, radiotherapy and brachytherapy, laser ablation, electrochemotherapy and curettage-based destruction, are increasingly used. Objective: To quantify the loss of tumour control and the cosmetic gain of these therapies relative to excision. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Europe PMC and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception for randomised and non-randomised controlled studies comparing these therapies with excision for primary BCC. The primary outcome was treatment failure. Risk ratios (RR) were pooled with Mantel–Haenszel random-effects models, and certainty was graded with GRADE. Results: Fourteen studies (11 randomised) were included; 12 studies with 1,737 lesions or patients informed the primary outcome. In randomised trials, failure was more frequent after ablative therapy (RR 5.34, 95% CI 2.76 to 10.33; I2=23.3%; moderate certainty). Across all studies the RR was 3.26 (95% CI 1.47 to 7.23; prediction interval 0.27 to 40.00), an absolute excess of 7.6 failures per 100 tumours; heterogeneity (I2=60.3%) was explained by study design. Early failure and late recurrence also increased. Good or excellent cosmesis was more frequent after photodynamic therapy in two trials (RR 1.87, 95% CI 1.54 to 2.26; low certain…

Neuromorphic-classical hybrid framework for real-time augmented reality processing: adaptive stream fusion with dynamic threshold modulation and uncertainty-aware sensor integration
abstract: Contemporary augmented reality systems must reconcile three competing demands: latency low enough to remain imperceptible; visual fidelity high enough to convince a viewer that virtual content belongs in the physical scene; and power draw low enough to enable extended mobile use. This study narrows its focus to three specific bottlenecks that recur across conventional pipelines and proposes an algorithmic remedy for each, evaluated through implementation and controlled synthetic execution rather than field deployment. The first bottleneck is feature extraction, which conventional pipelines were found to spend 42% of total processing time on. The second is unreliable multimodal sensor fusion, whose spatial-tracking accuracy, as the same profiling found, could degrade by 68% when lighting or motion departs from laboratory conditions. The third is reactive content delivery, whose 180 ms loading delays break immersion each time a user turns their head. The design targets that motivated these numbers—3D molecular visualization at 120 ± 3.2 Hz for education, anatomical overlays precise to 1.1 ± 0.15 mm for remote surgical guidance, assembly-instruction positioning within 1.8 ± 0.2 mm for industrial maintenance, and 28 ± 4 ms contextual content delivery for location-based entertainment—are presented strictly as potential applications suggested by this algorithmic evaluation, not as de…

title: Enhancing the manufacturing processes and productivity in Industry 5.0 with the integration of machine learning and cyber-physical systems
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine the synergistic integration of Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) and Machine Learning (ML) as a foundational enabler for Industry 5.0, focusing on creating human-centric, sustainable and resilient manufacturing ecosystems. Design/methodology/approach The study utilizes a synthesis and review approach, analyzing recent advances in ML-driven CPS applications such as workflow optimization and predictive maintenance, alongside enabling technologies like 5G and digital twins. Findings The findings show that the integration of ML in multi-tier Edge-Fog-Cloud CPS brings significant operational advantages for the shop floor, such as sub-millisecond real-time control, more efficient human–robot interaction and a 10–20% reduction in energy used by the shop floor. But, the benefits of such physical manufacturing solutions rely on the need to work through a number of operational challenges. These include formally verifying non-deterministic ML policies, reducing IT/OT cybersecurity threats, including data poisoning and signal spoofing, reducing data heterogeneity in Federated Learning (FL) and lowering high deployment costs for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Research limitations/implications Future implementation requires addressing the need for Explainable AI (XAI) for transparency, FL for privacy and reinforcement learning for human-in-the-loop c…

title: Inverse design of multi-mode OAM-generating pixelated THz metasurfaces
abstract: Introduction Traditional metasurface design relies on physical priors and parameter scanning, which is time-consuming and prone to getting stuck in local optima. Methods In this article, we proposed a pixelated metasurface inverse design method, which discretizes the metasurface elements into a 16 × 16 binary pixel array, with each pixel independently adjustable, expanding the design space. We constructed a deep neural network framework consisting of a forward prediction residual convolutional network and a tandem generative inverse network: The forward network takes the element structure image as input and quickly predicts its complex reflection coefficient spectrum. Results and Discussion The average mean square error (MSE) of the test set is 0.0017. The inverse network is implemented by concatenating pre-trained forward networks without the need for real geometric labels, with an average MSE of 0.0131 on the test set. Using the trained model, we designed a metasurface that generates orbital angular momentum (OAM) with topological charges of ±1 and ±2 in the 1.5-1.6 THz frequency range. The full wave simulation results confirm that the designed metasurface can achieve spatial separation and independent control of multi-topology OAM beams, and the far-field amplitude and phase distribution are consistent with theoretical expectations. This method significantly improves the des…

title: Variable task difficulty with augmented sensory feedback for motor training in virtual reality
abstract: Introduction This study examined how motor task difficulty and augmented sensory feedback (ASF) modality influence task performance, physiological responses, and perceptual experience during virtual reality (VR)-based upper-limb motor training. Building on related brace- and VR-based ASF platforms previously examined in neurotypical and spinal cord injury cohorts, the long-term goal is to support neurorehabilitation-oriented adaptive VR training; however, the present study used neurotypical participants as an initial validation step. Methods Fourteen right-handed neurotypical participants used a supportive upper-limb brace and surface electromyography (EMG) for myoelectric control of a virtual robotic arm in a two-dimensional tracking task. A 2 × 2 within-subject design crossed ASF modality (visual feedback versus visual + haptic feedback) with task difficulty (straight-line versus sinusoidal trajectory). Outcomes included normalized path length, task completion time, movement jerk, alpha- and beta-band electroencephalogram (EEG) power over motor cortex, heart rate, EMG amplitude, EMG-displacement-based virtual work, and perceptual ratings of agency, motivation, and utility. Short-term pre-to-post percentage changes were computed for each measure. Results VHF straight-line training produced the largest reductions in normalized path length (-4.69%) and completion time (-6.12%), …

title: Morphometry-based design and finite element assessment of primary stability in glenoid baseplate fixation for reverse shoulder arthroplasty for the Indian population
abstract: Introduction The geometrical and morphological parameters of the glenoid vary across ethnic groups, affecting the fixation of the baseplates in reverse shoulder arthroplasty. Studies have shown that using larger baseplates for smaller glenoids may not facilitate a better biomechanical outcome, and therefore a population-based investigation plays a crucial role in selecting an appropriate implant. Methods This work investigates finite element analysis of a pear-shaped glenoid baseplate, designed based on the morphometric parameters of the Indian glenoid. A percentile-based method was used to select the representative glenoid to select small, middle and large glenoid variations within the Indian population. Nine glenoid-baseplate assemblies were assembled from three different glenoid dimensions and three baseplate sizes. This baseplate-scapula construct was subjected to finite element analysis under specified loading conditions for various abduction angles to investigate mechanical load sharing and primary stability. Results These findings indicated that the fixation outcomes changed based on the baseplate-glenoid assembly, showing that the biomechanical performance did not depend on the baseplate size alone. Discussion Smaller baseplates and intermediate baseplates showed better primary stability in the Indian glenoid, supporting morphometry-guided baseplate selection based on i…

title: Family functioning and perceived academic achievement of adolescents from variable-centered and person-centered perspectives: the roles of teacher support and psychological capital
abstract: Introduction Academic achievement is of paramount importance for adolescent development. However, how family functioning affects academic achievement through psychological capital (PsyCap), and the role of teacher support in this process, remain largely unexplored. Moreover, whether PsyCap exhibits heterogeneous profiles and how different environmental factors distinguish among them warrant further investigation. Method A survey was conducted among 1,288 students from eight junior high schools in Jiangxi Province, China, using cluster and convenience sampling. Hayes’ PROCESS macro was used to test the moderated mediation model. Latent profile analysis (LPA) was conducted to explore the heterogeneous latent taxonomy of PsyCap. Results Significant positive correlations were observed among family functioning, PsyCap, teacher support, and perceived academic achievement.PsyCap fully mediated the relationship between family functioning and perceived academic achievement. Teacher support significantly moderated the effect of family functioning on PsyCap and the entire mediating pathway. LPA identified three distinct PsyCap profiles: low (15%), moderate (60%), and high (25%). These profiles showed a stepwise pattern of significant differences in perceived academic achievement. The higher the levels of family functioning and teacher support, the more likely students were to be classifie…

title: The Performativity of Public Space: Body and Space as Active Agents in Design
abstract: This study addresses the role that bodies currently play in the transformation of public space. This paper suggests a performative design approach that allows the body to be sustained as an active agent in the material construction of the public space; not just as a symbolic participant. At the same time, it seeks to recognize space as a live/active element, thus emphasizing its capacity to activate processes. To this end, three key axes of performative design for public space are defined: 1) A relationship between the body and public space in terms of agency and transformation; 2) A tension between fixity and fluidity; and 3) A focus on bodily and affective experience. The relevance of this study lies in its theoretical and methodological contribution integrating the bodily dimension into urban design, thus enhancing a sensitive, affective, and embodied perspective, which is so necessary in contemporary sedentary societies.

title: One Step at a Time: Design and Rationale for Stepped-Wedge Cluster Randomized Trials
abstract: Stepped-wedge cluster randomized trials provide researchers with an opportunity to simultaneously implement and evaluate systemic interventions in real-world settings. This study design may have advantages compared with other cluster randomized trial (CRT) designs by optimizing feasibility and uptake when resources or personnel are limited. We present strengths, limitations, and key considerations when deciding whether to use a stepped-wedge design. Statistical analysis of stepped-wedge trials differs from that of traditional CRTs and should account for changes in outcome measures due to the intervention separate from those due to secular or time-based trends. We conclude with an example of a stepped-wedge study at 26 hospitals that helped to establish the effectiveness and safety of the Eat, Sleep, Console approach to neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome.

title: Dynamics of trust in collaborative complex system design
abstract: Purpose This paper examines how trust is constructed, eroded and rebuilt in collaborative complex system design in safety-critical settings. Design/methodology/approach The paper uses a qualitative process study of a 13-partner European project developing mid-air collision avoidance systems (MIDCAS) for remotely piloted aircraft. Drawing on project documentation, practitioner observation, retrospective interviews and secondary material, the paper develops and applies a four-dimensional analytical framework integrating first- and second-order cybernetics with trust research. Findings Trust emerged as a dynamic governance achievement shaped by four interrelated dimensions: the balance between trust and control, trust asymmetry in heterogeneous consortia, feedback architecture and iterative trust calibration, and the rebuilding of trust at technical and organisational step-changes. Trust did not substitute for control but enabled viable coordination when formal governance could not absorb project complexity. Research limitations/implications The single-case design in a European defence aviation context limits generalisability, but the cybernetic framework offers transferable concepts for examining how trust, control, feedback and vulnerability co-evolve in other collaborative complex system design settings, including artificial intelligence (AI) enabled, autonomous and safety-crit…

Assembly processes and network structure of rhizosphere fungal communities in healthy and Ralstonia solanacearum-infected tomato plants
abstract: Introduction Bacterial wilt caused by Ralstonia solanacearum is a major constraint to tomato production worldwide. Rhizosphere microbial community is closely linked to plant health. However, how R. solanacearum invasion alters the assembly processes and co-occurrence network in tomato rhizosphere fungal communities remains largely unclear. Methods Here, we collected rhizosphere soil samples from three major tomato-producing regions in China to investigate how R. solanacearum invasion affects fungal community composition, network topology, and assembly processes in tomato rhizosphere. Results and discussion In this study, fungal community structure differed significantly between healthy and diseased rhizosphere soils, driven significantly by soil pH ( P < 0.05). The density of pathogen R. solanacearum in the diseased rhizosphere soil was significantly higher than that in the healthy tomato rhizosphere ( P < 0.05). Genera Trichoderma , Talaromyces , Mortierella , and Penicillium were significantly enriched in healthy soils ( P < 0.05). Network analysis revealed diseased soils had simpler and less stable fungal networks, with decreased node and edge numbers, reduced natural connectivity, and a smaller proportion of connectors. The neutral community model and null model revealed that stochastic processes explained 33.10% of the community variation in healthy tomato rhizosp…

In vitro assay and GC-MS profiling of Proteus sp.EKWG2I3 isolate obtained from Echinops kebericho M.: a traditional medicinal plant
abstract: Abstract Endophytic bacteria are a promising source of bioactive compounds valuable to medicine, agriculture, and industrial applications. This study investigates bioactive compounds of EKWG2I3 to evaluate their in vitro antibacterial and antioxidant activity against test strains. A healthy root of Echinops kebericho M. medicinal plant was collected for experimental analysis. 16 S rRNA gene sequencing was performed for accurate identification of a single potential isolate. In vitro antibacterial, antioxidant activities, and Gas Chromatography–Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS) profiling of crude extracts for EKWG2I3 isolate were performed. The potent isolate ( EKWG2I3) obtained from E. kebericho M. clustered with P. mirabilis ATCC 29,906 T (ACLE01000013) and designated as Proteus sp. EKWG2I3 (PV635194). The results revealed that the crude extract of the Proteus sp.EKWG2I3 showed notable antibacterial activity of (15 ± 0.0529 mm) against E. coli ATCC-25,922 T . This isolate also exhibited potent free radical scavenging potential with an inhibitory concentration at 50% (IC 50 ) with value of 45.46 µg/mL compared to ascorbic acid. Moreover, GC-MS analysis identified methyl phenylacetate (38.49%) and pentanoic acid, methyl ester (12.71%) as major compounds in the extract of Proteus sp.EKWG2I3. This study suggests that Proteus sp.EKWG2I3 (PV635194) associated E. kebericho M.M. could be a pot…

title: Favorable habitats of endangered halophytes harbor unique soil properties and bacterial communities, with a dominant root-associated genus promoting host plant growth
abstract: Understanding how edaphic factors and root-associated bacterial communities interact to shape plant growth is essential for effective conservation of halophytic species in coastal ecosystems. We investigated relationships among bulk soil, rhizosphere, and root bacterial microbiota; soil physicochemical properties; and Salicornia europaea growth spanning three distinct areas (Lakeside Park, Ubaranai and Misaki) within a brackish lake in Japan. Among the three study areas, S. europaea individuals from Lakeside Park exhibited the highest mean values for shoot length, fresh weight, dry weight, and number of primary branches, which were 1.9-, 11.2-, 12.1-, and 7.2-fold higher than those at Misaki in 2021, and 1.8-, 4.7-, 6.7-, and 4.7-fold higher than those at Misaki in 2022. Bacterial diversity and community composition associated with S. europaea varied in response to differences in plant growth and edaphic conditions. Soil texture, electrical conductivity, pH, total organic carbon, total nitrogen, C/N ratio, and water-soluble Ca 2+ were identified as key factors underlying microbial community structures. Based on heatmap and LEfse analyses, six bacterial genera, Bacteroidetes BD2-2, Candidatus Thiobios , SEEP-SRB1, Calditrichaceae , Bacteroidetes VC2.1 Bac22, and Luteibacter , were significantly enriched in areas where S. europaea exhibited vigorous growth. Among these, Luteibact…

High peak-current AlGaAs tunnel junctions for 10-junction GaAs laser power converters
abstract: Laser power converters (LPCs) are the core photovoltaic devices that act as receivers in optical wireless power transmission systems. In these devices, tunnel junctions (TJs) are employed to vertically interconnect multiple absorption sub-cells in series to construct high-voltage multi-junction LPCs. This work systematically investigates the effects of the Al composition, growth temperature, and doping levels on the performance of AlxGa(1−x)As TJs. Furthermore, the performance of TJs employing different doping schemes (conventional doping, Si + Te co-doping, and delta-doping) and structural designs [quantum well (QW) insertion] was evaluated. For samples with Al compositions of 0%, 7%, 22%, and 28%, the maximum peak tunneling current densities reached 31.0k, 20.3k, 4.8k, and 0.5k A/cm2, respectively, while the lowest tunneling resistivities achieved 1.17 × 10−5, 1.08 × 10−5, 1.89 × 10−5, and 1.39 × 10−4 Ω cm2, respectively. The optimized Al0.28Ga0.72As TJ, featuring a hybrid structure of Si + Te delta-doping and QW insertion, exhibited a peak tunneling current density of 14.6k A/cm2 in the as-grown state and maintained 1.1k A/cm2 after annealing. By applying this TJ structure to a 10-junction GaAs LPC, a photovoltaic conversion efficiency exceeding 60% was achieved.
