Light spectrum effects on huperzine A and B accumulation in axenic gametophyte cultures of Huperzia selago (L.) Bernh. ex Schrank et Mart
abstract: Introduction Huperzine A (HupA) and huperzine B (HupB) are high-value Lycopodiaceae alkaloids with potent, reversible acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitory activity and NMDA receptor antagonism. Their supply is limited by impractical field cultivation and conservation constraints on wild harvesting. Here, we evaluated axenic gametophyte cultures of Huperzia selago as a controllable and ethically sourced in vitro system and tested LED spectral control as a tool to modulate alkaloid accumulation. Methods Cultures were maintained for 24 weeks under three light treatments (WHITE-L, BLUE-L and RED–BLUE-L) or darkness. HupA and HupB were quantified by HPLC–DAD, while LC–MS/IT–TOF and MS/MS-supported profiling were used for target-alkaloid confirmation and characterization of the multi-component extract composition. Extracts standardized to HupA equivalents were evaluated for AChE inhibition. Results LED spectral control shaped HupA/HupB accumulation patterns. BLUE-L (≈450 nm) was associated with the strongest increase in HupA content, reaching 4.83 ± 0.21 mg·g - ¹ DW at week 12, whereas RED–BLUE-L (660/450 nm) maintained the highest mean HupA content over 24 weeks (3.61 ± 0.61 mg·g - ¹ DW). Darkness promoted relative biomass accumulation, whereas BLUE-L and RED–BLUE-L favored higher HupA/HupB accumulation during the 8–12-week harvest window. These complementary responses suggest a p…

title: Novel quantitative trait loci identified for bean rust and the fuscan subspecies of common bacterial blight in an F2 tepary bean population
abstract: Bean rust, caused by Uromyces appendiculatus , is one of the most critical diseases affecting common bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L.) worldwide. Similarly, common bacterial blight, caused by Xanthomonas fuscans subsp. fuscans (Xff) and Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. phaseoli (Xap), poses major threats to common bean production globally. While common bean exhibits limited natural resistance to these pathogens, tepary bean ( Phaseolus acutifolius A. Gray), a closely related species, has shown resistance to both rust and common bacterial blight. This study aimed to identify tepary beans resistant to rust and Xff, to pinpoint genomic regions controlling this resistance. Twenty-three tepary bean genotypes were inoculated with multiple rust races and Xff isolates. Several tepary genotypes exhibited immunity to eight rust races, and a few were also resistant to two isolates of Xff. An F 2 biparental tepary bean population was developed from one resistant and one susceptible genotype to map quantitative trait loci (QTLs) for resistance to these pathogens. The population was phenotyped by inoculating with two rust races and a mixture of two isolates of Xff. Genotyping by sequencing was employed to genotype the biparental population. A major QTL for the rust pathogen was identified on chromosome Pa10, and a major QTL for common bacterial blight fuscans was identified on chromosome Pa07. Neither…

title: Water use strategies of Populus euphratica across age classes along groundwater depth gradients in the lower Tarim River
abstract: How water source use and intrinsic water-use efficiency (iWUE) are linked across tree age classes under contrasting groundwater conditions remains unclear in desert riparian forests. We assessed water use strategies of young, middle-aged, and mature Populus euphratica in the lower Tarim River during ecological water conveyance (EWC) and non-EWC periods by combining hydrogen and oxygen stable isotopes of xylem and potential source waters with a Bayesian mixing model and leaf δ 13 C-derived iWUE. Across the five monitoring sections, mean groundwater depth was significantly lower during EWC than during non-EWC periods, averaging 4.7 and 4.9 m, respectively. At the Kunasite (DW) and Yingsu (F) sections, MixSIAR posterior mean contributions during EWC were 16.0–23.1% for groundwater, 14.4–17.6% for river water, and 6.6–19.0% for individual 40-cm soil layers. During non-EWC periods, posterior mean contributions from individual soil layers ranged from 10.9 to 20.3%, with relatively greater contributions from deeper layers. Associations between water source contributions and iWUE varied among age classes during EWC but were nonsignificant during non-EWC periods. Across sampling periods, mean iWUE was 58.29, 53.08, and 51.37 μmol mol −1 in young, middle-aged, and mature trees, respectively. The relationship between iWUE and groundwater depth also varied among sampling periods, with no c…

title: Power, inclusion and the role of SMEs in European public procurement
abstract: Purpose This study examines small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) participation in European public procurement, aiming to understand disparities across member states despite harmonised EU Directives. Design/methodology/approach Using a novel dataset of 839,778 tenders with information about SME participation from the Tenders Electronic Daily (TED) platform covering 29 countries from 2018 to 2023, we analyse SME participation rates, contract award shares, and geographic competition patterns. Findings Significant variation is observed: Eastern European countries exceed 80% SME participation, while several Western European countries remain below 40%. SMEs participate in about 80% of tenders but secure only 40–60% of contract values. Geographic proximity enhances SME competitiveness in local markets, especially for contracts under €500,000. Institutional and administrative factors appear more decisive than regulatory frameworks alone. Research limitations/implications Limitations include potential data quality issues. However, these were mitigated where possible, and the database remains the only available offering comparable data across Europe. Future research should explore institutional and cultural factors in greater depth through country-level studies. Practical implications Policymakers should adopt tailored approaches addressing administrative complexity and regional marke…

title: The Construction of Democratic Ideology and Institutional Identity in the Lyrics of the Song Mars KPU: An Analysis of Norman Fairclough's Critical Discourse
abstract: General elections in Indonesia often face a crisis of public trust that requires the KPU to strengthen its legal and cultural legitimacy. Using a qualitative approach and Norman Fairclough's Critical Discourse Analysis method, this study aims to uncover the hidden meaning and ideological representation behind the lyrics of "Mars KPU". The results of the analysis show that this march is not just a ceremonial anthem, but a discursive text that is full of ideology and institutional power. In the micro dimension (text), diction and imperative sentences construct an authoritative, idealistic, and filial image of the KPU, while the pattern of overwording of moral vocabulary (fair, honest, clean) dampens the collective anxiety of the community. In the meso dimension (discourse practice), this march functions double as an indoctrination of the internal integrity of the KPU as well as a massively distributed public participatory persuasion. In the macro (sociocultural) dimension, this discourse responds to the need of contemporary political history for a clean democracy to legitimize state power. In addition, the discourse acts as an instrument of cultural hegemony and the state's ideological apparatus in shaping the Indonesian national community. This research proves that institutional march functions strategically as a discursive instrument in the formation of institutional identity.
venue: Journal of Creative Power and Ambition (JCPA)

title: The eco–ultraprocessing paradox as evidence for a Tech–Nutri–Eco coherence framework in plant-based food sustainability governance
abstract: Plant-based foods are widely promoted as sustainable, yet a large share are ultra-processed — a tension that current assessment instruments cannot detect. NOVA, Nutri-score, and eco-score each evaluate a single dimension in isolation and share no criterion for reconciling them, so a product may score favourably on one while remaining unreconciled across the others. The absence of such a criterion is directly consequential for EU directive 2024/825, which requires environmental claims to be verifiable but sets no requirement of coherence across dimensions. The sustainability of a processed food product cannot be read from strong performance on any single dimension: coherence among the technological, nutritional, and environmental dimensions is a separate property, and one that current instruments do not assess. A synthesis of 2015–2025 literature yields 10 recurrent incoherence patterns in four structural families — metric reductionism, fragmented communication, scale and category errors, and pseudo-integration — from which we propose the Tech–Nutri–Eco framework and its operational measure, the integrated COherence iNdex (ICON), as a non-normative diagnostic. Applied to 49 plant-based products, ICON locates what we term the eco–ultraprocessing paradox — ultra-processed products with favourable nutritional or environmental scores — in 57% of the set, most often in plant-based dr…

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted design and CFD re-optimization of graded hybrid metal foams for faster hydrogen desorption in LaNi5 metal-hydride reactors
abstract: Introduction Heat delivery limits the discharge rate of LaNi5 metal-hydride reactors. This study develops PG-SADE-GHF to co-design radial foam porosity, CuCr1Zr/AlSi10Mg allocation, and transient heat-transfer/pressure scheduling. Methods The original MATLAB surrogate was used only for inexpensive screening. Its selected coordinates were then evaluated directly in OpenFOAM, and the same eight design variables were re-optimized within the original bounds, followed by an expanded-bound sensitivity study. Surrogate accuracy was assessed using 32 OpenFOAM development designs and 12 additional Sobol/maximin designs whose predictions were frozen before their CFD outcomes were computed. A CFD-corrected multifidelity model was then evaluated, and the optimized designs were verified with full-360-degree OpenFOAM calculations on a 196,608-cell mesh. Results The screening surrogate predicted td = 7.95 min, whereas direct OpenFOAM evaluation of the same coordinates gave 12.192 min. Re-optimization within the original bounds reduced td to 7.817 min, 21.83% faster than the 10-min CuCr1Zr-89% reference, while the expanded-bound sensitivity reached 6.442 min. On the locked held-out challenge, the original surrogate yielded RMSE = 3.354 min and MAE = 3.143 min; the CFD-corrected model achieved R2 = 0.982, RMSE = 0.159 min, MAE = 0.121 min, Spearman rho = 0.986, and 100% coverage of the nominal …

title: Child and Adolescent All-Cause Mortality in the United States vs Peer Nations: 1935–2023
abstract: BACKGROUND Children in the United States experience higher all-cause mortality than high-income peer nations, but the timing, durability, and age and sex contributions to this gap remain unclear. OBJECTIVES To characterize the timing, persistence, and age- and sex-specific patterns of the US child and adolescent mortality disadvantage relative to peer nations. METHODS Time-series comparison using vital statistics from the Human Mortality Database (1935–2023), comparing all-cause mortality among those aged 0 to 19 years in the United States vs those living in 13 high-income peer nations from the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). We estimated mortality rates, rate ratios (RRs), annual percent change (APC), and annual excess US deaths. RESULTS All-cause mortality declined 89.0% in the United States (477.6 to 52.4 per 100 000) from 1935 to 2023, compared with 96.6% in OECD13 (785.1 to 26.9 per 100 000). US mortality crossed over OECD13 in 1975 and remained higher thereafter. By 2023, the US disadvantage was largest among those aged 15 to 19 years (RR 2.9). From 2006 to 2023, APC was −1.2% (95% CI −1.7% to −0.6%) in the United States vs −2.3% (95% CI −2.7% to −2.0%) in OECD13. In 2023, those aged 15 to 19 years accounted for 40.4% of excess deaths, with male individuals contributing 30.6%. CONCLUSIONS The US child and adolescent mortality disadvantage da…

title: Breaking the silence in OMHCs: the impact of initial peer support on subsequent peer support provision
abstract: Purpose Peer support provision is critical for the success of online mental health communities (OMHCs). However, many posts seeking peer support often receive no replies. This study aims to investigate how initial peer support in OMHCs influences subsequent peer support provision. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the bystander effect and the anchoring effect, we examined how the empathy expressed in and informativeness of initial peer support, together with initial provider authority, influence both the likelihood of subsequent peer support and its characteristics. We collected data from the r/mentalhealth subreddit and conducted empirical analyses using the two-stage Heckman selection model. Findings Empathy expressed in initial peer support increases the likelihood of subsequent peer support provision and enhances empathy expressed in subsequent peer support. Conversely, the informativeness of initial peer support reduces the likelihood of subsequent peer support provision but positively affects the informativeness of subsequent peer support. Initial provider authority attenuates the relationship between empathy expressed in initial peer support and subsequent peer support provision, but amplifies the effect of initial peer support informativeness on the likelihood of subsequent peer support provision. In addition, initial provider authority weakens the positive relatio…

The SRG/eROSITA All-Sky Survey. Early dark energy and Hubble constant from the cluster mass function
abstract: The evolution of the mass function of massive galaxy clusters is a well-established cosmological probe. Using the eROSITA X-ray instrument on board the (SRG) mission, the western Galactic hemisphere of eROSITA's first All-Sky Survey (eRASS1) delivers a uniformly selected and securely confirmed sample of 5259 galaxy clusters spanning 0.1 < z < 0.8. When combined with overlapping weak lensing data from DES Year 3, KiDS, and HSC for mass calibration, this dataset enables precise tests of the standard Λ cold dark matter (łcdm) framework and beyond. In this work, we used the 0.1 < z < 0.45 subsample of the eRASS1 galaxy cluster catalog to place constraints on an axion-like early dark energy (EDE) scenario. Such models have been proposed as a possible mechanism to alleviate the tension between early- and late-Universe measurements of the Hubble constant. In this framework, a scalar field temporarily enhances the cosmic expansion rate around the epoch of recombination, after which its energy density rapidly dilutes at later times, leaving distinct imprints on the growth of structure. We leveraged these signatures across a redshift and scale range that have rarely been covered in the literature to present the first constraints on EDE derived from galaxy cluster number counts. Using eRASS1 number counts alone, we obtained an upper limit on the maximum EDE fraction of f_ < 0.3, consisten…

title: ‘Got to be the right fit, the right connection’: a scoping review of the peer support experiences and perspectives of adults with acquired neurological disability
abstract: Background Peer support for people with acquired neurological disability is gaining worldwide popularity, yet it is conceptually unclear what constitutes valuable peer interactions. To build a greater understanding from the lived experience perspective, this scoping review synthesised literature on how adults with acquired neurological disability experience and perceive peer support. Methods Peer-reviewed literature published between 2013 and 2024 was identified through systematic searches of five databases. Thirty-two studies were included, covering a range of disabilities (e.g. acquired brain injury, spinal cord injury, multiple sclerosis) and peer support forms (e.g. one-to-one, group, informal). Results Analysis revealed that peer support participants perceive value across three domains: (1) capacity-building, (2) social connection, and (3) psychological adjustment. However, they can also experience frustrations and challenges that directly oppose these benefits. Suitable characteristics of peers and structures of peer programs, including acknowledgement of individual differences in the peer support experience, were identified as key to successful peer interactions. Conclusions Peer support holds multifaceted value for people with acquired neurological disability; however, it is also a complex intervention that carries risks and requires sensitivity to individual variation.…

title: Risk-aware hierarchical reinforcement learning for investment and operations in cross-border energy supply chains under the belt and road initiative
abstract: Abstract Cross-border energy supply chains under the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) face unprecedented challenges, including geopolitical instability, macroeconomic volatility, and operational disruptions. Traditional optimization or flat reinforcement learning (RL) methods often struggle to address the scale, uncertainty, and multi-stakeholder complexity inherent in such environments. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a novel hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) framework that separates strategic investment planning from tactical operational control via a two-level architecture. The high-level agent makes long-horizon decisions on resource allocation and infrastructure deployment, while the low-level agent handles real-time logistics under dynamically imposed constraints. The framework explicitly incorporates multi-dimensional risk—political, economic, and operational—into both reward shaping and policy learning. Through extensive simulations on representative BRI corridors, the proposed HRL model demonstrates superior simulated performance over single-level RL, mixed-integer programming, and rule-based baselines across key metrics, including cumulative profit (+ 25%), service-level reliability, and robustness to stress scenarios. Ablation and continual learning experiments further confirm the contributions of hierarchical abstraction and risk-aware train…

Design of a novel hybrid advanced adiabatic compressed air and gravity energy storage system
abstract: Abstract To enhance the energy efficiency and energy density of physical energy storage (PES) systems, this study introduces a novel hybrid advanced adiabatic compressed air and gravity energy storage (HAACAGES) system. This system integrates advanced adiabatic compressed air energy storage (AA-CAES) and gravity energy storage (GES) components, utilizing the mass of the compressed air (denoted by Δ m ) to make the HAACAGES system overwhelm the capabilities of individual systems. A numerical analysis model was established to validate the proposed system. Results demonstrate the HAACAGES system outperforms the individual systems in terms of both energy efficiency and density. Specifically, the energy efficiency is always higher than the sum of the individual systems at altitudes from 0 to 3 km. At 3 km altitude, the energy density reaches nearly 1.5 times that of conventional AA-CAES systems. At 1 km altitude, it exceeds 10 times that of conventional GES systems. Overall, the HAACAGES system shows clear potential as a promising solution for the next generation of large-scale PES systems.

title: Not always protective: health literacy, school connectedness and adolescent healthy eating behaviors—the moderating role of physical activity participation
abstract: Purpose To explore the effects of Health literacy on adolescent healthy eating behaviors, a moderated-mediation model was constructed in this study to examine the mediating effect of School connectedness and the moderating effect of Physical activity participation. Methods Stratified cluster sampling was adopted. Questionnaires were administered to 3, 009 middle-school students recruited from 12 middle schools across 6 provinces nationwide, using the Health literacy scale, Eating behaviors scale, School connectedness scale, and Physical activity participation scale. Data analyses were performed using SPSS 26.0 and PROCESS Model 15. Results (1) Health literacy was significantly and positively associated with adolescent healthy eating behaviors. (2) A statistically significant indirect effect through School connectedness was identified; however, its direction was opposite to the hypothesized positive mediation, indicating a suppression pattern. (3) Physical activity participation significantly moderated the direct association between Health literacy and healthy eating behaviors, with this positive association progressively weakening as Physical activity participation increased. (4) Physical activity participation also moderated the second stage of the indirect pathway (School connectedness → healthy eating behaviors). The suppression pattern was stronger at low levels of Physical…

title: Processes of Public Space Appropriation: The Participation of Women Graffiti Writers and Urban Artists in Hermosillo, Sonora
abstract: Women's participation in the appropriation of public space by graffiti artists and urban artists in the city of Hermosillo, Sonora is explored. The dynamics involved in the hip-hop movement that creates graffiti, and urban artist collectives in the city within inequality urban contexts, marked by violence, insecurity, and a lack of opportunities for youths are analyzed. Observation and photographic recording of graffiti and urban art interventions was carried out, which were located on a map for a socio-spatial analysis, cross-referencing them with conapo data. In-depth interviews were conducted, focusing on women's access to urban art practices and interventions in public space. It was found that graffiti practices associated with the hip-hop movement are subjected to violent environments where women's participation is very limited, which contrasts with their participation in public space interventions through urban art. There is a trend toward the formation of artist collectives, and through collaboration with various municipal and state government programs, women are increasingly using institutionalized means to participate in the processes of appropriation of public space, contributing to the culture for development by rescuing public spaces and regenerating the social fabric through urban art.

title: Effect of urine storage conditions on circulating anodic antigen detection using the UCP-LF CAA test
abstract: Introduction Schistosomiasis is a parasitic neglected tropical disease that remains a major public health problem in many African countries. Accurate diagnosis is essential for control, surveillance and elimination efforts. Conventional parasitological methods have limited sensitivity, particularly in low-intensity infections commonly observed after treatment or in low-endemic settings. Circulating anodic antigen (CAA), released by live Schistosoma worms, is a highly sensitive and specific marker of active infection. The up-converting reporter particle lateral flow (UCP-LF) CAA test enables non-invasive urine-based diagnosis and is increasingly applied in low-endemic and near-elimination settings. For operational feasibility, urine samples may need to be stored before testing, but the effect of different storage conditions on CAA detection has not been systematically evaluated. Methods We investigated the effect of freezing and non-frozen storage on urine CAA detection using the UCP-LF CAA test, compared with freshly tested urine. The study was conducted among school-aged children in a near-elimination Schistosoma haematobium setting on Pemba, Tanzania. A total of 272 urine samples were tested fresh and after freezing at -20 °C for 5-7 days. For a subset of 153 samples with sufficient urine available, an additional aliquot was stored under non-frozen conditions (4-25 °C) and te…

title: Art-science collaboration for sustainability challenges: a systematic review of scholarship, sustainability framings, and stakeholder participation
abstract: Abstract Art-science collaboration (ASC) is increasingly presented as a response to sustainability challenges, yet the literature lacks a clear account of how the field has developed, how sustainability is substantively framed, and who participates. This systematic review synthesises 97 peer-reviewed ASC publications (2002–2024) using mixed quantitative and qualitative analysis organised around three strands. First, we characterise ASC scholarship and practice. The evidence base is rapidly expanding but weakly consolidated. Qualitative case studies dominate, the literature is process-heavy and evaluation-light, and syntheses and outcome-oriented evaluations remain rare. Peer-reviewed knowledge production is concentrated in universities and research institutes in a small number of Global North countries. Multi-media installations are the most frequently reported artistic format, alongside a substantial presence of socially engaged practice. Second, we examine sustainability framings through a triple-bottom-line lens (People, Planet, and Prosperity). Sustainability is most often framed through Planet-related topics. People is commonly implied through engagement and learning aims, while Prosperity is rarely treated as a primary concern. Many sustainability-relevant studies do not use sustainability terminology in titles or abstracts, limiting discoverability in sustainability-orie…

title: Assessing participation, satisfaction, and early risk detection in the pilot workplace NCD screening program in Tamil Nadu
abstract: Abstract Background Non-communicable diseases account for 74% of annual deaths worldwide. Early detection of these conditions is necessary for timely intervention, and prevention. The workplace serves as a suitable environment for screening by reaching large group of at-risk population. However, the effectiveness of implementing workplace screening programs depends on employee participation, satisfaction, and health outcomes. Therefore, this study aims to assess the employee satisfaction, participation rates, and factors influencing participation in workplace NCD screening programs along with the short-term outcomes, such as early detection rates. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted across 29 industries from April 2024 to March 2025 in which the workplace NCD screening programs were implemented by the government health department. Information on participants’ demographic profile, Morbidity status, overall perception of the screening program, and its possible outcomes was collected among its employees. Ethics approval was obtained from SRM IEC. Results A total of 296 employees participated in the study. 92.2% of the respondents had participated in a hypertension or diabetic screening program at their current workplace. Notably 43.8% of individuals with diabetes and 45.5% with hypertension were initially identified through workplace screening program, and 22…

First-principles investigation of hydrogen storage in pristine AlN nanosheets with a biphenylene framework
abstract: Abstract One of the most important aspects of the energy transition towards sustainable development is the efficient storage of hydrogen, for which a diverse range of materials is being studied. Here, we investigated the structural and electronic characteristics of biphenylene aluminum nitride (BP-AlN) nanosheet using density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Potential hydrogen adsorption sites were investigated and evaluated based on thermodynamic viability, as determined by the adsorption energy at these locations. The interatomic interactions and charge transfer were characterized based on Bader charges and density of states (DOS) at various concentrations of adsorbed hydrogen. The interatomic interactions were further determined using the quantum theory of atoms-in-molecules (QTAIM), which involves calculating various topological descriptors at the bond critical points. The detailed investigation of hydrogen storage in the BP-AlN nanosheet shows that the material exhibits high gravimetric and volumetric hydrogen storage capacities of 8.96 wt% and 105.41 g/L, respectively, exceeding the U.S. Department of Energy (US DOE) long-term targets of 6.5 wt% and 50 g/L. In addition, the calculated average hydrogen binding affinities range from − 0.24 to -0.29 eV/H 2 . The efficiency of the hydrogen uptake-release cycle was evaluated by calculating the hydrogen desorption temperat…

Efficacy, safety, and strategy-modifying factors of pulsed field ablation for persistent and long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is increasingly applied in persistent atrial fibrillation (PerAF) and long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation (LSPAF). Previous reviews of mixed AF populations suggested potential advantages in procedural efficiency and esophageal safety, but PerAF/LSPAF-specific evidence on long-term rhythm outcomes and on the value of posterior wall or extended substrate strategies remains limited, with substantial heterogeneity in lesion sets, endpoint definitions, and comparator types. Methods We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Scopus through April 18, 2026, with an updated verification search performed in August 2026. Because of clinical and methodological heterogeneity, formal pairwise pooling was restricted to comparisons supported by at least two clinically homogeneous head-to-head studies; single-study comparisons were synthesized narratively, and strategy-level outcomes were explored with single-arm proportion meta-analysis of exact-count cohorts. Off-antiarrhythmic drug (off-AAD) outcomes were prioritized when available. Certainty of evidence was rated using the GRADE approach. Results Twenty-two studies (approximately 3,100 patients) were included. In an exploratory pooled analysis of the only two available head-to-head comparisons (380 patients, with imbalanced study weights and different lesion sets: PVI-on…

Alpha-galactosylceramide as mRNA vaccine adjuvant modulates cellular immunity against tuberculosis and contributes to antigen-specific lung-associated T cells with a TRM-associated phenotype following prime-pull strategy
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains the leading cause of death from a single infectious agent worldwide, highlighting the need for improved vaccines beyond the limited protection currently provided by the Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine. Here we investigated the immunological impact of incorporating alpha-Galactosylceramide (αGC) into mRNA lipid nanoparticles (mRNA-LNPs) as a vaccination strategy against Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), the pathogen causing TB. Using Mtb antigens ESAT-6 and Ag85B, we demonstrate that αGC-adjuvanted mRNA-LNPs induce controlled activation of invariant natural killer T (iNKT) cells, thereby reshaping vaccine-induced immunity. Specifically, αGC incorporation promoted the generation of CD44 + CD69 + CD62L - CD4 + T cells in the spleen and altered the CD4 + T -helper (T H ) profile through the addition of modest T H 2 and T H 17 responses alongside robust T H 1 immunity. Furthermore, antigen-specific CD8 + T-cell responses against ESAT-6 and Ag85B were observed exclusively in the genetically diverse CB6F1/J mouse model, highlighting the importance of host genetic background in evaluating mRNA vaccine immunogenicity after homologous vaccination strategies. Finally, we demonstrate that using a heterologous prime–pull strategy combining intramuscular mRNA vaccination with local antigen instillation increased the frequency of antigen-specific lung-associat…

title: In Situ Cellulose Removal from Wood: A Novel Strategy for Preparing Simulated 80,000-Year-Old Waterlogged Archaeological Wood
abstract: Abstract Waterlogged archaeological wood (WAW), characterized by extensive degradation of cellulose and hemicellulose with concomitant relative lignin enrichment, represents a vital yet vulnerable class of cultural heritage materials. Due to the scarcity of archaeological wood specimens, the preparation of simulated WAW is essential for the systematic development and rigorous evaluation of consolidation and conservation treatments. However, existing simulation methods cannot adequately replicate the characteristic composition of WAW—namely, preferential polysaccharide loss and relative lignin enrichment—within practical timescales. This study presents a novel in-situ strategy utilizing recoverable lithium bromide (LiBr) under precisely controlled thermal conditions to fabricate simulated WAW with tunable degradation levels. Under optimized conditions (40 wt % LiBr, 150 °C, 8 h), the treated wood achieved a maximum water content (MWC) of 779% (degradation grade IV). Comprehensive characterization via FTIR, XRD, TGA, and polarized light microscopy confirmed faithful replication of archaeological degradation, including lignin enrichment, cellulose amorphization, and reduced crystallinity (13.3%). Concentration-dependent investigations revealed distinct mechanisms, swelling-mediated degradation versus cellulose dissolution, offering versatile control over degradation kinetics. The …

title: Targeting the CD4+ effector memory T cells re-expressing CD45RA suppressor galectin-7: a multi-omics-guided therapeutic strategy for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
abstract: Abstract Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a chronic, progressive interstitial lung disease with limited therapeutic options. Although single-cell and spatial transcriptomics have revealed cellular heterogeneity within the IPF lung microenvironment, the immune drivers with causal relevance remain poorly defined. Here, through large-scale Mendelian randomization integrating multi-omics data, we identified a consistent negative causal association between the proportion of CD4⁺ effector memory T cells re-expressing CD45RA (TEMRA) and IPF risk. Multi-platform validation—including single-cell RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, and multiplex immunofluorescence—confirmed a significant reduction in CD4⁺ TEMRA frequency in both peripheral blood and lung tissues of IPF patients, establishing this subset as a clinically relevant biomarker. Spatial transcriptomics further revealed a negative correlation between TEMRA differentiation signatures and local fibrotic burden. Mechanistically, integrated single-cell analyses pinpointed metaplastic KRT5⁺ basal cells as a key epithelial population with the capacity to disrupt immune homeostasis. These aberrant epithelial cells upregulate Galectin-7 ( LGALS7 ), which we demonstrate competes with IL-7 for receptor binding, suppresses STAT5 phosphorylation, and limits CD4⁺ TEMRA differentiation, thereby uncovering a previously unrecognized epithelia…

title: Polda Metro Jaya Public Relations Communication Strategy in the Implementation of the "Jaga Jakarta" Program through Internal and External Synergy
abstract: The development of public communication in the digital era encourages government institutions, including the National Police of the Republic of Indonesia, to implement adaptive, participatory, and collaborative communication strategies in building relationships with the community. One form of implementation is realized through the "Jaga Jakarta" Program initiated by the Metro Jaya Police as a preventive effort in building public security and order through internal and external synergy. This study aims to analyze the communication strategy of the Public Relations of the Metro Jaya Police in the implementation of the "Jaga Jakarta" Program through internal and external synergies as an effort to build public order. The research uses a qualitative approach with case study methods and constructivism paradigms. Data is collected through in-depth interviews, observations, and documentation, then analyzed using data reduction techniques, data presentation, and conclusion drawing from the Miles and Huberman model, with validity testing through triangulation of sources and techniques. The results of the study show that the Public Relations of the Metro Jaya Police implements a communication strategy that includes audience analysis, message preparation, method determination, and selection of communication media supported by internal coordination and collaboration with various stakeholders…

title: Grasping like humans: a stacked-fabric grasp localization strategy based on convex structure perception and hierarchical fuzzy decision-making
abstract: Introduction Due to the complex structures, variable morphologies, and multiple feasible grasping strategies for entangled fabrics during stacked sorting, achieving stable robotic grasping in such scenarios remains highly challenging. This study formulates the stacked-fabric grasping task as a problem of structural perception and multi-attribute decision-making. Methods A stacked-fabric grasping method is proposed. Specifically, a convex-structure perception method based on point cloud geometric features is developed to extract operable regions from point cloud data, and a set of candidate grasp poses is generated based on these structures. Furthermore, to address the difficulty of effectively evaluating candidate poses, a hierarchical fuzzy neural network is developed by simulating the human fuzzy decision-making process, enabling interpretable evaluation and selection of the optimal grasp pose. Results Comparative experiments are conducted on a constructed fabric grasping dataset. Compared with the best-performing baseline model, the proposed method improves the prediction accuracy of grasp feasibility, grasp separation effectiveness, and grasp reliability by 1.3%, 0.3%, and 0.7%, respectively. Robotic grasping experiments further show that the proposed method achieves a grasping success rate of 93.3% in randomly stacked scenarios. Discussion The results demonstrate that inte…

title: Scalable quaternary topological insulator for low-power spintronics
abstract: Topological insulators (TIs) with spin-momentum-locked surface states exhibit high charge-to-spin (C2S) conversion efficiency. However, binary and ternary TIs are constrained by a narrow tunable composition window for their insulating bulk states, which limits spintronic performance due to interference from bulk conduction. This work reports the development of a high-quality quaternary TI, [Sb2Te3(5−t)/Bi2Se3(t)]4, fabricated via scalable magnetron sputtering. By tuning the Bi2Se3 layer thickness, the quaternary TI exhibits high resistivity and low carrier concentration, effectively suppressing bulk conduction across a broad tunable window. Over a wide Bi2Se3 thickness range (t = 0.2–1.5 nm, corresponding to 3%–23% Bi2Se3 content), a high spin Hall angle (θSH) of 0.4–0.99 is maintained. Furthermore, in heterostructures based on this quaternary TI, the critical magnetization switching current density drops to as low as 3.3 × 105 A/cm2, which is two orders of magnitude lower than that of heavy metal Pt. Owing to the large spin Hall angle, the quaternary TI also exhibits power consumption approximately 20 times lower than ternary TIs for t = 0.2–1.5 nm. These results confirm that scalable quaternary TIs enable low-power spintronic devices with enhanced efficiency and processing flexibility, paving the way for advanced spintronic applications.

title: A hybrid deep learning–based OCR model for handwritten medical prescriptions
abstract: The current trend involving the use of paper-based medical prescriptions and the exchange of such by the social media is a major problem in automated and accurate text extraction in healthcare processes. This paper suggests a complete smart pipeline to digitize the images of medical prescriptions with lightweight deep learning-based classification, specialized Optical Character Recognition (OCR) engines, and comparative benchmarking of results using a large language model (LLM). The web scraped images of medical prescriptions are initially processed through a GhostNetV2 classifier to differentiate between handwritten and digital medical prescriptions. According to this choice, digital images are sent to PaddleOCR, and handwritten images are considered in Tesseract OCR so that each image could be processed by the best suitable recognition engine. The OCR outputs from both branches are benchmarked against GPT-4o (OpenAI) as an independent baseline to assess competitive performance and provide error-rate context. Experimental analysis shows that the suggested adaptive routing strategy is characterized by the fact that it has a high classification rate and the character and word error rates are significantly lower than those single-OCR techniques. The system is competitive with, though does not exceed, the raw accuracy of a state-of-the-art LLM-based OCR baseline (GPT-4o), while of…

Cyber-pornography use among a sample of Chinese university students: utilizing machine learning and network analysis
abstract: Background Due to the popularity and convenience of the internet, cyber-pornography use among youth has attracted the widespread attention of scholars. Cyber-pornography use among Chinese university students remains rarely investigated, especially based on ecological systems theory using machine learning and network analysis approaches. Therefore, the present study examined cyber-pornography use through machine learning and network analysis based on ecological systems theory among a sample of Chinese university students. Methods A sample of 1322 university students in different provinces of China were surveyed in a cross-sectional study. The survey included cyber-pornography use variables, demographic information, psychological variables, family variables, and school factors. Results Of 1332 participants, 25 students were classed as high-risk cyber-pornography users (1.9%). The XGBoost model of machine learning identified 15 important features of cyber-pornography use including social ostracism, moral disengagement, gender, teacher fairness, year of study, age, autonomy, self-control, depression, father and mother’s parenting style, relatedness, experience of being left behind, loneliness, and family closeness. In the network analysis, social ostracism was the strongest node in the total sample and among males, whereas depression was the strongest node in females. Conclusions P…

title: A Vision Transformer-based few-shot learning approach for leaf disease classification
abstract: Plant disease detection is often hindered by a lack of large, annotated image datasets, a key limitation for standard deep learning. Few-shot learning (FSL) addresses this challenge by transferring a learned comparison strategy from a data-rich source domain to a new, low-data target task. This paper investigates the robustness and limitations of this knowledge transfer process. A critical “metric domain gap” is first identified, demonstrating that an FSL model’s comparison strategy can fail catastrophically when meta-trained on a visually dissimilar source domain, even when paired with a state-of-the-art feature extractor. To resolve this, a synergistic training strategy is proposed, which combines in-domain meta-learning of a relation network with simultaneous fine-tuning of a Vision Transformer (ViT) backbone. This method ensures that both the feature representation and the similarity metric are co-adapted for the target domain. The final model, ViTRelNet, demonstrates the success of this approach, achieving a robust 87.38%, 92.72%, and 91.79% accuracy on unseen Jamun, Guava, and Cassava disease benchmarks using only five examples per class, effectively resolving the data scarcity challenge for this task.

title: The Implementation of the 5S Culture in Shaping the Religious Character of Pupils at MTs Safinatun Najah
abstract: The development of students’ religious morality requires educational environments that consistently integrate character values into daily practices. In Islamic educational institutions, school culture can function as a medium for character formation through repeated habituation and social interaction. This study aims to explore the implementation of the 5S culture (Smile, Greet, Say Hello, Be Polite, and Be Courteous) and its relationship with students’ religious morality at MTs Safinatun Najah, Blora. This study employed a qualitative descriptive approach. Data were collected through observations, semi-structured interviews, and documentation involving the head of the madrasah, guidance and counseling teacher, and student informants. Data were analyzed through data condensation, data display, and conclusion verification, with credibility strengthened through source triangulation, technique triangulation, and member checking. The findings indicate that the 5S culture has been institutionalized through madrasah policies, morning-duty teacher arrangements, teacher role modeling, and daily student interactions. Students demonstrated habitual practices of greeting teachers, practicing salim, communicating politely, and showing respectful interactions within the madrasah environment. Supporting documentary evidence showed a 35% decrease in recorded disciplinary violations, positive …

title: An ensemble machine learning approach for measuring and predicting formwork labor productivity
abstract: Abstract The construction industry is a major driver of innovation and economic growth. A key factor in this growth is the continuous focus on improving labor productivity, which directly impacts project timelines and costs. Maximizing labor productivity is crucial for overcoming project challenges, accurately forecasting activity durations, and achieving optimal efficiency. Despite its importance, many traditional methods for estimating labor productivity rely on theoretical assumptions that often prove to be inaccurate, leading to significant inefficiencies in both time and cost management. This issue is particularly pronounced in Egypt, where there are no standardized criteria for predicting labor productivity in the construction sector. Recent studies have shown that productivity has a significant effect on project cost and duration, indicating that this issue needs to be studied carefully in Egypt. Therefore, this research addresses the challenges of inaccurate productivity estimation by introducing a novel, data-driven approach. The study focuses on the specific activity of column formwork and was conducted at three Egyptian construction sites: Smouha, Beheira, and Moharam-Bek. The study analyzed 198 records collected from real construction sites. These records were distributed among the three studied sites as follows: 63 records from Smouha, 57 records from Beheira, and …

title: Machine learning-derived R-loop-related diagnostic signature for psoriasis: a multi-cohort and single-cell validation study
abstract: Background Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease characterized by dysregulated immune responses and keratinocyte (KC) hyperproliferation. Although therapeutic strategies have advanced considerably, achieving durable long-term remission remains challenging. R-loops are three-stranded nucleic acid structures involved in genomic stability and inflammatory regulation in multiple diseases; however, their role in psoriasis remains poorly understood. Objective To investigate the involvement of R-loops in psoriasis, develop an R-loop-related diagnostic signature, and identify key molecular drivers of disease pathogenesis. Methods Transcriptomic data from five public bulk RNA expression cohorts (GSE30999, GSE41664, GSE13355, GSE6710, and GSE14905) and one single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) dataset (GSE173706) were integrated for analysis of psoriatic and non-lesional skin samples. R-loop-related differentially expressed genes were identified and used to construct an R-loop-related diagnostic signature (RRDS) using the Elastic Net machine learning algorithm. Model performance was evaluated using three complementary analytical approaches, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was performed to quantify the contribution of individual genes. scRNA-seq data were further analyzed to validate the findings at the cellular level. In addition, the biological function of …

title: From feminist protest music to the war machine. A Philosophical Analysis of the Construction of War Machines against Patriarchy Arising from the Performative Act of Interpreting Feminist Protest Music
abstract: Protest music is a performative act that has allowed those who are invisible in the public sphere to intervene in the everyday soundscape, making their presence felt and denouncing the situations that afflict them. This performative act gives rise to the feelings embedded in the works that are performed and generates an effect on the listeners/spectators. This work proposes a philosophical analysis that sheds light on the performative act of interpreting feminist protest music, its role in the public sphere, the political action of art, and the formation of war machines that deterritorialize and territorialize subjectivities, everyday life, and structures.

title: How learning environments shape science achievement: evidence from PISA 2022
abstract: Purpose This study examines how students' perceptions of the school learning environment are associated with science achievement in Australia using PISA 2022 data. It focuses on five psychosocial dimensions drawn from the student questionnaire: sense of belonging, cooperation, trust, empathy, and leadership, and aims to clarify their relative associations with achievement within the learning environment's tradition. Design/methodology/approach The study uses Australian data from PISA 2022 and models relationships between five psychosocial learning environment dimensions and science achievement. Because PISA reports achievement through ten plausible values and uses a complex sample design, the analysis treats results as population-level associations rather than causal effects. Structural equation modelling was used to estimate the relationships among the focal constructs and science performance. Findings All five learning environment dimensions are positively associated with science achievement. Empathy and sense of belonging show comparatively stronger relationships than leadership, cooperation, and trust. However, the explained variance is modest, indicating that psychosocial dimensions matter but represent only one part of a wider set of factors linked to science performance among Australian students. Research limitations/implications The study is limited to cross-sectional P…

title: PENGARUH PENDEKATAN DEEP LEARNING BERBANTUAN APLIKASI LIVEWORKSHEET TERHADAP HASIL BELAJAR PENDIDIKAN PANCASILA PADA SISWA KELAS IV SD
abstract: ABSTRACT Pancasila Education at the elementary school level requires learning experiences that go beyond the acquisition of information by providing students with opportunities to understand and process subject matter more deeply. This study analyzes the effect of the deep learning approach assisted by Liveworksheet on the learning outcomes of fourth-grade students in Pancasila Education at SD Negeri 90 Palembang. The study employed a quantitative approach using an experimental method with a Posttest-Only Control Design. From a population of 79 students, 53 students were selected as the sample, consisting of 26 students from class IV-A as the experimental group and 27 students from class IV-B as the control group. Data were collected through tests and documentation, followed by normality and homogeneity tests prior to hypothesis testing. The final outcomes of the two groups revealed a substantial difference, with a mean score of 84.73 in the experimental group and 60.89 in the control group. This difference was confirmed through an Independent Samples t-test, yielding t = 12.959, df = 51, and p < 0.001. These findings confirm that the deep learning approach assisted by Liveworksheet affects students' learning outcomes in Pancasila Education within the context of this study, while also providing opportunities for the use of digital learning that remains oriented toward the depth…

title: Machine learning approaches for phishing detection and cybersecurity awareness in digital infrastructure
abstract: Introduction Phishing remains a dominant socio-technical threat to digital infrastructure, serving as an entry vector for credential-theft, ransomware, and supply-chain incidents. The machine learning literature on phishing-URL detection remains fragmented across heterogeneous datasets, inconsistent leakage controls, and explanation pipelines seldom cross-validated by independent attribution methods. Methods An end-to-end, leakage-controlled machine learning framework was developed over a balanced corpus of 11,430 instances and 87 engineered URL-lexical, HTML-content, and external-reputation features, with all preprocessing transforms fit on the training partition only. Eleven heterogeneous classifiers were benchmarked; the best classical model (LightGBM) was repurposed as a deterministic feature extractor whose out-of-fold posterior probabilities augmented the input to a hybrid CNN-BiLSTM. Statistical significance was assessed via Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm-Bonferroni correction on 10-fold cross-validation F 1 scores, and two explainable-AI methods (Tree SHAP and Permutation Importance) were applied alongside ablation studies. Results LightGBM attained F 1 = 0.9699 and AUC = 0.9943, significantly outperforming every other classifier ( p ≤ 0.002) except XGBoost ( p = 0.375). The CNN-BiLSTM hybrid attained F 1 = 0.9652 and recall = 0.9703. SHAP and Permutation Importan…

title: An inertial acceleration stochastic three-term conjugate gradient algorithm for machine learning
abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop a stochastic optimization algorithm that accelerates and stabilizes convergence in large-scale nonconvex machine learning problems. Motivated by the limitations of stochastic gradient descent and existing stochastic conjugate gradient methods, we propose an inertial-accelerated framework that incorporates both momentum and correction strategies to enhance convergence efficiency and robustness. Design/methodology/approach The proposed Projected Stochastic Accelerated Three-Term Conjugate Gradient (PSATCG) algorithm extends the three-term conjugate gradient framework by introducing a two-step inertial acceleration and a modified correction term. An improved inexact line search strategy ensures global convergence under mild conditions. Theoretical analysis establishes linear convergence, and numerical experiments are conducted on two nonconvex machine learning models across nine benchmark datasets. Findings Experimental results demonstrate that PSATCG consistently achieves faster and more stable convergence than stochastic gradient descent (SGD), SAGA, SARAH and adaptive optimizers such as Adam and RMSprop. The algorithm maintains strong robustness under weak regularization and noisy conditions, validating the theoretical findings on stability and linear convergence. Originality/value This work introduces two major innovations: a two-step inertia…

title: Multi-gate organic dendritic transistors for spatiotemporal BCM learning
abstract: The Bienenstock–Cooper–Munro (BCM) learning rule effectively mitigates the issue of synaptic weight oversaturation in Hebbian learning via a sliding threshold dependent on historical neuronal activity. However, existing hardware implementations focus primarily on temporal history while often overlooking the spatial attenuation pivotal for signal integration. Here, we report a bio-inspired multi-gate organic dendritic transistor based on poly(3-hexylthiophene) with electrochemical gating that integrates spatiotemporal information to implement the BCM rule via its spatial architecture. By tuning the physical distances between different gates and the channel, the device mimics the nonlinear signal attenuation mechanism of biological dendrites. Beyond reproducing fundamental synaptic plasticity, the device establishes a sliding threshold mechanism for homeostatic regulation by using physical distances to modulate historical activity states. This work demonstrates the feasibility of defining synaptic historical states using spatial factors, providing a strategy for neuromorphic computing systems that combine homeostatic regulation with spatiotemporal processing.

title: Religiosity as an Effort to Shape Students' Positive Behavior at UPTD SDN 54 Barru
abstract: This study examines how Islamic Religious Education (Pendidikan Agama Islam, PAI) develops religiosity and how participants perceive its association with pupils' positive behavior at UPTD SDN 54 Barru, South Sulawesi. Using a qualitative single-case study design, data were collected through non-participant observation, semi-structured interviews with the principal, PAI teachers, pupils in Grades V and VI, and parents or guardians, and a review of learning documents and school program records. Data were analyzed through condensation, display, and conclusion drawing and verification, with credibility supported by source, technique, and time triangulation, researcher diligence, and member checking. The findings identify five mutually reinforcing mechanisms: teacher exemplarity, habituation of religious activities, contextual and practical PAI learning, a supportive religious school culture, and school-family collaboration. Across these mechanisms, participants and observations linked religiosity to greetings and prayers, regular worship, politeness, respect, discipline, honesty, care, and responsibility. These findings should be interpreted as context-bound qualitative associations rather than evidence of causal effects. The study's main contribution is an integrated account of how religious knowledge, worship practice, adult modeling, school culture, and family reinforcement oper…

title: ChatGPT Use and Learning Motivation among Informatics Students: A Preliminary Correlational Study
abstract: Generative AI systems such as ChatGPT are increasingly used by university students for explanation, code inspection, idea generation, and immediate feedback. This preliminary cross-sectional study examines the association between ChatGPT use frequency and learning motivation among 17 Informatics Engineering students at Universitas Mulia, Balikpapan. Data were collected through an online questionnaire using a four-category measure of ChatGPT use frequency and four-point agreement responses for learning motivation. The original analysis reported a Pearson correlation of r = 0.685 with p = 0.002. Using the reported coefficient and sample size, the corresponding test statistic is t(15) = 3.642 and the Fisher-transformed 95% confidence interval is approximately 0.305-0.877, indicating a positive but imprecisely estimated association. The finding is consistent with literature suggesting that responsive AI tools may support engagement and perceived competence, but the correlational design does not establish that ChatGPT use increases motivation. Reverse causality, self-selection, prior achievement, digital confidence, purpose of use, and measurement limitations remain plausible explanations. The study contributes context-specific evidence from informatics students and identifies requirements for stronger follow-up research, including a larger sample, validated motivation measures, cle…

title: Strengthening Menstrual-Fiqh Literacy Through Islamic Tutoring Among Vocational High School Students: An Implementation Study at SMK Negeri 1 Jepon
abstract: Islamic Religious Education (PAI) in vocational high schools (SMK) has limited instructional time to address specific and sensitive religious topics such as menstrual jurisprudence (fiqh of haid), so that female students often only understand the prohibition of worship during menstruation without a comprehensive grasp of the related rulings. This study aims to describe and analyze the implementation of Islamic tutoring (bimbingan belajar Islami) as an effort to strengthen menstrual-fiqh literacy among female students at SMK Negeri 1 Jepon, covering students' initial understanding, the materials delivered, the implementation process, the role of the PAI teacher, and the supporting and inhibiting factors. This study used a qualitative approach with a descriptive case study design, involving 300 female students of SMK Negeri 1 Jepon who took part in the tutoring, together with the PAI teacher (Husnul) and a supporting team consisting of the guidance and counseling (BK) teacher, homeroom teachers, and the PIK-R and PMR student units, selected purposively as informants. Menstrual-fiqh literacy was identified through students' responses during discussion and interviews on key indicators, namely the concept of menstruation, the minimum-maximum duration of menstruation, the distinction between menstrual and istihadhah blood, and purification procedures, supported by a review of the tut…

title: Vibration–current multimodal fusion for within-batch recognition of predefined component faults of a high-pressure abrasive waterjet machine tool
abstract: Reliable recognition of component faults in high-pressure abrasive waterjet machine tools requires complementary information about local structural dynamics and machine-level load variations. This study presents a vibration–current multimodal fusion framework for recognizing normal operation and five predefined component faults. The framework integrates triaxial vibration features with machine-supply current features and evaluates feature-level and decision-level fusion using fivefold contiguous time-block cross-validation. Feature-level fusion with a support vector machine achieved a macro-F1 score of 98.27%, exceeding the current-only and vibration-only models by 7.06 and 14.50 percentage points, respectively. Both equal-weight and adaptive decision-level fusion achieved macro-F1 scores above 99.6%. Feature-group ablation further supported the contributions of time-domain, frequency-domain, and cross-axis vibration information to component-state recognition. An auxiliary deterministic rule-based module checks consistency between predicted states and monitoring locations and organizes observed feature deviations and predefined verification actions into structured evidence records while preserving the original classifier outputs. The reported performance represents recognition across time segments within a single experimental batch under fixed sensor placement, rather than gene…

title: Deep vein thrombosis exacerbated by syndecan-4 shedding and piezo1-dependent endothelial-mesenchymal transition
abstract: Abstract Background and Aims Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) remains a major health burden with incompletely understood mechanisms and limited therapeutic options. This study aims to investigate the role of key molecules in DVT and to explore the feasibility of treatment strategies based on this mechanism. Methods Plasma proteomic profiling (LC-MS/MS) was performed on DVT patients and healthy controls, identifying syndecan-4 (SDC4) as a differentially expressed protein. Functional investigations utilized SDC4 knockout mice, endothelial cell (EC)-specific lineage tracing models, and single-cell RNA sequencing to assess endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) during DVT progression. In vitro EndMT models were established in human umbilical vein endothelial cells. Protein interactions were confirmed by co-immunoprecipitation. Piezo1 was pharmacologically inhibited in vivo, and network pharmacology was used to seek a potential therapeutic agent. Results SDC4 levels were elevated in DVT patients. SDC4 deficiency exacerbated thrombus formation and promoted EndMT, as evidenced by reduced EC markers and increased mesenchymal markers. Single-cell sequencing revealed a specific EC subpopulation (C1) driving EndMT, with Piezo1 identified as a downstream mediator of SDC4. Co-IP confirmed direct SDC4–Piezo1 interaction. Piezo1 upregulation activated the PI3K/Akt pathway, Piezo1 knockdown a…

title: Diamond-based deep ultraviolet vortex beam generation with suppressed higher-order diffractions
abstract: Optical vortices (OVs) with unique singular phase and orbital angular momentum are widely used in various applications including particle manipulation, microscopy, and imaging scenarios. Regardless, the undesired higher-order foci introduced by the conventional vortex lens such as spiral zone plates may lead to additional artifacts and thus degrade contrast sensitivity. In this endeavor, based on the typical trapezoidal contour matrix and the neural network-based inverse design approach, we propose an innovative single-focus OV lens termed trapezoidal spiral zone plates (TSZPs) to eliminate the higher-order foci which unavoidably exist in the conventional muti-foci lens. Considering the low thermal expansion of diamond materials, we have fabricated the TSZPs sample based on high-quality single-crystal diamond substrate using electron beam lithography. To verify the stable single-focus performance even under harsh environments of such optics, a demonstration experiment in the deep ultraviolet region has also been performed. These findings provide an avenue for improving the image performance of diamond-based optics in solar-blind imaging.

title: The soundscape of uncertainty. A cry from childhoods in confinement
abstract: The critical period derived from the covid-19 pandemic brought with it a unique sensory perception in spatiality. In an environment located southeast of Mexico City, the way I experienced the soundscape of the place I live in had drastic changes. This is the product of a sound metacommunication, at a distance, promoted by a group of children fed up with confinement. But in addition to this experience, the way in which the sounds of nature made an appearance led me to keep an audiovisual record of what “was always there”, but acquired other meanings during social isolation. This article contributes to the field of aural studies around three issues: interventions to establish sound dialogues from the private to the public space; the sounds of nature and creative improvisation as companions of social isolation; the restructuring of ontological security brought about by the desire to inhabit space.

title: Semi-supervised Bayesian deep clustering with uncertainty-guided representation and robustness
abstract: Introduction In real-world data, tackling missing data, noisy observations, and uncertainty at the same time is hard since the number of labelled data is limited. Current deep clustering algorithms have considered the imputation, noise, semi-supervision, and uncertainty problems separately, such as without modelling the uncertainty in the noise, or without modelling the missingness in the missing data. There is still a need to develop an end-to-end deep clustering algorithm that incorporates all these four factors. Methods To overcome the limitations, we propose to robust the semi-supervised Bayesian Deep Clustering (RBDC), which involves four parts, namely: The Student-t decoder does not explicitly impute for missing features and yields a robust reconstruction for heavy-tailed noise. Label-guided Gaussian mixture priors provide partial class label guidance in the learning process within the latent space, which is positioned between supervised and unsupervised learning. An uncertainty-weighted Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO) scales the contribution of each sample by the posterior uncertainty, effectively being noisy or contaminated. Sytems with Hybrid EM + SGD optimisation strategy. The mixture is trained using the hybrid EM + SGD optimisation strategies. The latent uncertainty is used in the mixture updates. The framework is tested on University of California, Irvine (UCI) Adult I…

title: Heterogeneous electro-Fenton degradation of methyl orange: Multivariate optimization and voltammetric monitoring
abstract: Abstract The degradation of methyl orange (MO) was investigated using the heterogeneous electro-Fenton (het-EF) process, with synthetic goethite (S-Goe) as an iron-based catalyst in an undivided cell equipped with a Dimensionally Stable Anode (DSA) and an air-diffusion cathode. A full factorial design (FFD) combined with response surface methodology (RSM) was used to evaluate the effects and interactions of the variables pH and applied current on MO degradation. The best-performing conditions within the investigated experimental domain were obtained at pH 3.0 and 100 mA, decreasing the MO concentration from 20 mg L⁻ 1 to 1.04 ± 0.11 mg L⁻ 1 by spectrophotometry and to 0.860 ± 0.10 mg L⁻ 1 by differential pulse voltammetry (DPV), respectively, corresponding to approximated removal efficiency of 95%. The catalyst exhibited good stability and activity over four consecutive cycles, demonstrating its effectiveness in the het-EF process under the investigated conditions. Monitoring of Fe 2 ⁺, Fe 3 ⁺, and total dissolved Fe indicated limited iron leaching during treatment, supporting the contribution of heterogeneous Fenton reactions alongside homogeneous reactions involving dissolved iron species. DPV showed suitable analytical performance for monitoring MO, with limits of detection and quantification of 9.98 × 10 –7 mol L⁻ 1 and 4.73 × 10 –7 mol L⁻ 1 , respectively. The novelty lies…

title: Moderate-scale operation of family farms in China: underlying logic, practical constraints, and optimization pathways for sustainable food systems
abstract: The transformation of sustainable food systems must reconcile production efficiency and supply resilience with the protection of smallholder livelihoods, and for economies with large populations and limited arable land this reconciliation rests heavily on how the scale of family-farm operation is understood and organized. The academic community has long held theoretical disagreements on this issue between static efficiency standards and dynamic equilibrium perspectives, and no integrated explanatory framework that combines economic logic, social context and temporal dimensions has yet been established. Drawing on new institutional economics, economic sociology, family life-cycle theory and intergenerational transmission theory, and proceeding through theoretical deduction, institutional context analysis and secondary evidence from policy documents, official statistics and literature, this paper develops a triple-constraint dynamic equilibrium framework for the moderate-scale operation of family farms in China; its purpose is explanatory rather than estimative, since no uniform optimal scale is defensible across heterogeneous regional endowments, crop systems, service conditions and family structures. The framework holds that moderate scale is not a fixed value set externally but a dynamic equilibrium interval of operating scale: the economic-efficiency constraint sets its lower…

title: From point-to-point to hub-and-cluster: a systematic review of co-optimization of source–sink matching and transport networks for large-scale CO2 sequestration
abstract: Large-scale carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) requires coordinated source–sink matching (SSM), transport infrastructure, and geological storage planning. This review examines how published studies couple source allocation, network topology and capacity, CO 2 flow, and storage availability. Following PRISMA 2020 guidance, a reproducible Web of Science and Scopus search identified 17 studies for direct evidence synthesis. The evidence shows that integrated models can jointly represent source–sink allocation, transport-network investment, operational flow, and storage constraints, whereas sequential approaches may overlook system-wide trade-offs. Mathematical programming remains the most auditable basis for strategic planning because it provides explicit feasibility constraints and, in some cases, optimality bounds. Hub-and-cluster and multimodal configurations can improve infrastructure sharing, but their value depends on utilization, phased connection, access conditions, and cost recovery. Evidence for metaheuristics and AI-enabled methods remains case-specific; their comparative value cannot be established without common instances and complete reporting of feasibility, solution quality, and computational effort. Future research should develop physically valid large-scale benchmarks, adaptive planning models, and governance-aware mechanisms for shared CCUS infrastr…

Breeding of high-yield cold-adapted lipase fungi, optimization of fermentation conditions and isolation and purification of lipase
abstract: Abstract Cold-adapted lipases have attracted extensive research attention in enzymology owing to their unique low-temperature adaptability and catalytic properties, and investigations in this area continue to deepen. This study aimed to efficiently produce a cold-adapted lipase to overcome the limitations of conventional lipases under low-temperature conditions, such as low activity, high cost, and restricted applicability. Fungal strains were isolated from naturally cold environments, and subjected to multiple rounds of screening for lipase activity. A selected strain was further improved by UV-nitrosoguanidine (NTG) combined mutagenesis, followed by optimization of fermentation conditions. The lipasewas purified by ammonium sulfate precipitation, Q-HP anion exchange chromatography, and Superdex 75 gel filtration chromatography, and its enzymatic properties were characterized. A lipase-producing strain identified as Aspergillus niger was obtained through screening. Following combined mutagenesis, lipase activity by the mutant strain increased by 127.35%. Under the optimized fermentation conditions (temperature 21℃, pH 6.0, inoculation size 6.5 × 10 6 spores/mL), the lipase activity further increased to 57.26 U/mL. After purification, the cold-adapted lipase exhibited a specific activity of 113.52 U/mg. Its optimal reaction temperature was 30℃ and pH 7.0 and retained more than …

title: A feature-optimized EEG framework using multiscale entropy and metaheuristic optimization for cognitive analysis
abstract: Background Cognitive activity plays an important role by influencing working-memory, problem-solving, attention, response and decision making. EEG serves as a non-invasive approach to analyze neural activity associated with cognitive processing. The current study aims to identify the more contributing features to analyze the cognitive activity between sports and non-sports groups. Methods The present study included 100 participants, consisting of 80 males and 20 females aged between 19 and 23 years. EEG signals were acquired and preprocessed using filtering methods to remove unwanted noise and artifacts. The four-entropy metrics dispersion entropy, permutation entropy, sample entropy, and fuzzy entropy were applied to the coarse-graining method across multiple temporal scales to analyze the complexity of EEG signals. To identify the most informative feature subsets and reduce redundancy, filter-based methods such as Mutual Information, Pearson Correlation, Minimum Redundancy Maximum Relevance and wrapper-based methods such as Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization were applied. Finally for differentiating the cognitive activity, five machine learning classifiers that include Support Vector Machine, Artificial Neural Network, K -nearest neighbor, Decision Tree and Random Forest were applied. Statistical methods such as T -test and Fleiss kappa were used to analyse the…

Optimization of Okra [Abelmoschus esculentus (L.)] Production through Improved Technical Itineraries in Korhogo (Northern Côte d'Ivoire): Evaluation of some Agrophysiological Parameters
abstract: Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus) is cultivated throughout northern Côte d'Ivoire. However, it is threatened by poor soil quality, which reduces production. Our overall objective was to provide producers with technical itineraries to contribute to increased okra productivity. Therefore, planting beds consisting of flat ground (TP), ridges without polyethylene film cover (BSP), and ridges with polyethylene film cover (BAP) were prepared at densities of 20,000 and 80,000 plants per hectare. Fertilizers (F1, F2, F3, F4) were applied to the plants in three or four fractions. The trials were arranged in completely randomized blocks with three replications of four factors. Quantitative data were analyzed using STATISTICA 7.1 for analysis of variance (ANOVA) and XLSTAT version 2019 for principal component analysis (PCA). The results show that planting beds, planting density, fertilizer types, and application frequency significantly influenced vegetative parameters and okra weight (P < 0.001 at 5%). The highest weights were obtained with BAP (428.7 g), D20 density (610.2 g), and F4 fertilizer (856.4 g). The combination of these factors led to 48 technical itineraries. Principal component analysis (PCA) of the technical itineraries based on recorded growth and yield parameters revealed that all variables are positively oriented and strongly correlated with the F1 axis (86.06%). The distribu…
