title: Online capacitance-integrated development of a hybrid bioprocess model for industrial fungal fermentations
abstract: The growing demand for fermentation-based products has increased interest in bioprocess modelling approaches compatible with routinely available industrial process data. Capacitance probes are promising because they provide online data related to viable biomass, but their use in filamentous fungal fermentations remains challenging, as state-of-the-art cell-count-based calibration methods of capacitance data are not applicable to hyphal organisms under industrial settings. This study presents a capacitance-integrated hybrid modelling workflow for highly viscous, enzyme-producing filamentous fungal fermentations at pilot scale under data-scarce conditions. The oxygen mass transfer coefficient k L a was developed using an intra-batch design covering agitation, pressure, and aeration dynamics. The correlation achieved a model fit of R 2 = 0.95 and approximately 8% relative validation error. Capacitance data were used to define a pseudo-viable biomass state based on a single CDW-derived anchor point, reducing the need for repeated offline CDW measurements. A ±20% perturbation of this calibration point had only a minor effect on overall model accuracy within the dataset investigated. The hybrid model was assessed on two pilot-scale fermentations with distinct operating trajectories. One of the two batches was used for viscosity model selection and therefore does not represent a fully…

title: Evaluating on-line media and survey data to understand beliefs and sentiment associated with pastured and integrated poultry production among farmers and stakeholders
abstract: Commercial pastured and integrated poultry production (PIPP) represents an emerging area of poultry and crop production. As a “niche” area of commercial production, there is little overall knowledge about public opinion associated with PIPP. Here we utilized two complementary approaches to better understand current sentiment and associated challenges with PIPP-based production. Specifically, to understand farmer PIPP sentiment and challenges we surveyed commercial PIPP farmers. In parallel we captured stakeholder sentiment toward integrative farming (a slightly broader classification that includes PIPP) via the extraction of selected data (i.e., web-scraping) on the internet. The methodology combines web-scraping of various media and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to understand sentiment in a longitudinal fashion. Here we compared a farmer survey of 53 producers and 2,399 English language web-scraped online posts (e.g., from online forums, news sites, and blogs) from 1,089 unique authors between 2019 and 2021 to understand opinions of and experiences with PIPP. The survey data and online posts both highlighted soil health, animal welfare, and weed control as perceived benefits of PIPP. In addition, survey respondents identified food safety regulations or incidents, processing, and certifications as barriers to PIPP whereas these topics rarely appeared in online conversations…

title: Improvement of pedestrian road safety through Trunk Route 1 of the BRT system in Chihuahua: 2015–2020 analysis
abstract: The urban model of Chihuahua, characterized by its fragmentation, has intensified the dependence on the private automobile, generating negative externalities such as deaths and serious injuries due to road accidents that mainly affect pedestrians. In this context, the brt transportation system, inaugurated in 2013, represents the most important project in the state; however, there are no public studies that evaluate its impact. This work analyzes the influence of the brt trunk route 1 on pedestrian road safety through cartographic analysis and walkability audits. The results show that, although the objective of the brt was not to act as a road safety policy, its implementation has reduced the number of accidents in its surroundings. This is due to the geometric redesign and the incorporation of safe crossings at street level, which mitigate vehicle speed, the main risk factor for pedestrian safety.

Multi-valvular burden score and one-year mortality in ICU patients undergoing echocardiography: an exploratory cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background Multiple regurgitant lesions coexist in critically ill patients, yet cohort-level analyses typically represent each valve separately. We evaluated whether a Multi-Valvular Burden (MVB) score could summarize regurgitant involvement and whether its prognostic information differed from models retaining individual valve grades. Methods This retrospective cohort used MIMIC-IV v3.1 linked with MIMIC-IV-ECHO. Adults with an ICU admission and complete ordinal grading of tricuspid, mitral, and aortic regurgitation on an index echocardiogram within 72 h of ICU admission were included. MVB was the arithmetic sum of TR, MR, and AR grades (0–12). Cox models assessed 1-year all-cause mortality. Additional analyses compared MVB with separate valve-grade models, tested a high-burden definition requiring MVB > = 4 and at least two involved valves, used missing-aware AS/MS evidence proxies, and examined LVEF with structured RV-function classification. Results The cohort included 5,362 patients; 1,979 (36.9%) died within 1 year. Mortality increased from 24.6% at MVB 0 to 47.4% at MVB > = 4. After clinical adjustment, continuous MVB remained associated with mortality (HR 1.07 per point, 95% CI 1.05–1.09; P < 0.001), and MVB > = 4 was associated with higher mortality (HR 1.35, 95% CI 1.22–1.48; P < 0.001). The high-burden category predominantly reflected multivalve involvement: …

title: Enhancing Fritillariae Cirrhosae Bulbus authentication via Mask-AIR: a masked autoencoder driven information reconstruction and iterative attention framework for multi-view fusion
abstract: Fritillariae Cirrhosae Bulbus (FCB), a valuable medicinal and edible plant with antitussive properties, is frequently adulterated due to resource scarcity and high market price, necessitating rapid and accurate authentication. However, existing methods (morphological, molecular, chromatographic, etc.) are subjective, destructive, or suffer from DNA degradation. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a multi-modal information reconstruction framework based on a masked autoencoder (MAE) and an iterative attention mechanism that integrates a multi-view fusion strategy using three views (hyperspectral imaging, grayscale images, and pseudo-colour images) to enhance the authenticity identification of FCB. Specifically, multi-view data are fused to enrich information dimensions and thereby improve species recognition accuracy. An MAE operating in the latent feature space reconstructs randomly masked tokens from each modality, which enhances feature representation and mitigates cross-modal interference. Subsequently, hierarchical iterative attention module alternates query roles among modalities to balance fusion. Feature extraction, reconstruction, and classification are trained end-to-end, while inference retains only the encoder and classifier, incurring no extra cost. The experiments on a self-built FCB multi-view dataset show that the proposed method significantly impro…

title: Multi-omics profiling reveals homologous recombination repair hyperactivation as a therapeutic vulnerability in neuroendocrine cervical carcinoma
A semi-supervised multi-sensor remote sensing pipeline for mapping irrigation dynamics in ground-truth deficient conflict zones: a case study of the Kakhovka Dam failure
abstract: The ongoing war in Ukraine has drawn international attention to the impact of conflict on global agricultural production and food security. On 6 June 2023, the Kakhovka Dam was destroyed. The loss of this critical agricultural and energy infrastructure has left most farmers on the East bank of the Dnipro River without irrigation in Kherson and Zaporizhzhia oblasts. This study develops a multi-sensor Earth Observation framework combining high resolution satellite imagery (Sentinel-2, Landsat) with meteorological data (CHIRPS) and water productivity data (FAO WaPOR), using a semi-supervised machine learning pipeline. Using a rigorous stratified random-sampling approach with photointerpretation, we found pre-war irrigated areas between 2019 to 2021 to be on average 187.94 ± 14.43 kHa, approximately 4% of pre-war baseline cropland and 8% of summer season cropland in Kherson and Zaporizhzhia oblasts. In 2022, these numbers contracted to 140.04 ± 17.44 kHa with the expanded occupation of these territories by Russia, seeing an additional decline in 2023 to 74.97 ± 17.84 kHa. Fields in 2023 also exhibited variability in irrigation, ranging from interrupted irrigation owing to the destruction of the Kakhovka reservoir, to those that were sufficiently irrigated with water remaining in the channels. Irrigated areas diminished further in 2024 to 15.95 ± 9.97 kHa, a ∼91% decline from pre-wa…

Sustainable Logistics Management Practices and Performance of the Distribution Firm Industry in Kenya.
abstract: Sustainable logistics management practices have become a key driver of performance in the distribution industry as firms face increasing pressure to reduce environmental impact while remaining competitive amid rising operational costs, regulatory requirements and growing consumer awareness. However, many distribution firms in Kenya continue to rely on outdated transportation systems, inefficient warehousing and non-compliant waste disposal methods, which raise fuel costs, delay deliveries and weaken customer satisfaction. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to establish the effect of sustainable logistics management practices on the performance of the distribution firm industry in Kenya. It specifically examined the effect of sustainable transportation, sustainable packaging, sustainable inventory management and sustainable reverse logistics on performance. The study was anchored on the Resource-Based View, Triple Bottom Line Theory, Systems Theory and Closed-Loop Supply Chain Theory. A cross-sectional survey design was adopted, targeting 234 logistics mapping officers, dispatch officers, programme coordinators and supervisors in 26 distribution firms operating in Nairobi, Mombasa and Kisumu. A sample of 148 respondents was determined using the Yamane formula and selected through stratified random sampling. Data were collected using a semi-structured questionnaire and anal…

title: Looking for love in the wrong place: why marketers should focus on management accounting
abstract: Purpose Marketers and marketing academics are frustrated that the contribution of marketing to business success is inadequately represented in financial accounts. This study explains how marketers' interests are misaligned with the purpose and principles on which the financial statements are produced, and why and how marketers should focus on management accounting as the means for generating a more accurate portrait of the economic reality of the business. Design/methodology/approach We use a conceptual approach to investigate why external financial reports disregard the investment component of marketing and why this is unlikely to change. We examine the misalignment between marketing and financial accounting objectives, highlight issues on the marketing-accounting interface and suggest ways to address them. Findings We conclude that marketers' ambition to create a wider appreciation of the value they create is unlikely to be achieved through any changes to financial accounting rules in the foreseeable future. By focusing their efforts on financial accountants, rather than management accountants, marketers are looking for love in the wrong place. Practical implications We recommend marketers focus their efforts on management accounting, particularly in industries where marketing is a key driver of business performance, and suggest how to refocus. Originality/value This article …

title: A “family-school-hospital” collaborative oral health management model for preschool children: a prospective single-arm pre-post intervention study
abstract: Background Early childhood caries (ECC) remains a global public health challenge, yet preschool children lack autonomy in health management and depend heavily on family and school environments. Population-based oral health management models have proven effective in other fields but are rarely implemented in Chinese preschool settings. This study aimed to establish and evaluate a “family-school-hospital” collaborative oral health management model for preschool children in Chengdu, China. Methods The oral health management model for preschool children was established through population screening, baseline surveys, personalized oral health guidance, provision of diagnostic and treatment pathways, and the use of health behavior formation tools. The preliminary effects of promoting active health behavior formation were observed through oral health follow-up examinations and oral health-related questionnaire surveys conducted at 1-, 3-, and 6-month follow-ups. Results After establishing the oral health management model for preschool children, a total of 421 children completed the six-month follow-up, with a loss to follow-up rate of 11.4%. The increase in the number of teeth restored, the decrease in plaque index, the increase in the number of children participating in fluoride application or pit and fissure sealing, the improvement in the number of children using fluoride toothpaste…

title: ​Working Capital Management, Liquidity, and Profitability: The Moderating Role of Firm Size in Indonesia
abstract: This study investigates the empirical relationships among working capital management, corporate liquidity, and profitability while evaluating the moderating role of firm size within the Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) manufacturing sector in Indonesia. The investigation utilizes an exhaustive panel dataset of 23 consumer goods manufacturing firms listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange from 2016 to 2024, comprising 207 firm-year observations across four distinct industry subsectors. Working capital management is proxied by the Cash Conversion Cycle (CCC), liquidity by the Current Ratio (CR), corporate profitability by Return On Assets (ROA), and firm size by the natural logarithm of total assets. Moderated regression analysis demonstrates that the cash conversion cycle exerts a statistically significant negative effect on return on assets, confirming that accelerated operational velocity and reduced capital commitment enhance economic returns. Conversely, liquidity exhibits a significant negative relationship with profitability, demonstrating that excessive preservation of unproductive current assets imposes severe opportunity costs. Firm size directly bolsters profitability through economies of scale and institutional endowments, while acting as a significant quasi-moderator that intensifies the detrimental effects of both prolonged cash cycles and asset over-liquidity. title: Conservation concessions or green grabbing? A critical perspective on mega conservation investments
abstract: Market-based mechanisms have gained traction in environmental governance during the Anthropocene. One such mechanism is conservation concessions, which are promoted in the Global South as a neoliberal strategy that aligns ecological protection with economic rationality. Yet empirical evidence on their actual conservation outcomes and community benefits remains scanty. In this perspective, we argue that within prevailing capitalist frameworks, conservation concessions risk functioning as a form of green grabbing. Anchored in a political economy approach and critical agrarian studies, we synthesize evidence from multi-country case studies, with particular attention to Sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in Malawi, to examine the interplay between state power, transnational capital, and local agrarian structures. Our analysis reveals that despite being discursively framed as apolitical and win-win, conservation concessions can lead to: (i) restructuring of property and access rights, alienating customary users from their subsistence means; (ii) creation of precarious labor relations that often fail to offer viable alternatives for displaced smallholders; and (iii) reconfiguration of rural class dynamics, empowering conservation-oriented elites while marginalizing the agrarian poor. We conclude that conservation concessions represent a symptomatic response by capitalism to its own eco…

title: Development and Nationwide Multicentre Evaluation of Guideline-Grounded Large Language Model Chatbots to Support Patient Self-Management and Education in Rheumatology
abstract: Abstract Patients with rheumatic diseases have persistent information needs that are not fully addressed in routine care. We developed and evaluated guideline-grounded, large language model (LLM) chatbots to support patient self-management and education in rheumatology. Ten disease-specific chatbots based on German guidelines were co-developed and deployed through 13 rheumatology centres and six patient organisations. Chatbot users rated responses and completed a questionnaire. User questions, feedback, and response characteristics were analysed using category-based coding and a six-dimensional LLM-as-a-judge assessment, with LLM-based ratings compared with rheumatologist ratings in random subsets. Between September 2025 and January 2026, 6291 questions were recorded. Thirteen question categories were identified, most commonly disease-specific questions (50.2%), medication and monitoring (37.3%) and diagnostics (28.2%). The chatbots were unable to answer in 263 interactions (4.2%). Of 2671 responses rated by users, 2481 (92.9%) received a positive rating. Insufficient detail was the most common reason for negative ratings (125/190, 65.8%). Among 602 questionnaire respondents, 84.6% reported that the chatbot was easy to use, 84.1% that answers were easy to understand, and 80.2% that it was a useful addition to patient education. In the LLM-based evaluation, 95.3% of answers were…

title: Tilapia (Oreochromis spp.) as an Ecological Threat to Indigenous Fish Diversity in Indian Rivers and Reservoirs: Mechanisms, Evidence and Management Perspectives
abstract: The introduction and subsequent establishment of non-native tilapias in freshwater ecosystems have generated increasing ecological and fisheries-management concerns in India. Species belonging to the genus Oreochromis, particularly Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) and Mozambique tilapia (O. mossambicus), possess a combination of biological characteristics—including broad environmental tolerance, trophic plasticity, early sexual maturation, repeated reproduction, parental care and the capacity to exploit disturbed habitats—that can facilitate establishment outside their native ranges. Although tilapia are economically important aquaculture species and can contribute substantially to food production and rural livelihoods, their occurrence in open rivers and reservoirs presents a potential challenge for the conservation of indigenous fish assemblages when populations become established at high abundance. This review synthesizes available evidence on the ecological interactions between introduced tilapias and indigenous fishes in Indian rivers and reservoirs. Particular attention is given to competition for food and space, overlap in trophic niches, occupation of spawning and nursery habitats, potential effects on recruitment, modification of benthic and littoral habitats, and changes in fish-community structure. Evidence from Indian systems indicates that ecological responses …

title: Conditional vaccine performance benchmarks for reducing MRSA burden in an idealised national transmission model for Italy
Analisis Dampak Digital Financial Inclusion, Efisiensi Operasional, dan Struktur Dana Murah Terhadap Stabilitas Perbankan KBMI 4 di Indonesia (2020–2025)
abstract: This study analyses the impact of Digital Financial Inclusion (DFI), operational efficiency (BOPO), and the CASA ratio on banking stability (Z-Score) among KBMI 4 banks in Indonesia for the period Q1 2020–Q4 2025. The research method utilises a Fixed Effects Model (FEM) panel data regression on 96 quarterly observations of a saturated sample. The results indicate that, simultaneously, DFI, BOPO, and the CASA ratio have a significant impact on banking stability, with an Adjusted R-squared of 32.79%. Partially, Digital Financial Inclusion (DFI) has a significant negative impact on banking stability, confirming the ‘inclusion-risk hypothesis’ whereby digital expansion in the initial phase introduces investment burdens and new operational risks. Meanwhile, the BOPO and CASA ratios do not have a significant impact on banking stability, indicating that for systemic banks, fluctuations in operational costs and the volatility of digital low-cost funds do not immediately constitute primary shocks to bank solvency. The implication is that bank management must strengthen cyber risk mitigation and liquidity governance in navigating the dynamics of digital transformation.

title: Bridging The Gap In Food-Processing Msmes: Financial Behavior And Performance
abstract: Purpose - This study examines the effects of financial literacy and financial technology on the performance of micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), with financial behavior conceptualized as a mediating mechanism. Design/methodology/approach - The study used a quantitative design and survey data from 120 MSME owners in Malang City, Indonesia. The study used Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) to evaluate direct and indirect relationships among the constructs. Findings - Financial literacy and financial technology positively affect financial behavior. Financial behavior positively influences MSME performance and mediates the relationships between financial literacy and performance, as well as between financial technology and performance. Practical implications - Strengthening financial behavior through financial literacy initiatives and the effective use of financial technology may enhance MSME performance and long-term sustainability. Originality/value - Integration of the Resource-Based View and the Theory of Planned Behavior provides an explanatory framework for the mediating role of financial behavior in the MSME context. Paper type - Research Article

Audit Committee Size and Financial Reporting Quality of Listed Non-Financial Firms in Nigeria
abstract: Main purpose: This study examined the effect of audit committee size on the financial reporting quality of non-financial firms listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX). Methodology: Secondary data were obtained from the annual reports of 58 sampled non-financial firms, drawn from a population of 106 listed firms, covering the period from 2013 to 2024. The data were analysed using panel regression estimation techniques to determine the effect of audit committee size and relevant firm-specific variables on financial reporting quality. Findings: The results revealed that audit committee size had a positive and statistically significant effect on financial reporting quality (t = 2.2511, p < 0.05), indicating that larger audit committees may provide broader oversight of the financial reporting process. Leverage also had a positive and statistically significant effect on financial reporting quality (t = 2.0864, p < 0.05). In contrast, audit firm size had a negative and statistically significant association with financial reporting quality (t = −3.1325, p < 0.05), suggesting that the use of larger audit firms does not necessarily translate into higher financial reporting quality among the sampled firms. Practical implications: Boards of listed non-financial firms should maintain appropriately constituted audit committees with sufficient membership and members possessing relevant fi…

FinTechHub for digital financial inclusion in Saudi Arabia
abstract: Purpose This paper introduces FinTechHub as a knowledge-enabled fintech innovation platform designed to reduce fragmentation in Saudi Arabia's digital financial services. It explains how a governed access point can support discovery, comparison and guided journeys across multiple financial services while preserving delivery by licensed providers. Design/methodology/approach The paper develops a conceptual framework grounded in platform ecosystem theory. It specifies design principles for Arabic-first usability, accessibility, security-by-design, transparent consent, Sharia-compliant product governance and embedded digital financial literacy. It proposes a layered architecture that covers user experience, orchestration logic, data and analytics, standardized application programming interface (API) integration and governance controls. Findings The framework shows that integration breadth, interoperability quality, personalization and user control can strengthen perceived usefulness, trust and sustained use. It also positions embedded digital financial literacy support as a knowledge mechanism that helps users interpret fees, risks and product alternatives at the moment of choice, thereby supporting adoption and inclusion outcomes. Research limitations/implications As a conceptual paper, the framework requires future validation through prototypes, experiments and longitudinal stud…

title: Can Artificial Intelligence Applications Reduce Bank Non-Performing Loan Ratios? Evidence from the Text of Listed Banks' Annual Reports
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies are being rapidly deployed throughout the banking industry, yet their effect on credit risk still lacks systematic micro-level empirical evidence. Using a panel of 35 Chinese listed commercial banks over the period 2012-2025, this paper measures banks' AI adoption intensity by the frequency of AI-related keywords in the full text of their annual reports, and examines the effect of AI adoption on the non-performing loan (NPL) ratio together with its transmission mechanisms. The results are as follows. First, AI adoption significantly reduces the NPL ratio: a one-unit increase in the logarithm of AI keyword frequency lowers the NPL ratio by approximately 0.105 percentage points, and this conclusion remains robust after a battery of endogeneity treatments, including system GMM, a peer-mean instrumental variable approach (IV-2SLS), and the Oster coefficient stability test. Second, the effect is concentrated among city and rural commercial banks and weakens significantly as bank size increases. Third, AI improves asset quality mainly by lowering the cost-to-income ratio, with the mediating effect accounting for 22.2% of the total effect. Fourth, the effect strengthens over time, which is consistent with the accelerating iteration of AI technologies.

title: An assessment of the impact of lean framework design and lean enablers on business operational performance
abstract: Purpose The research explores the relationships between the effectiveness of lean framework design, lean implementation enablement and business operational success, thereby establishing a broader ground for successful lean implementation. Design/methodology/approach A questionnaire was used to collect data across various industries in South Africa. A total of 198 valid responses were obtained and analyzed using SMART-PLS 4. Findings A strong relationship was found between effective lean framework design, lean implementation enablement and business operational success. Also, lean implementation enablement mediates the relationship between lean framework design effectiveness and business operational success. This result indicates that paying proper attention to a lean enabling environment increases the likelihood of improving operational performance through the adoption of lean frameworks. Originality/value Researchers have attempted to understand how the presence of enablers affects the success of lean, and the role of lean frameworks in the success of lean implementation. No study has considered contextualized framework design and the mediatory influence of lean enablers on the effectiveness of lean frameworks, and their interactive influence on the success of lean implementation. By grounding this investigation in contingency theory and socio-technical systems theory, this stu…

title: Metacognitive Therapy for Comorbid Anxiety and Depression in Adults with Autism: A Replicated A–B Design
Mixture design optimization of Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) pâté formulated with mechanically separated meat: integration of sensory acceptance and formulation cost
abstract: Abstract A significant portion of aquatic food industry by-products is still directed to low-value applications, even though they have technological potential for food products, such as mechanically separated meat (MSM) in emulsified products. This study optimised theformulation of a pasteurised Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ) fish pâté using mixture design with component constraints, evaluating the combined effects of MSM, fat, and water on sensory performance and formulation cost. Eleven formulations were produced and assessed by 87 untrained panellists using a 9-point hedonic scale. The use of MSM met microbiological safety requirements. Significant differences were observed among formulations for sensory attributes, including odour, texture, flavour, overall acceptance, and purchase intention ( p < 0.05). Quadratic models demonstrated high predictive capacity, with adjusted coefficients of determination exceeding 0.99 for most responses. The optimal formulation based on desirability contained 0.53 MSM, 0.23 fat and 0.25 water, reaching an overall acceptance score of 7.71. An Economic-Sensory Efficiency Index (EI = overall acceptance/formulation cost, USD kg⁻¹) was proposed as a complementary decision criterion. Formulations with lower MSM content showed the highest EI values, maintaining acceptance above 7.1 while reducing formulation cost by up to USD 0.19 per kilog…

title: Design, modeling, and nonlinear model predictive control of a novel fully actuated uav for safe transport of hazardous liquids
abstract: Abstract Transporting hazardous liquids with unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) demands exceptionally high precision and stability in flight control to prevent catastrophic accidents caused by the destructive fluid sloshing phenomenon. This paper presents the design, mathematical modeling, and a hybrid control architecture (Clustered PID-NMPC) for a novel fully actuated UAV dedicated to the safe transportation of hazardous liquids. Featuring an innovative mechanical structure, the proposed UAV overcomes the inherent limitations of conventional underactuated drones by providing active dynamic decoupling between translational and rotational dynamics”. The dynamic model of the system is derived utilizing Newton–Euler and Euler–Lagrange formulations, and its validity is verified through comprehensive simulations. The designed controller significantly enhances system performance across three distinct scenarios (ideal conditions, step disturbance, and continuous sinusoidal wind) in comparison to a classical quadcopter. Simulation results demonstrate that, alongside superior trajectory tracking accuracy, faster transient response, and enhanced disturbance rejection capabilities compared to traditional UAVs, the proposed system achieves near-zero attitude deviation (near-horizontal cabin stabilization). By significantly minimizing translational-rotational coupling and dynamic angular pann…

title: Measuring AI literacy in design education: development and validation of the artificial intelligence literacy scale for design students
abstract: Abstract Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in design practice, challenging how design education fosters students’ AI literacy and thus prepares students to engage efficiently with AI. However, there is currently no domain-specific theoretical framework and reliable instrument in the literature to conceptualize and assess design students’ AI literacy, hindering its systematic cultivation. This study fills in this gap by developing and validating the Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale for Design Students (AILS-DS), in accordance with established standards for scale development. The opinions of a wide range of experts were gathered through a qualitative method in order to define the AI literacy for design students, and served as a theoretical framework for the scale’s item pool. Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA, N = 294) and Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA, N = 325) were then applied to explore the underlying factor structure of the scale and validate its psychometric properties. The final 23-item, five-factor scale demonstrated good reliability and construct validity. Five factors (AI Concepts and Technical Skills, AI Tool Proficiency, AI Ethics and Originality Awareness, Recognition of AI Value in Design, and Independent Evaluation of AI Outputs) in the AILS-DS capture both widely acknowledged AI literacy components and design-specific struct…
venue: International Journal of Technology and Design Education

title: Design thinking as a practice system for knowledge-enabled digital transformation: microfoundations of dynamic capabilities
abstract: Purpose Digital transformation (DT) demands more than technology adoption; it reshapes organisational routines, knowledge and decision structures, and the capabilities firms rely on to compete. Yet many firms fail to move DT beyond pilots, revealing a deeper problem: organisations lack the knowledge mechanisms needed to sustain transformation at scale. Design/methodology/approach This paper positions design thinking (DTk) as a knowledge practice system: an interrelated set of methods, mindsets and artefacts that shapes the microfoundations of dynamic capabilities (DCs) during DT. Drawing on semi-structured interviews with 14 practitioners in the Dutch financial services sector, the authors inductively identify and elaborate three DTk-shaped microfoundations: Adapting (sensing through problem framing bounded by strategic intent and short, iterative experiments), Governing (seizing through user evidence, structured decision checkpoints, role clarity and contracting mechanisms) and Conveying (reconfiguring through storytelling, boundary artefacts and shared vocabulary that transfer and translate knowledge across organisational boundaries). Findings The authors demonstrate how these mechanisms address key DT challenges – strategic misalignment, decision risks, legacy-system constraints and cross-functional coordination failures – that are, at their core, knowledge management (KM) c…

title: THE INSTITUTIONAL ROLE OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT IN SHAPING THE URBAN SPACE OF POST-REFORM KHERSON (SECOND HALF OF THE 19TH CENTURY)
abstract: The purpose of this article is to define the institutional role of the Kherson City Duma and the city administration in shaping the urban space of post-reform Kherson based on an analysis of municipal records, as well as to analyze the mechanisms through which local self-government influenced the modernization of the city’s infrastructure, socio-functional organization, and management practices, which shaped the nature of the city’s urban transformations during the post-reform era. The methodological foundation of the study is modernization theory, which allows for the interpretation of urban self-government as the driving force behind the transition from traditional to rationalized forms of urban space management. Additionally, elements of historical-genetic and structural-functional analysis are applied, enabling the identification of interrelationships between administrative decisions, economic resources, and spatial practices of urban development. The main focus of the article is on the analysis of the minutes of the Kherson City Duma meetings, which reflect key areas of urban policy: the development of transportation and logistics infrastructure (cleaning the Dnipro estuaries, regulating navigation, and establishing commercial infrastructure), the modernization of public utilities (water supply, sanitation, and urban improvement), as well as the institutionalization of edu…

title: Research on intra-day scheduling model of power system with shared energy storage in the provincial electricity spot market based on renewable energy groups combination forecasting
abstract: This study proposes an intra-day scheduling model for power systems with shared energy storage in provincial electricity spot markets based on renewable energy combination forecasting to mitigate the uncertainty of wind and photovoltaic output. Firstly, an EWM-LSTM-SVM model optimized by EO is proposed to improve prediction accuracy. Then, an intra-day optimal scheduling model with SES is established to minimize system operation cost. The proposed combined model achieves an R 2 of 0.96, MAE of 14.45, and RMSE of 21.60, significantly outperforming single forecasting models. Case results verify that the method optimizes SES strategies, reduces renewable curtailment and system cost, with total system cost reaching 7,634,351.42 RMB. Finally, policy recommendations are provided for stable market operation and renewable accommodation.

title: Integrated Valorization of Plastic Waste into Synthetic Fuels and Electricity via Multi-Stage Upgrading: Process Modeling and Techno-Economic Analysis
abstract: Abstract An integrated process for the valorization of 1000 kg/h of heterogeneous plastic waste (Plasmix) into hydrogen, purified CO2, light and heavy liquid fuels, and electricity was developed and simulated using Aspen Plus. The process combines non-catalytic pyrolysis with sequential syngas upgrading, tar catalytic conversion, and extensive heat integration to maximize product recovery and economic performance. In the pyrolysis stage (600 °C, 12 bar), Plasmix is efficiently converted into gas, tar, char, and wastewater, with the gaseous fraction representing the largest product share (42.1%), followed by tar (23.0%), char (20.6%), and water (14.3%). The syngas stream is upgraded via reforming, water–gas shift, CO2 separation, and pressure swing adsorption to produce hydrogen (59 kg/h) and purified CO2 (533 kg/h), while the tar fraction is converted into liquid fuels, yielding 228 kg/h of light fuel and 23 kg/h of heavy fuel. Process integration enables substantial energy recovery, resulting in a net electricity export of approximately 18.2 MW. Economic evaluation shows a fixed capital investment of 12.21 M$, with annual revenues of 15.50 M$/year and operating expenditures of 5.33 M$/year, confirming strong baseline profitability. Sensitivity analysis identifies hydrogen and electricity selling prices as the dominant economic drivers, whereas the plastic waste fee provides a …

title: Deep Learning-Based Gold Price Prediction and Cross-Market Arbitrage Strategy with Currency Hedging
abstract: This paper develops a reproducible framework for predicting gold-price direction and converting the forecasts into a currency-hedged SHFE-COMEX spread-trading strategy. Daily market data from January 2018 to December 2024 are divided chronologically into training, validation, out-of-sample testing, and frozen-model forward paper-trading periods to limit data leakage. A hybrid LSTM-Transformer-Attention model achieves 63.7% directional accuracy in 2023, although paired tests do not establish statistical superiority over the Transformer benchmark at the 5% level. The trading evaluation incorporates next-session execution, commissions, slippage, holiday mismatches, contract rolls, integer position constraints, and an SGX USD/CNH futures hedge. Under the stated assumptions, hedging reduces volatility and maximum drawdown and improves risk-adjusted performance. The findings provide preliminary, reproducible evidence of economic usefulness, but not proof of durable arbitrage profitability without intraday executable quotes and complete trade-level records.
venue: WSEAS Transactions on Business and Economics

title: An In-Depth Analysis on the Use of AI in Market Dynamics to Reduce Asymmetric Information
abstract: Information asymmetry within consumer markets relies on the mechanism of knowledge being manifest in only one party, with a cost to the other to attain that same information. The economic theories and observations apparent in markets have been modelled to a great extent by different economists to not only cover the causation but also the predicted outcome if such imbalance exists, to varying degrees. When adding the capabilities of AI to the use for consumers, we see a dramatic increase in the information a day-to-day person can attain, seeing as traditional factors that once barrier information no longer hold, such as complexity, variety, time etc. Through active exploration of two different platforms, ecommerce Amazon and Indian food delivery platform Swiggy, different AI features and their uses are examined to determine whether they are beneficial in reducing information asymmetry. The capability of AI, as seen on these platforms, actively combats information asymmetry for both consumers and sellers, but at a much faster rate for consumers than sellers. This is because consumer-facing AI features substantially reduce the barriers that traditionally prevented buyers from acquiring and processing information, allowing them to access, compare and interpret information that they previously could not realistically obtain. In contrast, seller-facing AI primarily increases efficien…

title: Labour market segmentation and the experiences of web-based platform workers in Nigeria
abstract: Abstract This study examines how labour market segmentation shapes the rise and lived experiences of web-based platform workers in a developing country, focusing on how digital platforms both reproduce peripheral employment and create new forms of economic opportunity and meaningful work amid local constraints. Adopting a qualitative research design, we conducted semi-structured interviews with 23 Nigerian web-based platform workers and utilised thematic analysis to capture their subjective experiences. We found that web-based platforms have significant implications for work and employment in Nigeria. This is discussed within the study’s three overarching themes, including ‘precarity and economic security’, ‘perception of work meaningfulness’, and ‘country-specific issues’, which point to an upward trajectory in the number of web-based platform workers in the near future. By developing the notion of algorithmic segmentation as a context-sensitive extension of labour market segmentation theory, we show how platform-mediated mechanisms, worker dependence, infrastructure, and reputational conditions shape unequal access to work, income stability, and bargaining power. Our findings highlight the socio-cultural dimensions of meaningful digital labour and inform policy aligned with SDG 8 (decent work), calling for formal legal recognition of platform workers, minimum income guarantee…

title: Future Exchange Pressure Risk Score (FEPR): Predicting Exchange Market Pressure in Emerging Economies
abstract: Emerging economies remain vulnerable to abrupt exchange rate depreciation and reserve losses, creating a need for early warning tools that distinguish current pressure from vulnerabilities that may precede future stress. This study developed the Future Exchange Pressure Risk Score (FEPR), using annual data for 19 emerging economies over the time frame 2000–2024. Three components make up the foundation of the FEPR: External Vulnerability Fundamentals (EVF), External Flow Fragility (EFF), and contemporaneous Exchange Market Pressure (EMP). In order to evaluate how well their model worked, they created a new way of testing it by using training periods 2000–2013, purging data in 2014 and 2015, training-only pre-processing and estimating EMP thresholds. Then they used the remainder of the sample for evaluating performance from 2016 to 2022. They found that the standard three-component model had a test ROC-AUC of 0.763 and test PR-AUC of 0.602. However, more importantly, they were able to demonstrate that EVF and EFF jointly provided additional predictive value beyond contemporaneous EMP. Specifically, the full model improved upon the models that relied solely on contemporaneous EMP with respect to both discrimination and loss functions, while the joint training sample country-clustered Wald test produced a [Formula: see text]-value of 0.0014. With respect to which pillar was providi…

title: THE DEVELOPMENT OF SPECIAL RISKS AND CONTINGENCY INSURANCE IN THE NIGERIAN INSURANCE MARKET
abstract: The Nigerian business and operating environment is increasingly exposed to complex, low-frequency, high-severity events that fall outside the scope of traditional insurance products. These include political violence, terrorism, cyber-attacks, supply chain disruption, event cancellation, and non-damage business interruption – collectively referred to as special risks and contingent insurance. The main objective of this study is to examine the challenges of special risks in the Nigerian insurance market. This study adopted a qualitative research method grounded in literature-based review to examine the concept, scope, and practice of special risks and contingent insurance in Nigeria. The findings from the study revealed three major insights. First, awareness and understanding of contingent covers among Nigerian businesses and even insurance practitioners remain limited, leading to significant protection gaps. Second, technical challenges including inadequate local data, limited reinsurance capacity, and shortage of specialised underwriting expertise constrain product development and pricing. Third, regulatory and market opportunities exist through risk based supervision, public-private partnerships, and the growing demand from infrastructure, energy, and event sectors. The study concluded that special risks and contingent insurance are no longer niche but essential components of …

title: Introduce 4π dynamic spot-scanning proton arc therapy (SPArc-4π) for pancreatic cancer: a comparative planning study with IMPT
abstract: Abstract Objective. Stereotactic body radiotherapy with a simultaneous integrated boost (SBRT-SIB) for locally advanced pancreatic cancer (LAPC) is constrained by the proximity of serial gastrointestinal organs at risk (OARs). Conventional intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) relies on a limited number of fixed beam angles, which may restrict dose shaping around these critical structures. This study evaluated whether non-coplanar spot-scanning proton arc therapy (SPArc-4π) could improve OAR sparing while preserving robust target coverage. Approach. 10 patients with LAPC were retrospectively selected in this study. For each patient, SBRT-SIB plans were generated using conventional IMPT and SPArc-4π. Plan robustness was assessed across 21 uncertainty scenarios. Target coverage, conformity, OAR doses, estimated delivery time, and Lyman-Kutcher-Burman normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) for four gastrointestinal endpoints were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Main results. SPArc-4π maintained target coverage comparable to IMPT, with similar clinical target volume (CTV) and boost-volume coverage, while CTV conformity improved with SPArc-4π (conformity index: 0.50 vs. 0.56; p = 0.02). SPArc-4π significantly reduced maximum dose (Gy(RBE)) to the stomach (30.01 to 24.53), duodenum (35.14 to 33.14), bowel (32.60 to 28.91), and spinal cord (15.38 to 5.58; all …

title: Chernovite-(Y) and a uranium hot spot in the City of Aberdeen: oxidative mineralization of an orogenic unconformity
abstract: The manganite (manganese ore) deposit at Grandhome, City of Aberdeen, has an anomalously high uranium content and negligible thorium content. The very low Th/U ratio is characteristic of a supergene environment, in this case during Devonian exposure of basement rocks at the Caledonian unconformity. The uranium exceeds 100 ppm in mineralized whole rock, and up to 360 ppm in manganite ore. In manganite uranium resides in the yttrium arsenate mineral chernovite-(Y) as a substituent along with rare earth elements. Arsenic levels are an order of magnitude above background. The occurrence exemplifies low-temperature mineralization on orogenic exposure surfaces.

title: Cross-numeraire relative pricing of ethereum: data authority, market frictions, and static arbitrage bounds
abstract: Abstract Using Gate.io hourly spot-order-book archives from January 2022 through June 2023, this paper reconstructs a long-horizon five-second panel for comparing the direct Ether/Tether (ETH/USDT) quote with the synthetic Ether/Bitcoin (ETH/BTC) $$\times $$ Bitcoin/Tether (BTC/USDT) representation. The reconstruction preserves ordered replay, source time, valid best-bid-and-offer states, and explicit missingness. Of 39,312 expected market-hour files, 39,147 are available, but only 4,391,146 of 9,434,880 grid timestamps (46.54%) support all three legs. All pricing distributions are conditional on joint archive readiness. On those timestamps, the median signed direct–synthetic wedge is 0.164 basis points and the median absolute wedge is 1.416 basis points; the ETH/BTC leg contributes approximately 91% of aggregate quoted friction. Gross directed inequalities occur in 20.25% of forward and 18.61% of reverse observations. Under a hypothetical five-basis-point fee per leg, only 64 forward and 56 reverse observations remain positive. Common-support diagnostics show that zero-ready hours have larger observed ETH/USDT absolute returns, realized volatility, quoted spreads, and archived message counts, but price-state coverage is only 56 of 160 such hours and no missing-at-random claim is made. title: Price volatility, market integration, and farmer income risk in the cayenne pepper agribusiness of Gorontalo
abstract: Purpose: to analyze cayenne pepper price volatility, market integration and price transmission, and marketing efficiency, and to examine their implications for farmer income risk in Gorontalo Province's cayenne pepper agribusiness. Method: this study used a narrative literature review of scientific publications and analyzed them thematically around price volatility, market integration, marketing efficiency, farmer income risk, and agribusiness development. Findings: cayenne pepper prices in Gorontalo are highly volatile, while marketing efficiency varies across supply-chain actors. Although markets are relatively integrated, price transmission is not always complete or symmetrical. These conditions increase farmers' exposure to price, production, and marketing risks, potentially resulting in unstable farm income. Implications: Gorontalo's cayenne pepper agribusiness requires integrated policies focusing on price stabilization, transparent market information, stronger farmer institutions, efficient marketing channels, and improved post-harvest management to reduce farmer income risk and strengthen agribusiness resilience. Originality: lies in integrating price volatility, market integration, marketing efficiency, and farmer income risk into a single analytical framework for the cayenne pepper agribusiness in Gorontalo Province.

title: Occupational task content and marital intentions in Czechia in the context of structural labour market change
abstract: Objective: This study examines how occupational task content, particularly routine task intensity, is associated with short-term marital intentions among partnered individuals in Czechia. Background: Technological advances like automation have contributed to structural shifts in labour demand, with routine-intensive occupations often identified as especially vulnerable to wage stagnation, job displacement, and weaker long-term career prospects. Because economic prospects shape family formation and perceived marriageability, occupational task content may be relevant for understanding marital intentions. However, little is known about whether routine-intensive employment is associated with marital plans, or whether this association differs by gender Method: We analyse data from 1,288 respondents in non-marital partnerships from the Czech Household Panel Survey (2015–2019), linked to occupational task measures from the European Skills, Competences, Qualifications and Occupations Database (ESCO). Using multinomial logistic regression, we estimate the association between occupational task content and marital intentions. Results: Men in highly routine-intense occupations are more likely to report no plans to marry. Women’s marital plans do not show a clear association with the content of their occupations. title: Scaling up the global Green Bond market: Integrating global policy frameworks with stakeholder perceptions from Australia and the United Kingdom
abstract: The Green Bond (GB) market has not been as effective as anticipated in tackling the global climate change crisis. There is a substantive investment gap worldwide in meeting the financing needs of green projects. Thus, this study reviewed key publications of international market players from 2007 to 2021 to identify how key stakeholders perceive the GB market. We employed a qualitative research approach using document analysis. In addition to this, a number of interviews were conducted to validate the findings by providing suggestive and supportive evidence. The findings indicate structural constraints affecting both supply and demand dynamics in the GB market. This study contributes to the literature by integrating documentary evidence and stakeholder perspectives into a unified conceptual framework that explains the institutional and market barriers affecting the global scaling of Green Bond markets and identifies implications for future policy development.

title: High-Resolution Spatiotemporal Distribution Characteristics and Environmental Conditions of Severe Convective Wind Events in China from 2016 to 2022
abstract: Abstract The high-resolution spatiotemporal distributions and environmental conditions of severe convective wind (SCW) events in China from 2016 to 2022 are examined. SCW events predominantly occur from April to September, with a June peak over North China–Northeast China (NC–NEC) and a relatively uniform distribution from May to August over South of the Yangtze River (SYR). SCW frequency increases markedly by 1200 BJT, with the majority occurring during the afternoon to early evening. A comprehensive analysis of key thermodynamic and kinematic parameters reveals pronounced seasonal and regional contrasts in SCW environments. In spring, SCW activity concentrates over SYR, where favorable synoptic forcing coincides with abundant low-level moisture, large surface-based convective available potential energy (SBCAPE), and pronounced vertical wind shear. By contrast, springtime events over NC–NEC occur in a deep, dry mixed boundary layer environment characterized by lower SBCAPE but steeper 0–3 km and 850–500 hPa lapse rates (LR03, LR85). In summer, synoptic forcing weakens, yet SCW activity peaks over NC–NEC, where sufficient buoyancy, relatively strong shear, and moderate LR85 support organized convection. Conversely, summer events over SYR develop beneath or along the periphery of the western Pacific subtropical high in a high-SBCAPE, weak-shear environment, indicating that buoya…

title: Enhancing Power Distribution System Performance through Machine Learning-Based Forecasting of Solar Power Generation
abstract: Abstract The expansion of Photovoltaic (PV) Energy has accelerated in the recent years, and many large-scale solar power plants are being installed. Due to the intermittent and uncertain nature of PV power plants and all other renewable energy sources, it is essential to find methods that can accurately predict their output power. Machine learning (ML) has become a valuable tool for predictive maintenance, system optimization, power forecasting and fault detection in renewable energy power plants. More specifically, parametric models for PV power forecasting depend on mathematical relationships that need extensive input data and parameters determination. In contrast, nonparametric models can capture complex nonlinear relationships directly from historic data without the need to parameters not a fixed functional form. Nonparametric ML models have been used in literature for power forecasting but never for large-scale PV farms. This work compares the implementation of ML and Deep Learning (DL) nonparametric ML models on the power forecasting of large-scale PV farm in Egypt taking the Kom Ombo 26 MW power plant as a case study. The Linear Regression model resulted in the lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) value and was further improved after removing the night hours from the dataset. However, the LSTM model proved to be the best model when dealing with historical records of the …

title: Digital Trend Analysis and Forecasting of Sustainable Hydroponic and Aquaponic Systems: Global and Türkiye-Based Perspectives on Aquaculture Integration (2015–2028)
abstract: Climate change and the depletion of freshwater resources are increasing the global importance of sustainable food production systems, particularly soilless agriculture (hydroponics) and integrated aquaculture-based plant production (aquaponics). This study aims to provide a comparative analysis of public awareness and digital interest trends related to these “green” and “blue” agricultural technologies at both global and national (Türkiye) scales. Relative Search Volume (RSV) data obtained from Google Trends (GT) for the 2015–2026 period were used. Without applying additional transformation, and in order to preserve periodic shocks in information-seeking behavior and natural variance, future projections up to 2028 were generated using the Exponential Smoothing (ETS) algorithm. The findings indicate that digital interest in hydroponic systems has reached a higher and more continuous level both globally and in Türkiye, suggesting greater public visibility and sustained online attention, with peak RSV values reaching 100. Conversely, while interest in aquaponic systems is concentrated in water-stressed regions and island nations globally, it follows a markedly low and flat trajectory (0–5 index) in Türkiye, indicating a prominent digital awareness gap. These findings should be interpreted as indicators of public attention and digital visibility rather than direct evidence of physi…

title: Customer Citizenship Behavior in Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises: The Role of Justifiable Price and Product Quality
abstract: This study examines the impact of justifiable price (JP) and product quality (PQ) on customer citizenship behavior (CCB) in small and medium enterprises (SMEs) operating at rest areas along the Batticaloa District. A quantitative research design was used, creating a structured questionnaire consisting of 21items on a five-point Likert scale. Data were collected from 132 customers of Small and medium food establishments through convenience sampling. Reliability analysis, correlation analysis and regression analysis were conducting using SPSS to measure the strength and direction of relationships between variables. The findings shows that customers exhibit moderate to high levels of price justice mean value is 3.94, product quality mean value is 3.94 and customer citizenship behavior mean value is 3.96. Reliability shows the Cronbach alpha for all variables were high, confirming measurement consistency. Correlation analysis showed strong positive relationship between product quality and customer citizenship behavior (r = 0.818), justifiable price and customer citizenship behavior (r=0.680) and price justice and product quality significantly predicts CCB (β = 0.665, p < 0.001), explaining a substantial portion of its variance. Justifiable price , however, did not; customers who perceive higher product quality are more likely to engage in discretionary behaviors such as recommendin…

title: Forecasting the volatility of energy transition metals
abstract: Abstract The energy and digital transitions are increasing demand for metals used in renewable energy, electrification, storage, and digital infrastructure. Many of these metals are traded in thin and concentrated markets with limited substitutability, making volatility a key constraint on investment, hedging, and policy design. This paper analyzes the return and volatility dynamics of 16 Energy Transition Metals. We combine exploratory and dimension-reduction methods with in-sample estimation and out-of-sample point and density forecasts, comparing a baseline GARCH(1,1) model with several stochastic-volatility specifications. The results reveal substantial heterogeneity across metals. Commodities commonly grouped by data providers or linked through geological co-occurrence often exhibit markedly different return and volatility characteristics. Forecasting performance is similarly heterogeneous: neither GARCH nor any single stochastic-volatility specification consistently dominates across commodities. Although some associations emerge between empirical features and model performance, they are not robust across metals or evaluation criteria. Overall, the findings support a metal-specific approach to volatility modelling and risk management and suggest that market maturity, liquidity, price discovery, and hedging opportunities may help explain these differences.

title: Predictive Modeling Techniques for Forecasting Emergency Department Overcrowding and Resource Needs in United States Public Hospitals
abstract: In the United States, emergency department congestion stealthily undermines the safety net of public hospitals for uninsured, underinsured, and medically complex populations, and the use of forecasting tools is limited where it is desired most. This research article proposes and tests a set of predictive modeling techniques for predicting the volume of patients in the emergency department (ED) and downstream hospital resource use for the next day or multiple days within public hospitals in the United States, based on 4 years of anonymized encounter data and calendar, weather, epidemiology, and hospital operational data. Different models, including naive, seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average with exogenous regressors (SARIMAX), Prophet, random forest, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), long short-term memory (LSTM), and attention-based transformer architectures were trained and evaluated using 1-day, 7-day, and 14-day forecasting horizons, and the results were converted to a discrete-event simulation of staffing and bed management.

abstract: Objective: to improve the grounding system for AC contact network supports by developing a device for remote monitoring of the state of spark gaps and gas-discharge protection devices, as well as substantiating the use of intelligent AI agents to process diagnostic data and transition from reactive to predictive maintenance. Methods: comparative analysis of existing control methods. A constructive solution based on a short- circuit indicator is proposed, in combination with unmanned aerial vehicles and intelligent video analytics tools. Results: the proposed solution provides contactless remote diagnostics without decommissioning the equipment and does not require significant design changes. Practical significance: continuous monitoring, early detection of hidden defects and degradation processes, increased electrical safety, optimization of operating costs and reduction of the burden on the personnel of the power supply service.

title: Bioactivity-driven prediction of antibacterial synergy using machine learning models
abstract: Motivation Combination therapies have demonstrated improved efficacy across diverse clinical settings. Predicting antibacterial drug synergy remains difficult due to strain variability and the limited scale of experimentally tested combinations. Existing machine-learning approaches for synergy prediction often rely on permissive cross-validation schemes that allow drug pairs to re-appear across folds, leading to inflated performance metrics. A rigorous evaluation framework and scalable feature representation are needed for robust generalization. Results We assembled a curated dataset of 3,160 drug–pair–strain interactions covering 97 antibacterial compounds and 10 bacterial strains. We then developed HALO ( Held-out Antibacterial interaction Learning from latent bioactivity Observations ), a synergy-prediction framework in which each drug pair is encoded using multi-level Chemical Checker (CC) similarity features spanning chemical, targets, networks, cellular, and clinical bioactivity domains. Using strictly nested, drug-pair heldout cross validation with fold-internal feature selection, HALO achieved consistent generalization to unseen combinations (ROC–AUC = 0.78). Performance dropped notably under increasingly stringent heldout schemes and inflated under random data splits, underscoring the importance of rigorous evaluation for this task. title: Model-Based Prediction of Surface Roughness and Thickness Reduction During Electropolishing of Additively Manufactured Metal Parts
abstract: Abstract Additive manufacturing (AM) enables the fabrication of complex geometries with high design flexibility. However, the resulting as-built surface quality often requires post-processing to meet functional requirements, particularly for inclined and overhanging features. Achieving defined surface roughness while maintaining near-net-shape geometry is essential.In this study, 316L austenitic stainless-steel samples produced by laser powder bed fusion were electropolished in the transpassive regime at varying passed charges. Surface roughness and thickness reduction were analyzed, and both a predictive model for roughness evolution and a finite element model (FEM) using COMSOL® Multiphysics for thickness reduction were developed.Validation of the roughness model shows good overall agreement. While the maximum height parameter (Sz) exhibits moderate deviations, the arithmetic mean roughness (Sa) is reproduced with high accuracy. Validation of the FEM for thickness reduction shows good overall agreement, with more than 92% of the experimental data for build angles of 75° and 90° being captured by the simulation.Overall, the results demonstrate that surface roughness evolution and the predictive agreement of the thickness-reduction model are influenced by the initial surface morphology and build angle. Dependent variable involved sales performance indicators such as market share, sales and profits, mediating variables were measured by restaurant ambience this included décor, interior design and spatial layout, moderating variables included organisational competence measured by management, transactional and operational competence. title: Determinants of the continuum of maternal healthcare service utilization in Nigeria: Evidence from the 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey
abstract: Background Maternal mortality remains a major public health challenge, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, with Sub-Saharan Africa bearing a disproportionate burden. Nigeria accounts for over one-quarter of all maternal deaths worldwide. This reflects gaps in access to and continuity of maternal healthcare. The continuum of maternal healthcare, which includes antenatal care (ANC), skilled delivery, and postnatal care (PNC) is critical for improving maternal and neonatal outcomes. This study examines the determinants of continuum of maternal healthcare service utilization in Nigeria. Methods This study utilized data from 13,596 women (weighted n = 14,183) from the 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey. Maternal Health Services Utilization (MHSU) was operationalized as a composite outcome (none, partial, adequate) based on ANC attendance, place of delivery, maternal and child PNC. Multilevel multinomial logistic regression models were fitted to assess individual, household, and contextual predictors. Variables significant at p < 0.20 in bivariate analysis were included in multivariable models. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results Overall, 44.0% of women did not utilize any services, 44.4% partially utilized services, and only 11.6% achieved adequate utilization. Women with secondary or higher education were significantly more likely to achieve …

EphA4 Mediates Protumoral and Antitumoral Effects through Upstream Negative Regulation of AKT in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
abstract: Abstract Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is driven by an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). We examined the immunomodulatory role of EphA4 in HNSCC using spatial analysis, multicompartment RNA sequencing from oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma, and three genetically engineered mouse models. Within the HNSCC TME, EphA4 is primarily expressed in regulatory T cells (Treg), macrophages, CD8+ T cells, and HNSCC cancer cells. EphA4 in Tregs promotes tumor growth, whereas EphA4 in myeloid cells, CD8+ T cells, and cancer cells limits it. EphA4 mediates these differential effects through shared negative regulation of AKT signaling where its knockout increases AKT activation, leading to reduced Treg immunosuppression, increased M2 macrophage polarization, impaired CD8+ T-cell memory differentiation, and enhanced cancer cell proliferation. APY-d3-PEG4, an EphA4 inhibitor, reduced tumor growth primarily by targeting Tregs. EphA4 expression on CD8+ T cells correlates with treatment response, representing a potential biomarker, and cell type–specific targeting via cis-bispecific antibodies offers a promising therapeutic strategy. Interrogating human data show that EphA4 expression on CD8 correlates to response to treatment, posing it as a potential biomarker for future studies. Mechanistically, our data show EphA4 inhibits AKT signaling, and its inhibition enhance…

abstract: Abstract: Heart disease is one of the leading causes of death and represents a growing public health concern. In Guntarano Village, Tanantovea District, Donggala Regency, hypertension is the most prevalent health problem, accounting for 32.05% of cases, and is a major risk factor for heart disease. This community service program aimed to improve the knowledge and practical skills of health cadres in identifying and screening cardiovascular risk factors and to strengthen family participation in adopting heart-healthy behaviors through Integrated Posyandu services. The program was conducted from June to July 2026 and involved 30 participants, consisting of 20 health cadres and 10 local community members. The main activities were conducted on June 8–9, 2026, and included health education, cadre training, cardiovascular risk screening through blood pressure, body weight, height, waist circumference, and body mass index measurements, as well as heart-healthy exercise. Program evaluation used pre-test and post-test assessments, practical skill assessment, and direct observation during follow-up Integrated Posyandu activities on July 14–15, 2026. The proportion of participants in the good knowledge and skill category increased from 30% before the intervention to 80% after the intervention, while the moderate category decreased from 30% to 10% and the poor category from 40% to 10%. abstract: The concept of the capacity to inherit seemed to be clearly defined in Hungarian jurisprudence, but it has been undermined by the rules on the transfer of agricultural land in the last decade. The inheritance rules of the Land Transfer Act have already been proven unconstitutional twice. Subsequent amendments to the law have had an impact on the definition of the capacity to inherit. The private law concept of the beginning of the capacity to inherit has been changed by human reproductive procedures. The new Civil Code and judicial practice have also brought new developments in relation to the capacity to inherit of legal entities that are not natural persons.

title: Characterization of lentil ( Lens culinaris Medik.) core collection for prebiotic carbohydrates, protein content, and antioxidant capacity
abstract: Abstract Lentil ( Lens culinaris Medik.) is an important pulse crop with notable functional food properties, characterized by high protein content, low levels of digestible carbohydrates, and a diverse array of bioactive compounds that contribute to human health. In the present study, a recently developed lentil core set of 143 accessions – 118 Indian (111 indigenous and seven released varieties) and 25 exotic lines – was evaluated across two locations. Carbohydrate fractions, protein content, and antioxidant activity were assessed in each genotype. ANOVA (analysis of variance) revealed significant genotypic effects for all traits across environments. Enzymatic analyses revealed mean concentrations of 0.11 g/100 g for D-glucose, 1.17 g/100 g for sucrose, and 1.91 g/100 g for raffinose among the studied genotypes. Protein content ranged from 19.66 to 24.05% (mean 21.74%), while antioxidant activity varied from 0.45 to 1.95% (mean 1.10%). Heritability estimates were high for all traits within individual environments but moderate to low across the locations, indicating significant genotype × environment interactions. Principal component analysis (PCA) revealed that the first two components explained 58.3% of the total variation, with PC1 and PC2 accounting for 38.0% and 20.3%, respectively. Trait loadings showed positive associations of glucose and antioxidant activity with PC1, w…

Fast-Pyrolysis Biochar from Invasive Eichhornia crassipes as a High-Capacity Adsorbent for Lead (II) Ions
abstract: This study evaluated biochar derived from the leaves and stems of Eichhornia crassipes for the adsorption of Pb(II) ions from aqueous solution. Dried biomass was thermally converted at temperatures between 300 and 700°C, and the resulting biochars were evaluated to identify the material providing the highest Pb(II) removal. Biochars produced at 300°C from leaves (BC300L) and stems (BC300S) were subsequently selected for batch adsorption experiments. The effects of contact time, adsorbent dosage, initial Pb(II) concentration, and solution pH were investigated. Maximum adsorption performance was observed at a contact time of 15 min and pH 5. The selected adsorbent dosage was 0.005 g, at which Pb(II) removal reached 95.24% for BC300L and 96.63% for BC300S under the reported experimental conditions. Adsorption capacity increased with increasing initial Pb(II) concentration. Equilibrium data were evaluated using Langmuir and Freundlich isotherm models. BC300S showed a stronger fit to the Langmuir model (R² = 0.9864), whereas BC300L showed a stronger fit to the Freundlich model (R² = 0.9595). The results indicate that biochar prepared from E. crassipes leaves and stems has potential for Pb(II) removal from aqueous systems. Further evaluation under continuous-flow, regeneration, and multi-component conditions is required to establish its practical applicability.

Complement in HER2-Positive Breast Cancer: A Conditionally Protective Mechanism Under Attack
abstract: The therapeutic efficacy of anti-HER2 monoclonal antibodies in breast cancer has traditionally been attributed to direct inhibition of signaling and antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC). Recent evidence, however, has established complement activation through the classical pathway as a possible adjunct mechanism underlying the synergistic activity of the trastuzumab and pertuzumab combination. This synergy is mediated by complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC) and complement-dependent cellular phagocytosis (CDCP), and is lost upon C1q deletion in preclinical models. Tumor cells evade complement-mediated killing through overexpression of membrane-bound complement regulatory proteins (mCRPs), particularly CD55 and CD59, which correlate with shorter disease-free survival in patients treated with trastuzumab. C1q itself plays a dual, context-dependent role: it acts as a complement-independent tumor suppressor in HER2-positive breast cancer while promoting tumor progression in most other malignancies. Emerging therapeutic strategies, including biparatopic antibodies such as zanidatamab, complement-redirecting immunoconjugates, and mCRP-targeting approaches, aim to overcome complement resistance and enhance antitumor immunity. On this basis, we propose that HER2-positive breast cancer represents a conditionally complement-protective tumor, in which the balance between antib…

title: Formation Mechanism and Semi-Quantitative Threshold Assessment of Metal-Induced Gel-like Agglomerate Blockages in Slickwater Fracturing Fluids
abstract: Abstract The reuse of flowback water in slickwater fracturing can introduce elevated concentrations of dissolved metal ions, intensifying the incompatibility between polyacrylamide-based friction reducers and multivalent metal ions and promoting the formation of rubbery gel-like agglomerates, commonly referred to as “gummy bears”. These agglomerates can adversely affect flowback, surface fluid handling, and well productivity. In this study, field sample characterization and laboratory simulation are combined to investigate the composition and formation mechanism of such gel-like agglomerates. The results show that these materials are not simple polymer residues, but polymer–inorganic composites composed of polyacrylamide components, metal ions, and inorganic particles, with Fe3+ and Al3+ playing a particularly important role in their formation. Furthermore, a molar-ratio-based semiquantitative method is introduced to describe the relationship between metal-ion loading and effective polymer reactive sites, and to predict the threshold for gel-like agglomeration. The results improve the understanding of polymer–metal incompatibility under flowback water conditions and provide practical guidance for risk evaluation, fluid design, and mitigation of gummy-bear formation in field operations.
