Tuning structural, optical, charge storage, and electronic transport properties of graphene oxide through functional group engineering
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the effect of oxidation temperature on the structural, electronic, and electrochemical properties of graphene oxide (GO) synthesized at 75, 95, and 115 °C. Increasing the oxidation temperature resulted in a reduction in crystallite size from 9.95 ± 1.24 to 8.05 ± 0.49 nm and a decrease in the interlayer spacing, accompanied by partial reorganization of the sp² carbon domains. The electrical properties were significantly improved, with enhanced carrier transport at higher oxidation temperatures. The optical band gap decreased from 4.11 to 3.69 eV, while the Urbach energy increased from 285 to 625 meV, indicating enhanced energetic disorder and band-tail formation. Electrochemical analysis revealed improved charge-transfer kinetics, with the charge-transfer resistance decreasing from 911 to 598 Ω and the relaxation time decreasing from 0.842 to 0.671 ms. The electrochemical response also showed a predominantly diffusion-controlled charge-storage contribution, while the apparent diffusion coefficient decreased from 2.094 × 10⁻⁷ to 5.792 × 10⁻⁸ cm²/s with increasing oxidation temperature. In contrast, the specific capacitance decreased from 668 to 328 F/g, which is attributed to the reduction of oxygen-containing redox-active sites and restricted ion accessibility. title: Environmental strategy and digital transformation: pathways to green innovation and sustainable performance in Vietnamese manufacturing firms
abstract: Abstract Manufacturing firms in emerging economies face dual pressures to improve both environmental performance and digital technology adoption. Both themes have attracted extensive research attention on their own, yet few studies ask whether—and through what mechanisms—a proactive environmental strategy is associated with a stronger orientation toward both digital transformation and green innovation as parallel routes to sustainable performance. Drawing on the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, this study develops and tests an integrated model in which proactive environmental strategy is examined as an organisational-level antecedent associated with digital transformation and green innovation among Vietnamese manufacturing firms. Data from 602 manufacturing enterprises were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4. Proactive environmental strategy is positively associated with both digital transformation and green innovation, and each of these, in turn, is positively associated with sustainable performance—a pattern consistent with partial mediation. Four antecedents predict proactive environmental strategy: organisational support, dynamic environment, green transformational leadership, and stakeholder pressure. title: Resultados Internacionales de Aprendizaje 2025 y Propuesta de Mejora para una Zona Escolar Rural de Puebla, México
abstract: La novena aplicación del principal programa internacional de evaluación de estudiantes de quince años, difundida en 2026, situó a México muy por debajo del promedio internacional en las tres áreas evaluadas y registró un retroceso significativo en matemáticas. El problema abordado es la distancia entre la disponibilidad de evidencia comparada y su uso efectivo en la escala donde se deciden las prácticas de enseñanza. El objetivo fue analizar críticamente esos resultados y traducirlos en una propuesta de mejora operable para una zona escolar de telesecundarias rurales de la Sierra Norte de Puebla, alineada con la meta 4.1 de los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible. Se empleó un enfoque cualitativo con diseño de revisión documental descriptivo-interpretativa. De cuarenta y ocho documentos identificados se incluyeron veinte, seleccionados por pertinencia, verificabilidad contra la fuente institucional, vigencia y accesibilidad pública. El análisis de contenido se organizó en cuatro categorías. Los hallazgos mostraron que siete de cada diez estudiantes no alcanzaron el umbral mínimo de competencia en matemáticas, que uno de cada doscientos llegó a los niveles altos, que cuatro de cada diez quedaron por debajo del umbral en las tres áreas simultáneamente y que la brecha por condición socioeconómica permaneció estancada durante una década. title: User Perceptions of the Lentera Learning Platform: Reanalysis of a Custom Usability Questionnaire
abstract: This study re-examines user perceptions of the Lentera learning platform using the 30-response, ten-item questionnaire dataset embedded in the source manuscript. The original report applied the alternating System Usability Scale (SUS) scoring rule and obtained 49.16, although all ten administered statements are positively worded and therefore do not match the directionally alternating SUS instrument. Recalculation reproduces the original arithmetic as 49.1667 but confirms that the value cannot be interpreted as a valid SUS score. Direct analysis of the 300 original responses yields an overall mean of 3.40 on the five-point scale, a respondent-level median of 3.45, and an exploratory Cronbach's alpha of 0.944. Item means range from 3.10 for the usefulness of error messages to 3.60 for perceived search efficiency. The strongest corrected item-total relationship is observed for overall satisfaction, while error handling remains the clearest descriptive area for follow-up. These results support a moderate, generally favorable perception of the platform in this sample, but they do not establish task effectiveness, objective efficiency, or a standardized usability grade. The paper therefore distinguishes custom-survey evidence from SUS benchmarking and outlines a more defensible evaluation design for future Lentera studies.

title: Transformasi Digital dalam Akuntansi Keuangan: Systematic Literature Review Menggunakan Pendekatan PRISMA
abstract: Aim: This study aims to analyze the development of digital transformation in financial accounting, identify dominant technologies and research themes, and explore research gaps in the field of digital transformation in financial accounting. Method: This study employs a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 framework. The data consist of scientific articles obtained from Scopus, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, Emerald Insight, Google Scholar, and other scholarly sources. A total of 18 articles published between 2017 and 2026 met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed using content analysis with a thematic analysis approach. Results: The findings indicate that blockchain is the most dominant technology in the transformation of financial accounting due to its contribution to transparency, accountability, financial reporting quality, and fraud mitigation. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and automation also play important roles in improving the efficiency of accounting and auditing processes and supporting data-driven decision-making. However, existing research remains largely dominated by conceptual and literature-based studies, while empirical research examining the implementation of digital technologies in accounting practices remains relatively limited. title: Underrated deep-water scleractinian species: an ecological study along the Italian coasts (Mediterranean Sea)
abstract: Abstract Scleractinians are key components of Mediterranean mesophotic and bathyal benthic ecosystems, comprising 30 species known to occur below 40 m. A large ROV dataset, including 625 dives, each corresponding to a distinct geographical site, conducted between 40 and 1825 m across the Italian seas, was used to assess the diversity of this taxon, focusing on the distribution, habitat preferences, and population density of four Data Deficient, yet well-represented species: solitary Caryophyllia cyathus , Paracyathus pulchellus , and Javania cailleti , and colonial Thalamophyllia gasti . The study recorded 18 scleractinian species (representing 60% of the known deep ones) and analysed almost 2600 records of the four target species. Caryophyllia cyathus , Paracyathus pulchellus, and Thalamophyllia gasti were the most common, occurring between 80 and 150 m on inclined outcropping rocks encrusted with coralline algae along the continental platform, with major hotspots in the Tyrrhenian Sea and average densities ranging between 2.4 and 36 individuals or colonies m −2 . Thalamophyllia gasti was observed for the first time in a cave habitat in Southwest Sardinia, forming large colonies. Javania cailleti was recorded at only 4% of the investigated sites, mainly along the Northeast Sardinian canyons, Corse Channel, Dohrn Canyon, and on seamounts between 400 and 550 m. Sistem Kendali LED RGB Berbasis ESP32 Dual-Core dan FreeRTOS dengan Sinkronisasi Multi-Platform
abstract: Sistem pencahayaan cerdas umumnya bergantung pada konektivitas internet sehingga fungsionalitasnya menjadi terbatas ketika akses jaringan tidak tersedia. Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang dan mengimplementasikan sistem kendali pencahayaan cerdas berbasis mikrokontroler ESP32 dual-core yang mengintegrasikan beberapa platform kendali, yaitu dashboard web React.js, Telegram Bot, dan mechanical switch sebagai kendali lokal. Sistem memanfaatkan Firebase Realtime Database sebagai layanan sinkronisasi berbasis cloud serta dilengkapi fitur adaptive brightness menggunakan sensor LDR untuk menyesuaikan tingkat kecerahan LED secara otomatis berdasarkan kondisi pencahayaan lingkungan. Untuk meningkatkan pengelolaan tugas, FreeRTOS digunakan untuk memisahkan proses komunikasi jaringan dan rendering LED pada inti prosesor yang berbeda. Evaluasi sistem dilakukan melalui pengujian fungsional, latensi, dan penanganan konflik data. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa seluruh fungsi sistem berjalan sesuai state machine yang dirancang dengan tingkat keberhasilan operasional 100% (18/18 skenario). Pengujian latensi menghasilkan rata-rata waktu respons 645 ms pada kendali lokal tekan singkat, 1202 ms pada kendali lokal tekan lama, 1844 ms pada dashboard web, 2018 ms pada Telegram Bot, dan 334 ms pada pembaruan telemetri sensor LDR. title: Between scripture and dharma: James Legge’s translation of Record of Buddhist Kingdoms and the transmission of Buddhist thought in Victorian Britain
abstract: Abstract This study examines James Legge’s 1886 English translation of Faxian’s Record of Buddhist Kingdoms (Foguo ji 佛國記), analysing how a Scottish missionary-scholar and Oxford Sinologist became a pivotal mediator of Buddhist thought to Victorian Britain. Through close textual analysis and historical contextualization, the research investigates the productive tension between Legge’s Congregationalist background and his evolving scholarly approach to Buddhist texts during a formative period in Anglophone understanding of Eastern religions. Drawing on recent developments in translation studies, the study situates Legge’s rendering within the broader landscape of nineteenth-century Buddhist translation in both English and French, demonstrating how his methods differed from those of contemporaries such as Samuel Beal and Stanislas Julien. The analysis reveals how Legge’s translation choices, terminological decisions, structural organization, and extensive footnotes, negotiated religious difference with a sophistication unusual for the period, though not without limitations in his handling of Mahayana philosophical concepts. title: DATA-DRIVEN ELECTRICITY LOAD FORECASTING FOR NIGERIAN UNIVERSITIES: A CASE STUDY OF EDO STATE UNIVERSITY IYAMHO
abstract: Reliable electricity demand forecasting is increasingly important for Nigerian universities because campus expansion, digitalisation, laboratory activity, student population growth, and variable electricity supply place pressure on limited energy resources. This study develops and evaluates a data-driven forecasting framework for monthly electricity consumption at Edo State University Iyamho (EDSU), Nigeria. The study uses historical cumulative meter readings obtained from the university's Electrical Section of the Estate and works unit and converted them into monthly consumption observations. The readings cover a period from December 2020 through 2025 as usable sample. The final reconstructed consumption contains 55 monthly consumption intervals, while 48 usable monthly records were retained for modelling. Three forecasting approaches—Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA),Prophet, and a hybrid SARIMA–Prophet forecast—were compared using Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). The errors were 55,473 kWh and 39,302 kWh for SARIMA, 39,550 kWh and 27,797 kWh for Prophet, and 42,244 kWh and 29,566 kWh for the hybrid model, respectively. On the numerical metrics, Prophet had the lowest RMSE and MAE, reducing RMSE by 28.7% and MAE by 29.3% relative to SARIMA. The hybrid model improved substantially on SARIMA but did not outperform Prophet. Th…

title: Market and Welfare Effects of Restructuring US Beef Packing for Competition and Resilience
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper examines the USDA strategy to restructure US beef packing to increase competition and resilience by supporting the entry of small processors. Unlike previous studies that impose or calibrate conduct or assume symmetry between entrants and incumbents, we develop and estimate an asymmetric structural dominant‐oligopsony/oligopoly competitive‐fringe model using 1987–2022 data and IV‐GMM, allowing dominant packer conduct to respond to fringe entry. Findings indicate that fringe packer entry increases, rather than decreases, dominant packers' market power—widening price spreads and raising profits at the expense of consumers and farmers—without meaningfully improving resilience. The counterintuitive link between dominant market power and fringe entry arises because, in addition to being cost‐disadvantaged, the fringe group bids up cattle prices by shifting demand, eroding its ability to influence the residual market and enabling the dominant group to exercise greater market power.

title: PROXIMATE AND PHYTOCHEMICAL ANALYSIS OF THREE SPECIES OF PEPPER GOTTEN FROM RELIEF MARKET, OWERRI
abstract: The proximate and phytochemical analysis of three species of pepper (Capsicum frutescens, Capsicum annuum and Capsicum genus) were investigated. The three species of pepper was obtained from Relief Market in Owerri, Imo State, Nigeria. The three species of pepper were washed with distilled water and then sliced thinly (diameter of 0.1±1.0cm and the thickness of 3-4 mm) and then treated with Concentrated Chlorine solution. The samples were oven dried at temperature of 60OC for 24 hours. The samples were ground with a woring blender and stored in air-tight container. The result of the analysis showed that the proximate composition of Capsicum genus was significantly (P<0.05) higher than Capsicum frutescens and Capsicum annuum in moisture. Carbohydrate contents was significantly (P<0.05) higher in Capsicum annuum than Capsicum genus and Capsicum frutescens. Protein content of Capsicum frutescens was significantly (P<0.05) higher than Capsicum annuum and Capsicum genus. Capsicum annuum was significantly (P<0.05) higher than Capsicum genus and Capsicum frutescens in fat, insoluble and soluble fibre contents. Capsicum frutescens was significantly (P<0.05) higher than Capsicum genus and Capsicum annuum in ash contents. title: Comparative Analysis of Total Phosphorus (P%) in Animal Feeds Available in the Libyan Market Using Spectrophotometry
abstract: Phosphorus is naturally present in a wide range of feed ingredients, including cereals, oilseed meals, animal-derived products, and mineral supplements. The research depends on conducting a general study of the phosphorus ratio in animals feed in the Libyan market including Broiler poultry feed, Egg-laying poultry feed, cow feed, sheep feed, Horses feed, growing pony, Bird Feed, Egg- laying birds feed. the present study aimed to confirm the amount of phosphorus and calcium in animal feed products available in the Libyan market using a spectrophotometric method. Significant difference in (P) concentration was observed between the feed categories. The comparatively large difference between feed kinds might reflect variance in feed formulation, ingredient composition, animal species, production stage, and the use of mineral P supplements.

Spot‐Based Basis and Basis Momentum in Commodity Futures Markets
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper revisits two widely studied predictors of commodity futures returns, basis and basis momentum, whose conventional measures using first‐nearby futures as proxies for spot prices may limit their ability to capture fundamental spot‐market risks. Motivated by this limitation, we construct two spot‐based signals from observed spot and futures prices, which are theoretically shown to contain incremental information about future returns beyond conventional measures. Using 41 Chinese commodity futures, we find that these signals robustly predict subsequent first‐nearby contract returns and remain significantly priced in time‐series and cross‐sectional tests, even after controlling for their conventional counterparts. We then develop a spot‐enhanced three‐factor model, including the market factor and the two spot‐based factors, which consistently outperforms three widely used benchmark models in pricing competing factors and explaining return anomalies.

Sistem Pendeteksi Area Blind Spot pada Kendaraan Truk Menggunakan Computer Vision dan Sensor Ultrasonik JSN-SR04T Berbasis Internet of Things
abstract: Bertambahnya jumlah kendaraan meningkatkan angka kecelakaan, salah satunya disebabkan area blind spot pada truk yang menghalangi pandangan pengemudi. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan sistem pendeteksi blind spot berbasis Internet of Things (IoT) yang mengintegrasikan sensor ultrasonik JSN-SR04T sebagai peringatan dini dan computer vision menggunakan YOLOv11n pada ESP32-CAM untuk deteksi objek. Metode penelitian meliputi pengumpulan dan augmentasi dataset awal 417 citra, pelatihan model YOLOv11n pada Google Colab, serta perancangan perangkat keras yang terdiri dari JSN-SR04T, ESP32-CAM, NodeMCU ESP8266, dan LED, dengan komunikasi data berbasis MQTT untuk pemantauan real-time. Hasil uji posisi menunjukkan akurasi tertinggi pada posisi depan untuk mobil sebesar 93% (jarak 142 cm), sedangkan jarak deteksi terjauh terjadi pada posisi belakang untuk pejalan kaki hingga 329 cm (akurasi 73%). Hasil uji kecepatan menunjukkan akurasi pada 10–20 km/jam mencapai 100% (mobil), 90% (pengendara motor), dan 80% (pejalan kaki), lalu menurun pada 50 km/jam menjadi 70%, 60%, dan 50%. Sistem efektif sebagai peringatan dini pada kecepatan rendah–sedang, namun memerlukan peningkatan untuk objek kecil pada kecepatan tinggi.

title: Adaptive Graph-Attention Model for Multi-Step PM2.5 Forecasting: Cross-City Validation Across Gurugram and Mumbai
abstract: An adaptive Graph-Attention (GAT) spatial layer has previously been shown, in earlier unpublished work by the author, to outperform a fixed, distance-based spatial weighting scheme for hyperlocal PM2.5 forecasting on a 62-station monitoring network in Gurugram, India, under a controlled, capacity-matched comparison. Like nearly every graph-based air quality forecasting study in the reviewed literature, that result was established on a single city, leaving open whether the advantage is a property of the method or an artefact of that network's density or geography. This paper reports an independent cross-city validation: the identical fixed-weight-versus- adaptive-GAT comparison, matched in parameter count and trained under an unmodified protocol, is applied to a separately collected dataset from Mumbai, India. Of 29 candidate CPCB/MPCB/BMC stations (hourly data, 2025), 19 were retained after a data-quality screen; wind speed was unavailable, so the feature set was reduced from seven inputs to six, applied identically to both models. Across three seeds and four forecast horizons (1, 6, 12, 24 hours — 12 seed-horizon comparisons), the adaptive model achieved a lower RMSE than the fixed-weight model in 10 of 12 cases; a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test rejects the null hypothesis of no systematic difference (W = 3, p =0.0024, two-sided). title: Monitoring and forecasting groundwater storage dynamics in arid Wadi systems using GRACE/GRACE-FO satellite observations and XGBoost machine learning: Wadi El-Assiuti, Egypt (2003–2030)
abstract: Abstract Progressive groundwater depletion in arid regions represents one of the most critical water security challenges of the twenty-first century. Despite intensive agricultural abstraction in Egypt’s Wadi El-Assiuti since the 1990s, a continuous basin-scale assessment of groundwater storage dynamics has remained lacking. This study integrates GRACE/GRACE-FO Terrestrial Water Storage Anomalies (TWSA), GLDAS-2.2 soil moisture data, CHIRPS precipitation, and multi-temporal Sentinel-2/Landsat land-use datasets to derive monthly groundwater storage anomalies (GWSA) and cumulative variations over the period 2003–2024. Long-term trends were evaluated using the Mann–Kendall test and Sen’s slope estimator, while relationships were quantified using Pearson correlation analysis. GRACE-derived estimates were evaluated against available piezometric records. An XGBoost machine learning model was trained on the period 2003–2016, independently validated over 2017–2024, and subsequently applied for a 72-month forecasting horizon extending to 2030. Results indicate statistically significant declining trends in both GWSA ( p < 0.001) and cumulative groundwater storage, with an average depletion rate of approximately − 987,000 m 3 yr⁻ 1 . title: A Hybrid Vae–Attention Gcn–Bilstm Framework For Spatio-Temporal Weather Forecasting
abstract: Distributed sensor networks for accurate short-range weather forecasting are difficult because of measurement noise, missing measurements, and complex spatio-temporal dependencies. In this research, an integrated four-stage deep learning system to robustly predict weather is introduced. First, a Variational Autoencoder with Noise Reduction (VAE-NR) is used to learn a 64-dimensional latent space, which is the same for the LSI space, using a symmetric autoencoder architecture, to denoise meteorological observations and to mask-conditioned reconstruct missing observations. Secondly, by introducing node-level attention and feature-level attention, a Hybrid Attention Graph Convolutional Network (HAGCN) models the relationships between stations with a Pearson-correlation based graph and mines the informative spatial representations for each station. Spatiotemporal-feature impact (STFI) mechanism then ranks and adaptively rescales the meteorological variables following the time-averaged attention scores. Third, the bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) network, which models the temporal dependence in both forward and backward directions, is used as the two-layer network. Finally, an adaptive regression boosting strategy is used to train ten learners of BiLSTM model on reweighted residual error in order to minimize systematic prediction error. Freemium-To-Premium Conversion In Youtube Music: Usability, Enjoyment, And Price Value
abstract: Purpose - This study examines how perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, perceived enjoyment, and price value shape user attitudes and the behavioral intention to subscribe to a freemium music-streaming service, and what these relationships imply for platform monetization. Design/methodology/approach - We used an explanatory quantitative design. Data were collected from 385 YouTube Music freemium users through an online questionnaire and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling with SmartPLS 4.1.8. Findings - All eleven hypotheses are supported. The model explains 73.9% of the variance in attitude toward use and 74.1% in behavioral intention, with a predictive relevance of 0.935 and an SRMR of 0.043. Perceived ease of use is the dominant antecedent of attitude (β = 0.416), while price value is the strongest direct predictor of behavioral intention among the exogenous constructs (β = 0.287). Attitude toward use partially mediates the effects of ease of use, usefulness, and enjoyment, absorbing 31-45% of their total effects. Practical implications - Conversion depends less on feature abundance than on the joint management of usability, affective experience, and perceived monetary fairness. title: Development and internal validation of a preoperative risk prediction model for postoperative delirium in older patients with hip fracture
abstract: Abstract Background Postoperative delirium (POD) is a common and serious complication in older patients undergoing hip fracture surgery and is associated with adverse long-term outcomes. Accurate preoperative risk stratification is essential for implementing targeted preventive strategies. Methods In this single-center retrospective cohort study, we developed and internally validated a preoperative risk prediction model for POD in patients aged ≥60 years with acute hip fracture (n = 1706; 341 POD events). The intended prediction time point was the preoperative assessment after admission but before surgery, once the delay status was known. POD was diagnosed using the Confusion Assessment Method. Ten predictors were prespecified based on prior literature and clinical relevance, and all were available before surgery. No univariable screening or stepwise selection was performed; all ten predictors were entered simultaneously into a single multivariable logistic regression model. Model performance was evaluated in terms of discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility in an internal test set. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was used as a visualization tool to illustrate individual predictor contributions. Results The final model included ten prespecified predictors. Development and Validation of an Interpretable Machine Learning Model for Osteoporosis Prediction Using Multimodal Musculoskeletal Ultrasound and Clinical Features
abstract: Objectives This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning model for osteoporosis prediction based on multimodal ultrasound and clinical features. Methods Participants with suspected osteoporosis were enrolled from 2 medical centers. Clinical variables and multimodal musculoskeletal ultrasound parameters, including muscle thickness, cross‐sectional area, and shear wave elastography measurements, were collected. LASSO regression was used for feature selection. Eight machine learning algorithms, including logistic regression, decision tree, random forest, k‐nearest neighbors, support vector machine, naïve Bayes, neural network, and XGBoost, were developed and compared. Model performance was evaluated in the training, internal validation, and external test cohorts using the area under curve (AUC), accuracy, and F1 score. Model interpretability was assessed using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results The LASSO regression demonstrated that age, gastrocnemius medial head's muscle thickness (GmhMT), rectus femoris' cross‐sectional area (RFCSA), gender, body mass index (BMI), and TibialisSWE were key features for osteoporosis. The XGBoost model demonstrated accuracy of 0.889, 0.825, and 0.773 in the training, validating, and testing sets. title: Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Low‐Voltage DC Circuit Breaker Contacts Based on a Shared Degradation Subspace
abstract: To reduce the influence of contact‐to‐contact differences in life prediction for arc‐eroded contacts of low‐voltage DC circuit breakers, this paper proposes a shared degradation subspace method. First, a resistance‐constrained region growing algorithm is designed to achieve stable extraction of the contact region, and three degradation features, namely contour rectangularity, edge activity, and gray structural entropy, are constructed according to the morphological evolution mechanism. Then, a low‐dimensional shared degradation subspace is established through global standardization, individual baseline debiasing, degradation direction normalization, and dominant degradation direction extraction, and a one‐dimensional shared degradation coordinate, inv1, is obtained. Finally, remaining useful life (RUL) prediction experiments are carried out using leave‐one‐subject‐out (LOSO) cross‐validation. The LOSO validation results for the tested contacts show that the proposed method can improve the prediction performance of life prediction models, especially for models that can effectively utilize the structural information of the feature space. © 2026 Institute of Electrical Engineers of Japan and Wiley Periodicals LLC.

title: Modelling and Optimization of Strut Configurations in Aircraft Landing Gear Assembly for Effective In-Service Duty Cycle
abstract: The landing gear configuration system is one of the most critical systems, subjected to intense dynamic loads and failure during landing and taxiing operations. The optimization of this system is of key importance to the aviation industry, with clear and direct effects ranging from integrity, safety, and fuel efficiency to maintenance dynamics. The present study focuses on the modelling and optimization of strut configurations in an aircraft landing gear assembly for an effective in-service duty cycle. Two strut configurations, consisting of a conventional single strut and an optimized dual strut, were modelled and comparatively analyzed using parametric CAD tools as well as Finite Element Analysis (FEA) within the SolidWorks simulation environment. The modelling and simulation involve the load and stress analysis of critical components, ranging from the main strut, retraction mechanisms, torque links, torque bars, and wheels to the actuator and main support. This approach was geared towards the premise of analyzing and optimizing the landing gear system by achieving weight reduction without compromising structural integrity. This was achieved through FEA of the design model. Modeling Nurse Performance and Error Risk With Neural Networks: The Moderating Role of Decision‐Making Styles
abstract: ABSTRACT Human error in emergency departments (EDs) arises from contextual human factors and individual cognitive differences, yet these streams are often studied separately. This study models ED nurse performance and error risk using artificial neural networks (ANNs), with decision‐making styles (DMSs) as a moderating variable. Twenty factors contributing to human error (FCHE) were identified and refined by ED experts. Data from 239 emergency nurses in three Iranian military hospitals over 1 year included incident‐based FCHE scores, a 40‐item performance instrument, and Driver et al.‘s DMS questionnaire. Reliability and validity were confirmed, and aspect weights were derived using the Best–Worst Method. Multilayer perceptron (MLP) and radial basis function networks were trained with leakage‐free fivefold cross‐validation. The MLP achieved an MSE of 0.0584 on a held‐out 15% test set, outperforming regression baselines. Efficiency scores were validated against DEA and sensitivity analysis ranked influential factors by DMS, supporting targeted staffing and decision‐support design.

title: Monitoring and Evaluation Tools, Stakeholder Involvement and Implementation of Digital Data Systems in the Public Service in Kenya
abstract: Purpose: The purpose of this study was to examine the role of monitoring and evaluation tools and stakeholder involvement in the implementation and sustainability of digital data systems in the public service in Kenya. Methodology: The study adopted a literature-based approach to examine existing knowledge on participatory monitoring and evaluation, digital data systems, stakeholder engagement, and project sustainability in the public service. The theoretical framework was guided by the stakeholder participation theories of Arnstein (1969), Burns, Hambleton and Hoggett (1994), and Wilcox (2003). Findings: The study found that effective stakeholder involvement in monitoring and evaluation enhances ownership, accountability, transparency, capacity development, service delivery, and project sustainability. The use of digital technologies facilitates timely data collection, information sharing, performance tracking, feedback, and evidence-based decision-making. However, effective implementation and sustainability may be constrained by inadequate resources, limited technical skills, poor institutional support, resistance to technological change, corruption, political interference, poor data quality, and weak monitoring structures. title: Genesis and transformation of state regulation of healthcare under the development of socially responsible medical entrepreneurship
abstract: The article substantiates the theoretical, historical, and applied foundations of the genesis and transformation of state regulation of healthcare in the context of socially responsible medical entrepreneurship. It argues that the state’s regulatory role has evolved from a paternalistic, budgetary, and administrative-permission model to one based on strategic purchasing, patient-centered service delivery, digital traceability, contractual accountability, and partnerships with private providers. Socially responsible medical entrepreneurship is interpreted not merely as a market segment, but as a socially significant institution that affects access, quality, continuity, and equity of care amid war, demographic losses, workforce shortages, fiscal constraints, and European integration. The paper systematizes the key theoretical approaches to healthcare regulation, including institutional theory, stakeholder theory, stewardship, New Public Management, responsive regulation, creating shared value, ESG/CSR approaches, and public-private partnership. The article develops a comparative framework of Ukrainian and foreign regulatory trajectories. title: Farmer’s Mini Cold Storage Technology for Reducing Postharvest Losses and Enhancing Storage Capacity of Mango Under Bangladesh Perspectives
abstract: Mango is a highly perishable fruit. It’s rapid ripening, softening and microbial deterioration cause substantial postharvest losses in Bangladesh. The present study evaluated farmer’s mini cold storage technology combined with simple packaging treatments for reducing postharvest losses and extending the storage life of ‘Banana Mango’ under Bangladesh conditions. Mango fruits were subjected to different washing and packaging treatments and evaluated at 3 day intervals up to 24 days after storage (DAS). Treatments included ambient storage, cold storage under open conditions, brown paper covering, individual brown paper covering with or without mango stalk, jute bag covering and polythene sheet covering using washed and unwashed fruits. Fruits stored at room temperature deteriorated rapidly and marketability declining within 9 DAS. Mini cold storage markedly delayed deterioration period. The treatments W1T4 (washed mangoes individually covered with brown paper while retaining the mango stalk) performed best. It maintained excellent colour and firmness up to 15 DAS and recorded 92.67%, 83.67%, and 42.33% marketable fruits at 18, 21, and 24 DAS, respectively. Overall, CoolBot driven mini cold storage combined with individual brown paper covering effectively delayed ripening, reduced decay and weight loss and extended mango storage period for reducing postharvest losses in Bangladesh…

Hybrid Quantum–Classical Machine Learning for Sustainable Drug Discovery: Heat Capacity-Based Drug-Likeness Evaluation
abstract: Sustainable approaches to molecular analysis can support the development of computational methods for early stage drug discovery. This work explores whether combining quantum derived molecular representations with a classical regressor improves the prediction of heat capacity, and considers what that might mean for drug-likeness assessment. The QM9 molecular dataset is first prepared through numerical preprocessing, feature scaling, and dimensionality reduction, after which the resulting representations are encoded into a quantum circuit to produce quantum-derived features. These are combined with conventional molecular descriptors and fed into an XGBoost regressor to generate the final heat-capacity (Cv) predictions. To gauge whether this hybrid design offers any real advantage, its output is compared directly against a purely classical model, using R², MAE, and MSE as the basis for comparison. The hybrid configuration reaches an R² of approximately 0.947, versus roughly 0.923 for the classical model a gap that suggests quantum-derived representations can meaningfully sharpen prediction of this thermodynamic property, at least under the conditions tested here. Overall, the framework offers a computationally grounded approach that could support molecular screening and contribute to more sustainable early-stage drug-discovery strategies.

title: Mechanism of Rule Alignment between the Hainan Free Trade Port and ASEAN
abstract: Rule alignment between the Hainan Free Trade Port and ASEAN is a dynamic governance process in which different rule systems move from coexistence toward compatibility under conditions of institutional heterogeneity. Building on the conceptualization of rule alignment and the “institutional interface,” this paper constructs an analytical framework of “factor flows—actor coordination—institutional diffusion” from the perspectives of institutional complexity and cross-domain collaborative governance, and examines the practical forms of alignment in such fields as goods trade, investment and trade in services, personnel qualifications, and the digital economy. The study finds that cross-border factor flows continuously render institutional frictions visible and generate demands for alignment; multiple governance actors form rule connections through coordinated interaction; and functional platforms drive the diffusion of institutional innovation through pilot experimentation. Current problems include bias in demand identification, fragmentation of actor coordination, and insufficient transformation of pilot outcomes. The effectiveness of rule alignment should therefore be improved through demand feedback, tiered coordination, and evaluation-diffusion mechanisms.

title: Mechanism of anti-crisis financial management of an insurance company amidst cyberattacks and digital shocks
abstract: The article provides a theoretical generalization and develops a practical mechanism for the anti-crisis financial management of an insurance company amidst the growing intensity of cyberattacks and resulting digital shocks. The study analyzes the contemporary operating environment of the Ukrainian insurance market, characterized by high military-economic uncertainty, strict regulatory oversight by the National Bank of Ukraine on compliance with capital and solvency requirements, and accelerated digitalization of business processes. The widespread adoption of online sales and automated claims settlement, alongside business advantages, has created high technological dependence and qualitatively new threats to insurers’ financial stability. The study aims to substantiate the conceptual foundations and develop a comprehensive anti-crisis mechanism for an insurance company’s financial management to ensure its liquidity, solvency, and operational continuity under conditions of digital shocks. In the research process, a set of scientific methods was applied: systemic, structural-functional, and comparative analysis – to examine the impact factors of the digital environment and assess the limitations of traditional anti-crisis management approaches; statistical, economic-mathematical, and graphical analysis—to study the dynamics, structure, and vectors of cyberattacks on the financial…

title: Economic mechanism of balanced environmental management in the territorial community life-support system: functional and financial aspects
abstract: The article substantiates the theoretical and applied foundations for forming and operating the economic mechanism of balanced environmental management within the territorial community’s life-support system. The key functional blocks of the mechanism – including regulatory, stimulating, control-protective, and social-safety functions aimed at ensuring a high-quality and safe living environment for the population – are identified and systematized. The study analyzes the financial and economic toolkit for supporting local-level environmental management. Based on an analysis of dynamics in resource payments to Ukraine’s consolidated budget for 2024–2025, the study reveals key trends in revenues from rent payments, land tax, and environmental taxes. The study supports increasing the share of environmental tax allocations to local budgets for communities with high anthropogenic loads. The study discusses the expediency of diversifying funding sources for eco-projects through private investment via public-private partnerships, the issuance of municipal green bonds, and community participation in European international programs. title: The Mechanism for Collateral Enforcement in Non-Performing Murabahah Financing at BSI Jombang Branch: A Sharia Economic Law Perspective
abstract: This study aims to analyze the mechanisms for enforcing collateral in non-performing murabahah financing and to assess their compliance with the principles of Islamic economic law. This study employs a juridical-empirical method using a conceptual approach and case studies, focusing on the Jombang Branch of Bank Syariah Indonesia (BSI). Data were collected through document review, observation, and interviews with a Legal Officer, an Account Officer, and a customer with a non-performing financing account. The results indicate that BSI Jombang Branch implements a systematic and phased mechanism, beginning with rescheduling, reconditioning, and restructuring, followed by the issuance of warning letters (WL I through WL III), providing the debtor with the opportunity to sell the collateral independently, and ultimately the execution of the collateral through an official auction at the State Assets and Auction Service Office (KPKNL). Procedurally, these stages comply with applicable regulations, including DSN-MUI Fatwa No. 68/DSN-MUI/III/2008 on Rahn Tasjily and the Compilation of Sharia Economic Law (KHES). However, from the perspective of Islamic economic law, the execution of such enforcement is deemed not to fully reflect the principle of al-'adl (justice), particularly regarding the determination of liquidation prices that are often far below fair market value, as evidenced in …

title: Innovation incentives in shaping the mechanism for motivating entrepreneurial activity in rural areas
abstract: The article examines how innovation incentives shape the motivational mechanism for entrepreneurial activity in rural areas. Innovation incentives are interpreted as a system of financial, institutional, digital, environmental, and social inducements that reduce the cost and risks of introducing innovations, expand access to knowledge, technologies, and resources, and increase the expected returns from entrepreneurial decisions. The study systematizes the main groups of innovation incentives by their functional role in the innovation transition and identifies the economic effects associated with their use. The study pays particular attention to incentive complementarity, since financial support without digital infrastructure and advisory services has limited effect, while technological solutions cannot scale without accessible financing, relevant skills, and institutional capacity. A comparative analysis of Ukraine and the European Union identifies the key preconditions for forming innovation incentives for rural entrepreneurship. The results reveal a marked asymmetry between Ukraine’s relatively high entrepreneurial activity and considerably weaker opportunities to implement innovation. This gap is reflected in lower innovation performance, significantly lower research and development expenditure, limited business capacity to finance innovation, and unequal access to digital i…

abstract: ABSTRACT Poly(3‐hexylthiophene) (P3HT) is introduced as a multifunctional conductive binder and redox mediator to fundamentally improve the performance and volumetric energy density of carbon‐free LiFePO 4 (LFP) cathodes. Unlike conventional Super P (SP):PVDF systems, P3HT can be electrochemically doped within the LFP operating potential range, forming an internal percolating conductive network that precedes and facilitates the LFP redox reaction. Strong π–π interactions and P3HT–Fe coordination enable P3HT to uniformly coat LFP particles, yielding intimate interfacial contact, enhanced adhesion, and an ultrathin, stable cathode–electrolyte interphase. As a result, P3HT‐based LFP cathodes exhibit significantly improved packing density (2.70 g cm −3 ), delivering volumetric energy densities up to 1402 Wh L − 1 , far surpassing SP:PVDF‐based counterparts (1.43 g cm −3 ; 738 Wh L −1 ). The P3HT‐based LFP cathodes achieve long‐term cycling stability and high‐rate capability comparable to or better than SP:PVDF‐based LFP electrodes. Density functional theory further reveals strong P3HT–LFP adsorption (−80 to −170 kJ mol − 1 ), substantial charge transfer, and narrowed bandgap at the P3HT‐LFP interface, confirming enhanced electronic coupling. This work shows that P3HT as a highly efficient binder can integrate conductivity, redox mediation, and interfacial stabilization, offering a …

title: Air/CO 2 Stepwise Induction of Fe Nanocluster Enrichment in FeMgAlOx Solid‐Solution Catalysts for Single‐Walled Carbon Nanotube Growth
abstract: ABSTRACT Solid‐solution catalysts hold great promise as low‐cost catalysts for the growth of small‐diameter single‐walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs); however, their catalytic performance is limited by low metal‐site utilization and unfavorable interfacial structures in conventional architectures. Here, we report a facile design strategy for FeMgAlOx solid‐solution catalysts featuring abundant active sites and enhanced interfacial structures that suppress nanocluster agglomeration. The successful synthesis of this catalyst relies on a high‐temperature‐induced two‐step strategy: high‐temperature oxidation enhances crystallinity, while high‐temperature air/CO 2 treatment facilitates the formation of strong metal‐support interactions (SMSI) on inert metal oxide supports. In this architecture, the ultrathin two‐dimensional morphology and ordered atomic arrangement promote active‐metal spillover, yielding abundant active sites; meanwhile, CO 2 induction significantly enhances the SMSI‐mediated confinement capability for Fe nanoclusters. Crystalline evolution and SMSI regulation synergistically facilitate the exsolution of active Fe species from the bulk solid solution, thereby forming thermally stable Fe nanoclusters. Furthermore, optimized single‐walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT) growth kinetics confirm that the modified solid solution possesses both a higher density of active sites and…

title: Waste-to-energy valorisation of municipal solid waste using elephant grass and abattoir waste as co-substrates
abstract: Abstract This study examined the anaerobic co-digestion of the organic fraction of municipal solid waste (OFMSW), elephant grass (EG), and abattoir waste (AW) to boost biomethane production in Kumasi, Ghana. Analyses of physicochemical, ultimate, lignocellulosic, and organic fractions showed that the substrates have complementary traits suitable for anaerobic digestion. Elephant grass had high carbohydrate levels and low lignin, while abattoir waste supplied nitrogen-rich compounds to enhance nutrient balance during digestion. Biomethane potential (BMP) tests under mesophilic conditions with various substrate mixes revealed that EG 100 generated a total methane yield of 275.55 mL CH₄ g⁻ 1 VS, a 26.7% increase over OFMSW mono-digestion (217.51 mL CH₄ g⁻ 1 VS). AW 100 produced 155.52 mL CH₄ g⁻ 1 VS. The co-digested mixture O50EG50 achieved the highest methane yield of 346.70 mL CH₄ g⁻ 1 VS, representing a 59.4% increase over mono-digestion of OFMSW. The modified Gompertz model estimated an ultimate methane yield (G₀) of 531.37 mL CH₄ g⁻ 1 VS for O 50 EG 50 , about 142.3% higher than for OFMSW alone, indicating that the co-digestion conditions need optimisation. These findings indicate that co-digesting OFMSW with elephant grass significantly enhances biomethane output and offers a sustainable waste-to-energy strategy for Ghana.

The Critical Role of Economies of Scale: A Techno‐Economic Assessment of Small‐ Versus Large‐Scale Biogas Upgrading in Rural Tanzania
abstract: ABSTRACT Access to clean and affordable energy remains a major challenge in rural Tanzania, where dependence on traditional biomass continues to drive deforestation, indoor air pollution, and energy insecurity. Biogas offers a promising alternative, yet limited evidence exists on the technical and economic feasibility of decentralized upgrading systems in rural settings. Building on the experimentally implemented and validated pilot‐scale waste‐to‐fuel system, this study undertakes a techno‐economic assessment of small‐ and community‐scale biogas upgrading under rural Tanzanian conditions. The systems were designed to upgrade raw biogas into usable cooking fuel by removing hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) using low‐cost purification methods powered by off‐grid solar energy. Rusted steel wool achieved effective H 2 S removal (< 2 ppm), while calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH) 2 ) achieved 62% CO 2 removal efficiency. Economic performance was evaluated using net present value (NPV) and Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE). The small‐scale system (100 L/day) achieved an LCOE of TZS 1572/kWh, indicating poor economic viability, whereas the modeled large‐scale system (6500 L/day) achieved an LCOE of TZS 241/kWh, demonstrating substantial economies of scale. Sensitivity analysis identified raw biogas production and system lifespan as the dominant economic drivers. The findings s…

title: Business planning strategy for energy-efficient construction projects
abstract: The article substantiates a strategic approach to business planning of energy-efficient construction projects. It shows that conventional business planning methodology, focused on estimated construction cost and the facility’s commissioning date, does not reflect the economic nature of an energy-efficient project, whose effect develops throughout the building’s entire operating period. Business planning for such projects is a coordinated sequence of analytical, computational, and organizational decisions that link the client’s energy targets with the project’s financial model and funding sources. A comparative analysis of traditional and life-cycle approaches to business planning is carried out according to the planning objective, calculation horizon, optimization criterion, cost structure, source of economic effect, composition of risks, performance indicators, and the role of monitoring. It is established that the transition to the life-cycle approach changes the very subject of the calculation: instead of minimizing capital expenditure, the task becomes the minimization of the discounted total cost of ownership of the building, which makes the incremental investment in the thermal envelope, heat recovery, automated control, and local generation economically justified. The business planning strategy is systematized in stages, covering strategic diagnostics and target setting,…

title: Detecting Anomalous Cell Behavior in Electrochemical Battery Testing Using Machine Learning
abstract: The growing availability of structured battery databases opens new opportunities for data‐driven quality control in battery manufacturing. Efficient identification of anomalous cells is critical for ensuring safety, performance, and longevity. In this work, we present a machine‐learning‐based framework for detecting anomalous cell behavior using rate‐test data and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements. A curated battery database serves as a reference and filter, enabling systematic comparison across 29 distinct coin cell configurations, each comprising 4–14 nominally identical cells. Rate‐test anomaly prediction using a support vector classifier (SVC) with a radial basis function (RBF) kernel yields a test accuracy of 90%, whereas anomaly detection based on EIS data with a convolutional variational autoencoder (CNN‐VAE) achieves an accuracy of 83.3%. Overall, these findings demonstrate the promise of combining structured battery datasets with advanced machine‐learning techniques to enable automated, accurate, and scalable diagnostic pipelines for next‐generation energy storage systems.

Evaluating the Techno‐Economic Feasibility of Grid‐Connected Hybrid Renewable Energy and Storage System
abstract: ABSTRACT Focusing on the renewable energy potential of Hurghada, Egypt, this study analyzes a grid‐integrated system that utilizes DSSC technology, wind turbines, and battery storage. A multi‐dimensional assessment is conducted, encompassing techno‐economic modeling, environmental impact through emissions tracking, and sensitivity analyses to evaluate system resilience under varying conditions. The optimization results indicate a decrease in the cost of energy (COE) from $0.149/kWh to $0.0485/kWh due to the integration of DSSCs, compared to a scenario relying solely on the grid. Additionally, the findings demonstrate that the proposed configuration can supply up to 85.6% of the required electricity. The study also compares grid power and DC voltage fluctuations with those of a system without storage, showing that the proposed system maintains stable DC voltage, which enhances overall system stability and power quality. CO 2 emissions drop drastically from 89,211 to 22,510 kg/Year, with similar reductions observed for SO 2 and NOx.

title: Internal Electric Field‐Regulated Dual‐Site Fe–Re Supramolecular Assembly for Photocatalytic CO 2 Reduction Toward Multicarbon Products
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic CO 2 reduction to multicarbon products remains challenging because C–C coupling is kinetically demanding and often limited by inefficient charge separation and poor control over reaction intermediates. Herein, a heterobimetallic supramolecular catalyst (Fe–Re SA) is constructed via electrostatic self‐assembly between a porphyrinic FeTCPP unit and a molecular Rebpy complex. Structural and spectroscopic analyses confirm that the Fe–N 4 and Re(I) carbonyl coordination environments remain preserved after assembly, while density functional theory (DFT)‐supported interfacial charge redistribution induces an internal electric field that promotes directional charge transfer and suppresses carrier recombination. In situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) reveals * CO‐related and C–C coupling‐related features, supporting a tandem catalytic mechanism in which the Re site catalyzes CO generation and the Fe‐centered porphyrin promotes subsequent C–C coupling. As a result, Fe–Re SA exhibits enhanced photocatalytic CO 2 reduction toward multicarbon products, achieving a C 2 H 4 formation rate of 4967 µmol g −1 h −1 with a total C 2 selectivity of 57.2% (C 2 H 4 selectivity of 47.5%) among carbon‐containing products. title: Self‑Powered All‑Fiber Hydrogen Sensor via Whispering Gallery Mode Microcavity and Built‑in Electric Field Synergy
abstract: Abstract Fiber‑optic hydrogen sensors offer intrinsic safety and remote operation, yet their application is constrained by expensive spectrometers and complex demodulation. Here, we present a self-powered all‑fiber hydrogen sensor (SAHS) that integrates optical excitation, electrical readout and gas detection on a single fiber tip, enabling remote and room‑temperature sensing at zero bias. By constructing a whispering gallery mode (WGM)-enhanced lateral ZnO/PEDOT:PSS n–p heterojunction on the fiber tip, we achieve synergy between the localized optical field and the built‑in electric field. The WGM microcavity confines and recycles incident light, markedly enhancing light-matter interaction and photogeneration on the tiny fiber tip. Meanwhile, the lateral built‑in field efficiently dissociates the photogenerated carriers, producing a substantial photocurrent without any external voltage. The self‑powered sensor exhibits outstanding room‑temperature H2 detection under 380 nm light excitation upon Pd functionalization, with a detection limit of ∼19 ppm and response/recovery times of 30 s and 7 s, respectively. This light‑activated, electrically‑read‑out architecture eliminates costly optical demodulation equipment, offering a low‑cost, user‑friendly and intrinsically safe solution for advanced hydrogen energy monitoring.

title: Spacing Effects in Guided Vertical‐Axis Wind Turbine Arrays for Highway Energy Harvesting Under Multi‐Vehicle Wake Conditions
abstract: ABSTRACT Highway‐induced airflow generated by passing vehicles represents an underutilized source of localized renewable energy that can be harvested using vertical‐axis wind turbines (VAWTs). While prior studies have demonstrated the feasibility of single‐turbine configurations, the aerodynamic interaction between vehicle wakes and multi‐turbine arrays—particularly the role of inter‐turbine spacing—remains insufficiently understood. In this study, two‐dimensional unsteady Reynolds‐averaged Navier–Stokes (URANS) simulations coupled with the SST k–ω turbulence model are employed to investigate the performance of guided elliptical Savonius‐type VAWT arrays operating under multi‐vehicle traffic conditions. Three‐turbine arrays are examined at normalized inter‐turbine spacings from S/D = 3 to 14, together with an additional phase‐aligned reference case at S/D = 30.114. The results reveal a strong non‐linear dependence of array‐level energy extraction on turbine spacing. Among the investigated configurations, the highest total energy capture is achieved at a spacing of 12 m (12D), yielding a total extracted energy of 697.34 J and representing a 68% increase relative to the most compact configuration. Smaller spacings are characterized by severe wake interference between turbines, whereas larger spacings exhibit progressive dissipation of vehicle‐induced flow structures despite near‐…

title: A Hybrid Model‐Data‐Driven Scheduling Strategy for Vehicle‐to‐Grid Interaction Based on Virtual Power Plant Coordination
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) have experienced vigorous development in recent years. However, their large‐scale integration into the power grid presents challenges related to the ‘curse of dimensionality’ and uncertainties, making it difficult to balance rapid grid demand response with the interests of EV users. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a hybrid model‐data‐driven scheduling strategy for vehicle‐to‐grid (V2G) interactions based on virtual power plant (VPP) coordination. It adopts a sequential model‐based aggregated charging scheduling and data‐driven power division mechanism to mitigate dimensionality and uncertainty problems. Furthermore, the data‐driven division strategy is implemented in two stages: both the EV bidding process in Stage 1 and the VPP clearing process in Stage 2 are driven by a distributed deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework with high sample efficiency. This design not only achieves rapid response to setpoints but also fully accommodates the interests of EV owners. The correctness and effectiveness of the proposed strategy are verified through simulations on a modified IEEE 33‐bus system integrated with massive VPPs and EVs. © 2026 Institute of Electrical Engineers of Japan and Wiley Periodicals LLC.

title: Examining Spatial Concordance of Knowledge Aggregated AHP TOPSIS and Random Forest for Electric Vehicle Charging Site Suitability
abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure planning in data-scarce megacities is often constrained by limited spatial data and expert-driven decision models whose underlying assumptions are rarely validated. This study presents an integrated GIS-based decision-support framework for identifying optimal EV charging locations in Dhaka, Bangladesh — a 22-million-resident megacity targeting 30% EV penetration by 2030, by combining expert-elicited Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) weighting with the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS). Unlike conventional GIS-MCDM studies, the proposed framework systematically evaluates criterion collinearity and assesses the spatial concordance between expert-derived suitability patterns and a machine-learning model using Random Forest with spatial cross-validation. Fourteen spatial criteria derived from open-access datasets and weighted by eleven domain experts were used to generate a 100-m suitability map. The analysis identified fifteen priority charging zones, with the Tejgaon–Hatirjheel corridor ranking highest. Reliable multimodal signals for in-vehicle heartbeat detection
abstract: Abstract Continuous and unobtrusive cardiac monitoring during driving is medically attractive but technically challenging due to motion artifacts, contact variability, and changing illumination. Building on our previously developed multimodal sensing platform that integrates steering wheel electrocardiography (ECG), photoplethysmography (PPG), and a camera (RGB), in this paper, we (i) propose an improved electrode design for steering wheel ECG acquisition, (ii) integrate infrared and thermal cameras, and (iii) combine these modalities for robust heartbeat detection under real-world driving conditions. We record data from 23 healthy adults on a standardized 55 km route that includes urban, rural, and highway segments. During each drive, we acquire a ground truth ECG using electrodes attached to the driver’s upper body. We use convolutional neural network models with early fusion, signal-based late fusion, sensor-based late fusion, and hybrid fusion. The steering wheel ECG achieves the highest single-modality performance (F1-score = 91.92%). Augmenting ECG with iPPG-RGB and iPPG-IR raises the F1-score to 92.14%. The vision-based signals provide limited complementary information but do not compensate for complete steering wheel electrocardiogram (ECG) loss. In future work, we will increase the reliability of physiological recordings by using data from the vehicle’s controller area…

title: Visual Classification of Vehicle Types Using Transfer Learning
abstract: Road traffic crashes remain a major cause of death among children and young people, and reliable visual recognition of the vehicles involved can support later accident documentation. Vehicle type classification is well studied on ordinary traffic imagery, whereas accident-related use requires models that remain informative when vehicles are damaged, occluded, or poorly illuminated. This paper reports a four-class vehicle type classification experiment that uses transfer learning with the Visual Geometry Group 16-layer network (VGG16). A curated corpus of 1,750 images was assembled from publicly accessible web sources through a manually supervised image-retrieval process and was manually annotated before being divided into training, validation, and testing partitions (1,260 / 140 / 350). Augmentation was applied only during training. On the held-out test set of 350 images, the classifier attained 89% overall accuracy and a macro-averaged F1-score of 0.89. Class-wise F1-scores were 0.95 for bike, 0.88 for bus, and 0.87 for both car and truck. Training curves show mild overfitting on the validation split, while the separate test partition confirms balanced four-class performance. The study is limited to a VGG16 baseline; comparisons with residual and transformer architectures, together with robustness and latency tests, remain future work. title: Sustainable and Rapid Preparation of the High-Performance MOR Zeolite Membrane for Acetic Acid Dehydration under Fluoride-Free Conditions via a Hydroxyl Radical-Promoted Strategy
abstract: Abstract The rapid preparation of high-performance MOR zeolite membranes for the dehydration of high-concentration acetic acid under fluoride-free conditions remains a significant challenge. In this study, a hydroxyl radical-promoted strategy was successfully applied to fabricate high-performance MOR zeolite membranes on macroporous mullite supports within only 3 h, under fluoride-free and organic-template-free conditions. The formation process of MOR zeolite membranes in the presence of hydroxyl radicals was systematically investigated. Furthermore, the roles of hydroxyl radicals and hydroxide ions in the synthesis mechanism of MOR zeolite membranes were discussed in detail using characterization methods such as SEM, XRD, EPR, and fluorescence spectroscopy. Compared with the synthesis system without hydroxyl radical participation, the hydroxyl radical-promoted MOR zeolite membranes not only exhibited a significantly shortened crystallization time but also enabled a reduction in the alkalinity of the reaction system. The membrane prepared under optimal conditions demonstrated excellent separation performance in a 90 wt % acetic acid/water mixture at 75 °C, with a permeation flux as high as 1.37 kg m–2 h–1 and a water content in the permeate exceeding 99.4 wt %. title: Business Development Strategy and Performance of Leather Product Enterprises in an Emerging Economy
abstract: Purpose: This study examines the direct effects of business development strategy dimensions on the performance of leather product SMEs in Kaduna and Kano States, Nigeria. Design/Methodology/Approach: A quantitative, cross-sectional survey design was adopted. Grounded in the Resource-Based View and the Dynamic Capabilities perspective, five hypotheses were formulated and tested on data collected from 361 leather product enterprises using simple random sampling and analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) on a psychometrically refined measurement model, following an iterative item-purification procedure. Research Limitation: The research is confined to a single industry and two states, limiting transferability beyond the leather product segment in Northwest Nigeria. Findings: The refined model achieved satisfactory reliability and convergent validity (Cronbach's alpha 0.82–0.92; composite reliability 0.82–0.92; average variance extracted 0.59–0.74) and acceptable, though not uniformly strong, discriminant validity and overall model fit. title: Upcycling Disposable Mask Straps Into Asymmetric PEDOT:PSS‐Based Triboelectric Nanogenerators Enabled by Saline‐Induced Power Enhancement
abstract: ABSTRACT This work demonstrates a sustainable upcycling strategy that transforms discarded mask straps into flexible direct‐current triboelectric nanogenerators (DC‐TENGs) through an eco‐friendly NaCl‐assisted modification. The PEDOT:PSS/PVA/Pullulan composite simultaneously serves as the electrode and triboelectric layer, enabling a simplified and metal‐reduced fabrication. The saline treatment introduces Na + –PSS − coordination, which sustainably enhances molecular mobility, interfacial polarization, and charge transfer without the need for toxic dopants or complex post‐processing. The resulting device delivers a peak voltage of ∼1 V, a current of ∼180 µA, and a maximum power density of 0.5 W m − 2 under mechanical deformation. By utilizing water‐based NaCl as a benign ionic modifier, this approach exemplifies a circular and green pathway to improve energy harvesting performance while mitigating mask waste pollution. The developed NaCl‐enabled DC‐TENG offers a practical route toward sustainable, self‐powered wearable and communication systems aligned with global carbon‐neutral and SDG objectives.

title: A High‐Efficiency Concurrent‐Capability Tri‐Band Power Amplifier Based on T‐ and L‐Section Dual‐Band Transformers
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents a simple three‐frequency matching structure formed by cascading T‐ and L‐Section dual‐band transformers (DBT). The main principle is that the T‐ and L‐Section DBT achieves tri‐band operate by jointly matching at three target frequencies, and based on this matching network, an optimal impedance matching design for a tri‐band concurrent power amplifier (PA) was carried out to achieve better performance. To verify the feasibility of the inference, a tri‐band concurrent output PA operating at 2.1/3.35/4.65 GHz was designed and fabricated. The measurement results show that the maximum drain efficiency (DE) of the PA is 66%/64.3%/52.2%, respectively, and the corresponding maximum output power is 40.5/40.4/41.3 dBm at this time. For this PA, this paper completed a digital predistortion (DPD) test using a 10‐MHz bandwidth and a peak‐to‐average power ratio (PAPR) of 7 dB for long‐term evolution (LTE) signals. The adjacent channel power ratio (ACPR) is −47.2/−45.8/−46.3 dBc, respectively.

Theorizing Cross‐Boundary Strategizing as Situated in Multilayered Supply Chains: A Strategy‐as‐Practice Approach to Supply Chain Management
abstract: ABSTRACT Supply chain strategy is increasingly recognized as a multilayered phenomenon, with firms strategizing not only within their own boundaries but across supply chain tiers, jurisdictions, and wider regulatory and ecological systems. Yet most existing supply chain management research tends to treat these tiers, jurisdictions, and systems as contexts for strategizing rather than as something strategizing helps to constitute, leaving the cross‐boundary character undertheorized. This article introduces the strategy‐as‐practice (SAP) lens as an epistemic tool for theorizing cross‐boundary strategizing in multilayered supply chains. Drawing on SAP's tripartite framework of practices, practitioners, and praxis (three Ps), we show that strategizing is inherently cross‐boundary, both implicitly through the knowledge practitioners draw on beyond their organization and explicitly through direct interaction with counterparts in other firms and institutions. We introduce three approaches SAP scholars use to conceptualize the complex systems within which strategizing is situated: a “tall” ontology separating intraorganizational from extraorganizational practice, a “flat” ontology treating strategizing as a web of practices stretching sideways, and a zoom‐in/zoom‐out approach tracing connectivity and identifying consequentiality across layers. abstract: هدف البحث إلى التعرف على أثر استخدام استراتيجية المناظرة التعليمية في تنمية مهارات التفكير الناقد وتعزيز الهوية الوطنية لدى طالبات الصف الثاني المتوسط في مادة التاريخ. ولتحقيق هذا الهدف اعتمدت الباحثة المنهج التجريبي باستخدام تصميم المجموعتين المتكافئتين (التجريبية والضابطة) ذي الاختبارين القبلي والبعدي. تكوَّنت عينة البحث من (64) طالبة من طالبات الصف الثاني المتوسط في متوسطه الامين للبنات التابعة إلى المديرية العامة لتربية الكرخ الأولى في محافظة بغداد للعام الدراسي (2026–2027)، بواقع (32) طالبة في المجموعة التجريبية و(32) طالبة في المجموعة الضابطة درست المجموعة التجريبية مادة التاريخ وفق استراتيجية المناظرة التعليمية، في حين درست المجموعة الضابطة بالطريقة الاعتيادية طوال مدة التجربة. ولتحقيق أهداف البحث أعدت الباحثة اختبارًا لقياس مهارات التفكير الناقد مكونًا من (30) فقرة، كما أعد مقياسًا للهوية الوطنية مكونًا من (30) فقرة، وقد تحقق من صدقهما وثباتهما وتوافرت لهما الخصائص السيكومترية المناسبة. واستُخدمت مجموعة من الوسائل الإحصائية، تمثلت في الاختبار التائي (t-test) لعينتين مستقلتين ولعينتين مترابطتين، ومعامل ألفا كرونباخ، ومعامل ارتباط بيرسون، واختبار مربع كاي، ومعاملات الصعوبة والتمييز أظهرت نتائج البحث وجود فروق ذات دلالة إحصائية عند مستوى دلالة (0.05) بين متوسط درجات طالبات المجموعتين في اختبار التفكير الناقد البعدي لصالح المجموعة التجريبية، كما كشفت النتائج عن وجود فروق ذات دلالة إحصائية في مقياس الهوية الوطنية البعدي لصالح المجموعة التجريبية، مما يؤكد فاعلية استراتيجية ال…

title: Priorities for School Infrastructure Investment in the Face of Uncertainty: An Intuitionistic Fuzzy Multi-Criteria Decision-Making Method Employing the Frank Weighted Averaging Operator
abstract: There is a need for a framework of decisions that is able to deal with the uncertainty and subjective nature of expert judgment as well as limited public funds. This paper presents an integrated multi-criteria decision-making approach using Intuitionistic Fuzzy Numbers and the Frank Weighted Averaging operator to prioritize school classroom building projects under a fixed capital budget. Four criteria—safety urgency, number of students affected, cost, and education impact—are measured by an IFN to reflect the membership, non-membership, and hesitancy built into expert assessments, and four candidate schools are assessed against these four criteria. The aggregation of the criteria into one fuzzy score for each alternative is done using a fuzzy operator, IFN-FWA, which is then converted to a crisp matrix using a score function. The obtained matrix is then assessed with five different MCDM methods (TOPSIS, WASPAS, VIKOR, MOORA, and CRITIC) to check the robustness of the ranking. The objective criterion weights are not subjectively assigned but are calculated with the CRITIC method, which will decrease subjectivity in the final recommendation. Although the mathematics involved in each method is different, the results consistently show that the top-ranked school is School4, followed by School2, School1, and School3, with a high level of agreement. The results validate that using the…

title: Behavioral approach to managing strategic transformations under conditions of uncertainty
abstract: The article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations for applying a behavioral approach to managing strategic transformations in business organizations under conditions of uncertainty. It shows that the effectiveness of strategic change depends not only on the quality of formal strategy and resource provision, but also on employees’ and managers’ behavioral reactions shaped by bounded rationality, cognitive biases, emotional states, trust, group norms, and corporate culture. The study systematizes the behavioral factors influencing managerial decision-making during transformation and identifies their consequences for the speed of adaptation, the quality of strategic choice, and employees’ acceptance of change. The study generalizes leadership mechanisms that support transformation, including emotionally competent interaction, transformational influence, trust building, and employee involvement. The study identifies the main organizational and psychological threats: resistance to change, cognitive traps, psycho-emotional exhaustion, crisis of trust, group disorganization, and value dissonance; it also proposes directions for diagnosing them. The study develops a conceptual architecture for the behavioral management of strategic transformations, integrating behavioral determinants, leadership mechanisms, zones of organizational vulnerability, team readiness assessm…

title: Facts or Feelings? How Virtual Streamers Reduce Consumer Uncertainty Across Product Types
abstract: ABSTRACT Advances in artificial intelligence have accelerated the adoption of virtual streamers in live‐streaming e‐commerce. Yet the effectiveness of emotional language used by virtual streamers remains unclear in existing research. Drawing on signaling theory and a consumer‐uncertainty perspective, this study examines how virtual streamers' language styles (informational vs. emotional) interact with product types (search vs. experience) to influence consumers' purchase intention, and how this interaction effect is moderated by live‐streaming room activity. This study conducts three scenario‐based experiments. Three experiments were designed to progressively examine the proposed hypotheses. The results reveal a clear matching effect between virtual streamers' language styles and product types. When promoting search products, the use of informational language helps reduce consumers' perceived uncertainty about the product, which in turn increases purchase intention. In contrast, when promoting experience products, emotional language is more effective because it decreases consumers' uncertainty toward the virtual streamer, ultimately generating higher purchase intention. Moreover, live‐streaming room activity serves as an important boundary condition that moderates this interaction effect. Specifically, this interaction effect will further strengthen under high‐activity levels, …
