From Policy Transmission To Business Adaptation: A Dual-Perspective PLS-SEM Analysis of Post-COVID Monetary Policy Effectiveness in India
abstract: Purpose – Monetary policy effectiveness in emerging economies depends less on the design of instruments than on how efficiently policy signals travel through financial intermediaries to economic agents. This study examines post-COVID monetary policy effectiveness in India through a dual-perspective framework capturing the supply side (banks) and the demand side (Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, MSMEs) of transmission simultaneously. Design/methodology/approach – Adopting a positivist, deductive, cross-sectional design, primary data were collected from 175 banking professionals and 159 MSME owner-managers in India using a structured five-point Likert instrument. Two structural models were estimated by Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) with 5,000 bootstrap resamples: the banker model links Policy Alignment (PA) to Banking Operational Resilience (BOR) through Transmission Efficiency (TE), and the MSME model links Policy Support (PS) to Adaptive Business Behaviour (ABB) through Credit Accessibility (CA). Findings – Policy Alignment drives Transmission Efficiency (β = 0.574), which strengthens Banking Operational Resilience (β = 0.475), with TE partially mediating PA–BOR (VAF ≈ 61%). Policy Support improves Credit Accessibility (β = 0.734), which enhances Adaptive Business Behaviour (β = 0.562), with CA partially mediating PS–ABB (VAF ≈ 63%). All eigh…

title: Cascading propagation of financial and resource imbalances in a construction project portfolio: transmission mechanisms and economic consequences for the enterprise
abstract: The article develops a network-based approach to analyzing cascading financial and resource imbalances in a construction project portfolio. The purpose is to formalize how a local shortage of liquidity or a critical resource is transmitted through inter-project dependencies, generates secondary deficits, and becomes an enterprise-level economic loss. The methodology combines systems analysis, network logic, structural decomposition, threshold diagnostics, and scenario modeling. The portfolio is represented as a network of interdependent projects competing for liquidity, credit limits, labour, equipment, materials, supplier capacity, and time buffers. Five transmission channels are identified: liquidity, resource, procurement and logistics, temporal, and financial and credit. The study introduces a transmission coefficient, project buffer capacity, a threshold condition for transition from a local imbalance to a secondary deficit, and a cascade load index that distinguishes shock absorption, transmission without substantial amplification, and portfolio-wide multiplication. Economic consequences are structured at project, portfolio, and enterprise levels and include direct additional costs, delay costs, financing costs, idle-capacity losses, and opportunity losses from postponed or canceled projects. The scientific novelty lies in integrating financial and resource imbalances int…

title: Lumbar Spinal Stenosis and Financial Hardship: A Patient-Centered Analysis from A Middle-Income Country
abstract: Objective: To evaluate the economic burden of Lumbar Spinal Stenosis (LSS) and to identify the contributing factors. Methodology: This Cross-sectional Study was conducted in the Department of Neurosurgery, MMC/BKMC Mardan, from January to June 2025. We recruited a consecutive sample of 100 adult patients diagnosed with radiologically and clinically proven lumbar spinal stenosis. We used a questionnaire to collect data on demographics, family income, treatment cost, transport cost, income loss, treatment delay, and self-reported financial hardship. We categorized financial hardship as mild (<25% of monthly household income), moderate (25–50%), and severe (>50%). Results: Among 100 patients, 58% were male and 42% female, with a mean age of 56.8 ± 11.4 years. Forty-seven percent of participants reported severe financial hardship, 32% moderate hardship, and 21% mild hardship. Patients with severe stenosis incurred significantly higher treatment costs than those with mild-to-moderate disease (PKR 68,500 ± 18,200 vs. PKR 39,700 ± 14,600; p = 0.002). Severe hardship was more common among unemployed/daily wage earners (63.4% vs. 28.7%; p = 0.001), rural residents (p = 0.004), and surgically managed patients (74.2% vs. 39.5%; p < 0.001). Household income inversely correlated with financial toxicity (r = –0.48, p < 0.001). Conclusion: Financial hardship is prevalent among patients with L…

title: The Effect of Accounting Understanding, Accounting System Utilization, Internal Audit, and Internal Control System on The Quality of Hospital Financial Statements: A Study at PT XYZ
abstract: This study investigates the impact of accounting comprehension, the accounting systems utilization, internal audit, and internal control systems on the quality of financial statements at PT XYZ, a state-owned enterprise managing four hospitals and five clinics in East Java. A quantitative research design with an associative approach was employed, with purposive sampling to select respondents. The final samples comprised 35 respondents consisting of accounting and finance staff directly involved in preparing financial statements. Data were collected using questionnaires and analyzed through multiple linear regression. The findings simultaneously indicate that the four independent variables significantly affect the quality of financial statements, with a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.845. Thus, 84.5% of the variation in financial statement quality can be explained by the research model. Partially, accounting comprehension and the accounting systems utilization exert positive but insignificant effects. While internal audit and internal control systems have positive and significant effects, with internal control systems being the most dominant variable. These results underscore that the reliability of hospital financial reporting is more strongly determined by the effectiveness of organizational control and oversight mechanisms than by individual competence alone. title: SOP Standardization as a Governance Instrument: Strengthening Governance and Sharia Compliance in Islamic Financial Institutions
abstract: This study examines Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) standardization as a governance instrument for strengthening Good Corporate Governance (GCG) and Sharia compliance in Islamic Financial Institutions (IFIs). Using a qualitative descriptive-normative literature review, data were drawn from 28 sources (2014–2026) and analyzed through a thematic coding framework, grounded in Agency, Stewardship, and Stakeholder Theory. A comparative case analysis contrasting the procedural breakdown at PT BPRS GP Medan with digitalized SOP practices at Bank Syariah Indonesia and KSPPS Nuri Jatim shows that rigid, automated SOP enforcement rather than manual, discretionary procedures is decisive in preventing Sharia agency fraud. Benchmarking against AAOIFI, IFSB, and Bank Negara Malaysia standards further reveals that Indonesia's predominantly ex-post supervisory model could be strengthened by a more proactive, line-management-based three-lines-of-defense framework. Findings indicate that SOP standardization enhances transparency, accountability, internal control, and Sharia compliance, functioning most effectively when systematically enforced and resistant to manual override. This study offers actionable implications for OJK, IFI management, and the Sharia Supervisory Board (DPS), while acknowledging its reliance on secondary, documentary case evidence rather than primary empirical data.

abstract: Introduction: Maternity leave is an essential component of legal protection for female workers because it concerns reproductive protection, employment continuity, and non-discrimination in employment relations. Although Indonesia has established a legal framework governing maternity leave, a gap remains between statutory protection and its practical implementation.Purposes of the Research: This study aims to examine the legal regulation of maternity leave for female workers in Indonesia and identify the principal barriers to its implementation and enforcement.Methods of the Research: This study employs normative legal research using statutory and conceptual approaches. Primary and secondary legal materials are analyzed qualitatively, while previous studies and policy reports are used as supporting evidence to examine implementation-related problems.Results Main Findings of the Research: The study finds that Indonesian law provides a normative basis for maternity leave and protection against discriminatory treatment of female workers. However, its effectiveness is constrained by weak labour-law enforcement and supervision, limited complaint mechanisms, workplace pressure, gender-based stigma, and the weak bargaining position of female workers. title: Frontex Accountability and Fundamental Rights: Legal Remedies and Institutional Reform in the European Union
abstract: The European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex) has become central to the management of the external borders of the European Union because of its increasingly operational capabilities. The broadening of its remit to improve border security and border management is intended to strengthen security and the control of migration, but it has raised concerns about respect for fundamental rights. This paper explores how far Frontex can be held legally liable for breaches of fundamental rights resulting from its activities. It examines the judicial and institutional procedures for holding Frontex accountable and reviews the current accountability framework. The study follows a doctrinal legal approach grounded in EU primary and secondary law, case law, institutional documents, scholarly work and human-rights reports. The paper finds that significant accountability challenges remain, given the distribution of responsibility between Frontex and the Member States, problems of attribution and causation, the limited availability of judicial remedies and the limited capacity of internal and external oversight mechanisms to secure compliance. The recent case law of the Court of Justice of the European Union on the non-contractual liability of Frontex is discussed in particular. The paper concludes with recommendations for legal and institutional reform to improve EU border management, foc…

title: A Hybrid Model‐Data‐Driven Scheduling Strategy for Vehicle‐to‐Grid Interaction Based on Virtual Power Plant Coordination
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) have experienced vigorous development in recent years. However, their large‐scale integration into the power grid presents challenges related to the ‘curse of dimensionality’ and uncertainties, making it difficult to balance rapid grid demand response with the interests of EV users. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a hybrid model‐data‐driven scheduling strategy for vehicle‐to‐grid (V2G) interactions based on virtual power plant (VPP) coordination. It adopts a sequential model‐based aggregated charging scheduling and data‐driven power division mechanism to mitigate dimensionality and uncertainty problems. Furthermore, the data‐driven division strategy is implemented in two stages: both the EV bidding process in Stage 1 and the VPP clearing process in Stage 2 are driven by a distributed deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework with high sample efficiency. This design not only achieves rapid response to setpoints but also fully accommodates the interests of EV owners. The correctness and effectiveness of the proposed strategy are verified through simulations on a modified IEEE 33‐bus system integrated with massive VPPs and EVs. © 2026 Institute of Electrical Engineers of Japan and Wiley Periodicals LLC.

title: Design and Fabrication of Automated Guided Vehicle
abstract: With the advancements of robotic technologies, the industrial environments are adopting more and more aspects of automation to enhance product quality and accuracy and to reduce product cost. One of these aspects is the use of Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV) which is gaining importance in industrial logistics and transportation systems. Automated Guided Vehicles are the essential parts of all automated factories.. No human intervention is required for its normal functioning during task-execution stage. In this paper, automated guided vehicle is interfaced with Programmable logic control, which is a new concept in the field of automation and replacement of traditional electro-mechanical control system. In steel plants, a lot of transporting is required inside the plant to help in production, such as, steel coils are transported from one location to another. For this purpose automated guided vehicle systems are very useful. Keywords— guided vehicle,AGV,line follower,smart trolley

title: Food supplement safety and market entry in Germany, Bulgaria, North Macedonia and China
abstract: Objective: To compare market entry controls for food supplements in Germany, Bulgaria, and North Macedonia with the health food framework of mainland China, and assess their relationship to scientific safety evaluation. Methods: A functional comparative legal review of legislation, judgments, and regulatory guidance was combined with a targeted medical literature review. Sources were checked through September 24, 2026. Vitamin B6, green tea extracts, and red yeast rice illustrate dose related toxicity and regulatory responses. Results: Germany uses notification, Bulgaria requires prior registration, and North Macedonia uses a compliance opinion followed by registration. China distinguishes registration involving assessment of safety, health function, and quality controllability from catalog-based filing supported by technical documentation. Chinese health foods and European food supplements are not identical legal categories. The examples demonstrate the importance of total exposure, preparation specific toxicity, and continued reassessment after market entry. An administrative status or regulatory dose ceiling cannot establish universal safety or therapeutic efficacy. Conclusion: Good practice combines transparent classification, proportionate evidence requirements, prominent warnings, controlled product changes, and post-market surveillance. title: Botulinum Neurotoxins in dermatology and interdisciplinary medicine: pharmacology, European regulation, clinical applications, and future directions
abstract: Background: Botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) has evolved from a cause of foodborne paralysis into a precisely dosed biologic used in aesthetic medicine and multiple therapeutic specialties. Objective: To review its pharmacology, European regulatory landscape, established clinical uses, emerging applications, immunogenicity, health economic concepts, and contemporary procedural epidemiology. Methods: A structured narrative review was updated through 24 September 2026. The original manuscript was used as the conceptual starting point; scientific claims were checked against PubMed indexed reviews and systematic reviews, regulatory claims against European Medicines Agency documents, and procedural statistics against the International Society of Aesthetic Plastic Surgery (ISAPS) Global Survey 2024. Results: BoNT inhibits neurotransmitter release through serotype-specific proteolysis of SNARE proteins. European products include both centrally and nationally authorised formulations, and their units are not interchangeable. Established uses include focal hyperhidrosis and several neurological and urological indications. Evidence for temporomandibular disorders, rosacea, scar modulation, chronic pruritus, and psychiatric applications is promising but heterogeneous and generally off-label or investigational. title: Clinical and patient reported improvement after metabolic optimization and autologous platelet based facial rejuvenation: a case report
abstract: Response to autologous platelet-based facial rejuvenation is variable, and patient related factors may contribute to this heterogeneity. In this paper is reported a caase of a patient with repeated poor response to previous platelet rich plasma (PRP) procedures which improved after correction of selected nutritional and metabolic abnormalities and subsequent multimodal platelet based treatment. A 61 year old postmenopausal woman, smoker, with arterial hypertension and a history of breast cancer, had undergone five PRP procedures and several chemical peels without satisfactory benefit. Examination showed xerotic, atrophic, photoaged facial skin with solar elastosis, dermal laxity and rhytides. Laboratory assessment revealed borderline thrombocytopenia, low ferritin, vitamin D, vitamin B12, zinc and albumin, with elevated thyroid-stimulating hormone and C-reactive protein. After six weeks of supportive correction, two sessions combining injectable platelet rich fibrin, PRP, microneedling and albumin PRF were performed. At three months, clinical improvement was accompanied by FACE-Q score increases for Satisfaction with Skin (42–81), Satisfaction with Facial Appearance (48–79), Psychological Function (55–76) and Social Function (68–80). Clinical and patient reported improvement followed correction of identified abnormalities and multimodal autologous platelet treatment. Because se…

title: Penerapan Model Transformers untuk Analisis Sentimen pada Survei Tahunan di Aplikasi Market Visit pada PT ASDFE
abstract: PT ASDFE menggunakan survei tahunan untuk mengevaluasi kinerja perusahaan berdasarkan masukan dari mitracabang dan distributor. Seiring dengan peningkatan jumlah responden survei tahunan dari berdampak padalamanya proses analisis data survei tahunan secara manual. volume data yang terus bertambah berdampak waktuyang dibutuhkan untuk mengekstrak opini dan mengevaluasi kinerja perusahaan menjadi tidak efisien. Penelitianini mengembangkan sistem analisis sentimen otomatis berbasis web menggunakan model Transformer, denganmemanfaatkan model pra-latih IndoBERT untuk data berbahasa Indonesia dan RoBERTa untuk data berbahasaInggris. Dataset yang digunakan berasal dari survei tahun 2021–2023 yang telah diberi label untuk proses fine-tuning pada masing-masing model. Evaluasi model dilakukan menggunakan metrik AUC-ROC dengan hasil 0,99untuk IndoBERT dan 1,00 untuk RoBERTa menggunakan 10% dari total dataset, serta pengujian User AcceptanceTest (UAT). Hasil implementasi menunjukkan bahwa sistem mampu mengurangi waktu analisis dari 360 menitmenjadi 35 menit dan mencapai tingkat kepuasan pengguna sebesar 98%. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa modelTransformer efektif dalam mengotomatisasi analisis sentimen dengan tingkat akurasi yang tinggi.

title: Evaluating Virtual Reality Tourism from Tourism Businesses’ Perspectives: Evidence from an Emerging Market and Implications for Strategic Adoption
abstract: Abstract Virtual reality (VR) tourism has emerged as a promising digital innovation capable of transforming tourism experiences and business practices. However, limited empirical research has examined how tourism enterprises evaluate the opportunities and constraints of this technology, particularly in emerging tourism markets. This study investigates tourism businesses’ perceptions of virtual reality tourism in Ho Chi Minh City and proposes a strategic framework for its practical application. A mixed-method approach was employed, combining a questionnaire survey of 260 tourism enterprise representatives with fifteen in-depth interviews with senior managers. The findings indicate that tourism businesses recognize several advantages of VR tourism, including its ability to expand tourism accessibility, enhance destination marketing, and support sustainable tourism by reducing environmental pressure on destinations. At the same time, enterprises identify significant limitations, such as the lack of sensory authenticity, limited social interaction, high technological investment costs, rapid technological obsolescence, and shortages of specialized human resources. Based on these findings, the study proposes a strategic application framework that positions VR tourism as a complementary tool supporting marketing innovation, inclusive tourism development, heritage interpretation, and s…

Organizing Livestock Markets in Kenya's Drylands: Evolution, Institutional Arrangements, Business Models and a Framework for Sustainable Market Coordination
abstract: Abstract: Livestock production is central to the livelihoods and economies of pastoral and agro-pastoral communities in Kenya’s drylands, yet its commercial potential is constrained by fragmented production and marketing systems, weak institutional coordination, inadequate infrastructure, information asymmetries, insecurity, climatic shocks and unequal bargaining power. This study examined the evolution, institutional arrangements and business models underpinning livestock-market organization in Kenya’s drylands and developed a framework for sustainable market coordination. A qualitative-dominant multiple-case study design was employed, focusing on four models: the Organized Livestock Marketing Model, Livestock Marketing Associations (LMAs) and Co-management Model, Meat and Livestock Assembly Model, and Livestock Market-Yard Management Model. Turkana County constituted the principal empirical case, supplemented by evidence from Marsabit, Isiolo, Samburu, Baringo and Tana River. Data were collected through 45 semi-structured key-informant interviews, 10 focus group discussions, documentary review and direct market observation, and analyzed using thematic, historical, within-case and cross-case approaches. Findings show that the four models represent complementary dimensions of livestock-market development. The Organized Livestock Marketing Model provides market architecture by c…

title: Capital Market Opening-up and High-Quality Innovation of Enterprises
abstract: At present, China’s innovation field is facing the structural dilemma of quantity priority and insufficient quality. In the critical window period when the economy turns to high-quality development, the improvement of enterprise innovation level has become an important issue. Based on the quasi-natural experimental scenario of capital market opening, this paper constructs a multi-period difference-in-differences model to test the effect of capital market opening on the quality of enterprise innovation. Both theoretical deduction and empirical test show that capital market opening helps to improve the quality of enterprise innovation, and this effect is more significant in state-owned enterprises and enterprises with overseas business income. From the perspective of mechanism, on the one hand, the opening of capital market promotes the improvement of innovation quality by improving corporate governance and alleviating financing bottlenecks ; on the other hand, due to the increase of stock liquidity, the quality of innovation is suppressed. Overall, the positive effect is dominant. This paper not only expands the theoretical analysis of the relationship between capital market opening and enterprise innovation, but also provides a useful reference for policy practice.

abstract: Abstract The Pediatric Glittre Activities of Daily Living Test (TGlittre-P) is a field test designed to assess the functional performance of activities of daily living (ADL) in pediatric patients with cystic fibrosis (CF). However, the effects of TGlittre-P on heart rate response and the clinical determinants of test performance in this population remain insufficiently understood. To compare the heart rate response elicited by the TGlittre-P and the six-minute walk test (6MWT), and to identify pulmonary and extrapulmonary factors associated with TGlittre-P performance in pediatric patients with CF. Fifty-four pediatric patients with CF (mean age = 14.46 ± 2.16 years, 31 females and 23 males) were included in this cross-sectional study. ADL performance was assessed using the TGlittre-P, and functional capacity was assessed using the 6MWT. Pulmonary function, including forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV₁) and forced vital capacity (FVC), maximal inspiratory and expiratory pressure (MIP and MEP, respectively), handgrip strength (HGS %) and quadriceps muscle strength (QMS %) were measured. A multiple linear regression analysis model was used to determine independent predictors of TGlittre-P performance. The mean TGlittre-P duration was 2.00 ± 0.53 min. title: Response to Global Refugee Crisis: In Search of Best Practices for the States
abstract: The global refugee crisis has become a critical concern in international law. Despite the presence of an international refugee law regime, the refugee hosting countries have resorted to different approaches in responding to the issue. In most cases, responding countries take a defensive approach towards the refugees, and the international refugee law regime itself is not enough to ensure their protection due to its weak enforcement mechanism. However, there are some exceptions. Some countries have set benchmarks in responding to the refugee crises by going beyond their legal obligations. This paper has analyzed the international legal framework on refugee protection, explored the responses by Germany, Turkey, Uganda, and Columbia, and attempted to identify their good practices that can be role models for other refugee hosting states. While comparing the approaches of the four states, the study found that, inter alia, the economic condition of a refugee hosting country is not a barrier to ensuring the rights of the refugees, the conventional humanitarian approach is evolving into an integration strategy, and the willingness of the hosting state is more significant than its legal obligation. Based on the findings, the paper has made recommendations that can be guidelines for the refugee hosting states in responding to the refugee crisis.

title: Evaluation of the non-specific effects of a two-dose BCG vaccination scheme on immune response and milk production in dairy cows
abstract: Abstract Bovine tuberculosis (bTB) is a chronic disease primarily caused by Mycobacterium bovis , a zoonotic pathogen with worldwide distribution that causes economic losses in milk and meat production systems. In dairy cattle from central Chile, disease prevalence remains high, and the national control and eradication program has faced the reluctance of producers to implement the test-and-slaughter strategy due to the lack of compensation. Within this epidemiological context, vaccination with the M. bovis Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) strain has proven to be a useful tool for disease prevention and control and has shown non-specific effects in humans and animals. The objective of this study was to assess non-specific immunological responses of peripheral blood monocytes and the impact on dairy production traits following vaccination with the BCG Russia strain administered in a two-dose scheme, in a commercial dairy farm with a free bTB status. A total of 198 12-month-old heifers were vaccinated via the subcutaneous route with the equivalent of 1 human dose of BCG. Ninety-six of them were revaccinated with a similar dose during first 30 d of their lactation period. In addition, 39 control animals were not vaccinated and received saline. Pro-inflammatory cytokine responses to ex-vivo homologous (PPD-B) and heterologous (LPS) stimulation was evaluated in peripheral CD14 + monocy…

Using Limestone to Assess the Impacts of Passivation and Ca-Silicate Formation on Lime Carbonation Efficiency for Looping Technology
abstract: Abstract Maximizing process efficiency in the lime looping process for direct air capture (DAC) is essential for reducing costs and energy demands to scale up this carbon dioxide (CO2) removal (CDR) technology. Here, we investigated two inefficiencies in the lime looping process: (i) surface passivation in relation to the particle size of the initial limestone powder and (ii) the presence of silicate impurities and their thermal reaction with CaCO3 during calcination. Passivation-limited carbonation to <68% completion for coarser (>25 μm) lime particles compared to ∼88% for finer (<25 μm) particles, emphasizing the need to pulverize limestone to very fine particle sizes to optimize efficiency. Limestones naturally contain unreactive impurities that will reduce CDR efficiency. For instance, the presence of 7.5 wt.% non-carbonates in the limestone used in this study reduced CO2 capture efficiency by an equal percentage. Additionally, formation of relatively inert Ca-silicates from the reaction of silicates (primarily quartz) with CaO during calcination (900 °C) further reduced efficiency by lowering CaO availability and potentially passivating reactive surfaces. Carbonation of very high-purity limestone (55.6 wt.% CaO) and synthetic CaCO3 (56.01 wt.% CaO) yielded greater reaction extents of ∼93 and ∼98%, respectively, compared to that of limestones with varying SiO2 cont…

The Effects of Recruitment, Selection, and Job Placement on Ship Crew Performance at PT Pelayaran Guntur Line
abstract: This study investigates the effects of recruitment, selection, and job placement on ship crew performance at PT Pelayaran Guntur Line. The research was prompted by increases in minor incidents, safety nonconformities, and suboptimal performance evaluations between 2023 and 2025. An associative quantitative design was applied to 100 active crew members selected through convenience sampling from a population of 133. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed with partial least squares structural equation modeling in SmartPLS 4. Recruitment had a significant positive effect on performance (β = 0.269; p = 0.009), whereas selection had no statistically significant effect (β = −0.230; p = 0.062). Job placement produced the strongest positive effect (β = 0.889; p < 0.001). The final model explained 79.6% of the variance in crew performance. These findings indicate that candidate information obtained during recruitment and selection should be integrated into competency-based placement decisions and systematic post-assignment evaluations

title: The Impact of Digital Transformation on Improving the Performance of Contemporary Political Systems: An Analytical Study in Governance and Decision-Making
abstract: Government digital transformation is an ever-expanding part of modern governance. Governments increasingly implement digital platforms, big-data analytics, artificial intelligence, cloud computing, digital identity systems and integrated information infrastructures. These developments can affect the delivery of public services as well as institutional coordination, citizen–government interaction, policy formulation and decision-making. This paper explores how digital transformation affects the performance of contemporary political systems, particularly in governance and governmental decision-making. It examines the potential of digital technologies to enhance administrative efficiency, institutional responsiveness, transparency, accountability, citizen engagement and evidence-based policy-making, together with the problems of cybersecurity, privacy, digital exclusion, algorithmic bias, institutional capacity and over-reliance on technology. The study is qualitative and analytical: it reviews and synthesizes the academic literature and the reports of international organizations. Digital transformation is not simply the conversion of traditional administrative procedures into electronic processes; it is institutional change in its own right. Current studies suggest that it requires organizational transformation, sound data governance, interoperability, an adequate legal framework…

title: HIP OSTEOARTHRITIS IN PRIMARY HEALTH CARE: CONSERVATIVE MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES, CURRENT EVIDENCE, AND CHALLENGES IN CHILE
abstract: Introduction: Hip osteoarthritis is a common degenerative disease that can cause pain, functional limitation, and deterioration in quality of life. Primary Health Care plays a fundamental role in its initial diagnosis, conservative treatment, and follow-up. Objective: To review the current evidence on the main conservative management strategies for hip osteoarthritis in Primary Health Care and to analyze the main challenges associated with their implementation in the Chilean context. Methodology: A narrative review of the literature was conducted through searches in PubMed/MEDLINE and SciELO, complemented by official documents from the Chilean Ministry of Health. Systematic reviews, meta-analyses, clinical trials, and relevant studies addressing diagnosis, therapeutic exercise, education, weight control, pharmacological treatment, injections, and the organization of primary care were prioritized. Results: The evidence supports a multimodal management approach based primarily on therapeutic exercise, self-management education, and modification of risk factors, including weight control when appropriate. Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs may contribute to symptomatic control in selected patients, while intra-articular corticosteroid injections may provide short-term relief. In Chile, the integration of rehabilitation services into Primary Health Care represents a relevant strat…

The need for sustainable and high-quality information transfer must have an appropriate level of attention to its tools in order to ensure the effectiveness of all necessary processes. Digital means of communication are able to reach their potential precisely in this environment, since their prerogative is effective communication between subjects. It is necessary to understand how important it is for citizens to be able to quickly and easily communicate their public opinion, file a complaint or a proposal, and solve their widespread problems without making lengthy entries to the necessary government structure. And civil servants will find out about them faster and respond promptly. In recent years, there has been relatively intensive scientific work in the field of thesis defense on the topic of political and network communications. However, it should be recognized that most of them explore the Internet either from the point of view of sociology, psychology, journalism, or are related to other areas of political communication theory. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa proses retur penjualan didukung oleh prosedur administrasi dan dokumentasi yang melibatkan beberapa fungsi internal perusahaan. title: Overtourism governance and resident wellbeing. A social exchange framework for understanding community support under visitor management measures
abstract: Overtourism has moved destination scholarship from the description of visitor pressure to the design of measures that contain it. Caps, timed entry, tourist taxes, short-term rental controls, cruise berth limits and dispersal schemes are now common, yet the field still explains community reactions with a model built for a different question. Social exchange theory has long framed resident support as a judgement about the benefits and costs of tourism itself. This article argues that visitor management changes the object of that judgement. Once an authority intervenes, residents evaluate two linked exchanges, one with visitors and the tourism economy, and one with the body that governs it. The article develops a dual-exchange framework in which the governance relation has its own currencies, its own fairness criteria and its own temporal profile, and in which resident wellbeing is the medium through which both exchanges are experienced. Fourteen propositions specify how anticipated and experienced justice, institutional trust, dependence and the internal incidence of regulatory costs shape support for measures and for tourism. A typology classifies instruments by whose behaviour they restrict and where their costs fall inside the host community, and it is used to argue that effectiveness and diffuseness of cost may trade off against one another. AI-MEDIATED PLATFORM WORK: MEANINGFULNESS UNDER ALGORITHMIC MANAGEMENT
abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly mediates how platform work is matched, monitored, evaluated and performed. This conceptual paper develops a meaningfulness-based framework for AI-mediated platform work. Gig and platform work provide the bounded empirical setting because automated coordination, opaque evaluation, fluctuating demand, dependence on ratings and limited possibilities for contestation make the relevant tensions especially visible. The scientific problem is the under-specification of how co-occurring substitution and augmentation within a task bundle interact with platform-level control and governance to shape the significance workers attribute to a focal work episode. The purpose is to specify that relationship. The object isthe AI-mediated platform-work episode, operationalized through itstask bundle; the subject isthe relationship among task-level AI effects, platform-level control and governance, meaningfulness pathways and worker context. Drawing on theory synthesis and abductive model development, the article integrates research on gig work, algorithmic management, task-based labour economics and meaningful work. Contextual evidence from the OECD, the European Union and the World Bank establishes the scale and relevance of the setting but does not test the proposed relationships. Substitution and augmentation are treated as non-exclusive task-level effects, …

title: Design of an IoT-Based Waste Management System for Biogas Production as a Renewable Energy Source
abstract: The increasing volume of organic waste presents serious environmental challenges while the demand for renewable energy continues to rise. This study proposes the design and implementation of an Internet of Things (IoT)-based smart biodigester system for converting organic waste into biogas as a renewable energy source. The system integrates an ESP32 microcontroller with DHT22 temperature, MPX5700 pressure, and MQ-4 methane gas sensors for real-time monitoring of fermentation parameters. A K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) regression algorithm is embedded to predict methane pressure and enable automated system control. Experimental results indicate that the optimal model configuration at k = 4 achieved a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.18 and a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.21, demonstrating high predictive accuracy. The developed prototype improves methane production stability and enhances overall energy conversion efficiency. This research contributes to sustainable organic waste management and decentralized renewable energy systems.

title: Development and validation of objective performance metrics for robot-assisted basic surgical skills in a simulated anastomosis task using a single-port robotic system
abstract: Abstract Introduction The chicken anastomosis task is a widely adopted model for training robotic suturing and knot-tying. Aim of this study was to develop and validate objective performance metrics for this task on the Single-Port (SP) robotic platform and to establish a proficiency benchmark for training and assessment. Methods Seven experts in robotic surgery training and Proficiency Based Progression (PBP) developed the metrics for the SP chicken anastomosis task. The proposed metrics were refined among a panel of n = 14 participants with significant experience in PBP and/or robotics and/or the SP system, through a modified Delphi process. Construct validity was assessed by comparing recorded performances of n = 12 expert ( ≥100 SP RARPs) and n = 12 novice surgeons, blindly scored by two reviewers. Proficiency benchmarks were established based on performance distribution. Results Delphi consensus achieved 100% agreement on the proposed performance metrics ( n = 5 steps, n = 20 errors, n = 1 failure to progress and n = 4 critical errors [CE]). abstract: The green transformation promoted by the European Union (EU) affects not only infrastructure, but also managerial work organization decisions. By 2050, the EU has set a goal to decarbonize the environment and use only clean technologies for energy production. Changing legal regulations encourage investment development, which affects the work of both business entities and other organizations. The need for management skills and the change of competencies is becoming one of the most serious challenges in implementing important infrastructure projects. When it comes to the municipal energy production sector, not only the need to evaluate investment decisions, but also aspects of ensuring security of supply are highlighted. The article presents an example of the transformation of the municipal heating sector at the municipal level in Lithuania, while emphasizing the need for management changes. The possibilities of replacing worn-out heat production infrastructure are assessed, considering the goals set by the EU. Both traditional investment payback methods and innovative approaches, such as Response Surface Methodology, were employed for this purpose. The research conducted in the article showed that investments in new-generation infrastructure are inseparable from a comprehensive assessment, taking into account the future prospects of the region. PROJECT INTEGRATION GOVERNANCE FOR MANAGING FRAGMENTATION IN HYBRID ENVIRONMENTS
abstract: Contemporary project environments increasingly combine specialized digital platforms, decentralized teams, hybrid project-management methods and multi-level governance arrangements. Although such heterogeneity can strengthen flexibility and local adaptation, it also increases the need for integration. Existing project-management research examines complexity, hybrid methodologies, information overload, knowledge transfer and governance, but these streams provide only a partial explanation of the cumulative coordination problem created when tools, information, methods, knowledge and decision rights are insufficiently connected. The purpose of this study is to conceptualize project management fragmentation (PMF) as a multidimensional integration problem and to propose a Project Integration Governance framework for limiting its dysfunctional effects while preserving useful flexibility. An exploratory qualitative expert survey was administered during April–May 2026. The analytical sample comprised 12 experienced projectmanagement professionals with 7–18 years of experience, predominantly from service-intensive sectors. Open-text responses were analyzed through deductive-inductive thematic coding and cross-case comparison. Five recurring dimensions of PMF were identified: tool and system fragmentation, data and information fragmentation, methodological fragmentation, knowledge fragme…

title: Social Commerce Risk Management for Business Sustainability: A Qualitative Study of Batik SMEs in Lampung, Indonesia
abstract: Batik SMEs in Lampung utilize social commerce to expand their markets and reach customers beyond the local region. However, the exposure of batik motifs and digital content creates risks to creative assets and brand identity. This study aims to identify the risks arising from social commerce use and analyze their management in supporting business sustainability. A qualitative approach was employed through in-depth interviews, digital observation, and documentation involving Batik SMEs that use social commerce for marketing and sales. Data were analyzed thematically to identify risk forms and management responses. The findings reveal three main risks: theft of batik motif ideas, imitation of batik motifs, and imitation of digital content. These risks challenge SMEs in maintaining product uniqueness and brand identity. Risk management strategies include continuous motif development, strengthening brand identity, using watermarks on digital content, monitoring digital activities, and developing new content concepts and designs. The findings indicate that social commerce risk management is not limited to preventing losses but also forms part of an adaptation and learning process to maintain competitiveness and support the sustainability of Batik SMEs.

abstract: At present, the invasive species red imported fire ants have become a major threat to local ecosystems and the daily lives of people in China. Long-term reliance on chemical control has led to the development of resistance in red imported fire ants, resulting in unsatisfactory control effectiveness. To address this issue, this paper, from a biomathematical perspective, for the first time introduces mathematical modeling into the population control of red imported fire ants. Predators are incorporated into the model and two different control strategies are adopted to reduce the risk of resistance development. Criteria for the existence and stability of predator-free periodic solutions are also established, followed by bifurcation and sensitivity analyses with respect to key parameters. Numerical simulations are finally presented to demonstrate the validity and practical effectiveness of the proposed control strategies. Theoretical and numerical results indicate that implementing two different control strategies reduces the likelihood of resistance development in red imported fire ants, and the introduction of predators makes the control strategies more long-term and effective. title: Combating Cyberbullying and Child Online Exploitation in Nigeria: Legal Strategies and Enforcement Realities
abstract: The rapid expansion of digital technologies and internet access has transformed communication, education, and social interaction globally. This digital revolution, however, has also exposed children to increasing risks of cyberbullying, online grooming, sextortion, child sexual abuse materials (CSAM), and other forms of technology-facilitated exploitation. In Nigeria, the growing number of young internet users, coupled with limited digital literacy and inadequate online safeguards, has heightened children's vulnerability to cyber-related harms. This paper examines the legal and institutional strategies adopted to combat cyberbullying and child online exploitation in Nigeria, with particular emphasis on enforcement realities. Using a doctrinal and comparative legal research methodology, the study analyzes relevant legal frameworks, including the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Act 2015, the Child Rights Act 2003, constitutional provisions, and data protection regulations. It further evaluates the roles of key enforcement institutions such as the Nigeria Police Force, the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, the Nigerian Communications Commission, and other agencies. The paper identifies significant enforcement challenges, including inadequate technical capacity, weak inter-agency coordination, low reporting rates, societal stigmatization of victims, judicial lim…

title: When Consumers Cross Borders: The Extraterritorial Limits of Article 9's Perfection Rules
abstract: Consumer credit has become mobile in ways that Article 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code did not anticipate. Article 9’s choice-of-law rules for perfecting a security interest assume that a debtor has one stable, easily identifiable location, ordinarily the debtor’s principal residence, an assumption that dual-resident, remote-working, and expatriate consumers do not always satisfy. This article examines how UCC §§ 9-301, 9-307, and 9-316 apply to cross-border consumer-credit transactions, such as auto-secured installment credit, against the backdrop of a buy-now-pay-later market that is growing quickly and moving toward longer-term installment structures, and identifies a doctrinal gap: because individual cross-border consumer disputes are too small in dollar value to justify litigation, the choice-of-law problems created by consumer mobility have been absorbed quietly as a cost of doing business rather than resolved through case law or statutory reform. Drawing on recent Federal Reserve research on buy-now-pay-later growth, a bankruptcy decision applying the petition-date freeze rule to a lapsed Article 9 financing statement, and New York’s rollout of the 2022 UCC amendments, the article argues that this gap will not stay latent as cross-border consumer lending scales. It concludes with practical compliance recommendations for lenders and counsel: treating a debtor’s location …

title: SEO as a tool for managing the company's digital presence
abstract: This article explores the role of search engine optimization (SEO) as a strategic management tool for a company's digital presence. Using a comparative analysis of industry data, it examines the dynamics of the global SEO software market and the bipolar structure of the Russian search market: Yandex relies on behavioral factors, while Google prioritizes content quality and reputation. This divergence requires Russian companies to pursue two coordinated, yet distinct, optimization strategies. The ROI of digital channels is analyzed: SEO delivers the highest long-term returns, although the payback period ranges from nine to sixteen months. The impact of AI Overviews blocks is also examined: their proliferation has led to a significant drop in organic click-through rates and has brought GEO (Generative Response Evaluation) to the forefront: a strategy aimed at reaching cited sources of generative responses. The results are intended for digital marketing and corporate management professionals.

title: Price and Physical Evidence on Consumer Decisions Regarding Damri Executive Class Bus Services
abstract: Purpose: This study examines whether price perceptions and physical evidence are associated with consumer decisions among users of DAMRI Executive Class bus services on the Pontianak-Sintang corridor. Research Method: A quantitative associative design used questionnaire data from 100 purposively selected users aged 17 years or older with direct experience of the service. Price, physical evidence, and consumer decisions were measured using five-point Likert scales and analyzed with instrument checks, descriptive statistics, multiple linear regression, partial tests, and a simultaneous model test. Results and Discussion: More favorable evaluations of price and physical evidence were each positively associated with consumer decisions, and the two predictors were jointly related to the outcome. Implications: The cross-sectional, single-corridor, purposive-sample design and two-predictor model limit generalization. The findings support managerial attention to fare-value alignment and consistent maintenance of cleanliness, comfort, vehicle condition, and supporting facilities. Originality: The study provides route-specific evidence on how monetary and tangible service attributes jointly relate to executive intercity bus choice.

Emotional Self-Regulation And Adaptive Coping As Psychological Resources In Law Enforcement Activity
abstract: Law enforcement activity requires officers to maintain effective professional functioning in situations characterised by uncertainty, interpersonal conflict, emotional pressure, responsibility and potential threat. These conditions make emotional self- regulation and adaptive coping important psychological resources for maintaining professional stability. The purpose of this paper is to analyse the role of emotional regulation and coping strategies in the psychological adaptation of law enforcement officers. Particular attention is paid to the ability to recognise and regulate emotional reactions, select adaptive responses to stressful situations, maintain cognitive control under pressure and recover psychological resources after demanding professional experiences.

Gut dysbiosis, blood pressure regulation, and cardiometabolic risk in polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS)
abstract: Abstract Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), formerly known as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is a common endocrine-metabolic disorder associated with increased hypertension and cardiometabolic risk. Gut dysbiosis is also frequently reported in affected women, raising the question of whether microbiome-linked pathways contribute to blood pressure elevation or vascular risk in this syndrome. To evaluate and synthesize the available evidence linking gut dysbiosis, gut microbial function, and microbiome-related mechanisms to hypertension, blood pressure regulation, and cardiovascular risk in women with PMOS, we conducted a narrative review of the literature in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and citation tracking. Search terms included PCOS, PMOS, gut microbiota, gut dysbiosis, hypertension, blood pressure, cardiovascular risk, microbial metabolites, bile acids, intestinal permeability, inflammation, renin-angiotensin signaling, renal sodium handling, and autonomic regulation. Human studies, animal models, interventional studies, and mechanistic investigations relevant to PMOS and hypertension were reviewed according to predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. Eligible publications were preclinical studies, human studies, English language, adult females, and peer-reviewed original or review articles. Clarifying whether gut dysbiosis contributes …

title: The nursing workforce crisis in Bulgaria: Workforce imbalance , educational capacity, and urgent health policy reform
abstract: Bulgaria faces a structural nursing workforce crisis that threatens the accessibility, safety, and continuity of health and social care. This review analyzes the scale and age structure of the nursing shortage, the imbalance between nurses and physicians, the educational pipeline, and policy options for rapid and sustainable workforce recovery. A structured narrative review and secondary analysis of official data from the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), Bulgarian National Statistical Institute, Ministry of Health, Sofia Municipality, European Union legislation, professional organizations, and peer-reviewed workforce studies were conducted, using information available through 24 September 2026. In 2025, Bulgaria had 28,357 practicing nurses and 30,409 physicians under a main employment contract, corresponding to only 0.93 nurses per physician. More than 76% of nurses were aged 45 years or older and 18.4% were aged 65 years or older. OECD data show 4.4 nurses per 1,000 population in Bulgaria versus 9.1 on average across OECD countries, while the nursing graduate rate was 7.6 per 100,000 population versus 45.7 across the OECD. Increasing university admission alone cannot correct the shortage within the necessary time horizon. abstract: Abstract The transition to a carbon–neutral electricity system depends on the widespread integration of distributed and inverter-based renewable resources. The U.S. Department of Energy and the North American Electric Reliability Corporation have identified these resources as increasing the grid's cybersecurity attack surface faster than current oversight can manage. Federal reviews have also found that guidance for assessing grid cybersecurity risk remains incomplete. In response, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission has introduced a mandatory internal network monitoring standard and, for the first time, a voluntary financial incentive for cybersecurity investment beyond compliance requirements. However, neither these measures nor the academic literature on security economics and infrastructure capital budgeting provides a clear method for allocating cybersecurity capital as distributed and renewable generation continues to expand. This paper develops a four-component investment appraisal framework that combines the compliance floor established by NERC's Critical Infrastructure Protection standards, the loss-based investment benchmark implied by the Gordon-Loeb model, the timing flexibility provided by real options analysis, and the rate-recovery incentive created by FERC Order No. 893. The Contrasting Roles of pH, Na+, and Ca2+ on Transport and Deposition of Colloidal Activated Carbon in Single and Mixed Na+-Ca2+ Systems in Saturated Porous Media
abstract: Abstract Colloidal activated carbon (CAC) barriers have been widely adopted for in situ groundwater remediation of legacy and emerging contaminants. The design and installation of CAC barriers require an understanding of CAC transport and deposition as a function of site geochemistry, particularly for coastal sites where spatial variations in salinities are high and CAC placement with or without in situ flocculation by CaCl2 may be complex. Our column study has explored this complexity over a wide range of salinities (0.1–0.7 M) and relevant CaCl2 concentrations (0.0125–0.23 M) by considering individual and combined effects of Na+ and Ca2+ at pH 3 and 7. For the first time, retention profiles (RPs) and SEM-EDX images of CAC retained on sand are presented alongside breakthrough curves (BTCs) to elucidate CAC transport and retention behaviors. abstract: Under the background of "double carbon" goal, green finance is an important institutional arrangement to promote green and low-carbon economic transformation. Based on China's provincial panel data from 2006 to 2023, this paper constructs a comprehensive evaluation index of green finance, and uses panel fixed effect model, mediating effect model and instrumental variable method to test the impact of green finance on regional carbon emission intensity. The results show that the development of green finance significantly reduces regional carbon emission intensity, and the conclusion is still valid after robustness test. Green finance reduces carbon emission intensity by increasing the output of green patents, and green innovation plays a complete intermediary role; Heterogeneity analysis shows that the promotion effect of green finance is more obvious in areas with low economic level and after the low-carbon policy node in 2015. This paper provides empirical evidence for improving the green finance policy system and promoting regional differentiated low-carbon development.

title: Administrative Leadership's Strategic Planning for AI Integration in Public Secondary Schools: A Qualitative Study in Kuala Lumpur
abstract: The aim of this qualitative study is to examine how administrative leaders in public secondary schools in Kuala Lumpur approach strategic planning for artificial intelligence (AI) integration in education. Three consolidated research objectives guided thc inquiry: (1 ) to explore administrators' understanding and strategic planning of AI integration, (2) to identify challenges and barriers in AI integration planning, and (3) to examine stakeholder engagement and leadership support required for successful AI integration. Through semi-structured interviews with ten experienced school administrators, including principals, senior assistants, and heads of departments, and employing reflexive thematic analysis, the study revealed five major themes: infrastructural and resource considerations, pedagogical transformation and teacher preparedness, ethical and equity concerns, stakeholder engagement strategies, and adaptive leadership approaches. Findings indicate that while administrators recognize AI' s transformative potential, strategic planning remains fragrnented, resource-constrained, and lacking systematic frameworks. The study underscores the critical need for multilevel support systems to ensure equitable and effective AI adoption in Malaysian secondary education. title: Energy-Efficient Optimal Control of a Hexarotor UAV Based on High-Order Fully Actuated Gust Disturbance Rejection
abstract: To address the challenge of simultaneously satisfying attitude stability constraints and achieving multi-motor energy efficiency optimization for a hexarotor UAV under complex low-altitude gust disturbances, this paper proposes a coordinated control method that integrates high-order fully actuated disturbance rejection with energy-efficient allocation. First, a low-altitude composite wind field model incorporating random wind, gusts, and improved Dryden turbulence is established. On this basis, a mapping relationship from wind field parameters to attitude disturbance torque and motor load is constructed to characterize the load imbalance among the six motors induced by gust disturbances. Second, an extended state observer (ESO) is designed at the attitude layer to estimate and compensate for the equivalent disturbances in the angular-acceleration channels. At the actuator layer, a bank of six Z-type extended state observers (ZESOs) is constructed to estimate the lumped disturbance acting on each individual motor channel. Based on the compensated motor dynamics, a coordination protocol is further developed to ensure coordinated reference tracking of the six motors under nonuniform gust loads and actuator constraints. title: Rethinking Educational Participatory Action Research with Migrant and Racialized Youth in Border Contexts
abstract: Abstract Youth-led participatory action research (YPAR) has gained increasing relevance as an approach for promoting youth agency and addressing social inequalities in educational contexts. However, when implemented with migrant and racialized youth in border regions, participatory research faces specific ethical, political, and methodological challenges that may limit its transformative potential. This article offers a situated reflection on the possibilities and constraints of educational participatory action research developed with migrant and racialized young people in the Canary Islands, one of the main border territories of southern Europe. Drawing on 15 years of experience in participatory research, education, and community action, as well as practice-based insights from Emancipatory Communicative Action Laboratories involving migrant and racialized youth, the paper reflects on recurring tensions that arise in these processes. Five recurring challenges are discussed: functional interculturalism, academic extractivism, performative decoloniality, ethnocentric and adult-centred practices, and the effects of structural violence associated with border regimes. In response, the article proposes a critical anti-racist and dialogical framework grounded in reflexivity, recognition, shared knowledge production, and the creation of safe participatory spaces. abstract: Digitalization is increasingly recognized as a key driver of energy efficiency, renewable energy development, and the decarbonization of energy systems. Nevertheless, significant differences remain among the EU Member States regarding their levels of digitalization, energy efficiency, renewable energy deployment, and greenhouse gas emissions. Assessing these differences is essential for designing effective policies that support both the digital and green transitions. The aim of this study is to develop the multidimensional measurement framework and to assess the EU Member states according to their digitalization, energy, and emissions performance. This study examines digitalization, energy and environmental sustainability in the 27 European Union Member States using the Eurostat data for 2010–2023. abstract: Abstract Background Identifying individuals with undiagnosed HIV remains a global challenge. Mobile health (mHealth) approaches that leverage social networks hold potential to increase HIV testing uptake but also raise ethical considerations. Methods We conducted a qualitative study in Moshi, Tanzania, to examine how a pilot test of an SMS-based confidential referral system for HIV testing (CONSORT) was experienced by individuals sending and receiving testing invitations. Focus group discussions were conducted prior to the pilot, while phone-based interviews were conducted both before and after pilot implementation. Data were analyzed thematically using the four ethical principles of mHealth delivery: transparency, agency, accountability, and equitable access. Results Interpretations of message origin and purpose varied, shaping levels of trust and engagement. While many participants viewed the messages as supportive reminders, a few expressed confusion or concern about why they were selected. Attitudes also varied regarding the sharing of phone numbers without prior consent, with some participants viewing this as acceptable and others raising privacy concerns. Perceptions of confidentiality, message timing, and message content influenced acceptability of the intervention. These perspectives informed modifications to the design of the CONSORT system. title: Computational systems immunology and multi-scale modeling for the design of a Multi-Epitope Vaccine (MEV) against emerging multidrug-resistant Klebsiella michiganensis
abstract: Abstract Klebsiella michiganensis , an emerging multidrug-resistant member of the Klebsiella oxytoca complex, has become an important opportunistic pathogen responsible for nosocomial infections, including bacteremia and ventilator-associated pneumonia. Owing to its rapidly evolving resistance to carbapenems, new preventive strategies are urgently needed. This study presents a computational systems immunology framework integrating subtractive proteomics, reverse vaccinology, and immunoinformatics to design a multi-epitope vaccine (MEV) against K. michiganensis strain ATCC 8724. From the complete proteome (5,483 proteins), four proteins associated with the bacterial envelope and LPS-related processes were prioritized as computational vaccine targets: the outer-membrane β-barrel proteins BamA and LptD, the periplasmic LPS transport component LptA, and the outer-membrane lipoprotein LolB. These were selected as non-homologous and antigenic candidates. Cytotoxic T-lymphocyte, helper T-lymphocyte, and B-cell epitopes derived from these proteins were evaluated for antigenicity, toxicity, allergenicity, and global HLA population coverage. The selected epitopes were assembled using AAY, GPGPG, and KK linkers with the Mycobacterium tuberculosis 50 S ribosomal protein L7/L12 as an adjuvant to construct a 386-amino-acid chimeric MEV. Pada tahap analisis, observasi dan wawancara mendalam dilakukan dengan pengurus panti. Prototype dievaluasi menggunakan instrumen System Usability Scale (SUS) dengan melibatkan enam responden yang terdiri dari pengurus panti dan perwakilan donatur. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan nilai rata-rata SUS sebesar 86,6. Nilai tersebut menempatkan aplikasi pada kategori Excellent, Acceptable, dan Grade B. abstract: Abstract Automated harvesting is pivotal to smart agriculture, yet precisely localizing picking points in complex orchard environments remains a key challenge for robotic harvesting systems. To this end, this study proposes a collaborative perception framework integrating a lightweight pose estimation model termed RepViT-DSConv-ARC-PoseHead enhanced YOLO (RDA-YOLO) with Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2). RDA-YOLO is the lightweight component responsible for real-time fruit detection and keypoint localization, while SAM2 is adopted for fruit contour segmentation and occlusion assessment. Based on the YOLOv11n-POSE architecture, we introduce Distribution Shift Convolution (DSConv) to reduce computational overhead and design the C3k2_RepViT module to enhance multi-scale feature fusion. Crucially, a specialized Adaptive Regression Coordination Pose Head (ARC-PoseHead) is developed to replace traditional prediction structures, employing log-scale polar regression and subpixel refinement to significantly improve coordinate perception of jujubes and key points under complex backgrounds. RDA-YOLO performs real-time detection and locates key points such as the pedicel-fruit transition zone to calculate optimal harvesting angles, while SAM2 performs fine-grained contour segmentation based on detection boxes to determine occlusion status and establish harvesting priority. From Participation to Exposure: NFTs and the Socio-Environmental Tensions of Digital Innovation
abstract: Digital innovation is typically discussed in terms of inclusion, efficiency, and value creation. Non-fungible tokens (NFTs) reveal a less visible dimension of digital innovation: their benefits can accrue to a relatively small number of actors, while their environmental and social costs extend beyond those who participate in, or benefit from, the technology. Using NFTs as a revealing case, we examine the tension between digital value creation and socio-environmental cost externalisation. Drawing on the Anthropocene and, in particular, the Capitalocene as a productive interpretive lens, we examine how digital artifacts, often perceived as intangible, are embedded in economic, infrastructural, and institutional arrangements through which benefits, responsibilities, and socio-environmental consequences are unevenly distributed. We argue that this tension adds an important dimension to digital inequality because participation and exposure need not coincide. We therefore call on Information Systems scholars to examine not only who accesses, participates in, and captures value from digital innovation, but also who bears responsibility and who is exposed to its (unintended) consequences. We outline avenues for doing so through multidimensional approaches to digital inequality, climate justice, socio-environmental externalities, and critical futures thinking.

title: Historical roots of commodity markets: from mercantilism to the theory of storage
abstract: Commodity markets today are shaped by financialization, price volatility, and the demands of the energy transition. This paper traces the historical development of commodity market theory from the seventeenth to the mid-twentieth century, identifying two parallel trajectories. The first examines the evolving conception of commodities—from precious metals as instruments of state power, through land as a gift of nature, to standardized outputs of finite natural resources traded as financial assets. The second traces the transformation of income from mere ownership—from classical land rent, through scarcity rent, to convenience yield. By integrating traditions often studied separately—mercantilist bullionism, physiocratic natural philosophy, classical rent theory, neoclassical marginalism, conservation economics, Keynesian forward-market analysis, and the theory of storage—the study reveals both conceptual continuities and methodological shifts. In doing so, it traces the historical roots of contemporary approaches to commodity pricing, risk transfer, and sustainable resource use.

Trust, privacy, and habit in retail central bank digital currency adoption among the unbanked
abstract: Retail central bank digital currency (CBDC) is frequently justified as a tool for financial inclusion, yet the three retail CBDCs in live operation have struggled to attract sustained use, and the people they were meant to reach remain largely absent from the adoption literature. Existing studies of CBDC acceptance draw on samples of banked, digitally connected consumers and apply technology acceptance models whose assumptions those samples satisfy. This paper argues that the unbanked violate several of those assumptions and that three constructs at the centre of adoption theory, trust, privacy, and habit, operate differently for them. Drawing on research in information systems, monetary economics, consumer payments, and development finance, the paper develops a conceptual framework in which trust is layered across the state, intermediaries, and the technology, privacy concern is directed primarily at the state rather than at commercial actors, and cash habit acts both as a barrier to first use and as the mechanism through which sustained use must eventually be secured. Ten propositions specify how these constructs and their interactions shape adoption intention, initial use, and habituated use, and how CBDC design choices such as tiered identification, offline capability, agent networks, and government to person payments moderate the relationships. title: Physics-Informed Multimodal Sensing and Machine Learning Framework with Real-Time Digital Twin for Intelligent Structural Health Monitoring of Marine Wharves
abstract: Marine wharves, consisting of concrete or steel decks supported by pile foundations, operate in harsh marine environments involving waves, vessel impacts, and corrosive seawater. Even minor cracks or early-stage corrosion in piles can lead to sudden structural failure. Early detection is therefore essential. Traditional vibration-based structural health monitoring (SHM) methods often struggle to deliver reliable results in real operational settings because environmental and operational variations can mask damage-induced frequency changes. This study presents a multimodal SHM framework that integrates accelerometers, strain gauges, high-resolution cameras, acoustic transducers, and corrosion sensors with edge computing, advanced machine learning, and a real-time physics-informed digital twin. Edge nodes preprocess sensor data to extract modal frequencies, crack indicators, and acoustic features, reducing communication loads by over 90% while preserving diagnostic fidelity. A hybrid pipeline combined attention-based multimodal fusion, XGBoost screening, and a feedforward deep neural network trained using a composite physics-informed objective. The physical loss numerically penalised positive damage-related modal-frequency shifts after environmental and operational condition compensation and stiffness ratios outside the admissible range of 0.70–1.00. title: Implementasi Face Recognition Berbasis Support Vector Machine dan MediaPipe
abstract: Autentikasi berbasis biometrik dengan wajah menawarkan kemudahan dan keamanan, namun akurasinya masih dipengaruhi dengan adanya perubahan pencahayaan, pose, ekspresi, dan occlusion. Penelitian ini mengimplementasikan sistem face recognition yang ringan dan praktis dengan deteksi wajah menggunakan MediaPipe Face Mesh, ekstraksi fitur melalui face encoding (dengan dukungan pola tepi ala HOG), dan klasifikasi identitas memakai Support Vector Machine (SVM) dengan tiga varian kernel yang dibandingkan secara sistematis. Sistem dikembangkan dalam Python (MediaPipe, OpenCV, scikit-learn) dengan antarmuka web untuk pendaftaran dan identifikasi wajah. Data uji berupa citra wajah pengguna yang diubah menjadi vektor embedding, kemudian pelatihan/validasi dilakukan memakai 5-fold cross-validation dan perbandingan beberapa kernel SVM. Hasil menunjukkan sistem mampu mengenali wajah dengan baik pada kondisi pencahayaan normal dan pose frontal. Kernel Linear memberikan akurasi rata-rata tertinggi 99,38% (confusion matrix 100%), disusul RBF 98,72% dan Polynomial 96,11%. Mekanisme stabilisasi confidence antar frame membuat tampilan identifikasi lebih halus dan konsisten. Meski demikian, ukuran data yang terbatas membuat performa belum sepenuhnya merepresentasikan kondisi nyata dan masih rentan terhadap occlusion serta pencahayaan ekstrim (indikasi overfitting). title: INOVAÇÕES PEDAGÓGICAS EM AMBIENTES DE E-LEARNING: O IMPACTO DAS METODOLOGIAS ATIVAS NA EDUCAÇÃO CONTEMPORÂNEA
abstract: Este estudo tem o objetivo de identificar e avaliar as estratégias implementadas por esses gestores para fomentar uma abordagem pedagógica que seja tanto inovadora quanto interativa, buscando resultados que contribuam para uma educação mais engajadora e alinhada com as necessidades educacionais contemporâneas. A pesquisa centra-se no papel dos gestores educacionais na implementação de plataformas de e-learning, destacando como podem tanto reforçar práticas tradicionais quanto facilitar abordagens pedagógicas inovadoras. Este artigo foi desenvolvido com base em uma metodologia bibliográfica, selecionando referências teóricas pertinentes abordadas na disciplina e ajustadas às discussões relativas ao contexto atual relevantes que discutem as interseções entre gestão educacional e TICs, focando em como os gestores podem utilizar essas ferramentas para promover um ensino mais interativo e participativo. A análise revela que uma liderança eficaz e a formação contínua dos docentes são essenciais para aproveitar o potencial das tecnologias de e-learning, necessárias para criar ambientes de aprendizado inclusivos e eficazes. Conclui-se que os diretores são fundamentais na atualização das práticas educacionais, ressaltando a necessidade de uma utilização crítica e inovadora das Tecnologias de Informação e Comunicação para aprimorar a qualidade e a acessibilidade da educação.

abstract: This study aimed to develop the Cyber Office Administrator Application based on Digital Administration competencies to support learning for Digital Office Administration students. The study employed a Research and Development approach using the ADDIE model, consisting of Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation. The participants were 35 students enrolled in a Digital Records Management course. Data were collected through needs analysis, expert validation, student responses, and pre-test and post-test assessments. The application obtained an expert feasibility score of 87%, categorized as highly feasible, while student responses reached 86%, indicating high practicality. Students’ mean scores increased from 83.03 in the pre-test to 87.09 in the post-test. Although the paired-test result showed a significant difference, the N-Gain value of 0.24 was categorized as low. The findings indicate that the application is feasible and practical as a competency-based digital learning environment, while further experimental testing is needed to establish its learning effectiveness

abstract: Abstract Four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) is a high-throughput measurement used to comprehensively acquire diffraction patterns across a region of interest in a specimen. While the measurement is useful for identifying crystallographic microstructures, the data analysis requires significant effort owing to the complexity and high dimensionality of the data. Furthermore, the analysis of low signal-to-noise data from beam-sensitive materials such as polymers is particularly challenging. This study proposes an automatic analysis pipeline that leverages denoising and unsupervised crystallographic analysis for 4D-STEM data. The denoising method is based on a self-supervised approach that eliminates the need for clean training images. The developed method is extended to 4D-STEM data by utilizing diffraction patterns observed at neighboring probe positions. The subsequent unsupervised analysis is designed to be invariant to the crystal in-plane rotations, enabling the effective identification of crystal components. The efficacy of the proposed pipeline is evaluated using both synthetic and experimental 4D-STEM data.
