title: An Intelligent Sleep Staging Framework For Sleep-Quality Characterization And Digital Interaction Design For Older Adults
abstract: Advancing age is commonly accompanied by a decline in sleep quality, while objective clinical sleep assessment often relies on polysomnography (PSG), which is costly and burdensome for older individuals. To address this issue, we develop an age-adaptive framework using single-channel EEG for automatic sleep staging, staging-derived sleep characterization, subsequent Sleep Quality Index (SQI) calibration, and digital interaction. The proposed framework consists of three successive stages. First, single-channel EEG is acquired using a low-burden sensing configuration. Second, sleep stages are predicted using a multi-scale CNN, channel-wise feature recalibration, and BiLSTM model optimized with focal loss and age-adaptive fine-tuning. Finally, sleep-architecture and continuity measures derived from the predicted hypnogram, including total sleep time (TST), sleep efficiency (SE), wake after sleep onset (WASO), N3 proportion, REM proportion, and fragmentation index (FI), are organized as candidate variables for subsequent SQI calibration. Evaluation on older-adult recordings from Sleep-EDF yielded an accuracy of 87.6% for five-stage classification and a Cohen’s kappa of 0.83, while ablation experiments further demonstrated the effectiveness of the individual design components. Correlation and multicollinearity analyses showed physiologically meaningful associations among the staging…
venue: Journal of Mechanics in Medicine and Biology

title: SOFT GELATIN CAPSULES: APPLICATION OF QUALITY BY DESIGN (QbD) APPROACHES IN FORMULATION DEVELOPMENT AND STABILITY CHALLENGES
abstract: Soft gelatin capsules are widely used for delivering drugs, nutraceuticals, and poorly water-soluble active ingredients. However, their quality and stability are influenced by complex interactions among the gelatin shell, fill formulation, manufacturing process, packaging, and storage environment. This review highlights the application of Quality by Design (QbD) principles in softgel development, focusing on the Quality Target Product Profile, Critical Quality Attributes, Critical Material Attributes, Critical Process Parameters, risk assessment, Design of Experiments, and control strategies. Major stability challenges, including gelatin cross-linking, moisture migration, shell brittleness, leakage, fill-shell interactions, oxidation, and dissolution changes, are discussed. The effects of temperature, relative humidity, light, oxygen, formulation, packaging, and transportation are also examined. Emerging approaches such as Process Analytical Technology, predictive stability modelling, advanced packaging, and digital technologies are highlighted for improving softgel robustness and lifecycle management. Overall, QbD provides a systematic approach for developing stable, reproducible, and high-quality formulation of soft gelatin capsule products.
venue: GLOBAL JOURNAL OF PHARMACEUTICAL AND SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH

title: Design of a Highly Linear Voltage Differencing Transconductance Amplifier Using Source Degeneration
abstract: This paper presents a highly linear voltage differencing transconductance amplifier (VDTA) utilizing a source degeneration technique to enhance input linearity while maintaining wide bandwidth. The incorporation of source degeneration within both transconductance stages of the proposed VDTA significantly improves the linear input range and suppresses harmonic distortion through controlled local negative feedback. The proposed VDTA is implemented using 180nm CMOS technology and the circuit operates at 0.9V with a bias current of 50A. The proposed VDTA achieves an asymmetrical linear input range from -310 mV to +321 mV (631 mV pp ) at 1% transconductance error bound, extending to -410 mV to +419 mV (829 mV pp ) at 5% error threshold and exhibits low THD of about 0.76%, provides a transconductance gain of 1mS and attains a 3dB bandwidth of 478MHz. A thorough performance evaluation is conducted through DC, AC, transient, and Monte Carlo analyses. The design exhibits excellent robustness under PVT variations and demonstrates electronic tunability. The proposed VDTA thus offers a practical and efficient solution for linear, high frequency analog signal processing applications. To validate the practical applicability of the proposed architecture, a voltage-mode universal MISO biquad filter has also been implemented and verified through SPICE simulations.
venue: Journal of Circuits, Systems and Computers

title: Conceptual design and prototype implementation of a robotic inspection system for sewer geometry analysis
abstract: Abstract Sewer systems are critical components of public infrastructure, requiring regular inspection and maintenance to ensure their functionality and protect both the environment and public health. Current inspections are primarily performed using robotic platforms equipped with pan-tilt-zoom cameras. By adding a high-resolution laser scanner to such platforms, it is possible to capture a point cloud containing geometric information of the sewer system. With a high-performance computation unit, data analysis can be performed during the inspection process to ensure data completeness and quality, detecting pipe segments or damage, and supporting the navigation of the robotic system. This research demonstrates that integrating a laser scanner into mobile robots for underground sewer inspection enables the detection of pipe connections and their alignment. Additionally, it allows for the objective quantification of deformations and deposits, which represent a significant portion of operational defects in sewer systems. Under laboratory conditions, the prototypic robotic system achieved an average point-to-point deviation of less than 10 mm relative to a terrestrial laser scanner reference. By analysing the scanned profiles during the inspection on the robotic platform, accurate sewer models can be derived. By enabling autonomy, inspection capabilities can be enhanced. As more com…

title: Design of Apron Floodlight Lighting System at Husein Sastranegara Airport
abstract: One of the important aspects of ensuring smooth operation, safety, and security in the terminal apron area is a lighting system that complies with applicable standards. However, substandard lighting conditions are still found at Husein Sastranegara Airport, as indicated by apron user complaints validated by the Assistant Electrical Manager, showing inadequate illumination levels that may affect safety and visual performance. Measurements showed that the average illumination level of the existing apron lighting system was 12.38 lux, which did not meet the standards specified in ICAO Annex 14 Volume 1 requiring 20 lux. This study aims to redesign the apron floodlight system to meet the applicable standards using the Research & Development method. The design was evaluated using DIALux evo software considering luminous flux, beam angle, mounting height, pole spacing, and lighting distribution. The simulation results showed that the proposed design successfully achieved the required illumination standard.

title: DESIGN AND EVALUATION OF A 1.8 GHz MMIC RF POWER AMPLIFIER FOR LTE BAND 3
abstract: Driven by the growing demand for high-performance wireless communications, the development of efficient radio frequency (RF) power amplifiers for LTE applications has become crucial. Operating at 1.8 GHz, LTE Band 3 is highly prevalent in modern cellular networks, necessitating RF front-end components with robust gain, efficiency, and linearity. This study presents the design and characterization of a 1.8 GHz Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) RF power amplifier tailored for LTE Band 3, implemented using the Keysight Advanced Design System (ADS). The design integrates a TQP7M9102 MMIC device with microstrip-based input and output matching networks implemented on an FR-4 substrate. Small-signal and large-signal behaviors were analyzed through S-parameter and Harmonic Balance simulations. The simulation results indicate that at 1.8 GHz, the amplifier achieves an input return loss (S11) of -14.2 dB, an output return loss (S22) of -12 dB, and a forward gain (S21) of 11.8 dB. Furthermore, it exhibits a peak Power Added Efficiency (PAE) of 52.3%, an output 1-dB compression point (OP1dB) of 19.2 dBm, and an output third-order intercept point (OIP3) of 20.1 dBm. These findings validate that the proposed MMIC RF power amplifier delivers sufficient gain, impedance matching, efficiency, and linearity for LTE Band 3 deployment, showcasing the utility of ADS-based simulations in…
venue: Bulletin of Network Engineer and Informatics

title: Computational Design Strategies for Nanoscale 3D Auxetic Metastructures from DNA
abstract: Abstract Auxetic metamaterials exhibit negative Poisson’s ratio (NPR) behaviors due to their architecture of periodically arranged unit cells. Although mechanical metamaterials are well established at the macroscale, programmable auxetic units remain scarce at the nanoscale. DNA origami offers a promising platform to bridge this gap, but design principles for dynamically deformable 3D auxetic nanostructures remain largely unexplored. Here, we develop design strategies for such 3D auxetic metastructures built from wireframe DNA origami. As a model system, we use a 3D re-entrant triangular unit composed of double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) bundle edges connected by single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) joints. Using coarse-grained molecular dynamics (MD) and umbrella-sampling free-energy simulations, we examine how edge design and joint-connection schemes govern auxetic responses and the energetics of the structural transformation. Our results show that auxetic performance and deformation energetics emerge from the coupled effects of DNA bundle rigidity and connector mechanics at the joints. This study provides mechanistic insights and design guidelines for programmable auxetic motion and energetics in 3D DNA origami metamaterials, advancing the development of stimuli-responsive nanomechanical devices.

title: Methane consumption by a landfill cover soil under variable soil moisture and temperature conditions
abstract: Landfills are one of the largest anthropogenic sources of methane (CH 4 ), and hot-spots of CH 4 emissions in landfill cover soils can enrich microbes that oxidize CH 4 to carbon dioxide (CO 2 ). CH 4 oxidation rates are modulated by multiple variables including soil moisture and temperature, although the interactive effects of these factors on CH 4 oxidation rates have not been well-studied. Here, we conducted closed-headspace batch incubations with cover soil from a former landfill in Ontario, Canada to measure the variations in CH 4 consumption and CO 2 efflux rates associated with combined variations in soil moisture and temperature. Soil samples were incubated under a factorial design of 5 soil moisture contents (20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, and 100% water-filled pore space; %WFPS), and 4 temperatures (1, 15, 25, and 35 °C). At each temperature and moisture combination, CH 4 was spiked into the headspace through multiple consecutive injections, and headspace CH 4 and CO 2 concentrations were measured to calculate CH 4 consumption and CO 2 efflux rates. The maximum CH 4 consumption rate was observed at the moderate soil moisture and temperature conditions (330 ± 12.3 nmol h -1 g DW -1 at 60% WFPS and 25 °C), while the maximum CO 2 efflux rate was observed at the maximal WFPS and temperature conditions of the experiment (652 ± 85.0 nmol h -1 g DW -1 at 100% WFPS and 35 °C). A diffusi…

title: Nursing Evaluation of Nutritional Status Using the Subjective Global Nutritional Assessment in Orphanage Children: Cross-sectional design
abstract: Background: Nutritional problems among orphaned children remain an important public health concern, particularly in institutional settings where children may experience inadequate dietary intake and poor health monitoring. Nurses play a critical role in the assessment and management of nutritional status among vulnerable children(1). Aim: To assess the nutritional status of orphanage children using the Subjective Global Nutritional Assessment (SGNA) tool in Karbala City. Methods: A cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted among 40 orphanage children aged 3–6 years in Karbala City. A purposive sample was used. Data were collected using two instruments: a demographic questionnaire and the Subjective Global Nutritional Assessment tool. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 26.0 through descriptive and inferential statistics. Results: The findings showed that 62.5% of children were aged 3–4 years and 55% were female. According to the SGNA evaluation, 57.5% of children had mild malnutrition, 25% had moderate malnutrition, and 5% had severe malnutrition. A significant association was found between age and nutritional status (p < 0.05), whereas no significant association was found between gender and nutritional status. Conclusion: Mild malnutrition was common among orphanage children. Early nutritional screening and nursing interventions are necessary to improve…

title: AI-Driven Data Governance Framework for Enterprises in Cloud Environments: Design, Implementation, and Enterprise Evaluation
abstract: Challenges cloud-based enterprise data governance is encountering include data growth, regulatory changes, and the inflexibility of traditional rule-based systems. This systematic literature review, based on PRISMA guidelines, analyses 67 peer-reviewed papers (2019–2026) under three research questions related to AI-driven governance. Five weaknesses of a rule-based government are identified: rigidity of policies, poor scalability, semantic ambiguity, slow adaptation of policies, and weak anomaly detection. The benefits of AI techniques such as machine learning classifiers, large language models to extract policies, reinforcement learning to control access dynamically, and graph neural networks for federated lineage are measurable, with an 85-95% accuracy in detecting compliance and 38-70% reduction in manual effort. There is a common layered architecture (ingestion, intelligence, policy and enforcement) with policy-as-code, active metadata and federated lineage revealed in a comparative analysis. But there are still some stark contrasts, such as in the balance between the accuracy of a process and its explanation, between automation and auditability, and between cost reduction and assurance of compliance. The review presents a reference architecture and governance maturity model for enterprise adoption, and identifies open challenges such as model drift, multi-cloud consistency…
venue: American Journal of Smart Technology and Solutions

title: Beyond heartbeats: re-thinking interoception in autism through virtual reality and computational modelling
abstract: Interoception, the sensing and interpretation of internal bodily signals, is increasingly invoked to explain heterogeneity in autism, yet empirical findings remain inconsistent. A major reason is methodological: the field remains cardio-centric and relies heavily on heartbeat counting tasks and trait questionnaires, which are vulnerable to cognitive strategies, attention, expectancy effects, and confounds such as alexithymia and anxiety. Autism research further indicates that interoception is multidimensional (accuracy, sensibility, metacognitive awareness) and developmentally dynamic, with evidence for dissociations across components and compensation across the lifespan. We argue that progress requires reframing interoception as an inference problem: the brain estimates hidden physiological states from noisy sensory evidence under context-dependent precision weighting (predictive processing/active inference). Building on this framework, we propose a participatory, multimodal research program for autism that integrates (i) lived experience as hypothesis-shaping data, (ii) virtual reality (VR) as an experimental testbed to manipulate embodiment, sensory load, agency cues, and feedback, and (iii) computational physiological modelling to estimate latent cardiovascular–respiratory and autonomic-control parameters, which could subsequently constrain separately specified models of pe…

title: Observations of 4–5 h oscillation periods in virtual height during the fall seasons of 2020–2023 across the eastern United States
abstract: Since the early 1960s, many studies have documented ionospheric virtual height oscillation with periods ranging from 30 min to 3 h. However, in this investigation, we find a consistent, much larger period in the oscillations of virtual height, as estimated using Coastal Ocean Dynamics Applications Radars (CODARs), whereas few previous studies have consistently observed periods of oscillation in this range. The purpose of this investigation is to investigate day-to-day bottomside variability, and we report a consistently observed 4–5-h period of virtual height oscillation, along with providing potential physical interpretations of the observations. We use bistatic high-frequency data from CODARs, collected nearly continuously between 2020 and 2023 at a 2-min time cadence. The frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) waveforms of these radars are suitable as a single-frequency oblique ionospheric sounder. We estimate the group delay from which the virtual height of an ionospheric layer can be estimated. We present statistical results from several virtual height oscillations with varying periods across September, October, November, and December during 2020–2023. For each year, we compare three to four CODAR transmitters located in the Eastern United States, operating at 4–5 MHz. The receiver is located near Clemson University. We frequently observe ( ≈ 25% of the time) the 4–5-h…
venue: Frontiers in Astronomy and Space Sciences

title: Moving beyond anthropomorphism: demographic cues as a new lens for understanding virtual influencer effectiveness
abstract: Purpose This study examines how demographic cues, specifically age, race, and gender, interact to shape stereotype-based evaluations of virtual influencers (VIs) and influence downstream behavioral intentions in pro-environmental campaigns. Design/methodology/approach Two online survey-based experiments were conducted with U.S. social media users recruited through CloudResearch. Study 1 used a 2 VI age × 2 VI race between-subjects design (N = 492), and Study 2 used a 2 VI age × 2 race × 2 gender between-subjects design (N = 430). Participants viewed a pro-environmental campaign stimulus featuring VIs with visually manipulated demographic cues and then reported key measurements. ANCOVA and moderated mediation analyses examine the interaction effects of VI demographic cues on purchase and pro-environmental intentions through perceived warmth and competence. Findings Older racial and ethnic minority female VIs received the highest warmth and competence evaluations and generated the highest purchase and pro-environmental intentions. Perceived warmth and competence mediated the interaction effects of VI demographic cues on purchase and pro-environmental intentions. These effects were robust to participant–VI demographic matching, suggesting that VI demographic portrayals function as broadly legible social signals. Originality/value This study advances VI research by moving beyond ge…
venue: Journal of Research in Interactive Marketing

title: The emerging charisma of 0 s and 1s: unraveling the intricacies of virtual idol adoption
abstract: Abstract This research explores the factors that influence perception, adoption intention, and trust of K-pop virtual idols. Drawing on a unified stimulus-organism-response (S–O-R) framework integrated with parasocial interaction (PSI) theory, this study investigates how industry-driven environmental stimuli (i.e., visual appeal, narrative openness, socially present conversational style, content-driven engagement, institutional trust) shape the internal psychological state of the audience to drive adoption behavior. The study employs an online survey of K-pop fans ( N = 259) with a series of statistical analyses to examine the relationships between the identified factors and outcome variables. The results demonstrate that relational and identity-driven stimuli operate as dominant predictors that effectively bridge the psychological distance caused by the idol's artificial nature. In contrast, visual appeal and institutional trust exhibit critical boundary limitations. Crucially, the findings reveal that realistic perception and parasocial relationship serve as the underlying mechanisms that translate digital stimuli into genuine emotional trust and long-term behavioral commitment. This study contributes to the emerging field of virtual idol research, providing implications for virtual idol creators, developers, and industry stakeholders seeking to enhance adoption rates and fan…

title: Micro-foundations of sustainability: entrepreneurial identity and interaction patterns in plant-based food microenterprises
abstract: Purpose The paper aims to identify how entrepreneurs’ identities intersect with interaction patterns to facilitate sustainability-driven activities in microenterprises. In addition, it proposes a typology of sustainable entrepreneurs, ranging from Mission-Embedded Activists to Instrumentally Sustainable Entrepreneurs. Design/methodology/approach This paper adopts a qualitative study and presents the results of in-depth interviews conducted with entrepreneurs running 20 plant-based restaurant ventures, serving as a suitable context for examining sustainable entrepreneurship. Findings Sustainability-oriented activities in microenterprises emerge through the interplay between entrepreneurial identity, sustainability-driven identity and interaction patterns. This study develops and implements a four-part typology of sustainable entrepreneurs: Mission-Embedded Activists, Value-Oriented Practitioners, Health-Oriented Problem Solvers and Instrumentally Sustainable Entrepreneurs. Based on this typology, the study demonstrates how different identity configurations translate into distinct approaches toward actor selection, relational openness and the use of close cooperation and pure exchange interactions. The findings further show that interaction patterns are shaped not only by sustainability-driven values but also by resource availability, operational constraints and actors’ local pro…

Capital Punishment in India: A Critical Analysis of the “Rarest of Rare” Doctrine, Judicial Sentencing and the President's Clemency Power under Article 72
abstract: Capital punishment is the most irreversible form of State power and therefore demands an unusually reliable legal process. This article examines the Indian death-penalty framework through the connected questions of the “rarest of rare” doctrine, individualised judicial sentencing and presidential clemency under Article 72 of the Constitution. It uses doctrinal and analytical research, examining the Constitution, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, leading Supreme Court decisions, Law Commission reports, international standards and empirical scholarship on death-row prisoners. The analysis finds that Indian law formally treats life imprisonment as the rule and death as the exception, but that the application of broad expressions such as “collective conscience” and “exceptional depravity” has produced avoidable uncertainty. The principal weakness is not the absence of safeguards on paper, but the uneven quality of mitigation investigation and sentencing reasoning. Courts may possess detailed evidence concerning the offence while lacking reliable information about poverty, childhood trauma, mental health, intellectual disability, prison conduct and prospects of reform. Article 72 remains an essential constitutional safety valve, yet delay, incomplete records, inadequate representation and limited transparency can undermine its correctiv…
venue: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities

Effects of cultivation of herbaceous perennials on soil microbial community structure and nitrogen cycling functions
abstract: This study aimed to elucidate the impacts of cultivating different herbaceous perennials on the rhizosphere microenvironment, nitrogen-cycling microbial communities, and functional genes in black soils of urban green spaces in Northeast China, thereby providing a scientific basis for rational urban plant configuration and interspecific differences in soil nutrient cycling. Focusing on five commonly utilized herbaceous perennials in Changchun ( Lycopus lucidus [P-LL], Salvia japonica [P-SJ], Hemerocallis fulva [P-HF], Hosta ensata [P-HE], and Pseudolysimachion spicatum [P-PS]), this study integrated conventional physicochemical analyses, metagenomic sequencing, co-occurrence networks, and Random Forest modeling to analyze rhizosphere soil nutrient profiles, nitrogen-cycling microbial community structures, and key functional gene abundances after two years of continuous cultivation. Different floral treatments significantly altered rhizosphere nutrient status and microbial community composition. The P-LL treatment exhibited relatively higher contents of total nitrogen (TN), soil microbial biomass nitrogen (SMBN), available phosphorus, and available potassium, demonstrating a high-level soil multifunctionality index (SMI). The P-PS treatment showed higher available nitrogen and ammonium nitrogen but lower SMBN, accompanied by a higher relative abundance of Actinomycetota and the a…

title: Enhancing Chemistry Learning through an Android-Based Virtual Laboratory on Acid-Base Titration
abstract: Chemistry practicums in many schools are constrained by inadequate laboratory facilities, while acid-base titration requires learners to connect macroscopic observations with submicroscopic and symbolic representations; a preliminary study at the research site found limited equipment and a mean mastery score of 62.6, below the school minimum. This study aimed to develop an Android-based virtual laboratory for acid-base titration and to evaluate its validity, readability, practicality, and effectiveness. A research and development design following the ADDIE model was applied at SMAN 1 Suwawa. The product was built in Adobe Animate with ActionScript 3.0 and compiled as an Android application. It was validated by a media expert, a material expert, and a chemistry teacher; readability was trialled with 12 students, and 64 students joined the large-scale trial with a pre-test, post-test, and response questionnaire (Cronbach's alpha = 0.905). Validity, readability, and practicality were analysed as percentages, and effectiveness through N-Gain. The virtual laboratory obtained 88.1% validity, 89.7% readability, and 84.72% practicality, while the mean score rose from 9.45 to 16.02, giving an N-Gain of 0.768 (high category). The product is therefore valid, practical, and effective, and offers a workable virtual practicum for schools where laboratory facilities are the binding constraint…

title: Development of a flipped classroom module based on virtual reality technology for the teaching and learning of Thirukkural among year four pupils in Tamil National-Type Schools
abstract: This study aims to develop a teaching and learning module based on the Flipped Classroom approach integrated with Virtual Reality Semi Immersive (VRSM) technology to enhance the effectiveness of teaching Thirukkural among Year 4 pupils in Tamil National Type Primary Schools (SJKT). The study addresses challenges related to students’ low motivation and limited understanding of the moral and philosophical aspects of Thirukkural, particularly when conventional teacher centered pedagogies remain dominant. The module was designed using the ADDIE instructional model and validated through the Fuzzy Delphi method. A quasi-experimental design was employed with two groups, an experimental group (using the VR Flipped Classroom module) and a control group (using traditional methods). The sample consisted of 60 Year 4 pupils from four SJKT in the Kinta Utara Zone, Perak. Quantitative data were collected through pre and post-tests and a learning motivation questionnaire, analyzed using paired t-tests and ANCOVA. Findings revealed a significant improvement in both achievement and motivation among the experimental group compared to the control group (p < .05). The study concludes that VR-based flipped learning enhances interactivity, comprehension, and value appreciation in Thirukkural learning within the 21st-century pedagogical context.
venue: Muallim Journal of Social Science and Humanities

title: Design of a prognostic alert system for coal power plants using FMEA and the proportional hazards model
abstract: Purpose The power plants face failures during start-up or operation which may cause long disruptions in electricity generation, a serious problem for both electricity producer and market operater. The capacity of coal plant is submitted to the day-ahead market for the next day. When the plant is scheduled for the operation, a failure prevents power generation and causes capacity loss and downtime cost. Hence, a framework needs to be developed to estimate the failures before the operation and market settlement. Design/methodology/approach In this work, we use historical data for plant failures and analyze the failure types, modes and components using descriptive statistics. Then Failure Mode Effect Analysis is used to analyze the faults, errors and failures for each plant. To address varying risk levels, risk priority numbers are calculated for each failure type that can cause crucial failures for each plant. Then, the Andersen–Gill’s extended proportional hazards model (PHM) is applied to calculate the probability of failures in power plants at different times. Findings Using a threshold level for survival probability, which indicates the probability of a failure for each plant, a prognostic alert system is created that can predict the timing of an upcoming failure. The proposed methodology provides both plant and previous failure-based survival curves to help decision makers w…
venue: International Journal of Quality & Reliability Management

title: Strategies for sustainable crop production in the Yangtze River Basin of China: insights from field experiments and farm surveys
abstract: Introduction Rice-based cropping systems in the Yangtze River Basin of China are diverse. Objectives However, most previous studies have focused primarily on improving the yield, resource use efficiency, or reducing the carbon emissions of individual systems, with few comprehensive comparisons across different systems. Methods To address this knowledge gap, a two-year field experiment combined with a survey of 190 farmers was conducted to evaluate the sustainability performance index (SPI) of four systems in this region: rice−fallow (RF), rice−green manure (RG), rice−wheat (RW), and rice−rapeseed (RR). Results showed that the RR and RW systems achieved higher yields than the RG and RF systems in both experiments and surveys. Results and conclusions Average rice equivalent yields of the RR, RW, and RG systems exceeded those of the RF by 124.5%, 86.2% and 13.3%, respectively, in the experiments (RF, 9.34 t ha -1 ), and by 66.9%, 58.2%, and 2.8% in the surveys (RF, 8.96 t ha -1 ). The RR and RW systems also exhibited higher net energy, radiation use efficiency, and accumulated temperature production efficiency. Although the RR and RW systems incurred higher carbon and agricultural cost, their superior grain yield resulted in a greater net economic income, net ecosystem economic budge, and benefit-cost ratio than the RF and RG systems. Furthermore, the carbon emission intensity of …

title: Bringing virtual reality-integrated social-emotional learning into schools: a dual-phase validation and feasibility study with adolescents in a collectivist society
abstract: Social-emotional learning (SEL) is increasingly recognised as an important approach to adolescent mental health promotion in school settings. However, evidence regarding culturally adapted and technology-supported SEL interventions in non-Western educational contexts remains limited. This study reports the expert-validation and pilot-feasibility components of the REAL™ (Read Emotion and Learn to Regulate) module, a culturally adapted, virtual reality (VR)-integrated SEL intervention developed for Malaysian lower-secondary students. These developmental phases preceded a subsequently completed and separately reported randomised controlled trial (RCT). A sequential two-phase design was used. In Phase 1, six Malaysian experts from psychiatry, psychology, education, and social-emotional learning completed a three-round Modified Delphi process evaluating 15 module structure and delivery components and 12 activity stations on a 5-point Likert scale. Content validity was assessed using the item-level content validity index (I-CVI), scale-level average content validity index (S-CVI/Ave), and interquartile range (IQR). In Phase 2, a single-session school-based feasibility pilot was conducted with 15 lower-secondary students, four facilitators, and one school administrator to assess practical implementation of one chapter from the initial 12-station module. In Round 1, the S-CVI/Ave acros…

title: Plant compartment and understory habitat jointly shape endophytic bacterial communities in Monochasma savatieri
abstract: Introduction Monochasma savatieri is a rare medicinal plant endemic to China that currently faces extinction, with wild-simulated understory cultivation representing a key conservation strategy. Endophytic bacteria play important roles in nutrient acquisition and environmental adaptation of hemiparasitic plants; however, how the understory environments influence above- and belowground endophytic bacterial communities remains poorly understood. Methods We collected soil and plant tissue samples from four contrasting understory habitats ( Pinus massoniana , Camellia oleifera , Phyllostachys edulis , and Gardenia jasminoides ). The endophytic bacterial communities were characterized by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. The soil physicochemical properties were measured to identify environmental drivers. Multivariate statistics, including permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA), redundancy analysis (RDA), and Mantel tests, were applied to link the community variation with environmental factors. Results Permutational multivariate analysis of variance revealed that the type of plant tissue, habitat, and their interaction (all p < 0.001) significantly shaped the endophytic community structure. Belowground tissues generally harbored higher diversity than aboveground tissues, although this pattern was habitat-dependent. Each habitat enriched distinct bacterial genera. Func…

title: Short-term responses across two sequential plant-based activity sessions: an exploratory fixed-order pilot study
abstract: Background Structured plant-based activities combine natural materials, purposeful manual work, sensory engagement, and social interaction, but direct comparisons of practical formats in community adults remain limited. We characterized short-term responses during two sequential sessions and compared within-session changes. Methods Twenty-five adults participated in a single-group, fixed-order pilot study. Session 1 involved horticultural crafting; 1 week later, Session 2 involved balm crafting followed by horticultural crafting. Twenty-three attended both sessions. DASS-21 and STAI-S were principal outcomes; horticultural wellbeing, HRV, and forehead single-channel EEG were exploratory. Within-session changes and complete-case between-session differences were estimated with 95% CIs. Post hoc TOST examined exploratory equivalence bounds. Results Both sessions were followed by favorable short-term psychological changes. DASS-21 scores decreased by 8.57 points in Session 1 [95% CI (5.41, 11.72), n = 23] and 5.53 in Session 2 [(2.65, 8.41), n = 17]. STAI-S scores decreased by 7.30 points in Session 1 [(5.23, 9.37), n = 25] and 6.86 in Session 2 [(4.07, 9.66), n = 22]; all four Holm-adjusted p values were <0.001. Complete-case comparisons showed no statistically detectable between-session difference in DASS-21 improvement [3.12 points, 95% CI (−1.51, 7.75)] or STAI-S improvement…

title: A proof-of-concept EEG study of responses to peer speech in collaborative learning
abstract: Background This study focused on internal aspects, including cognitive states and motivational engagement, that may be overlooked by external indicators of participation in collaborative learning, such as utterance counts or observable behaviors. This proof-of-concept feasibility study explored whether neurophysiological responses related to auditory attention could provide information relevant to interpreting conventional behavioral indicators of participation. Using electroencephalogram (EEG) indices (N1 and P2 components), associations with self-regulated learning and interest during collaborative learning were explored. Methods EEG data were collected during real, discussion-based collaborative learning activities conducted in a university classroom setting. EEG data were recorded using wearable devices from nine Japanese university students enrolled in the course. Utterances were categorized as surface- or deep-level regulation utterances according to definitions from a prior study. Using a multivariate temporal response function approach, the N1 and P2 amplitudes elicited by each type of utterance were estimated. The degree of self-regulated learning was indexed by the number of deep-level regulation utterances, and interest in learning was evaluated using subjective rating scores. The relationships between these indices and the N1 and P2 amplitudes were analyzed using li…

title: The association between sports participation and fertility intentions among Chinese youth: an empirical study based on the China family panel studies
abstract: Objective This study aimed to examine the association between sports participation and fertility intentions among Chinese youth and to assess the potential mediating roles of life satisfaction and confidence in the future. Methods Data were drawn from the 2018 and 2022 waves of the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS). A serial mediation model was specified to examine the potential psychological pathways linking sports participation to fertility intentions. Two-way fixed-effects regression models were used to assess the statistical association between sports participation and fertility intentions. The significance of the specific indirect effects and the serial indirect effect was evaluated using an individual-level cluster bootstrap procedure with 5,000 resamples. Results Sports participation was significantly and positively associated with fertility intentions ( β = 0.046, p < 0.01). Mediation analysis revealed that the total indirect effect of life satisfaction and future confidence was 0.015 (95% CI = [0.009, 0.020]). Specifically, the independent indirect effect of life satisfaction was 0.007 (95% CI = [0.003, 0.011]), and the independent indirect effect of future confidence was 0.005 (95% CI = [0.003, 0.007]). Furthermore, the chain mediating effect of life satisfaction and future confidence was 0.003 (95% CI = [0.001, 0.005]). Conclusion Sports participation, as a positi…

title: Research on start-up transition process of high-head pumped storage units
abstract: To understand transient behavior during the start-up of high-head pumped storage units under turbine operating conditions and to identify an optimal start-up strategy, this study takes a 350 MW Francis reversible pump-turbine as a case study. It compared one-dimensional transient flow simulations to four start-up methods: large-acceleration open-loop guide vane control (Method 1), small-acceleration open-loop control (Method 2.1), acceleration-controlled closed-loop control (Method 3), and combined open-loop plus closed-loop control (Method 4). The start-up time, rotational speed evolution, and pressure pulsation characteristics at the spiral casing and draft tube were evaluated. The results show that Method 1 has the shortest start-up time (40.59 s) but causes the highest pressure pulsation (peak-to-peak pressure at the spiral casing inlet reaching 193.81 m during the simultaneous start-up of two units). Methods 3 and 4 significantly reduce pressure pulsation but result in excessively long start-ups (69.38 s and 72.70 s, respectively). Method 2.1 offers the best trade-off between start-up time (52.64 s) and pressure suppression, reducing peak-to-peak pressures at the draft tube inlet and outlet by 17.2% and 25.3%, respectively, compared with Method 1 for a single-unit start-up. Furthermore, after adjusting the guide vane motion parameters, the entropy weight method—comprehensi…

title: Silent I-Positions: Dialogical Exploration of Student Classroom Participation
abstract: This article explores social and cultural influences that affect East Asian American students’ verbal participation in classroom settings, aiming to promote learning environments in which East Asian American students feel welcome to share their insights.

title: Beyond participation: procedural justice, relational legitimacy, and sustained engagement in evaluating the effectiveness of DDR programs
abstract: Evaluation of disarmament, demobilization, and reintegration (DDR) programs tends to focus on weapons collection, demobilization of combatants, reduction of violence, and participation in programs. These measures provide less insight into why people remain engaged in peacebuilding implementations after the programs have concluded. Drawing on qualitative data from Nigeria’s Niger Delta Presidential Amnesty Program, this article develops a procedural justice–relational legitimacy–sustained participation framework. Analysis reveals that neutrality, trustworthiness, dignity and respect, and opportunities for voice are dimensions of procedural justice which may influence the relational legitimacy of program authorities and institutions. The framework suggests that procedural justice and relational legitimacy perceptions are important to sustaining participation and commitment over time. Therefore, evaluation should consider sustained participation, in addition to security achievements, to assess the effectiveness of DDR. The framework offers a way to examine how people’s experiences of program implementation influence their continued engagement in peacebuilding.

title: Hydrogen storage and diffusion in shale nanopores: molecular dynamics effects of pressure, temperature, confinement, and wall chemistry
abstract: Introduction Underground hydrogen storage in shale is governed by pore occupancy, interfacial interactions, and molecular diffusion. This study examines their combined effects on hydrogen retention and transport. Methods Molecular dynamics simulations were performed for five mineral slit-pore models and type I–III kerogen pores. The effects of temperature, pressure-associated loading, pore width, kerogen type, and pore-wall type were assessed using adsorption heat, pore H₂ population (the mean number of H₂ molecules within the pore region), density profiles, and directionally averaged self-diffusion coefficients. Results Higher prescribed loadings corresponding to higher pressures increased pore H₂ population and were accompanied by reduced diffusion. Heating decreased adsorption heat and pore population while enhancing diffusion. Narrower pores accommodated fewer molecules and restricted molecular motion, with the largest change in diffusion between the sampled pore widths occurring from 2 to 3 nm in quartz. Differences among kerogen types were modest, although type III exhibited a tendency toward stronger H₂ retention. Pore-wall type yielded more pronounced differences: quartz exhibited the highest adsorption heat, calcite combined the largest pore population with the lowest diffusion coefficient, and graphite supported the fastest diffusion. Discussion The differing rankings…

title: Efforts to Increase Community Participation in Agroforestry Land Conservation on the Slopes of Mount Muria
abstract: Background: The slopes of Mount Muria serve as a water catchment area, a habitat for biodiversity, and a source of community livelihoods through agroforestry. However, land-use conversion, non-conservation-oriented cultivation practices, erosion, and landslides threaten the sustainability of these areas. Objective: This study aims to describe community activities on agroforestry land, identify the forms and assess the levels of community participation, and formulate strategies to strengthen participation in agroforestry land conservation in Colo Village, Dawe Subdistrict, Kudus Regency. Methods: A descriptive quantitative approach with a cross-sectional survey design was employed. From a population of 454 coffee farmers, 46 respondents were selected through proportional random sampling. Data were collected using questionnaires, observations, interviews, and documentation and were analyzed using descriptive percentages based on Abu Huraerah’s forms of participation and Arnstein’s Ladder of Citizen Participation. Results: Community participation was classified as good, with a score of 78.57%. Material contributions (85.76%) and labor contributions (81.30%) were dominant, while skills contributions (74.13%) required further strengthening. The level of participation was also categorized as good, with an overall score of 70.96%, comprising Nonparticipation (77.81%), Citizen Power (7…

title: Estrategias psicopedagógicas basadas en la neuroeducación para fortalecer la participación académica en estudiantes universitarios de carreras en línea
abstract: La participación académica constituye un desafío relevante en la educación universitaria en línea. El objetivo de este estudio fue evaluar los cambios asociados con una intervención psicopedagógica fundamentada en principios neuroeducativos sobre la participación académica de estudiantes de carreras en línea de la Universidad Estatal del Sur de Manabí. Se desarrolló un estudio cuantitativo, aplicado y cuasiexperimental con pretest, postest y grupos no equivalentes. Participaron 120 estudiantes, distribuidos en un grupo experimental y uno de comparación, con 60 integrantes cada uno, además de 12 docentes. La intervención se implementó durante ocho semanas e integró segmentación de contenidos, recuperación activa, recursos multimodales, retroalimentación, actividades colaborativas y estrategias metacognitivas. La participación global del grupo experimental aumentó de 3,01 a 3,84 puntos, mientras que en el grupo de comparación pasó de 3,04 a 3,12. El análisis ajustado mostró una diferencia media de 0,69 puntos entre los grupos (IC95 %: 0,56–0,82; p < 0,001). Se concluye que la intervención se asoció con mayores niveles de participación académica, aunque los efectos deben interpretarse considerando su carácter multicomponente y el diseño cuasiexperimental.
venue: Revista Multidisciplinaria Voces de América y el Caribe

Latent profiles of sport participation motivation and their association with campus sports culture among higher vocational college students
abstract: Objective This study identified latent profiles of sport participation motivation among higher vocational college students and examined their associations with campus sports culture. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted in 2026 among students from three higher vocational colleges in Jiangsu and Zhejiang Provinces using convenience sampling. Campus sports culture and sport participation motivation were assessed using the Campus Sports Culture Scale and the Chinese version of the Behavioral Regulation in Exercise Questionnaire-3. Latent profile analysis was performed in Mplus 8.3, followed by chi-square tests and the R3STEP three-step procedure to examine demographic differences and associations between campus sports culture and profile membership while accounting for classification uncertainty. Results Four motivational profiles were identified: the Low-to-Moderate Flat Profile (5.8%), Autonomous Orientation Profile (33.1%), High Controlled–Amotivation Profile (8.4%), and Moderate Mixed-Motivation Profile (52.6%). The Moderate Mixed-Motivation Profile was the largest subgroup. With the Low-to-Moderate Flat Profile as the reference category, higher overall campus sports culture scores were associated with greater odds of membership in the Autonomous Orientation, High Controlled–Amotivation, and Moderate Mixed-Motivation Profiles, with the strongest association ob…

title: Temporal evolution and decline of seismicity associated with cyclic operations at the Serajeh underground gas storage, Iran
abstract: Abstract Underground gas storage (UGS) operations can perturb reservoir conditions and modulate local seismicity, but the temporal evolution of this response under cyclic injection–withdrawal remains poorly constrained. We investigate seismicity around the Serajeh UGS in central Iran by combining 29,781 deep-learning-based single-station earthquake detections, multi-station relocation, centroid moment tensor inversion, and operational records. The relocated hypocentres form a compact cluster near the Serajeh structure, primarily at depths of 3–8 km, overlapping with and extending below the 2.4–3.0 km storage interval. Independent comparison with relocated earthquakes confirms that S–P time at the nearby GHVR station provides a useful first-order proxy for local source distance. Cross-correlation between monthly gas injection and seismicity shows a distinct maximum at an offset of approximately 8 months. This feature is reproduced by the phase-randomized ReshuffleCorr analysis, while additional structure-preserving tests indicate that its global statistical strength and exact timing depend on the treatment of temporal variability. An objective change-point analysis identifies a marked decrease in seismicity centred on April 2015, nearly four years after storage operations began, and the decrease remains evident using a conservative magnitude threshold. Seismicity subsequently re…

title: A hybrid MCDM approach for site selection of electric vehicle battery swapping station
abstract: A promising strategy for decarbonising the transportation segment, both commercial and domestic, is based on transitioning from traditional to electric mobility, which is dependent on the Electric Vehicle (EV), their adoption is hindered by range anxiety, insufficient charging infrastructure, and long waiting times. This research aims to commission a battery swapping station (BSS) at a significant location selected through a data-driven hybrid Multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) technique to satisfy the urban sustainable mobility needs while minimising charging congestion. Monte Carlo analysis was employed to determine whether the proposed model is resilient to input perturbations, confirming the rank stability. Alternative L4 retained the first position in 100% of simulations, while L3 consistently remained second. Spearman's rank correlation coefficient between the deterministic and simulated ranks was tested (r s =1.00), indicating perfect agreement. This paper establishes that the criteria related to EV adoption and cost overrule other identified criteria. The Expert-based cross-validation of ranking confirms that the proposed ranking is highly robust to reasonable variations in criteria weights and that the identified optimal alternative remains unchanged under uncertainty. The peripheral nodes of the Chennai Metropolitan Area (CMA) outperform other selected locations du…

title: Transport Systems and Revenue Generation: A Case of Boda-Boda Transport System in Mbarara City, South Division
abstract: Purpose: The purpose of this article was to understand Transport Systems and Revenue Generation. A Case of Boda-Boda Transport System in Mbarara City, South Division. Objectively, the article was to find out the factors influencing the increased boda -boda Industry in Mbarara City South. Methodology: A cross-sectional research design was used, and both qualitative and quantitative approaches were employed. The sample size was composed of 40 respondents, comprising 5 police officers, 5 Mbarara City officials, 5 staff from the boda-boda riders association, and 25 Boda-Boda riders who were selected. Data were collected using a questionnaire and interview guide. Findings: The study revealed that, though there are factors driving people into the boda-boda business, the majority agree that unemployment is the major driving factor that forces people into the Boda-Boda business. The study also revealed that many boda-boda riders are sure of getting enough money as income to cater for their families and foster development, though they don’t pay revenue in the form of taxes to Mbarara City South. The study finally reported that the issue of safety in terms of traffic accidents and robberies is the major challenge boda-boda riders face in the boda-boda business. Conclusion: The boda-boda business operates as a gap-filler in Mbarara City South's public transportation system. It provides em…

title: Micrographic Evaluation of Water-in-Oil Emulsion Stability up to Critical Electric Field
abstract: Abstract Electrostatic demulsification is widely applied in the petroleum industry for the separation of water-in-oil emulsions; however, the relationship between microscopic droplet dynamics and the macroscopic electrical response remains insufficiently understood, particularly regarding the definition of the critical electric field (CEF). This work presents a quantitative investigation of electrocoalescence using optical microscopy coupled with electrical current monitoring under a direct current electric field. Water-in-oil (W/O) model emulsions were evaluated through a factorial experimental design comprising 81 experiments, in which the electrode gap (100–300 μm), water cut (5–15 wt %), and surfactant concentration (0.5–1.5 wt %) were systematically varied. Real-time observations enabled the identification of droplet polarization, chain formation, coalescence, and the development of conductive pathways. The CEF, ranging approximately from 0.7 to 4.0 kV/cm, was determined from the simultaneous occurrence of current spikes and the visual formation of coalesced droplets that establish conductive pathways within the emulsion. The results demonstrate that droplet alignment occurs at the initial stages of electric field application and does not correspond to a significant increase in current. Instead, the abrupt rise in current was associated with the growth of droplets that est…

title: Towards sustainable public transit: development of representative driving cycles for electric and CNG buses using naturalistic micro-trip data from Patna, India
abstract: Abstract With the increasing emphasis on sustainable urban mobility, electric buses are rapidly being integrated into public transportation networks in Indian cities. A critical component in evaluating their energy consumption and operational efficiency is the development of representative driving cycles that reflect local driving conditions. This study presents a data-driven methodology to construct real-world driving cycles for electric and CNG buses operating on mixed urban and rural roads in Patna, India. High-frequency trajectory data, collected over a 1000 km stretch using VBOX GPS loggers, were segmented into micro-trips. The study proposed two methods, Modified Random Selection and k-means clustering, to identify representative segments for cycle construction. The resulting Patna Electric Bus Driving Cycle (PEBDC) and Patna CNG Bus Driving Cycle (PCBDC) are benchmarked against both Indian and international standards. It is observed that the Patna cycles exhibited lower average speeds and reduced time spent in acceleration and deceleration phases, when compared to driving cycles of other Indian cities.

Targeted post-weaning intervention of weaners with low growth rate pre-weaning is a profitable strategy to increase the productivity of Merino sheep
abstract: Context The post-weaning period is critical for the lifetime productivity of Merino sheep, yet weaners with low weaning weights present a significant management and economic challenge for producers. Strategies to mitigate poor performance in these ‘tail-end’ animals are essential for improving overall flock efficiency. Aims This study aimed to evaluate the biological and economic merit of preferentially feeding and managing Merino weaners with a low growth rate pre-weaning to enhance their bodyweight and wool production, and to determine whether any production gains were maintained post-treatment. Methods In total, 332 Merino weaners were separated 1 week after weaning at 3 months of age into the following three groups for a 14-week period: a group of low growth pre-weaning (LOW), a group of high growth pre-weaning (HIGH), and a mixed high and low growth pre-weaning control group (CTRL). The LOW group received a supplement averaging 200 g/head.day (provided three times per week) and fortnightly anthelmintic treatments. The HIGH and CTRL groups were managed under industry best practice. Bodyweight, growth rates, and wool characteristics were measured. Key results The LOW group exhibited significantly higher growth rates (70.5 ± 2.0 g/day; P < 0.0001) during the treatment period (Period 1), demonstrating effective compensatory growth. Consequently, the LOW group attained a sig…

title: Preferential phosphodiesterase inhibition as a novel strategy to modulate key pathways in systemic sclerosis
abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a complex autoimmune disease marked by vasculopathy, immune dysregulation, and progressive fibrosis of the skin and internal organs. The high disease burden and impact on quality of life highlight the need for therapies that target underlying pathogenic mechanisms rather than merely treating organ-specific symptoms. Phosphodiesterases, including phosphodiesterase 4B (PDE4B), are key regulators of cellular function and inflammatory responses of several cell types central to SSc pathogenesis. Given PDE4B’s broad effects, targeting it may provide benefits beyond organ-specific manifestations and improve current care. Selective PDE4B inhibition represents a novel therapeutic approach for SSc, with improved subtype selectivity compared with earlier pan-PDE4 inhibitors. Nerandomilast preferentially inhibits PDE4B (ninefold over PDE4D), potentially improving tolerability versus oral pan-PDE4 inhibitors by avoiding adverse events such as gastrointestinal intolerance. Preclinical findings in SSc-relevant mouse and cell models show that PDE4B inhibition modulates inflammatory cytokine secretion, smooth muscle cell tension, endothelial and epithelial barrier integrity, and extracellular matrix synthesis under oxidative stress; this suggests nerandomilast could attenuate immune dysregulation, fibrosis, and potentially impact vasculopathy. Two pivotal Phase III t…

title: More, shorter, newer? How monetization reshapes creator strategy on YouTube Shorts
abstract: Purpose This study examines the causal impact of YouTube Shorts' ad-revenue sharing policy on creator production strategies in the short-form video creator economy. Design/methodology/approach Using 36,507 videos from 342 top global channels, we employ a regression discontinuity in time design. Computer vision techniques measure four attributes of each creator's production strategy: output volume, video length, editing pace, and content novelty. Findings The policy drove an immediate reduction in video length without expanding output volume, consistent with substitution toward cheaper per-unit configurations rather than output scaling. Entertainment creators shortened their videos most sharply, while informative creators slowed their editing pace to preserve comprehension. Long-type creators pursued per-unit cost reduction, while short-type creators invested in content novelty. Research limitations/implications The sample covers top-tier global channels, so emerging creators may respond differently. The findings show that the quantity-expansion result from low-marginal-cost user-generated content settings does not extend to high-marginal-cost production, where incentives reallocate effort within existing output rather than expand it. Practical implications A uniform monetization policy does not produce uniform outcomes. Incentive design should anticipate that creators adjust di…

title: Damned if you do, damned if you don’t: the interpretive dilemma of strategic and compassionate leadership
abstract: Purpose This paper challenges the perceived antagonism between strategic leadership and compassionate leadership. It argues that the tension is not inevitable in organizational decision-making, but arises from essentialist assumptions that treat strategy and compassion as fixed leadership attributes. Design/methodology/approach This scholarly essay develops a conceptual argument grounded in social constructionist and attributional perspectives on leadership. Organizational episodes are used illustratively, rather than as empirical cases, to show how leadership discourse and observer interpretation can produce and stabilize the apparent conflict between strategic and compassionate leadership. Findings Two leadership myths are identified: that strategy requires emotional distance and that compassion undermines strategic resolve. These myths are sustained through attributional habits, institutional reinforcement, professional socialization, and psychological defense. When leadership is reframed as interpretive rather than essential, the perceived incompatibility diminishes. Integration is shown to be provisional, audience-dependent, and contingent upon interpretation. Practical implications People in leadership positions cannot ensure that their actions will be interpreted as both strategically necessary and compassionately enacted, although framing, communication, and attention t…

title: Entrepreneurial leadership, AI adoption, and innovation performance: evidence from Indian entrepreneurial ventures
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to explore the effect of Entrepreneurial Leadership (EL) on Innovation Performance (IP) with the mediation of Organizational Learning Culture (OLC) and the moderation of Artificial Intelligence Adoption (AIA). There is little empirical evidence encompassing the complex elements of EL and OLC in the context of Indian companies. The authors believe that this study can support leaders in implementing the right strategies to foster a learning culture and drive innovation. Design/methodology/approach An empirical study of 241 employees working in entrepreneurial ventures across India was conducted using a survey questionnaire. Structural Equation Modeling was used to examine the mediation and moderation effects using the SPSS AMOS statistical package. Findings The findings of this study align with existing research in that EL does affect the OLC, and AIA plays a moderator role in this effect. However, OLC is not found to affect IP. The authors suggest that future researchers in this field can take into account other organizational features to examine the effect more closely. Research limitations/implications This study’s findings are limited by contextual factors and sample demographics. Future research should explore additional organizational traits and technological readiness for a deeper understanding of innovation performance enablers. Origin…

title: From potential value to recognised value: situational value theory
abstract: Purpose To develop Situational Value Theory (SVT), a conceptual explanation of how the value potential of human capability becomes organisationally realised under particular situational conditions. The paper addresses the limited understanding of why equivalent capabilities generate markedly different organisational value despite no substantive change in their underlying knowledge, skills, or behaviours. Design/methodology/approach This paper adopts a conceptual theory-building approach. It synthesises literature on human capability, organisational value, and valuation to develop SVT. The theory distinguishes between value potential, the latent capacity of human capability to contribute to organisational outcomes, and organisationally realised value, which emerges through the interaction of capability, situational conditions, and recognition. Findings SVT proposes that organisational value is not a stable property of individuals or competencies but is realised through the alignment of capability with situational conditions and the recognition of contribution by organisational actors. The theory explains why human capabilities generate different organisational value across contexts without assuming changes in the capabilities themselves. Originality/value SVT reconceptualises the relationship between human capability and organisational value by explaining not how human capabilit…

title: Treatment stacking in aesthetics: improved patient outcomes or practice strategy?
abstract: As aesthetic treatment options continue to expand, combination treatment can offer valuable benefits, but more is not always better. This article explores how patient-led consultation, evidence-based treatment planning and staged interventions can help practitioners determine which treatments are truly needed.

title: Bifurcation Analysis and Chaos Control of H-Bridge Inverter with Improved Power Reaching Law Sliding Mode Control
abstract: To address the nonlinear instability phenomena existing in the H-bridge inverter under improved power reaching law sliding mode control, a discrete iterative mathematical model of the system is derived based on the stroboscopic mapping theory. Through bifurcation diagrams, folding diagrams, frequency spectra, and the fast-varying stability theorem, the mechanism of how control parameters influence the dynamical behavior of the inverter system is analyzed. The research results indicate that an excessively large sliding mode gain will cause the system to enter a chaotic state via period-doubling bifurcations, significantly degrading the operational stability and efficiency of the inverter. To mitigate this potential instability, a conventional one-step discrete time-delayed feedback control (dTDFC) realization is adopted as an auxiliary feedback in the improved power reaching law sliding mode controller. By introducing a differential feedback between the state variable and its delayed state, this feedback regulates the discrete dynamical evolution process of the system, thereby improving its operating state. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the composite controller, providing a theoretical basis for the parameter optimization and engineering design of the H-bridge inverter under improved power reaching law sliding mode control.

Competing through quick commerce: evidence from urban nanostores
abstract: Purpose Q-commerce research often treats speed as the outcome of logistics infrastructure, platform scale and technological sophistication. This study challenges that view by examining how quick-commerce capability operates in urban nanostores and how it shapes consumer purchase intention through perceived nanostore competitiveness. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from 340 consumers across 60 nanostores in Bandung, Indonesia. The conceptual model was analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Findings Consumer convenience, delivery satisfaction and digital service quality strengthen perceived nanostore competitiveness. Perceived nanostore competitiveness then increases two dimensions of purchase intention: product-digital appeal and price-based intention. The mediation effects are heterogeneous. Perceived nanostore competitiveness mediates the effects of consumer convenience and delivery satisfaction, but not the effect of digital service quality. This suggests that digital service quality can generate direct experiential appeal without necessarily being interpreted as a relative retail advantage. Research limitations/implications The study is limited to consumers of urban nanostores in one developing economy. It distinguishes perceived immediacy from infrastructural scale and positions perceived nanostore competitivenes…

title: Hyperspectral imaging and machine learning in brain tumor surgery: Current evidence, clinical applications, and future directions
abstract: Background: Brain tumor surgery aims to achieve maximal safe resection while preserving neurological function; however, accurate intraoperative discrimination between tumor tissue and normal brain remains a major challenge. Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) has emerged as a promising label-free optical imaging modality that provides quantitative information on tissue biochemical and physiological characteristics. The integration of machine learning (ML) has further enhanced its potential for automated tissue classification and real-time intraoperative decision support. This narrative review summarizes the current evidence regarding HSI and ML in brain tumor surgery, highlighting technological principles, clinical applications, current limitations, and future directions. Methods: This narrative review was based on a comprehensive literature search of PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar to identify studies evaluating the application of HSI and artificial intelligence (AI) in brain tumor surgery. The search strategy included combinations of the keywords “ hyperspectral imaging ,” “ brain tumor ,” “ glioma ,” “ machine learning ,” “ deep learning ,” “ artificial intelligence ,” and “ neurosurgery .” Priority was given to peer-reviewed original research articles, narrative and systematic reviews, and clinically relevant investigations describing the technical development, intraoperative ap…

title: MLCL: LVLM-guided multi-level contrastive learning for fake news detection
abstract: Abstract The widespread dissemination of multi-modal disinformation on social media platforms poses a serious threat to public safety and social stability, elevating the need for automated detection of such content. Although existing studies have started to incorporate multimodal data, effectively modeling cross-modal interactions remains difficult, often leading to insufficient mining of information within individual modalities. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel LVLM-Guided multi-level contrastive learning network (MLCL). Within the textual modality, BERT and CLIP encoders extract features at varying granularities, while ResNet and CLIP encoders capture visual representations. Additionally, a Large Vision-Language Model is leveraged to derive text-based representations that reflect both local details and global contexts from images. We further introduce a multi-level alignment strategy: inside each modality, a normalized InfoNCE loss aligns features from the two encoders to reduce redundancy. Before cross-modal fusion, we jointly align the three modality-level features using both InfoNCE loss and batch-hard triplet loss, thereby explicitly modeling their consistency and relative distance. A modality-wise attention module is also incorporated to adaptively reweight and aggregate features. Experiments on two real-world datasets show that our approach outperforms…

title: Predicting Chemical Stressor Effects on Conjugative Plasmid Transfer Rates Using Machine Learning
abstract: Abstract Chemical stressors in environmental and clinical settings can alter conjugative plasmid transfer, which is a key process driving antibiotic resistance dissemination. However, predicting these effects across chemically diverse compounds is challenging. Here, we compiled and curated data on the effect of chemical stressors on RP4 plasmid transfer, extracting compound identity, concentration, conjugation frequency, and experimental metadata from 73 in vitro studies. Chemicals were characterized by functional use categories and molecular descriptors, including physicochemical properties, MACCS keys, Morgan fingerprints, and extended descriptors from the OCHEM platform (AlvaDesc, Dragon 7, and 3D-shape descriptors). An exhaustive evaluation of 1022 feature set combinations across 3066 models showed that chemical concentration alone provides no meaningful predictive signal (Q2ext <0), whereas integrating Morgan fingerprints substantially improves predictive performance. The best-performing model combined concentration, Morgan fingerprints, and experimental conditions using extreme gradient boosting (XGB), achieving Q2ext = 0.373 on a held-out compound-aware test set and a median Q2ext of 0.319 within the defined applicability domain across 20 independent splits. SHAP analysis revealed that Morgan fingerprints account for 69% of total predictive weight, with quaternary amm…

title: Immune and inflammatory features associated with pyroptosis- and myocardial fibrosis-related genes in HFpEF: a machine learning study
abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous syndrome marked by inflammation, immune dysregulation, and myocardial fibrosis. Whether pyroptosis intersects with fibrotic remodeling in HFpEF remains uncertain. Two murine cardiac transcriptomic datasets were integrated after batch correction and intersected with curated pyroptosis- and myocardial fibrosis-related gene sets. Functional enrichment, univariate logistic regression, support vector machine–recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE), and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression were used for feature selection. Complete separation in the ordinary three-gene logistic fit prompted refitting with Firth bias-reduced logistic regression. Performance was assessed by apparent area under the curve (AUC), stratified bootstrap optimism correction, and repeated nested cross-validation; the panel was re-estimated in a human left-ventricular dataset for exploratory replication. Cell-type Identification by Estimating Relative Subsets of RNA Transcripts (CIBERSORT) estimated immune-cell fractions, and expression was examined in a high-fat diet (HFD)/N ω -nitro-L-arginine methyl ester hydrochloride (L-NAME) murine model and whole blood from patients with HFpEF. Six candidates— Pparg , Ace2 , Smad2 , Lcn2 , Ptpn11 , and Sqstm1 —were identified. Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Gen…

title: Desinformacion y Alfabetización Mediática: Clasificación de Patrones de Confianza en Noticias entre Adolescentes mediante Machine Learning
abstract: Este estudio examina la detección de noticias falsas entre adolescentes utilizando técnicas de Machine Learning. Se plantean dos preguntas fundamentales: cómo reaccionan los jóvenes ante la desinformación y qué nivel de confianza tienen en la veracidad de las noticias. A través de un análisis detallado con algoritmos de aprendizaje automático, como k-means, Decision Trees y Random Forest, se clasificaron las respuestas de los participantes, revelando patrones significativos en su confianza hacia los medios de comunicación. Los hallazgos sobre esta muestra indican que aproximadamente el 15% de los adolescentes no confían plenamente en las noticias y casi el 50% carece de habilidades para identificar información falsa. Esto resalta la necesidad urgente de implementar programas de alfabetización mediática que fortalezcan la capacidad crítica de los jóvenes para discernir la veracidad de la información en un entorno digital saturado de desinformación. Además, el estudio sugiere que futuras investigaciones deben explorar otros algoritmos de Machine Learning y evaluar el impacto de intervenciones educativas en la alfabetización mediática.

title: Machine Learning-Based Modeling and Multi-Criteria Optimization of Wire-EDM Parameters
abstract: Wire-EDM (Wire Electrical Discharge Machining) plays a crucial role in the precision manufacturing of complex geometries, particularly for materials that are difficult to machine using conventional methods. Intelligent modeling and optimization of process parameters are required to improve performance, especially to maximize Material Removal Rate (MRR) and minimize kerf width. This study presents a machine learning (ML)-driven approach for predictive modeling and multi-objective optimization of Wire-EDM input settings. Using 31 experimental data points from existing literature, the influence of four important parameters i.e. V g (Average gap-voltage), W f (wire feed-rate), T on (pulse-on time) and T off (pulse-off time) on MRR and kerf width was systematically investigated. Three advanced regression techniques i.e. RFR (random forest regression), SVR (support vector regression), and GBR (gradient boosting regression) are utilized to capture the complex nonlinear relationships between inputs and outputs. Among these, the SVR model demonstrated superior performance, achieving a high R 2 value of approximately 0.92, indicating strong predictive accuracy. To interpret the model and assess feature significance, SHAP analysis is conducted, identifying gap voltage as the most influential factor affecting both MRR and kerf width. The optimized parameters generated by the SVR model led …

title: Generative AI in creative education: baseline-linked evidence on learning processes, artistic performance, and authorship
abstract: Introduction Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly shaping creative learning in higher education art courses, yet its educational value remains contested when creative support, output generation, authorship, and skill development become intertwined. This study investigates AI-supported creative learning in an undergraduate art course. Methods The study used linked data from 133 students, including prior course performance, final creative-performance assessment, and post-project questionnaire responses. AI use was operationalized through two dimensions: assistive use for ideation, refinement, process management, and technique learning, and content-generative use involving AI contributions to creative output. The analysis combined baseline-adjusted outcome models, performance-change models, propensity-score adjustment, AI-use intensity comparisons, and robustness checks across alternative AI-use definitions. Results The findings show a clear process-outcome decoupling pattern. AI use was associated with stronger perceived support and skill transfer, while final artistic performance and baseline-to-final performance change showed no corresponding improvement. Content-generative AI use was associated with lower evaluated authorship, suggesting that AI-shaped artifacts may reduce the visibility of students' creative decision-making in final outcomes.
