title: Full-protein release assay in a reconstituted yeast translation system using GGQ-methylated eRF1
abstract: Translation termination in eukaryotes requires the concerted action of release factors eRF1 and eRF3, together with accessory factors including eIF5A and Rli1, to achieve efficient peptide release from the ribosome. Here, we establish a yPURE system-based Termi-nLuc assay, in which pre-termination complexes (PreTCs), carrying full-length nanoluciferase (nLuc) peptidyl-tRNA, are formed by simply omitting release factors from the reconstituted yeast translation system, enabling rapid and sensitive analysis without the need for sucrose density gradient purification. To enable direct biochemical analysis of GGQ methylation—a physiologically important modification of eRF1 whose effects on peptide release activity had not previously been examined in vitro —we also established an Escherichia coli co-expression system of eRF1 and its GGQ-methylating enzyme, yielding fully GGQ-methylated eRF1. Using this platform, we characterized the individual and combined contributions of eRF1, eRF3, eIF5A, and Rli1 to peptide release, and demonstrated that the full complement of these factors is sufficient for efficient release. Under the current assay conditions, neither GGQ methylation of eRF1 nor the identity of the penultimate amino acid of the protein detectably affected peptide release activity, consistent with the possibility that eRF1•eRF3 recruitment to the ribosome, rather than the chemica…

title: Microfluidics-Integrated Microwave Cytometry for Dielectric Characterization at the Micron Scale
Analisis Return On Investment Menggunakan Pendekatan Du Pont System Pada Perusahaan Agribisnis Di Bursa Efek Indonesia
abstract: This study aims to analyze the financial performance of agribusiness companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange using the Du Pont System approach. ROI is broken down into two main components: Net Profit Margin (NPM) and Total Asset Turnover (TATO). The objects of this research are PT Astra Agro Lestari Tbk, PT Sampoerna Agro Tbk, and PT Bakrie Sumatera Plantations Tbk during the 2020–2024 period. Data were obtained from annual financial reports and analyzed using descriptive quantitative methods. The results indicate that PT Astra Agro Lestari has relatively stable ROI performance, PT Sampoerna Agro shows significant increases in certain years due to production cost efficiency, while PT Bakrie Sumatera Plantations has low ROI due to high expenses and suboptimal asset utilization. Therefore, it can be concluded that the Du Pont System approach provides a comprehensive overview of the impact of cost efficiency and asset effectiveness on the financial performance of agribusiness companies.
venue: Journal of Agribusiness and Rural Development (Jurnal Agribisnis dan Pengembangan Pedesaan)

title: Decoded Antarctic snow accumulation history reconciles observed and modeled trends in accumulation and large-scale warming patterns
abstract: Increased snow accumulation on the Antarctic Ice Sheet mitigated global sea level rise by ∼ 11 mm during 1901–2000 according to ice core reconstructions. However, in the most recent 40 years of more intense observation and warming, the trend in the Antarctic-wide accumulation rate has been negligible. We attribute these trends by evaluating Earth system model experiments in comparison with dynamically consistent reconstructions of surface climate. Single-forcing experiments reveal that rising concentrations of greenhouse gases (GHGs) have been the underlying driver of increased accumulation, yet acting alone would have caused twice the observed accumulation-related sea level mitigation during 1901–2000. Aerosol-driven cooling partially compensates this overprediction, but the reconstructions provide evidence that poorly modeled processes can explain observation-model trend discrepancies. In particular, these data support a hypothesis that high-latitude winds have been working together with ice-shelf meltwater fluxes to dampen Southern Ocean surface warming and suppress the GHG-driven accumulation increase since the initiation of West Antarctic ice shelf thinning in the mid-20th Century. The wind pattern associated with strengthening of the Southern Hemisphere westerlies and deepening of the Amundsen Sea Low distributes accumulation unevenly across the continent in an orographic…

title: A Multi-Chip Cascadable MIC6_V4 ASIC for the NICA-MPD Inner Tracking System
abstract: To meet the upgrade requirements for the Inner Tracking System (ITS) of the Multi-Purpose Detector (MPD) at the Nuclotron-based Ion Collider facility (NICA) for extremely high spatial resolution and low material budget, we present a monolithic active pixel sensor array chip, MIC6 V4, using GSMC 130 nm CMOS process. The chip features a pixel array size of 497 rows by 980 columns, with individual pixels measuring 30.53 μm × 26.8 μm, and the overall die area of 30mm × 15 mm. The MIC6_V4 chip communicates with external readout electronics through a high-speed data output interface with a maximum data rate of 1.2Gb/s, and also supports data transfer between chips via a bidirectional parallel bus with a clock frequency of 40 MHz. This paper primarily describes the digital peripheral design and implementation of the MIC6_V4 chip, presenting a digital readout architecture that accommodates varying pixel hit rates within the Inner Tracking System (ITS) and supports both single-chip standalone operation and multi-chip interconnection.
venue: International Journal of Modern Physics A

title: Seasonal influence on post-fire debris flow likelihood after the 2020 Lake Fire
abstract: The increasing severity of wildfires in Western North America is widely hypothesized to lead to an increase in the likelihood of post-fire debris flows (PFDF), specifically those triggered by high-intensity rain. PFDF likelihoods are highest in the first year and tend to decrease over time. However, it is not well understood how seasonal variation affects PFDF initiation in the years following a fire. Here, we investigated how different physical parameters influence seasonal PFDF likelihood, informed by four years of field and satellite observations from the 2020 Lake Fire in Southern California. We found that unsaturated hydraulic conductivity was an order of magnitude greater during the dry season than during the wet season, significantly reducing the PFDF likelihood. Our simulations show that vegetation cover has less of an impact on PFDF likelihood than hydraulic conductivity or grain size. This study helps clarify the relative importance of hydraulic conductivity, grain size, and vegetation on PFDF as these parameters vary seasonally and evolve over four years after the fire. Our results suggest that seasonal variation plays a major role in determining PFDF likelihood and therefore, climatic and seasonal patterns need to be considered in future field and modeling studies.
venue: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences

title: Global research landscape of ferroptosis in colorectal cancer: a multi-database bibliometric analysis (2017–2025)
abstract: Objective Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death, has attracted increasing attention in recent years because of its critical roles in tumor progression, therapeutic resistance, and immune regulation. Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most prevalent malignancies worldwide and imposes a substantial mortality burden. This study aimed to systematically analyze the global research landscape, hotspots, and developmental trends of ferroptosis in CRC research from 2017 to 2025. Methods English-language publications related to ferroptosis and CRC published between January 1, 2017, and December 31, 2025, were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and Scopus databases. A total of 1, 354 original articles and reviews were included. VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and the bibliometrix package in R were used for bibliometric and visualization analyses to evaluate annual publication trends, country/region and institutional collaboration networks, author contributions, journal distribution, co-cited references, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic evolution. Results The number of publications in this field increased rapidly after 2020 and peaked in 2025. China ranked first in both publication output and total citations, followed by the United States, and China–United States collaboration constituted the core of the international collaboration network. Central …

title: A Multi-Source Heterogeneous Data Empowerment Method for AI Product Profiling that Integrates Distant Supervision and Large Language Models
abstract: Abstract Purpose This paper aims to support AI-product evaluation and management by automatically extracting AI products and their multi-dimensional attributes from multi-source heterogeneous data, supporting personalized product-design optimization and enterprise market insight. Design/methodology/approach An end-to-end AI-product profiling framework is built over a constructed multi-source heterogeneous dataset. It integrates a Document Image Transformer (DiT) and large language models (e.g., Qwen, ChatGPT) for webpage data, report layout analysis and target-chart recognition; chart processing filters relevance at the title level, with attributes taken from captions and surrounding text rather than pixel content. Product names are extracted by a domain-adapted distantly supervised pipeline (AI-product lexicon, dependency-based context filtering and LLM-assisted boundary disambiguation with BERT/RoBERTa-CRF), and fine-grained attributes by a LoRA-fine-tuned Qwen-32B model. Findings On the constructed dataset, the framework attains F1 above 90 % on all three core tasks: target-chart recognition (BERT, 96.5 %), product-name extraction (RoBERTa + CRF, 91.7 %) and attribute extraction (Qwen-32B, 92.4 %). The distantly supervised pipeline is competitive with larger generative models while relying mainly on weakly labelled data and targeted human verification. Research limitations P…
venue: Journal of Data and Information Science

title: Heterogeneous hydroformylation of propene over surface rhodium coordinated by immobilized multi-N ligands
abstract: Olefin hydroformylation is an extremely important reaction for producing bulk oxygen-containing organic functional molecules and homogeneous rhodium catalysts with organic phosphorous ligands are most commonly used. We report here a highly active heterogeneous catalyst for propene hydroformylation with Rh immobilized by alumina bonded 3-trimethoxysilylpropyl-diethyle-netriamine, of which ligand is more readily available, inexpensive, low toxic and no loss in reaction. The catalyst Rh-NQ62/Al 2 O 3 shows a TOF value as high as 710 h −1 for propene conversion to C 4 oxygenates in selectivity higher than 99% in a fixed-bed reactor and sustains stable for at least 1000 h without any deactivation. Characterization and theoretical calculation reveal that the atomically dispersed Rh species in surface-bound configurations by the multi-N ligand effectively promotes the heterolytic cleavage of H 2 at the Rh-N site and enhances the overall propene hydroformylation. We envisage the work establishes a blueprint for development of better catalysts using multi-N ligands for heterogeneous hydroformylations.
venue_publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science

title: Transportability Of Pathway-Based Survival Models From RNA Sequencing To Microarrays In Gastric Cancer: A Multi-Cohort Study
abstract: Whether pathway-based survival models developed from RNA sequencing preserve patient risk ordering in external microarray cohorts remains uncertain. Differences in assay platform and patient-cohort composition jointly shape external performance. We quantified joint cross-platform and cross-cohort transportability and compared modelling strategies within a leakage-controlled benchmark. Three pathway encodings, two featureselection states, and five survival learners formed 30 systems developed in TCGA-STAD. The development cohort included 387 patients; four external cohorts included 975 patients. Before external outcome evaluation, the protocol-locked analysis fixed the encodings, feature states, learner set, four GEO cohorts, fitted parameters, and prediction files. Regularised Cox provided the most consistent external discrimination, with an unweighted four-cohort macro Harrell C-index of 0.582, indicating modest preservation of risk ordering. Graph-based and recent neural learners varied across cohorts. Stability selection produced the same external patient ordering as its matched identity-gate Cox model. A separately frozen clinical–molecular model was evaluated in GSE183136 after removal of overlapping expression profiles and failed both prespecified confirmation criteria. This study defines a controlled pipeline for evaluating transcriptomic prognosis across assay platforms…
venue: Journal of Mechanics in Medicine and Biology

title: Research on key node identification method based on multi-attribute fusion in complex networks
abstract: Abstract Accurate assessment of node importance in complex networks is crucial for enhancing network robustness and security, for instance, by protecting critical data nodes or reinforcing core hubs. However, existing importance metrics often struggle to simultaneously accommodate local connectivity, neighborhood influence and global mediation effects. Moreover, they frequently yield similar importance scores for a large number of nodes, resulting in insufficient discriminability and failing to effectively identify key nodes. In this paper, we propose the CRITIC-based Multi-Attribute Fusion Indicator (CR-MAFI) within the CRITIC (Criteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation) framework. CR-MAFI integrates degree centrality, degree and neighborhood information centrality, and betweenness centrality, and employs Shannon entropy and inter-criterion conflict to derive objective weights, thereby enhancing the dominance of high-discriminability metrics in the fusion process. By integrating network structural information from multiple perspectives, the proposed method provides a more comprehensive assessment of node importance. Experiments are conducted on four types of real-world networks, including the aviation network USAir97, social network fb-pages-food, criminal collaboration network crime-moreno and power network 1138_bus. The results show that CR-MAFI achieves stable an…

title: Multi-Domain Representation Learning For Enhanced EEG-Based Emotion Recognition
abstract: In recent years, significant progress has been made in EEG-based emotion classification using convolutional neural networks; however, effectively leveraging multi-domain EEG features to improve emotion recognition accuracy remains challenging. To address this, we propose a dual-branch feature fusion architecture that integrates complementary EEG features. Specifically, the Global Temporal Branch uses a Transformer to capture long-range dependencies, while the Local Multi-domain Branch employs a bidirectional gated recurrent Unit (BiGRU) to extract local temporal dynamics from multi-domain features. Their collaboration enables effective exploitation of complementary EEG information. Finally, experiments on the public SEED and SEED-IV datasets show that the proposed model outperforms existing methods.
venue: Journal of Mechanics in Medicine and Biology

title: POTENTIAL OF POLYHERBAL FORMULATIONS: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW ON THEIR ROLE AS PROMISING THERAPEUTIC AGENTS FOR DIABETES MANAGEMENT
abstract: Polyherbal formulations have emerged as promising therapeutic options for the management of diabetes, offering a multifaceted approach to addressing the complex pathophysiology of the disease. Through a comprehensive review of preclinical and clinical studies, this review highlights the efficacy, safety, and potential applications of polyherbal formulations in diabetes management. Key findings indicate that these formulations, composed of synergistic combinations of herbs, demonstrate significant improvements in glycemic control, insulin sensitivity, and reduction of diabetes-related complications. Importantly, polyherbal formulations exhibit favorable safety profiles, making them suitable for long-term use as adjunctive therapies alongside conventional treatments. Embracing holistic principles, these formulations address not only glycemic control but also overall health and well-being, aligning well with the principles of integrative medicine. Moving forward, opportunities for further research include optimization of formulations, elucidation of mechanistic insights, and large-scale clinical validation to facilitate their integration into mainstream clinical practice. By capitalizing on the synergistic benefits of polyherbal formulations, clinicians and healthcare providers can enhance therapeutic outcomes and improve the quality of life for individuals living with diabetes.
venue: GLOBAL JOURNAL OF PHARMACEUTICAL AND SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH

title: Public Purpose in Indian Land Acquisition Law: A Doctrinal Reassessment
abstract: This article undertakes a doctrinal reassessment of ‘public purpose’ in Indian land acquisition law. It argues that the concept of ‘public purpose’ must function as a meaningful constitutional and statutory limit on State power rather than as an elastic, deferential label. Tracing the jurisprudence from the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 through the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, it shows how the Supreme Court’s treatment of ‘public purpose’ as flexible and vague enabled broad executive discretion in favour of market-oriented development. The analysis highlights where judicial decisions blurred the statutory distinction between acquisition for a public purpose and acquisition for a company. The article proposes a multi-dimensional framework for interpreting ‘public purpose’ under Article 300A that integrates statutory fit and spirit. By recalibrating ‘public purpose’ along these lines, it argues, the judiciary can preserve the State’s capacity for legitimate development while preventing the concept from degenerating into a legal fiction that legitimises unjust dispossession.
venue: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities

title: Dampak Transparansi Manajemen Perubahan Iklim terhadap Kesulitan Keuangan (The Impact of Climate Change Management Transparency on Financial Distress)
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menguji pengaruh transparansi pengungkapan perubahan iklim terhadap financial distress pada perusahaan manufaktur yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia periode 2019–2023. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode regresi data panel. Sampel penelitian berjumlah 23 perusahaan yang dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling berdasarkan ketersediaan laporan tahunan dan laporan keberlanjutan. Financial distress diukur menggunakan Altman Z-Score, sedangkan transparansi pengungkapan perubahan iklim diukur melalui skor pengungkapan berdasarkan indikator yang relevan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pengungkapan perubahan iklim berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap financial distress. Hasil ini mengindikasikan bahwa semakin tinggi transparansi pengungkapan perubahan iklim, semakin baik kondisi keuangan perusahaan dan semakin rendah indikasi financial distress. Temuan penelitian menunjukkan bahwa transparansi iklim dapat menjadi instrumen strategis untuk memperkuat ketahanan keuangan perusahaan dan mendukung pencapaian tujuan pembangunan berkelanjutan.

title: Peran Moderasi Agency Cost terhadap Kinerja Keuangan melalui Agresivitas Pajak dan Green Accounting
abstract: Financial performance is influenced not only by operational and financial decisions but also by tax strategies, environmental practices, and agency relationships. Tax aggressiveness may provide tax-saving benefits, while green accounting can support resource efficiency and environmental risk management; however, both strategies may produce different financial consequences when agency conflicts and information asymmetry are present. This study aims to examine the conceptual role of agency cost in moderating the relationships of tax aggressiveness and green accounting with financial performance. The study adopts a quantitative research design using secondary data from companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange, with purposive sampling based on the availability of financial, tax, and environmental information. The proposed moderation model examines the direct effects of tax aggressiveness and green accounting on financial performance and their interactions with agency cost. The conceptual analysis indicates that the relationship between tax aggressiveness, green accounting, and financial performance is context-dependent and may be influenced by agency costs, corporate governance, industry characteristics, and tax-related risks. Agency cost is therefore expected to condition how effectively tax and environmental strategies are translated into financial performance. Empirical …
venue: SCIENTIFIC JOURNAL OF REFLECTION : Economic, Accounting, Management and Business

title: Pengaruh Kepemilikan Institusional, Financial Distress, dan Pergantian Auditor terhadap Audit Delay
abstract: This study aims to examine the effect of institutional ownership, financial distress, and auditor turnover on audit delay. The population in this study was all property, real estate, and building construction companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2018-2023 period. The sample size for this study was 45 companies obtained through purposive sampling. A total of 225 samples were obtained. The data type in this study was secondary data, using quantitative research methods and an associative approach. The analysis technique used was panel data regression with a significance level of 5%. This study, processed using EViews 12 software. The findings suggest that audit timeliness is shaped more by the continuity and effectiveness of audit processes than by ownership structure or financial difficulties. This highlights the importance of well-managed auditor transitions, adequate documentation, and effective communication between management and auditors. Strengthening these practices can support timely financial reporting and improve the reliability of information available to stakeholders.
venue: SCIENTIFIC JOURNAL OF REFLECTION : Economic, Accounting, Management and Business

title: Kinerja Keuangan Memediasi Pengaruh Kebijakan Dividen dan Pertumbuhan Aset terhadap Harga Saham (Financial Performance Mediates Dividend Policy and Asset Growth on Stock Prices)
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk memperoleh bukti empiris mengenai pengaruh kebijakan dividen dan pertumbuhan aset terhadap harga saham dengan kinerja keuangan sebagai variabel mediasi pada perusahaan sektor consumer non-cyclicals yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia periode 2020–2024. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode asosiatif. Sampel dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling dan diperoleh 33 perusahaan. Analisis data menggunakan regresi data panel dengan bantuan EViews 12. Fixed Effect Model digunakan pada Model 1, sedangkan Random Effect Model digunakan pada Model 2. Pengujian mediasi dilakukan menggunakan uji Sobel. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kebijakan dividen dan pertumbuhan aset tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap harga saham, sedangkan kinerja keuangan berpengaruh signifikan terhadap harga saham. Kebijakan dividen dan pertumbuhan aset tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap kinerja keuangan. Selain itu, kinerja keuangan tidak mampu memediasi pengaruh kebijakan dividen maupun pertumbuhan aset terhadap harga saham.

title: Financial literacy and its determinants amongst Indian students: an empirical inquest
abstract: Purpose The present study endeavoured to assess the financial literacy (FL) of the Indian students. Efforts have also been made to unearth the socioeconomic and demographic factors affecting such FL amongst the students, which were also explored in the study. Design/methodology/approach Secondary data on 3,064 Indian students from the Financial Inclusion Insights, 2017 database was used in the study. The S&P Global Fin Lit Survey FL questions were used to estimate students’ FL. Appropriate statistical techniques and a Generalized Structural Equation Model were used to identify the determinants of such FL. Findings The outcome of the study revealed that the FL score of Indian students was found to be merely 41.2% (just above poor). Of the total sample, nearly 59.8%, 22.2% and 18% exhibited poor, moderate and high levels of FL, respectively. Region, gender, family size, economic status, level of educational attainment and active bank account status were found to be the significant antecedents of such FL. Practical implications The findings help policymakers and educational institutions design targeted FL programmes for Indian students. Originality/value Assessment of FL amongst students, especially in the context of emerging economies like India, is relatively scanty in the literature. The handful of existing studies are region- or institution-specific and therefore lack generali…

title: Deteksi Fraudulent FinaDeteksi Fraudulent Financial Reporting melalui Perspektif Fraud Pentagonancial Reporting melalui Perspektif Fraud Pentagon: Studi pada Perusahaan Sektor Kesehatan di Daftar Efek Syariah
abstract: This research is motivated by the rise in financial reporting fraud cases in the healthcare sector, which ranks fourth globally (12%), and the case of PT Indofarma Tbk in Indonesia. Based on the fraud pentagon theory, there are five elements that trigger fraud: pressure, opportunity, rationalization, capability, and arrogance. This study aims to analyze the influence of these five elements, both partially and simultaneously, on fraudulent financial reporting in healthcare companies listed on the Sharia Securities List (DES) for the 2022-2024 period. The independent variables are proxied by Return on Assets (ROA), Board Outages, total accrual to total assets, director change, and frequency of CEO's picture, while the dependent variable is proxied by financial statement restatements. The research method used is descriptive quantitative with a purposive sampling technique. Secondary data in the form of audited annual reports were analyzed using panel data logistic regression through EViews 14 software. The partial results of the study showed that ROA, board out, director’s change, and frequent of CEO’s picture had no significant effect, while total accrual to total asset (rationalization) had a significant negative effect on fraudulent financial reporting. Simultaneously, the five fraud pentagon variables had a significant effect with a coefficient of determination of 26.67%.
venue: Inisiatif: Jurnal Ekonomi, Akuntansi dan Manajemen

title: Analisis Faktor-Faktor Manajemen Keuangan Pribadi terhadap Kesejahteraan Keuangan Mahasiswa (Determinants of Financial Well-Being Among University Students)
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh pengetahuan keuangan, sikap keuangan, dan perilaku keuangan terhadap kesejahteraan keuangan mahasiswa di Kota Mataram. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). Data diperoleh dari 106 mahasiswa dan dianalisis melalui evaluasi model pengukuran dan struktural. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pengetahuan keuangan, sikap keuangan, dan perilaku keuangan berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kesejahteraan keuangan mahasiswa. Perilaku keuangan menjadi faktor yang memberikan pengaruh paling kuat. Temuan ini menegaskan pentingnya pengelolaan keuangan yang bertanggung jawab dalam meningkatkan kesejahteraan keuangan mahasiswa.

title: Pengaruh Opini Audit, Temuan BPK, dan PAD terhadap Kinerja Keuangan Pemerintah Daerah (Effect of Audit Opinion, BPK Findings, and PAD on Government Financial Performance)
abstract: Studi ini dirancang untuk menguji sejauh mana opini audit, temuan BPK, dan PAD memengaruhi kinerja keuangan pemerintah kabupaten/kota di Provinsi Kalimantan Barat pada rentang waktu 2020–2024. Pendekatan kuantitatif digunakan melalui regresi data panel model Fixed Effect dengan EViews 14, pada 70 observasi dari 14 kabupaten/kota yang dipilih melalui metode sensus. Kinerja keuangan diproksikan melalui rasio efektivitas PAD. Pengujian parsial menunjukkan temuan bahwa opini audit dan temuan BPK tidak berpengaruh signifikan, sementara PAD berpengaruh positif signifikan. Pengujian simultan menunjukkan ketiga variabel berpengaruh signifikan. Kapasitas fiskal daerah melalui PAD terbukti menjadi faktor penentu utama efektivitas kinerja keuangan pemerintah daerah.

title: Does digital tax enforcement alleviate corporate financial misconduct? An information perspective
abstract: Purpose This study examines whether digital tax enforcement (DTE) reduces corporate financial misconduct (CFM) using China's Golden Tax Project III as a quasi-natural experiment. It also investigates the mediating role of internal controls and the moderating role of analyst scrutiny. Design/methodology/approach The sample includes 35,979 firm-year observations of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2011 to 2022. A difference-in-differences model is employed, with CFM measured by the number of misconduct cases, DTE by GTP III implementation, and analyst scrutiny by the number of analyst reports. Control variables include leverage, ROA, cash flow, firm age, size, and Tobin's Q, with firm, year, and industry fixed effects. Findings The findings show that DTE significantly reduces corporate financial misconduct, with improved internal controls serving as a key mechanism. Analyst scrutiny amplifies this deterrent effect, indicating a complementary relationship between digital enforcement and external monitoring. Interestingly, analyst scrutiny alone is associated with more misconduct, suggesting a dual role. The results remain robust across various sensitivity tests, including parallel trend and placebo checks. Originality/value This study is the first to use a quasi-natural experiment to reveal that digital tax enforcement curbs corporate financial misconduct, with internal control a…

title: DESIGN, FORMULATION AND EVALUATION OF MEFENAMIC ACID EMULGEL FOR IMPROVED TOPICAL DELIVERY AND ANTI-INFLAMMATORY EFFICACY
abstract: Mefenamic acid is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug with poor aqueous solubility and lipophilic properties, which may limit its suitability for conventional topical delivery. The present study was undertaken to develop and evaluate a Mefenamic acid emulgel for improved topical drug delivery. Ten formulations (F1F10) were prepared using Carbopol 934 as the gelling agent, isopropyl myristate as the oil phase, and Tween 80 and Span 80 as emulsifying agents. The prepared formulations were evaluated for physical appearance, homogeneity, pH, viscosity, spreadability, extrudability, drug content, in-vitro drug release, and stability. All formulations showed satisfactory physical characteristics with acceptable pH and good homogeneity. The drug content of the formulations ranged from 96.5% to 99.7%. Formulation F5 showed satisfactory overall characteristics, with a pH of 6.5, viscosity of 24,890 cP, spreadability of 22.4 g•cm/sec, extrudability of 91.2%, and drug content of 99.6%. F5 exhibited 98.2% cumulative drug release after 12 h and was selected as the optimized formulation based on its overall physicochemical and release profile. Stability studies showed that F5 maintained satisfactory physical appearance, pH, viscosity, and drug content without phase separation during storage. The results indicate that the developed Mefenamic acid emulgel provides satisfactory formulation c…
venue: GLOBAL JOURNAL OF PHARMACEUTICAL AND SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH

title: Optimize the least required quantity of decoupling capacitors in PDN design
abstract: A least required quantity (LRQ) calculation of each decoupling capacitor (decap), considering power distribution network (PDN) lumped circuit model parameters is presented in this passage. The proposed method uses equivalent impedance which contains the impedance of Voltage Regulator Model (VRM) and the impedance of the Power/Ground Planes for the LRQ calculation. As to meet the PDN design requirements, the equivalent impedance combined with each capacitor’s impedance in parallel must not exceed the target impedance. Therefore, a more accurate LRQ calculation is presented. The results show that it can minimize the numbers of decoupling capacitors used in a PDN design and reduce the area occupied on board, compared with the conventional LRQ calculations. The simulations also demonstrate that the variation of the inductance between the VRM output and IC can affect the low frequency decap’s LRQ while the variation of plane capacitance can affect the high frequency decap’s LRQ. In general, the advantage of the proposed method is that it takes PDN circuit parameters into consideration which provides a new perspective of optimizing the numbers of decoupling capacitors in PDN design.
venue: Journal of Circuits, Systems and Computers

title: Framework for user-centred design and pre-occupancy design evaluation of higher education buildings
abstract: Purpose Higher education (HE) buildings often exhibit persistent performance gaps that compromise user comfort, health and satisfaction. These adverse outcomes are frequently linked to inadequate end-user engagement in the design phase. This study develops and validates a holistic framework for end-user engagement that systematically integrates user inputs throughout the design process to enable user-centred design and pre-occupancy evaluation, proactively mitigating performance gaps. Design/methodology/approach The framework was formulated through an integrative review and idea mapping from three knowledge areas: user engagement theories, functional performance specification and design elements. The framework was validated through 70 structured interviews: 35 with end-users, 17 with HE building professionals, and 18 with industry architects. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Kruskal–Wallis and Dunn tests. Qualitative insights were examined through content analysis. Findings The study presents a novel framework featuring a process-flow model and modules for user-requirements acquisition and design evaluation to engage end-users throughout HE building design. The framework’s overall effectiveness for end-user involvement across pre-design, schematic and detailed design was rated 8.4 out of 10. Study participants identified many benefits of the framewo…

title: Integrating digital learning media for local history education: A design framework based on the story of Radin Intan II
abstract: Local history learning in primary education requires learning resources that can connect historical events with cultural meanings, visual representations, and opportunities for active engagement. However, the development of digital media for local history often results in separate instructional products whose pedagogical functions are not explicitly connected. This study aimed to develop an integrated design framework for local history education by synthesizing findings from four digital learning media development studies centered on the historical narrative of Radin Intan II, a national hero associated with the history of Lampung. The study employed a design-oriented research approach informed by Design-Based Research principles and used cross-study synthesis as the main analytical procedure. Empirical findings from four related development studies—Creative Wayang Story, digital comic, 3D flipbook, and educational game—were examined through descriptive quantitative analysis, qualitative coding, and comparative mapping of their pedagogical affordances. Expert validation across the media ranged from 90% to 98%, while student responses ranged from 95% to 97%. The synthesis identified differentiated but complementary functions: narrative-cultural grounding, visual-narrative representation, spatial-temporal elaboration, and interactive exploration, respectively. These findings were…
venue: Premiere Educandum : Jurnal Pendidikan Dasar dan Pembelajaran

title: Evaluation of tillage and cover cropping systems on the overwintering of angular leaf spot, yield, and quality in dark tobacco
abstract: Abstract Angular leaf spot (ALS; Pseudomonas syringae pv. tabaci ) has become an increasingly important disease in dark tobacco [ Nicotiana tabacum L.] production since 2015. Current recommendations for controlling ALS include selecting dark tobacco varieties with low ALS susceptibility and using agricultural streptomycin. In the last decade, resistance to streptomycin has been documented, leaving tobacco producers with chemical options that offer limited efficacy. The objectives of this project were to evaluate the impact of tillage and cover crop types on ALS occurrence, tobacco yield, and leaf quality. Field plots were arranged in a split‐block design with four replications. Tillage type (conventional and no‐tillage) was applied to the main plot, and cover crop treatment (hairy vetch, crimson clover, cereal rye, and fallow) was applied to the subplots. Field inoculations of ALS were applied to separate dark tobacco trials in 2022–2023 and 2023–2024. Inoculated tobacco was terminated and left in the experimental area to serve as ALS inoculum for the subsequent tobacco crop the following year. Tobacco yield was reduced under no‐tillage production in both study years, but cover crop selection did not affect it. Disease progression was not statistically influenced by tillage or cover crop type during the second year of the first trial in 2023. However, conventional tillage reduc…

title: Ex-Situ CO2 Mineralization: Bridging Laboratory Science and Industrial Reality. Part II: Techno-Economics, Life-Cycle Assessment, and Market-Driven Deployment Strategies
abstract: Abstract Ex-situ CO2 mineralization is moving from laboratory demonstration toward early commercial deployment, but gigaton-scale implementation requires credible economics, favorable life-cycle performance, real product markets, and standards-based verification. This second part of a two-part review examines the techno-economic, environmental, market, policy, and certification dimensions of the technology. Processing costs for industrial-residue systems are approximately $30 to $80 per ton of CO2 on a cradle-to-gate basis for facilities colocated with the CO2 source, excluding CO2 capture and product credits, at a nominal 100 ktCO2/year scale and $0.08/kWh electricity; costs outside these boundary conditions differ substantially and are reported separately throughout. Revenue from carbonated aggregates, supplementary cementitious materials, precipitated calcium carbonate, and carbon-removal credits can offset a significant portion of these costs. Net carbon-removal efficiencies range from approximately 50% to 95% across pathways, a spread driven principally by feedstock activation demand and grid carbon intensity rather than by carbonation chemistry; residue-based systems integrating renewable energy typically achieve 75% to 95%, whereas activation-intensive natural silicate routes remain more energy sensitive. Commercial operators (CarbonFree, Fortera, Neustark, Greenore) sta…

title: ESG Integration and Risk‐Adjusted Portfolio Performance in an Emerging‐Market Institutional Context: Evidence From Brazil's Corporate Sustainability Index
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how ESG integration is associated with portfolio performance in an emerging market. Unlike conventional ESG versus non‐ESG comparisons, it investigates heterogeneity among sustainable portfolios composed of firms listed in Brazil's Corporate Sustainability Index. Using 400,000 simulated portfolios from 2022 to 2025, we estimate pooled OLS models with year fixed effects across aggregate, decile‐based, and dimension‐level ESG specifications. Higher ISE scores are associated with higher returns, lower risk, and higher Sharpe ratios, although risk‐adjusted gains are stronger at intermediate sustainability levels and become less pronounced in the highest deciles. ESG dimensions also exhibit heterogeneous associations, with business model and innovation and social capital showing the most favorable profiles and corporate governance and top management the least favorable. These findings extend ESG‐performance research by revealing dimension‐specific heterogeneity within sustainable portfolios and show investors that aggregate ESG scores may conceal different performance profiles in emerging markets.
venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management

title: Achieving Flexible Operation by Aggregating Structured Operating Protocols: An Electrolysis Case Study Using Real Market Data
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical devices can play a critical role in providing demand-side flexibility to the power grid, enabling greater integration of renewable power and enhancing system resilience. However, highly dynamic operation that tracks fluctuating market signals can accelerate degradation. To address this challenge, this work proposes a parallel aggregation framework in which multiple device modules operate under predefined structured protocols, defined as stable and periodic operating patterns assigned to individual units. Using a hydrogen electrolysis system participating in the real-time electricity market operated by the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) as a case study, we develop an optimization framework that determines optimal mixing of predefined structured protocols that minimizes total electricity costs. Our results show that the cost of the protocol-based parallel setting closely approximates that of fully flexible operation. This trend is consistently observed across multiple protocol sets and different market days, demonstrating the wide applicability of the proposed concept. The proposed approach can also enhance predictability and practical implementation.

title: ESG Disclosure and Audit Fees: The Moderating Role of Board Gender Diversity in an Emerging Market Context
abstract: Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure has become increasingly important in corporate reporting and accountability; however, evidence regarding its implications for audit pricing remains mixed and is particularly limited in emerging markets, where ESG reporting and assurance practices are still evolving. This study investigates the association between ESG disclosure and audit fees and examines whether board gender diversity moderates this relationship in the Egyptian institutional context. Using a panel dataset of 80 non-financial firms listed on the Egyptian Exchange (EGX100) from 2018 to 2023, comprising 480 firm-year observations, the study applies pooled ordinary least squares and fixed-effects regression models. Sensitivity analyses and instrumental variable estimation are employed as additional robustness and endogeneity checks. The findings indicate a significant positive association between ESG disclosure and audit fees, consistent with the argument that ESG reporting may entail additional audit complexity and risk assessment. Board gender diversity is negatively associated with audit fees and significantly attenuates the positive association between ESG disclosure and audit fees. This moderating pattern is consistent with the view that gender-diverse boards may strengthen governance and the credibility of corporate disclosure, although the underlying au…
venue: Journal of Risk and Financial Management

title: A framework for unit-level biodiversity credit integrity and market-level governance
abstract: Abstract Biodiversity credits (BCs) are one innovative financing scheme that the Global Biodiversity Framework proposes to mobilise private capital and narrow the biodiversity financing gap. BCs and the voluntary biodiversity markets (VBMs) around them are nascent, offering an opportunity to learn from shortcomings of the adjacent voluntary carbon markets and design them for both ecological and social integrity from the outset. This paper examines the requirements for the effective functioning of BCs and VBMs at the unit and market levels. We propose a requirements framework based on a horizon scan and semi-structured interviews with market participants. Key five unit-level criteria, comprising four environmental integrity criteria (measurement and monitoring, durability, additionality and leakage minimisation) and one social integrity criterion (environmental and social safeguards), are proposed. At the market level, three components underpin functioning VBMs: clearly defined, fairly allocated and easily transferable rights. Building on lessons from carbon markets, we derived mitigation measures to guide the development of an improved market architecture.

title: Board Expertise and Firm Profitability: The Moderating Roles of Product Market Competition and Institutional Quality
abstract: This paper investigates the association between board expertise and firm profitability. Using an international sample of 42,623 firm-year observations from 2002 to 2021, we find that firms with greater industry and financial expertise on their boards exhibit significantly higher profitability. This finding suggests that board expertise function as an important internal governance mechanism through which firms strengthen managerial oversight, improve strategic decision-making, and ultimately create shareholder value. We further show that the effectiveness of board expertise depends on the external governance environment. Specifically, the profitability-enhancing effect of board expertise is more pronounced in competitive product markets, consistent with a complementary relationship between market discipline and board-level governance. Product market competition appears to enhance the effectiveness of skilled directors in monitoring management and making strategic decisions that create shareholder value. Conversely, the positive relationship between board expertise and firm profitability is less pronounced among firms operating in countries with stronger institutional quality, consistent with a substitution view whereby effective legal systems, regulatory frameworks, investor protection, and enforcement reduce the incremental governance benefits of skilled boards.
venue: Journal of Risk and Financial Management

title: From ESG Commitment to Sustainable Construction Practices: Evidence from an Emerging European Market
abstract: This study examines the relationship between ESG integration and sustainable construction practices in the Bulgarian construction sector. The analysis is based on 143 valid responses from representatives of construction companies operating in Bulgaria. The study employed descriptive statistics and comparative analysis based on enterprise size, as well as correlation and regression analysis. The average index for ESG integration is 3.44, and for sustainable construction practices, it is 3.40. Management commitment, social policies, safety, energy efficiency, and waste management are more developed. Reporting, circular practices, green certification, and carbon control remain less institutionalized. A positive correlation was found between the two indices (r = 0.615; 95% CI [0.501; 0.708]; p < 0.001). The results obtained do not allow for the establishment of a cause-and-effect relationship between the two.
venue: Journal of Risk and Financial Management

title: Addressing the Kessler Syndrome Through Market-Based Removal Obligation Trading
abstract: One of the most alarming scenarios facing space operations is the onset of Kessler syndrome, wherein the density of objects in low Earth orbit leads to collisions that generate further debris, increasing the likelihood of a cascading chain reaction. This self-sustaining cycle could render critical orbital regions unusable, severely hindering current and future space activities. Urgent action and innovative policies are required to preserve space as a viable resource. While technologies for active debris removal are advancing, an effective legal and economic framework is equally necessary to assign liability and incentivize cleanup. Currently, ultimate responsibility largely resides with the launching state of the debris, creating a complex and often inefficient system of accountability that discourages remediation. This article proposes the creation of a formal clearinghouse for debris mitigation responsibilities under a sovereign backstopped model. Within this model, nations or other liable entities post mitigation obligations. Private sector companies specializing in debris removal then bid to fulfill these obligations, assuming the contractual responsibility for removal in exchange for a fee. The launching state retains its underlying treaty liability as a sovereign backstop but delegates execution to competitive private contractors through a centralized, transparent platfor…

title: Between Fire and Electricity: A Cultural-Historical Analysis of Activity, Sense Formation, and Energy Transition among Wayuu Indigenous Women
abstract: Abstract Energy transitions are typically framed as technical processes of infrastructure replacement. This study challenges that framing by examining how Wayuu Indigenous women from the Uriana clan in La Paz–Manaure (La Guajira, Colombia) form personal sense within culturally mediated activity systems as electricity gradually enters their territory. Drawing on Cultural-Historical Activity Theory, we analyse the hearth as a central mediating artefact that integrates embodied knowledge, intergenerational transmission, matrilineal authority, and the reproduction of collective life within the desert ecosystem. Through repeated ethnographic fieldwork (2022–2024), guided by Zemelman’s methodological orientation toward totality, displacement, and epistemic reorientation, we reconstruct two partially overlapping activity systems, fire-based and electricity-based, and examine the contradictions that arise at their intersection. The analysis shows that the introduction of the electric stove simplifies operations at the surface while reconfiguring motive–object relations, altering temporal and sensory structures of activity, and transforming the conditions under which personal sense is formed. These findings contribute to cultural-historical psychology by showing how technological change in marginalised Indigenous territories works as a dialectical transformation of activity, a process t…

title: Landings and First-Sale Prices of Greek Coastal Fisheries: A Multi-Market Time-Series Analysis (2013–2025)
abstract: Understanding how landings and prices of commercially important species co-vary through time is relevant to managing Mediterranean coastal fisheries, yet few studies have examined both jointly across multiple species, markets and years in the eastern Mediterranean. We analyzed monthly landings and nominal, undeflated first-sale prices for eight species at twelve Greek fish markets, from 2013 to 2025 (9313 cleaned records), using descriptive, trend, spatial, multivariate and forecasting methods. Landed quantities were three to six times more variable than prices. Gross first-sale value totalled €795 million; landed quantity accounted for at least 95% of the variance in log value in every species, against 2–5% for price, and otter-trawl species supplied 12% of the landed weight but 37% of the value. Trends were modeled with a Tweedie generalized linear mixed model including harmonic seasonality, market random intercepts and first-order autocorrelation. Once serial dependence was absorbed, only two species retained a significant trend: round sardinella increased by 9.6% per year, and big-scale sand smelt declined by 7.2% per year. Same-year landings–price correlations were negative for abundant finfish and pelagics but positive for the two trawl crustaceans. Landings and value were concentrated in three hubs. First-sale market records offer a complementary monitoring tool.

title: Orphaned by an Evidentiary Standard: How Efficacy Review Emptied the Anabolic‐Androgenic Steroid Market, and What Doping Control Inherited
abstract: ABSTRACT The anabolic‐androgenic steroids have largely left clinical medicine while remaining in wide non‐medical use. This review documents how that happened from the supply side, using the US Federal Register from 1970 to 2026, approval and patent records, statutes, treaty texts, and the peer‐reviewed analytical literature. Three European firms created the class in 1935, their research contracted to university laboratories, and seven firms in five countries built it out by 1962, into a market where branded androgen preparations were already sold. The FDA's Drug Efficacy Study Implementation 7630 then condemned the tissue‐building claims in 1970, retained an osteoporosis claim only while no alternative existed, and closed in 1985 after no sponsor completed the studies. A parallel proceeding on the estrogen‐androgen combinations, opened in 1972, was resolved only in 2026. No safety finding drove any of it. Only one product in the class, oxandrolone, was ever determined withdrawn for reasons of safety or effectiveness, and 21 CFR 216.24 contains no anabolic‐androgenic steroid. Most applications lapsed. The two jurisdictions then diverged. The US moved these substances into narcotics law in 1990 while European states did not make that move, with consequences for the public health work possible in each. Three of the first designer steroids identified in sport had never been sold a…

title: The Neurodiversity Blind Spot: A Legal Gap Analysis of India's New Labour Codes and the RPwD Act, 2016
abstract: India’s decision to fold its labour statutes into four Codes, operative since late 2025, has been presented as a modernisation of the employment relationship. The present paper examines whether this reform, read alongside the 2016 disability rights statute, protects neurodivergent employees, that is, autistic persons, persons with dyslexia and other learning differences, persons with ADHD and persons with Tourette syndrome. A doctrinal gap analysis was conducted on the enacted texts of the four Codes, the 2016 Act and its Rules, the official disability assessment guidelines and selected rulings of the higher judiciary. Nine stages of working life were coded as explicit, partial or absent for each instrument. The analysis indicates that the four Codes neither use the expression “persons with disabilities” nor refer to reasonable accommodation, and that none of them cross-refers to the 2016 Act. The 2016 Act recognises autism, specific learning disabilities and mental illness, but it omits attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and Tourette syndrome, ties its strongest employment rights to Government establishments and conditions reservation on a forty per cent benchmark that sits uneasily with neurodevelopmental assessment. Courts have partly filled these gaps by extending reasonable accommodation beyond benchmark disability, but judicial relief remains individual and uneven. …

title: The cryptocurrency market ecosystem: evolution, formation and development prospects
abstract: The paper substantiates the proposition that, against the backdrop of the rapid development of digital technologies and during the rise of decentralized finance (DeFi), AI services, infrastructure projects, and other areas, cryptocurrencies remain one of the most promising investment markets for both investors and the general public (for the latter, digital assets open up new avenues for opportunities and self-fulfillment). Cryptocurrencies have definitively evolved from a narrow niche into a global financial trend, as evidenced by the formation of corporate crypto reserves and investors’ focus on macroeconomic indicators. A retrospective analysis shows that, from the moment Bitcoin emerged in 2009 to the present day, active processes have been underway to shape a genuine cryptocurrency market: having evolved from a niche sector into a global ecosystem, the key characteristics of which are high volatility and the application of cutting-edge technological developments, whilst its constant evolution creates new opportunities for developers, entrepreneurs and investors. The crypto industry is increasingly offering opportunities for growth as a sector of the digital economy, encompassing cryptocurrencies (such as Bitcoin), blockchain technology, related assets (tokens, NFTs), and an ecosystem of services (exchanges, DeFi, mining). This suggests the possibility of applying an ecosys…

title: Muslim Consumer Behavior in Choosing Halal Products at the Genteng Wetan Traditional Market
abstract: The level of public awareness regarding the importance of consuming halal products among Muslim consumers when making purchasing decisions for food items available at traditional markets. This study aims to analyze the factors influencing Muslim consumers in their selection of halal products at the Genteng Wetan traditional market. This study employs a descriptive qualitative approach, utilizing data collection techniques such as observation, interviews, and document analysis of consumers; the sampling technique used in this study is purposive sampling. Data analysis was conducted through data reduction and the drawing of conclusions via validity testing using triangulation. The results indicate that Muslim consumers’ behavior can be influenced by their knowledge of halal products, the presence or absence of halal labels among vendors, and the quality of the products they intend to purchase. Religious values and product knowledge are the most dominant factors, thereby influencing purchasing decisions and fostering trust in vendors regarding whether a product is halal or not. This study indicates that social relationships in traditional markets can play a role in shaping Muslim consumers’ behavior when selecting halal products, as they place their trust in vendors when making product choices.

How Online Reviews Shape Market Acceptance of Green Entrepreneurial Offerings: The Role of Review–Product Matching
abstract: Green entrepreneurial offerings increasingly enter digital markets, yet their environmental benefits do not necessarily translate into consumer acceptance. For green entrepreneurs, a key challenge is therefore how consumer-generated information reinforces—or conflicts with—the value propositions of their offerings. Using a 2 × 2 online experiment with 788 Chinese consumers, this study examines how egoistic versus altruistic review–product matching affects green purchase intention. The results show that matched review–product combinations significantly increase both green perceived value and purchase intention. Green perceived value partially mediates this effect, while green self-efficacy strengthens the indirect pathway from matching to purchase intention. Specifically, the indirect effect is not significant at low green self-efficacy but becomes significant at moderate and high levels. These findings demonstrate that the market acceptance of green offerings depends not simply on whether online reviews emphasize egoistic or altruistic benefits, but on whether consumer-generated information aligns with the product’s underlying value proposition. The study contributes to green entrepreneurship and digital-market research by identifying motivational congruence as a mechanism through which consumer-generated information can facilitate the market acceptance of green entrepreneurial…

title: Impact of Leishmania RNA virus 2 on immune response and pathogenesis in Leishmania major-infected BALB/c mice
abstract: Abstract Leishmania RNA virus (LRV)1 has been associated with altered disease outcomes in cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL), but the role of LRV2 in Leishmania major ( L. major ) infection remains poorly understood. This study investigated the impact of LRV2-positive L. major (Lm-LRV2 + ) on disease progression and host immune responses. J774A.1 macrophages were infected with Lm-LRV2 + or LRV2 - (Lm-LRV2 - ) parasites, and cytokine gene expression was measured by qPCR. BALB/c mice were inoculated subcutaneously with either strain; lesion development was monitored weekly, and parasite burden, cytokine responses (IFN-γ, IL-4, IL-17 A), and humoral responses (IgG, IgG1, IgG2a) were assessed. Macrophages infected with Lm-LRV2 + showed significantly elevated IL-6 and IL-1β mRNA levels compared to Lm-LRV2 - ( p < 0.01). In vivo, Lm-LRV2 + infection resulted in larger lesions and higher parasite loads ( p < 0.01). Lymphocytes from Lm-LRV2 + mice produced significantly more IFN-γ, IL-4, and IL-17 A at eight weeks ( p < 0.05), and antigen-specific IgG responses and IgG2a/IgG1 ratios were also increased. These findings demonstrate that LRV2 presence in L. major enhances pro-inflammatory cytokine expression and drives a more severe disease phenotype, with notable shifts in both cellular and humoral immunity. Our results underscore the critical role of LRV2 in CL pathogenesis and suggest that v…

title: Low-Velocity Impact Response of Biaxial Glass-Fiber Fabric Composites: Influence of Fabric Layer Number Under Progressively Increasing Impact Energy
abstract: Glass-fiber-reinforced polymer composites are of interest for lightweight structural applications, including marine structures, where accidental low-velocity impact is an important design consideration. This study investigates the low-velocity impact response of polyester-matrix composites reinforced with 4 layers, 6 layers, and 8 layers of biaxial glass fabric. A progressive test program, designed according to the number of fabric layers, used increasing impact-energy levels to cover both an indentation-dominated non-perforating regime and complete perforation, with the transition toward complete perforation in each configuration guiding the energy range selected for the configuration with the next higher number of fabric layers. Instrumented drop-weight tests with a 16 mm hemispherical impactor were analyzed using force, displacement, velocity, and energy histories. At the highest fully non-perforating energy levels of 30 J, 60 J, and 100 J, maximum contact forces were 7.25 kN, 13.05 kN, and 17.45 kN, while absorbed energies were approximately 28.7 J, 54.1 J, and 95.3 J. At 40 J, 80 J, and 120 J, respectively, the composite series entered the transition regime, with complete perforation observed for some of the tested specimens. The investigated parameters showed different diagnostic values: some were sensitive to the impactor mass–velocity combination, whereas displacement, …

title: Mechanical Response and Stability Assessment of Deteriorated Tunnel Linings Under Prescribed Cyclic Stress Changes
abstract: This study investigates how initial material deterioration and repeated stress changes affect the response of lining–rock systems during tunnel reconstruction and expansion. Monotonic uniaxial compression tests on limestone specimens with gypsum linings were monitored using digital image correlation. A corresponding numerical model was compared with the monotonic test response and used for incremental–static cyclic loading simulations. The numerical series examined cyclic stress amplitude, initial lining deterioration and initial surrounding-rock deterioration separately. Higher cyclic stress amplitudes produced greater convergence and more extensive plastic-zone development. The lining plastic-zone fraction increased more markedly between surrounding-rock deterioration levels of 20% and 30% than across the lower sampled levels, indicating a possible transition within the investigated range. Axial work-density changes depended on the parameter series and were not uniformly monotonic. A weighted five-indicator framework with prescribed engineering weights combines convergence, plastic-zone fractions and lining cohesion loss for relative comparison of the simulated cases. The findings identify regions and material conditions that warrant attention when assessing deteriorated linings and planning tunnel reconstruction and expansion.

title: Unified Pressure and Field Response Across Distinct Charge‐Order Regimes in Ti‐Doped CsV 3 Sb 5
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the phase diagram of kagome superconductors from a microscopic perspective is crucial for clarifying the interplay between charge order and superconductivity. Here, we report muon spin rotation () study of Ti‐doped at two representative compositions: underdoped (–CVS) and optimally doped (–CVS), exhibiting long‐range and short‐range charge order, respectively. Using zero‐field and high‐field , we find the presence of spontaneous weak internal magnetic fields in the normal state of both compositions, suggestive of time‐reversal‐symmetry (TRS) breaking. The TRS breaking response is strongly enhanced by an applied magnetic field and associated with long‐range and short‐range charge‐order, respectively. In the superconducting state, both samples exhibit anisotropic nodeless pairing with low superfluid density. Hydrostatic pressure substantially enhances both the superconducting transition temperature and the superfluid density (by 2.5), revealing a linear correlation between them and pointing to unconventional pairing. Above 1 GPa, a crossover from anisotropic to isotropic nodeless pairing is observed. Despite the different nature of charge order in the two doping regimes, the superconducting responses are remarkably similar, suggesting that the competition between superconductivity and charge order occurs on a local scale, largely independent of the long‐ran…

title: How Tumor Immune Neighborhoods May Help Predict Lung Cancer Treatment Response
EZH2 Inhibition Induces a Metabolic Stress Response Sensitizing Triple-Negative Breast Cancer to Glutaminase Targeting
abstract: Abstract EZH2, the catalytic subunit of the histone methyltransferase complex PRC2, is overexpressed and associated with poor prognosis in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Although EZH2 inhibition significantly alters chromatin landscapes and gene expression, it has limited impact on the growth of TNBC models, suggesting adaptive compensatory mechanisms. Here, we demonstrated that EZH2 inhibition causes the accumulation of misfolded proteins and double-stranded RNA (dsRNA), triggering an essential integrated stress response (ISR) through PKR and PERK activation. By inducing ISR-mediated ATF4, EZH2 inhibition enhanced amino acid flux and promoted glutaminolysis to support TNBC cell survival. Pharmacological targeting of this metabolic axis with a glutaminase inhibitor in combination with EZH2 inhibition significantly impaired TNBC cell proliferation and tumor growth. These findings reveal a stress-driven metabolic adaptation that sustains TNBC survival upon EZH2 blockade and highlight inhibition of this pathway as a strategy to enhance the efficacy of EZH2 inhibitors in TNBC.

title: Response of Vestibular Schwannomas in NF2-Related Schwannomatosis (NF2-SWN) to Losartan: A Case Series
abstract: Objective: Identify response rates of vestibular schwannomas in NF2-related Schwanomatosis to treatment with losartan alone or combined with other treatments. Study design: Single-institution retrospective case series. Setting: Tertiary referral center. Patients: Twenty patients with NF2-related Schwannomatosis. Intervention(s): Losartan alone, Losartan plus other therapy (bevacizumab, brigatinib, axitinib). Main outcome measure(s): Volumetric progression, defined as a change in VS size >20%, in accordance with the Response Evaluation in Neurofibromatosis and Schwannomatosis (REiNS) criteria. Audiometric progression is defined as a change in hearing measures, either a 10 dB or greater increase in PTA or a 10% or greater decrease in WRS. Results: This study included 20 patients, with 33 VSs, treated at our institution from 2014 to 2023. Losartan treatment duration ranged from 8.09 to 153.04 months (mean: 53.8, SD: 37.32). Twelve VSs were concurrently managed with antineoplastic therapy. Among 21 VSs treated with losartan alone, volumetric regression, progression, and stability were seen in 23.8%, 47.6%, and 28.6% of tumors, respectively. Among 5 VSs treated with combination losartan and bevacizumab, 40% of tumors regressed, 20% progressed, and 40% remained stable during the combination period. One tumor that progressed during bevacizumab monotherapy treatment achieved volumetric…

Semiparametric Panel Generalized Additive Models for Separate Forecasting of GDP Growth and Inflation in African Economies
abstract: Reliable forecasts of GDP growth and price dynamics support macroeconomic monitoring and economic planning, particularly in heterogeneous African economies where macroeconomic relationships may vary across economic conditions. This study develops and evaluates separate semiparametric Panel Generalized Additive Models (Panel GAMs) to examine nonlinear conditional associations and forecast GDP growth and the inverse hyperbolic sine-transformed Consumer Price Index (IHS-CPI). We analyse quarterly panel data for 53 African economies covering 2005Q1–2025Q4. The models represent the effects of exchange rate, money supply, interest rate, and time using smooth functions while accounting for country-specific heterogeneity through country-level random effects. We evaluate out-of-sample forecasting performance against a Linear Mixed Model. The estimated smooth terms provide evidence of statistically significant nonlinear conditional associations for both GDP growth and IHS-CPI. The Panel GAM achieves adjusted R2 values of 0.230 for GDP growth and 0.709 for IHS-CPI, indicating stronger in-sample fit for IHS-CPI. For out-of-sample forecasting, the Panel GAM produces RMSE and MAE values of 3.465 and 2.027 for GDP growth and 1.669 and 1.211 for IHS-CPI, respectively, compared with 3.368 and 1.931 for GDP growth and 1.632 and 1.192 for IHS-CPI from the Linear Mixed Model. Thus, the Panel GAM d…

title: Decoding Gen Z’s Second-hand iPhone Purchases: The Interplay of Price, Brand Image, Quality, and Psychological Factors
abstract: This study aims to analyze the factors influencing Generation Z (Gen Z) consumers’ decisions to purchase second-hand iPhones in Indonesia. Four main variables were examined: price perception, product quality, brand image, and psychological factors, including trust and risk perception. Data were collected from Gen Z respondents who had experience with or were interested in purchasing second-hand iPhones, and were analyzed using SmartPLS. The results show that all variables have a positive and significant influence on purchasing decisions, with price perception being the most dominant factor. These findings indicate that Gen Z prioritizes economic value and affordability while still considering device quality and trust in the seller. In addition, Apple’s brand image contributes to purchasing decisions through the symbolic value attached to young consumers’ digital identities. This study confirms that the decision to purchase a second-hand iPhone is influenced not only by rational factors such as price and quality but also by psychological and symbolic factors. These findings have important implications for refurbished-industry players to develop competitive pricing strategies, improve transparency in product quality, and build consumer trust through clear guarantees and information.

title: Pooled Information and Model Flexibility: Decomposing Machine-Learning Gains in Corporate Budgeting and Forecasting
abstract: Corporate financial planning and analysis (FP&A) is being reorganised around machine learning, yet the supporting evidence consists largely of vendor case reports using undefined accuracy measures. This study decomposes the machine-learning advantage into components that prior work bundles together—information recency versus model re-estimation, and pooled estimation versus learner flexibility—measured on corporate income-statement data rather than retail or equity series. An open benchmark from SEC XBRL data covering 2599 non-financial US filers and 118,406 firm-quarters, from 2011 to 2025, evaluates five pre-registered hypotheses under rolling-origin validation with clustered inference. First, the advantage of continuous re-forecasting over annual budgeting derives from information recency rather than parameter updating: supplying current quarterly actuals to a model estimated once at fiscal year start recovers 27 to 58 percent of forecast error, whereas quarterly re-estimation produces no detectable improvement (p = 0.82), a result that holds across the COVID-19 and 2022 inflation regimes. Second, the advantage is an interaction rather than a main effect: a pooled linear model modestly outperforms a Theta benchmark, a flexible learner fitted per firm underperforms it, and a foundation model pooled across unrelated domains underperforms further; only pooling across comparable…

title: A Layered Decision-Aware Forecasting Architecture for Noisy Panel Environments
abstract: Machine learning forecasting systems in noisy, non-stationary, multi-entity environments are commonly optimized for pointwise predictive accuracy, although many downstream decisions depend on the relative ordering of entities rather than exact numerical forecasts. This creates a potential prediction–ranking–decision misalignment, where the model with the lowest forecast error may not generate the most useful ranking or decision outcome. This paper proposes a Layered Decision-Aware Forecasting Architecture (LDFA) that separates predictive calibration from decision-oriented transformation. Layers 1 and 2 generate heterogeneous forecasts through base learners, stacking, and adaptive weighting, while the main methodological contribution is Layer 3: a selective post-prediction controller based on source selection, activation gating, veto logic, and regime-aware scaling. LDFA is evaluated using daily data for 30 EGX firms from 2020 to 2025 under a leakage-controlled expanding-window walk-forward protocol. The results show that prediction, ranking, and decision metrics favor different models: the Ridge meta-model provides the strongest target-scale accuracy, the XGBRankerLTR learning-to-rank baseline achieves the strongest ranking information coefficient (IC), and the SoftmaxHybridGate achieves the highest Sharpe ratio. Determinants of Purchase Intention for Natural Organic Cosmetics: Price, E-Service Quality, Product Quality, and Social Media Marketing
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effects of selling price, electronic service quality, and producte quality on customer satisfication. It also examines the effects of the product itself and social media marketing on consumers’ purchasing intent for natural based cosmetics products, spesifically Deepmire Skin brand. This study employs a quantitative approach, collecting data through a questionnaire administrated to 171 respondents. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Square-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) method with the assitance of SmartPLS software. The resulth of this study indicate that selling price has a significant effect on consumers’ purchasing intent toward Deepmire Skin products, with coefficient value of 0,4333 an a p-value of 0,000. In addition, the quality of electronic service also has a positive effect on consumer purchasing intent with a coefficient of 0,283 and a p-value 0,001. Meanwhile, product quality also influences consumer purchasing intent but in a negative direction, with a coefficient of -0,384 and p-value od 0,001. Meanwhile, social media marketing has positive effect on consumer purchasing interest, with a coefficient 0,701 and p-value of 0,000, making it the variable with the greatest influence. These findings indicate that consumer purchasing interest is influenced by price, digital services, product quality, and social media marketing…

title: Biases in near-surface meteorological conditions over Alaska within the HRRR model revealed using observations from the U.S. Climate Reference Network
abstract: Abstract The Arctic atmosphere intricately impacts midlatitude weather and climate across diverse timescales. Thus, an accurate representation of the Arctic and its surrounding regions in numerical weather prediction models is critical across many applications, including fire weather, aviation forecasts, marine forecasts, etc. Doing so requires that models properly simulate near-surface radiation, temperature, and moisture fields. However, knowledge of model performance over the Artic is limited largely due to the paucity of observations. To help close this gap, we used five years of observations obtained from 1 Jan 2021 through 31 Dec 2025 from 22 stations comprising the U.S. Climate Reference Network in Alaska to evaluate how well the 1-h through 48-h forecasts from version 4 of the High-Resolution Rapid Refresh (HRRR) model represent incoming shortwave radiation ( SW d ), surface (i.e., skin) temperature ( T s ), near-surface air temperature ( T a ), and humidity (RH) on interannual, seasonal, and diurnal timescales. We found that the HRRR had a net positive SW d bias but, counterintuitively, had negative T s and T a biases during the summer. In the winter, the T s and T a biases were positive. Overall, the T s and T a biases were smallest from 06 – 15 UTC and largest from 18 – 00 UTC. They were also largest on the subset of days with the largest T a changes and SW d . In cl…
